Synopsis: Prohibiting a leasehold tenant of an unregistered ground lease from being required to hold more than 3 years of ground rent in escrow; requiring a ground lease holder to mail certain notices or bills to a leasehold tenant in a certain manner under certain circumstances; requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to make available on its website the form a ground lease holder must use to provide a leasehold tenant bills or notices; etc.
Title: Ground Leases – Notices and Billing – Forms and Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill modifies the regulations surrounding ground leases in Maryland by prohibiting ground lease holders of unregistered leases from requiring tenants to hold more than three years of rent in escrow. It requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) to create and host standardized forms for ground rent billing and notices of possession. Additionally, it establishes stricter mailing requirements for ground lease holders, prevents them from charging tenants for these mailing costs, and mandates that ground lease transferees notify SDAT of any transfers.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Ground lease holders, leasehold tenants, and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) can comply with the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business impacts are expected to be minimal, though ground lease holders are prohibited from being reimbursed by tenants for specific mailing and notice costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes specific notice and mailing requirements that must be met before a ground lease holder can file an action for possession for nonpayment of ground rent in the state court system. The AOC provides operational and legal support to the Maryland Judicial Branch, which handles these cases.

The OAG serves as the primary legal counsel for state agencies, including the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), which is tasked by this bill to develop new form notices and bills. It also has a mandate to enforce consumer protection laws, which are relevant to the rights of leasehold tenants.

The bill includes a formal declaration of intent by the General Assembly regarding the State Department of Assessments and Taxation's ground rent redemption program, which falls under the executive branch's oversight. The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees executive branch enforcement of laws.

The department's mission is to ensure safe and secure housing for Maryland residents. Ground lease regulations and redemption programs are central to property ownership and housing stability in several Maryland jurisdictions.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and personnel for state agencies. While the fiscal note indicates the bill can be implemented with existing resources, DBM is responsible for the overall fiscal planning for the department implementing these changes.

Synopsis: Requiring a treatment plan for an individual with a mental disorder admitted to a certain health care facility to include a discharge goal and an estimate of the probable length of the inpatient stay before the individual can be transferred to a certain setting; requiring certain facility staff to review and reassess a plan of treatment within certain time periods; requiring the Department of Health to report annually to the General Assembly on the Resident Grievance System and the grievances received related to State facilities; etc.
Title: Mental Health - Treatment Plans for Individuals in Facilities and Resident Grievance System

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires mental health treatment plans to include long-range discharge goals and inpatient stay estimates, mandates regular clinical reviews, and allows family participation in the treatment process with patient consent. It also establishes a grievance and appeals process for patients in State-operated facilities through the Resident Grievance System and requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit annual reports to the General Assembly.
stakeholders: Individuals with mental disorders admitted to health care facilities, family members of patients, and facility treatment staff
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase to hire additional staff to manage treatment plan reviews, reassessments, and appeals, and to cover costs for patients requiring treatment at outside facilities. A specific dollar estimate is unavailable as the impact depends on the volume of requests. The Maryland Department of Health can handle regulatory and reporting requirements within existing budgeted resources. Local fiscal impact is negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing state behavioral health facilities and the administration of the Resident Grievance System, MDH is responsible for implementing the new treatment plan requirements, adopting regulations for the appeals process, managing the increased staffing needs, and submitting the annual report to the General Assembly.

The bill text explicitly designates the Office of Administrative Hearings to conduct de novo hearings and issue decisions for individuals in State facilities who request a reconsideration of their treatment plan review and reassessment.

The fiscal note indicates that MDH will require additional general fund expenditures for personnel and potential treatment costs outside of state facilities to comply with the bill, which falls under DBM's oversight of state budget and personnel management.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for representing indigent individuals in involuntary commitment and mental health proceedings; they are listed as an information source for the bill due to their role in safeguarding the rights of facility residents.
The bill provides for judicial review of administrative decisions in the Circuit Court, impacting the judicial branch's operations. The AOC is also listed as an information source in the fiscal note.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MDH and would be responsible for helping draft the required regulations and representing the state in administrative or judicial appeals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is listed as an information source in the fiscal note, as they manage individuals with mental health needs within correctional settings and may interact with the state's mental health facility and grievance systems.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates services for residents with disabilities, including mental health disorders, and ensures that policies are inclusive and integrated, making this bill relevant to their advocacy and coordination mission.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved (MDH) and the Governor signed the bill into law; the office also coordinates broad policy initiatives related to behavioral health.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain plug-in electric drive vehicles for which a permit has been issued by the Motor Vehicle Administration to use high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes regardless of the number of passengers in the vehicles; requiring the Administration to charge a fee, not to exceed $20, for issuing the permit; and requiring, on or before January 1 each year, a report to be submitted to the Governor and the General Assembly on the effect of the use of the plug-in electric drive vehicle permits on the operation of HOV lanes.
Title: Vehicle Laws – HOV Lanes – Plug–In Electric Drive Vehicles

bill_summary: This bill reestablishes the authorization for certain plug-in electric drive vehicles to use high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes regardless of the number of passengers, provided the vehicle has a maximum speed of at least 65 miles per hour and the owner obtains a permit from the Motor Vehicle Administration.
stakeholders: Owners of plug-in electric drive vehicles in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are estimated to increase by up to $380,000 through fiscal 2026, assuming the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) charges the maximum authorized fee of $20 for an estimated 19,000 permits. TTF expenditures are expected to increase by approximately $26,220 through September 30, 2025, to cover the cost of purchasing HOV decals. MVA can implement reporting and programming requirements using existing resources. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary agency responsible for issuing the HOV permits, collecting the associated fees (up to $20), and co-authoring the annual report on HOV lane operation and permit usage.

SHA designates HOV lanes and is responsible for their management. Under the bill, SHA must consult on permit design, recommend limits on the number of permits to prevent lane degradation, and co-author annual reports to the Governor.

As the parent agency of both MVA and SHA, MDOT oversees the implementation of this policy. Additionally, the fiscal impact of permit fees and decal expenditures directly affects the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which MDOT manages.
The Department of State Police is specifically tasked with consulting on the design of the HOV permit and is responsible for enforcing traffic laws related to HOV lane restrictions.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch agencies (MVA, SHA, MSP) implementing the bill. Furthermore, the bill mandates that MVA and SHA provide an annual report directly to the Governor regarding the impact of the permits on HOV lane operations.

bill_summary: This bill streamlines Maryland's government reporting requirements by repealing, consolidating, and rescheduling numerous mandated reports from various State agencies. The revisions target reports that are obsolete, duplicative, or unnecessary, aiming to improve administrative efficiency and ensure that only relevant data is collected and reported to the General Assembly.
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies and departments, the Maryland General Assembly, local government entities, and local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and has no direct effect on State or local finances. According to the Fiscal Note, some agencies may experience operational efficiencies due to the repeal, rescheduling, or consolidation of existing reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is the recipient of numerous mandated reports addressed in this bill, and the Governor is responsible for appointing members to several boards whose reporting requirements are being modified or repealed.
The bill modifies the reporting dates for the Comptroller regarding beer production for various license holders and updates the Comptroller's role in auditing 9-1-1 fee collection and remittances.
The bill centralizes telework reporting requirements, making the Department responsible for submitting a single consolidated report for all state units rather than each unit submitting individually.
The bill repeals a reporting requirement for the Department regarding conditional loans or grants provided to companies for headquarters construction and retention.

The bill modifies reporting for the LYNX High School and affects reporting mechanisms for students who are foster care recipients or homeless youth, which involves coordination with the State Board of Education.
The bill modifies the annual reporting requirements for the 9-1-1 Board, which is overseen by the Department of Emergency Management, including updates on Next Generation 9-1-1 transitions.
The bill modifies reporting dates and requirements for climate change mitigation, the Bay Restoration Fund, and solid waste management/recycling programs administered by the Department.
The bill repeals the requirement for the Department (via the Records Management Division) to submit a consolidated annual report on forms management activities from all state departments.
The Department takes over the lead reporting role for home visiting programs and has reporting date adjustments for the Governor's Wellmobile Program and tobacco retailer violations.
The bill reduces the frequency of the Department's reports on minority business participation in the Energy Efficient Homes Construction Loan Program from semi-annual to annual.
The Department is designated as the lead agency for submitting the outcomes evaluation report for children's services, coordinating with other departments.
The bill repeals a reporting requirement for the Department related to the 'End the Violence' P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.
The Department will receive precinct boundary information electronically rather than via written documents and continues to co-author reports on the impact of wastewater treatment upgrades on growth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies inmate data reporting (removing place of birth) and repeals the Department's reporting role in the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.
As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, the Department is impacted by the repeal of several MVA reporting mandates concerning service of process and organ donation.
The Commission takes on new reporting duties for FAFSA completion data and foster care/homeless youth data while several of its other reporting requirements are repealed or modified.
The bill repeals the Department of State Police's reporting requirement regarding the progress of the 'End the Violence' P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.
The bill modifies how the State Administrator sends precinct boundary descriptions and maps to other departments, requiring electronic transmission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals reporting requirements for the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board regarding interoperability and modifies reporting for other advisory bodies.
The Children's Cabinet, of which this office is a key part, has its reporting requirements for home visiting programs modified and shifted to the Maryland Department of Health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office (formerly GOCPYVS) is removed as the lead reporter for home visiting programs and has its reporting role for the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program repealed.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office will no longer receive certain video lottery employee data reports from the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission due to the repeal of that requirement.
The bill repeals a requirement for the Board to submit an annual report on the procurement system, as this information is already reported by the Procurement Advisor.
The bill repeals the requirement for the Commission (referenced as the Public School Construction Program) to report annually on the use of alternative financing mechanisms for school construction.
The reporting date for the Center's annual report and its report on the use of the Fund and investment outcomes is changed from October to December.
The bill transfers certain FAFSA reporting duties to the Higher Education Commission and modifies the Center's requirements for publishing foster care and homeless youth data dashboards.
The bill removes the requirement for the Commission's independent audit reports to be submitted to the Department of Legislative Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals requirements for the Commission to submit data regarding Baltimore City video lottery operation employees.
The bill repeals several reporting requirements for the Board of Trustees related to rehired retirees in local school systems.
The bill reduces the corporation's reporting frequency from quarterly to every six months and repeals a duplicative report on the Maryland Technology Incubator Program.
As a public institution of higher education, the university is impacted by changes in how data on foster care recipients and homeless youth is reported to the state.
Several of the MVA's reporting requirements are repealed, including those regarding service of process for nonresidents and annual reports on organ donor designations on licenses.
The bill repeals a reporting requirement where the Public Service Commission was required to use input from the Attorney General regarding VoIP consumer complaints.
The bill repeals a reporting requirement where the Public Service Commission was required to use input from the People's Counsel regarding VoIP consumer complaints.
The bill repeals the Commission's discretionary reporting requirement concerning consumer protections and complaints for Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services.
As a public institution of higher education, the college is impacted by changes in how data on foster care recipients and homeless youth is reported to the state.
The bill repeals reporting requirements for the Board of Regents regarding business entities established by the university and specifically repeals reporting for UMCEED.
The bill maintains the Service's role in coordinating with the Office of Recycling to study and report on recycling centers and solid waste management.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the District Court, in aid of enforcement or execution of a money judgment resulting from a certain small claim action, from ordering the appearance of an individual for an examination or ordering an individual to answer interrogatories.
Title: District Court - Small Claims - Enforcement of Money Judgments
bill_summary: This bill prohibits the District Court from ordering an individual to appear for an examination or answer written interrogatories to enforce or execute a money judgment resulting from a small claims action (claims for $5,000 or less).
stakeholders: Small claims judgment creditors (including small businesses), judgment debtors, and the Maryland District Court.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances. Implementation costs for the District Court, such as updating forms and webpages, can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Small businesses may experience a meaningful impact due to the limitation of methods available to collect on small claims judgments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts District Court operations by prohibiting specific enforcement tools (examinations and interrogatories) for small claims judgments. The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency responsible for updating the court's forms, digital systems, and public brochures to comply with these procedural changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes the legal basis for body attachments (arrests for civil contempt) in small claims cases by prohibiting the prerequisite orders for examination. This impact is noted in the fiscal note as it reduces the potential for individuals to be taken into custody and processed within the state's detention systems for these specific civil matters.

As the chief legal officer for Maryland, the OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding changes in judicial procedures and the enforcement of money judgments, and may be involved in interpreting the impact of these changes on state-held small claims judgments.

Synopsis: Converting enhanced underinsured motorist coverage from an opt-in offering of coverage into an opt-out coverage option under provisions of law establishing requirements for private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance; requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to conduct a study on the impact of converting enhanced underinsured motorist coverage to an opt-out coverage option and report its findings to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by December 31, 2026, and December 31, 2028; etc.
Title: Private Passenger Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance - Enhanced Underinsured Motorist Coverage - Opt-Out Option

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicle Insurance -see also- MD Auto Insurance Fund

bill_summary: This bill converts enhanced underinsured motorist (EUIM) coverage from an opt-in to an opt-out option for new private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance policies issued on or after July 1, 2024. Insurers are required to provide EUIM coverage unless the insured affirmatively waives it in writing. The bill also mandates the Maryland Insurance Administration to study the impact of this change on premiums and consumer selection, with reporting requirements through 2028.
stakeholders: Maryland drivers purchasing private passenger motor vehicle insurance and motor vehicle liability insurance companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) increase minimally from a $125 rate and form filing fee. General fund revenues from the 2% premium tax may increase minimally because EUIM coverage is generally more expensive than standard uninsured motorist coverage, resulting in higher total premiums. The MIA can implement the bill's requirements and conduct the mandatory study using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of Maryland's insurance market, the MIA is responsible for implementing the transition to an opt-out system for enhanced underinsured motorist coverage, which includes reviewing and approving the required waiver forms and conducting a mandatory multi-year study on the impact of the coverage conversion on premiums and consumer choice.

As the state-created insurer of last resort for drivers unable to obtain private insurance, MAIF is directly impacted by changes to coverage standards; additionally, the bill explicitly establishes that enhanced underinsured motorist coverage is primary to any right to recovery from MAIF.

The bill requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to conduct a formal study and submit interim and final reports regarding its findings and recommendations on the insurance coverage conversion directly to the Governor.

The bill prohibits the use of binding arbitration for disputes related to enhanced underinsured motorist coverage, effectively directing these legal challenges into the Maryland court system and potentially impacting judicial caseloads.

As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller oversees the general fund, which is anticipated to receive a minimal increase in revenue from insurance premium taxes due to the potentially higher premiums associated with the shift toward enhanced underinsured motorist coverage.

Synopsis: Repealing the crime of unnatural or perverted sexual practice.
Title: Criminal Law – Unnatural or Perverted Sexual Practice – Repeal
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 796

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the criminal offense of unnatural or perverted sexual practice from Maryland law. It updates references in various statutes—including those related to child abuse, vulnerable adult abuse, and sex offender registration—to instead refer to any other sexual conduct that is a crime, and it establishes specific rules for the expungement or vacating of past convictions related to this repealed offense.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and State's Attorneys' offices
stakeholders: Maryland residents, the judiciary, law enforcement, and individuals with past convictions for the repealed offense.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. According to the Fiscal Note, the statute being repealed was already largely unenforceable for consensual private activity due to existing case law, and the number of annual convictions is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial operations by altering the criminal code, establishing new criteria for expungement petitions, and providing for motions to vacate judgments in specific circumstances. The AOC provides the operational and technological support for the courts to process these filings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enables individuals convicted under the repealed statute to file motions to vacate judgments if they were victims of human trafficking and to seek expungements. The OPD will represent indigent defendants in these proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies classifications for Tier III sex offenders for past convictions and impacts the maintenance of criminal records and the sex offender registry, both of which are managed by DPSCS.

The bill amends the Family Law Article and Criminal Law Article regarding the definition of 'sexual abuse' and 'sexual molestation or exploitation' of children, which are critical to the department's child protective services and social service missions.
As the chief legal representative of the state, the OAG provides counsel to state agencies on the repeal of criminal statutes and handles appeals related to criminal convictions and registry status.
The repeal of a criminal statute and changes to definitions of sexual activity affect law enforcement investigations, charging procedures, and the maintenance of police records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The GOCPP coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy; changes to sexual offense laws and sex offender tiering fall under its policy purview.
The bill's provisions regarding the expungement of police and court records impact the Archives' role as the central depository for permanent government records.
Changes to definitions of 'sexual abuse' and 'sexual molestation' of minors are relevant to the department's assessment and supervision of youth in the juvenile justice system.
The bill amends definitions related to the abuse and exploitation of 'vulnerable adults,' a population for whom MDH sets policy and provides health and safety services.
The bill's modification of child abuse and exploitation definitions relates to the office's mission to coordinate networks that protect and promote the well-being of Maryland's children.

The repeal of the 'unnatural or perverted sexual practice' statute is historically and legally relevant to civil rights, as these laws were frequently used in a discriminatory manner against the LGBTQ+ community.

Synopsis: Altering certain qualifications for a journeyman license to provide heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration services to require having held an apprentice license for 4 rather than 3 years and having completed at least 6,000 rather than 1,875 hours of training under the direction and control of a licensed contractor.
Title: Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Services - Journeyman License - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: The bill increases the qualifications for a journeyman license in heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) services by requiring applicants to have held an apprentice license for at least four years (up from three) and to have completed at least 6,000 hours of training (up from 1,875).
responsible_party: State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors
stakeholders: HVACR apprentices, applicants for HVACR journeyman licenses, and HVACR contractors and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund licensing revenues may be delayed as applicants spend more time in training before applying for a journeyman license, though the Maryland Department of Labor does not expect a material effect on State finances. There is no local fiscal impact. Small businesses providing apprenticeship training will be impacted by the increased oversight and duration requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor (MDL) is the primary agency impacted as it oversees the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program (MATP) and the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration (HVACR) Contractors. The bill directly alters the licensure and training hour requirements that the department is responsible for regulating and enforcing.

The board serves as the governor's chief policy-making body for the state's workforce system. This bill aligns HVACR journeyman licensing requirements with the state's registered apprenticeship system, which is a key component of the state's workforce strategy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a meaningful impact on small businesses, as those that train HVACR apprentices must provide training and oversight for a longer duration (four years and 6,000 hours instead of three years and 1,875 hours).

The OAG serves as legal counsel to all state agencies, including the Department of Labor and its various licensing boards. They would provide legal guidance on the implementation and enforcement of the new licensing standards.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors state revenues. The fiscal note mentions that special fund licensing revenues may be delayed as applicants spend more time in training before paying for journeyman licenses.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. Stricter licensing and training requirements could potentially lead to an increase in contested cases or appeals regarding license applications and board decisions.

Synopsis: Limiting the percentage of the weekly benefits amount that the Secretary of Labor may deduct from weekly benefits payable to a claimant to recover certain overpayments of unemployment insurance benefits to 50% of the weekly benefit or 25% if the benefit is less than $100; and clarifying the circumstances under which the Secretary may use certain methods to recover overpayments of unemployment insurance benefits.
Title: Unemployment Insurance - Recovery of Benefits - Limitation and Methods

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill limits the percentage of weekly unemployment insurance benefits that the Secretary of Labor may deduct from future payments to recover non-fraudulent overpayments. Deductions are capped at 50% of the weekly benefit amount, or 25% if the benefit amount is $100 or less.
stakeholders: Unemployment insurance claimants and the Maryland Department of Labor
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase nonbudgeted Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund (UITF) expenditures by limiting the amount that can be recouped via benefit offsets. The Maryland Department of Labor estimates a one-time programming cost of $16,400. While the exact total impact is unknown, the fiscal note provides a context of approximately $9,000,000 in unrecouped overpayments based on 2022 data.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for administering the unemployment insurance program and implementing the bill's new limits on benefit recovery deductions from future payments.
The Comptroller's Office is responsible for revenue collection and tax intercepts, which are noted as primary alternative methods for recovering benefit overpayments when deductions are limited.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees state finances and coordinates the collection of debts owed to the state, which may include unrecovered unemployment benefit overpayments.
The Governor oversees the Department of Labor and the executive branch's administration of the state's unemployment insurance system and fiscal policies.
The Treasurer's Office acts as the custodian of state funds, including the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund, which is fiscally impacted by the timing and volume of benefit recoveries.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and represents the state in civil actions or appeals related to the recovery of improperly paid benefits.
The state judiciary may handle civil suits filed by the Secretary of Labor to recover benefit overpayments from claimants.

Synopsis: Renaming the Commission on LGBTQ Affairs to be the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs; increasing the number of members of the Commission from 15 to 21; altering certain qualifications for members appointed to the Commission; staggering the terms of Commission members; and altering the duties of the Commission.
Title: State Government – Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs – Alterations

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill renames the Commission on LGBTQ Affairs to the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs and expands its scope to explicitly include questioning, intersex, asexual, agender, and aromantic identities. It increases the commission membership from 15 to 21 individuals, staggers their terms, and updates the qualifications for members to reflect broader diversity standards while refining the commission's duties regarding advocacy and data collection for the LGBTQIA+ community.
stakeholders: The LGBTQIA+ community in Maryland, including individuals who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, questioning, intersex, asexual, agender, or aromantic.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's changes, including expense reimbursements for the additional members, can be handled with existing budgeted resources according to the Fiscal Note. There is no estimated impact on local government or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its units, including the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives where the Commission is housed. The Governor is also responsible for appointing the 21 members of the Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs is a unit within the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives (GOCI). The bill directly alters the name, membership, and duties of a unit GOCI is responsible for managing.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions. This bill increases the commission's membership from 15 to 21 and adds specific diversity requirements for these appointments.

The bill requires the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs to collect data across State agencies regarding complaints alleging discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity. The Commission on Civil Rights is the primary state agency responsible for investigating such complaints.

As the central personnel agency for the State, DBM is a primary source of data regarding the implementation of LGBTQIA+-inclusive policies across state agencies, which the Commission is now mandated to collect.
The bill empowers the Commission to create surveys and appoint advisory committees in several fields, specifically including education.
The bill empowers the Commission to create surveys and appoint advisory committees in several fields, specifically including health and safety.
The bill empowers the Commission to create surveys and appoint advisory committees in several fields, specifically including labor and employment laws and policies.
The bill empowers the Commission to create surveys and appoint advisory committees in several fields, specifically including law enforcement.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state agencies, boards, and commissions. It would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the implementation of the bill's changes to the Commission's membership and data collection mandates.

Synopsis: Requiring a person who fails to reactivate a real estate broker license on inactive status within 3 years to comply with specified requirements to obtain a license.
Title: Real Estate Brokers - Inactive Licenses - Requirements After Expiration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill requires real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and salespersons who fail to reactivate an inactive license within three years to meet the same requirements as new applicants, including specific education and examination standards, to obtain a license. This change aligns the reinstatement process for inactive licensees with that of active licensees.
stakeholders: Real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons whose licenses are on inactive status in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Real Estate Commission can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect state finances or operations, and there is no fiscal impact on local governments. Small business impacts are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Real Estate Commission, which is responsible for the licensing and regulation of real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons affected by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Real Estate Commission is an ongoing regulatory body that directly manages the licensing process for brokers and will be responsible for implementing the new requirements for inactive licenses.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and its regulatory boards, ensuring that licensing requirements and disciplinary actions comply with state law.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases involving state regulatory agencies, which may include disputes over the denial or expiration of professional licenses such as those for real estate brokers.

Synopsis: Exempting applications for changing certain resident agents from the requirement that the Board of License Commissioners for Howard County hold a public hearing on the applications; and authorizing the Board to hold a public hearing on certain applications if the Board determines there is good cause for the hearing.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages - Public Hearing Ho. Co. 13-23
bill_summary: This bill exempts applications for changing certain resident agents from public hearing requirements in Howard County when the applicant is already a license holder for that license and has previously been approved at a non-violation hearing. The Howard County Board of License Commissioners may still require a hearing if they determine there is good cause.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders in Howard County and the Howard County Board of License Commissioners
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Howard County expenditures for hearings are estimated to decrease by up to approximately 14000 dollars annually beginning in fiscal 2024 because fewer hearings for resident agent changes will be required. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the public hearing and notification procedures for the Howard County Board of License Commissioners. In Maryland, local boards of license commissioners are state-authorized administrative bodies created by the General Assembly to regulate alcoholic beverages, and this category encompasses such boards.

The Comptroller of Maryland is the principal state official responsible for regulating the alcoholic beverages industry. This bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages Article of the Maryland Code, which falls under the Comptroller's general regulatory and oversight domain.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signed this bill into law. The bill concerns the administrative procedures of boards established under state law to execute local regulations.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and statutory interpretation for state boards and commissions, including those authorized under the state's Alcoholic Beverages Article.

Synopsis: Altering the entity that must administer or approve an apprenticeship program for electricians; substituting the term "uninsured" for the term "inactive" in certain provisions of law relating to liability insurance requirements for certain electricians; prohibiting a certain electrician from contracting to provide electrical services unless the electrical work is covered by certain liability insurance; specifying who is authorized and required to purchase certain insurance; etc.
Title: Maryland Electricians Act - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill revises the Maryland Electricians Act by renaming 'inactive' license status to 'uninsured' and updating the authority responsible for approving electrician apprenticeship programs to the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning. It prohibits electricians from contracting to provide services unless they are covered by specific liability insurance and allows 'uninsured' master electricians to work as journeypersons under supervision. Additionally, the State Board of Electricians must now denote insurance status on each license issued.
stakeholders: Licensed master, journeyperson, and apprentice electricians, electrical contracting businesses, and apprenticeship program providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no material impact on State or local finances. The State Board of Electricians can handle the required administrative and procedural changes using existing resources, and there is no projected change in State revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts two entities within the Department: the State Board of Electricians, which must manage the transition to 'uninsured' licensing status and verify insurance requirements, and the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning, which is designated as the new authority for approving electrician apprenticeship programs.

The bill establishes specific liability and property damage insurance mandates for licensed electricians and requires insurers to notify the State Board of Electricians upon policy cancellation, touching upon the administration's regulation of insurance contracts and carrier notifications.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the State Board of Electricians, and will likely be involved in interpreting the revised insurance requirements and status terminology for regulatory enforcement.

The OAH adjudicates contested licensing cases for state agencies; it may be called upon to handle appeals related to the 'uninsured' status of electricians or enforcement actions taken by the Board regarding insurance compliance.

As the body responsible for Maryland's workforce strategy, the board has a policy interest in the approval and administration of apprenticeship programs, which this bill reassigns to the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the implementation of bill revisions that affect agency operations, even though the fiscal note indicates the changes will be handled within existing resources.

bill_summary: This bill establishes that the adaptive reuse of existing buildings to create affordable multifamily housing is an eligible use of loan proceeds from certain programs administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It further requires DHCD to notify applicants for these housing-focused programs that repurposing existing buildings for affordable housing is a permitted use of funds.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
stakeholders: Applicants for DHCD housing loans, developers of multifamily housing, and low-income individuals seeking affordable housing units.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. The Department of Housing and Community Development already provides loans for adaptive reuse projects under existing programs and can fulfill the bill's notification requirements using current budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary entity responsible for implementing the bill, as it must incorporate adaptive reuse as an eligible use for its affordable multifamily housing loan programs and notify applicants of this eligibility.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy priorities; the bill was approved by the Governor and affects a cabinet-level department's affordable housing strategy.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Housing and Community Development and would likely be involved in reviewing the regulatory language or application notices required by the bill.
DBM manages the state's budget and oversees the fiscal execution of DHCD's loan programs, ensuring that the use of funds for adaptive reuse aligns with state fiscal planning.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and community revitalization; adaptive reuse is a critical land use strategy that aligns with the agency's mission to manage infrastructure and resources effectively.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on sustainable development and reducing the state's carbon footprint; the adaptive reuse of existing buildings for housing directly supports these environmental and revitalization goals.

bill_summary: This bill requires landlords to provide residential tenants with written notice of rent increases within specific timeframes based on the duration of the lease, such as 90 days for tenancies exceeding one month. It prohibits lease provisions that require tenants to accept notice of rent increases solely through electronic delivery. Additionally, local jurisdictions that adopt rent control laws must report details of those laws and annual building permit data for multifamily rental units to the General Assembly.

stakeholders: Residential tenants, landlords, and local county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Small business impacts on landlords are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces laws regarding residential leases and unfair or deceptive trade practices. This bill establishes new statutory requirements for rent increase notifications that the OAG may need to provide guidance on or enforce.

As the principal agency for housing policy and community revitalization, the Department of Housing and Community Development has a direct interest in regulations affecting rental housing and the reporting of local laws and building permits related to residential developments.

The Maryland Judicial Branch adjudicates landlord-tenant disputes, including those where rent increases and retaliatory actions are at issue. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports these operations, which will be affected by changes to notice requirements in residential leases.

The bill requires local jurisdictions that implement rent increase limits to report data on building permits for multifamily dwellings. This requirement aligns with the Department of Planning's role in coordinating land use data and promoting sustainable growth.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill specifically references state of emergency declarations issued by the Governor as a condition for certain reporting exceptions and requires local reporting to the General Assembly.

bill_summary: This bill alters the Urban Agriculture Grant Program by expanding eligibility to all urban areas in Maryland, allowing grants to be issued directly to producers and higher education institutions, and creating the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee. It mandates an annual appropriation of at least $100,000 to the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund from fiscal 2025 through 2029.
stakeholders: Urban agricultural producers, nonprofit organizations, institutions of higher education, and socially disadvantaged farmers in Maryland urban areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least 100000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2029 due to a mandated appropriation to the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly. There is no significant impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Urban Agriculture Grant Program and the Urban Agriculture Water and Power Infrastructure Grant Program, both of which are significantly altered by this bill. MDA will staff the new Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee and the Secretary of Agriculture is responsible for appointing members and designating the chair.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires a representative of MARBIDCO, designated by its Executive Director, to serve on the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to recommend guidelines and policies for the program. MARBIDCO's mission to support agricultural sustainability aligns with the bill's goals.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of at least $100,000 to the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for implementing the mandated appropriation in the state budget and overseeing the budget execution for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee, a body comprised of appointed public and private experts tasked with providing recommendations on the implementation and guidelines of the Urban Agriculture Grant Program.
The bill specifies that the State Treasurer shall hold the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.
The bill mandates that the Comptroller account for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund, ensuring fiscal tracking and management of the program's revenues and expenditures.

Under the bill, institutions of higher education are now 'qualified applicants' eligible to receive grants. Several USM institutions may apply for funding to provide education and training to urban farmers.
As an institution of higher education, Morgan State University is eligible to receive grants under the modified program to support urban agriculture viability and training.
As an institution of higher education, Saint Mary's College is eligible to receive grants under the program to provide training and technical assistance to urban agricultural producers.
MHEC oversees the institutions of higher education that are now eligible for grants and provides the policy framework within which these institutions operate agricultural training programs.

OLA is responsible for auditing state programs; the expansion of this grant program and the creation of a mandated appropriation would fall under their periodic fiscal compliance and performance audit responsibilities.

bill_summary: This bill changes the selection process for the student member of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners from an appointment to an election by middle and high school students. It expands the student member's voting rights to include matters such as capital and operating budgets, school boundaries, and student disciplinary issues, though they remain barred from voting on personnel and collective bargaining. Additionally, the bill establishes a Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members to evaluate board member pay and the potential addition of a second student member.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners and the Office of the Mayor of Baltimore City
stakeholders: Middle and high school students in Baltimore City Public Schools, the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. State expenditures may increase minimally for task force member travel reimbursements, which are assumed to be absorbable within existing budgets. Local expenditures for Baltimore City Public Schools may increase minimally to manage new student member election procedures, but these costs are also expected to be absorbable. The Office of the Mayor of Baltimore City is responsible for staffing the task force using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, a temporary body tasked with studying governance issues and providing recommendations.
The bill alters the selection process and voting rights of student members within the Baltimore City Public School System, which falls under MSDE's oversight and leadership of local school systems.
The bill requires the established Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor, who oversees the executive branch and policy coordination.
The bill provides for Task Force members to be reimbursed for expenses according to state budget regulations, which are managed by DBM.

Synopsis: Providing that a resident of the State meets certain residency requirements for an applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Residency Requirements Ho. Co. 11-23
bill_summary: This bill modifies the residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Howard County, allowing any resident of the State of Maryland to qualify. It applies to applications made by individuals, partnerships, corporations, and limited liability companies, and also updates petition of support requirements.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Prospective alcoholic beverages license applicants in Howard County, Maryland residents, and the Howard County Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Howard County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state regulator for the alcohol industry. The bill explicitly references the Comptroller regarding the application forms required for alcoholic beverages licenses, which will need to reflect the new state-level residency requirements for Howard County.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Local boards of license commissioners are state-authorized bodies that manage alcoholic beverage licensing within their jurisdictions. The Howard County Board, which falls under this category, is directly responsible for implementing the changed residency requirements for license applicants.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its agencies, including those involved in industry regulation, and the Governor is responsible for signing the legislation into law.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions, including the Comptroller and local liquor boards, and may be called upon to provide guidance on the legal interpretation of these updated residency requirements.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority from issuing bonds beginning June 1, 2023; requiring the Department of Legislative Services to evaluate the Authority providing enough detail for the General Assembly to determine whether the Authority should continue in its current form; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority (NMWDA) from issuing new bonds starting June 1, 2023, and initiates a process to evaluate the authority for a potential merger into the Maryland Environmental Service (MES). The Department of Legislative Services (DLS) is required to conduct a formal evaluation and draft merger legislation by December 2024, while MES must analyze NMWDA's active contracts and personnel for assumption. MES is also directed to temporarily manage NMWDA's functions during any future transition or merger.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Legislative Services and Maryland Environmental Service
stakeholders: Employees of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority, and member jurisdictions including Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Frederick, Harford, Howard, and Montgomery counties and Baltimore City.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a $100,000 increase in State nonbudgeted expenditures and revenues in FY 2024 for the Maryland Environmental Service to hire consultants for the required review. Local expenditures for member jurisdictions are estimated to increase by approximately $100,000 in FY 2024/2025 to cover NMWDA legal, accounting, and staff costs associated with the evaluation. There is a potential for significant but currently indeterminate fiscal impacts starting in FY 2026 depending on the outcome of the merger evaluation and the assumption of contracts and employees by MES.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MES is the primary agency tasked with reviewing the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority's functions, employees, and contracts. It is also mandated to temporarily assume those aspects during any merger process.
The bill requires a specific evaluation of the impact of the Authority's discontinuation on the State Retirement and Pension System and the retirement benefits of the Authority's employees.

The bill terminates the bonding authority of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority, which directly impacts the Treasurer's role in overseeing state debt, bond issuance, and fiscal management.

As part of the Department of Legislative Services, OLA is responsible for the type of fiscal and performance evaluations mandated by the bill to assess the Authority's statutory compliance and efficiency.
The Authority's primary work involves waste disposal and waste-to-energy facilities, which are key areas regulated by MDE to ensure environmental protection and restoration.
The bill amends sections of the Natural Resources Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland, which provides the statutory framework for the Authority and the Maryland Environmental Service.
The bill requires a review of the Authority's procurement and contract awarding systems to determine if any conflicts of interest have been created.
DBM is responsible for state personnel policies and budget supervision, making it relevant to the evaluation of employee transfers and pension impacts associated with the Authority's transition.
OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and would be involved in the legal analysis of contract assumptions and the transfer of functions from the Authority to MES.
The Board oversees significant state procurements and contracts, which would be relevant if Authority contracts are transferred or if new financing arrangements are required.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and must approve any merger of the Authority into the Maryland Environmental Service.
The potential reassignment of the Authority's employees to another state entity involves labor relations and collective bargaining issues within PERB's jurisdiction.
The Authority operates waste-to-energy facilities, which produce electricity and steam; this aligns with MEA's mission to promote renewable energy and efficiency in Maryland.
PSC regulates electricity and energy generation; the waste-to-energy projects operated or contracted by the Authority fall under the broad scope of utility and energy regulation.
As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is relevant to the fiscal oversight and contract management transitions mandated by the bill.

bill_summary: This bill requires law enforcement officers of the Crisfield Police Department to participate in the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) if the department becomes a participating governmental unit. It allows current officers to transfer service credit from the Employees' Pension System to LEOPS and exempts them from having to personally pay the difference in contribution rates for their prior service, instead making the city responsible for the associated liabilities.
responsible_party: Crisfield Police Department and the State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Full-time law enforcement officers of the Crisfield Police Department and the City of Crisfield
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Local fiscal impact is contingent on the City of Crisfield electing to participate in LEOPS. If the city joins, its pension liabilities increase by $1,000,000, and total annual employer contributions increase by approximately $120,700. There is no material effect on other participating governmental units or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary entity responsible for the administration and management of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). This bill directly mandates the agency to manage new membership requirements, calculate service credit transfers, and oversee the transfer of assets and liabilities associated with the Crisfield Police Department's participation.

As the state's principal personnel and fiscal agency, DBM oversees the State Personnel and Pensions Article, which this bill amends. The agency is responsible for the policies regarding state employee benefits and the fiscal oversight of state-administered pension systems.

The Governor signed the bill into law (Chapter 72). The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for implementing the pension changes and coordinates policy initiatives regarding public safety personnel and their benefits.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Maryland State Retirement Agency. It would be involved in interpreting the statutory changes to the State Personnel and Pensions Article and ensuring the legal transfer of creditable service and assets complies with state law.

The State Treasurer acts as the principal custodian of state funds, including those within the pension systems, and holds a key leadership position on the board of the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and serves as a key member of the board overseeing the state's retirement and pension systems, ensuring the fiscal integrity of the revenue and fund transfers mentioned in the bill.

The OLA is responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of the State Retirement Agency. It will oversee and verify that the transfer of assets and crediting of service for Crisfield law enforcement officers are executed correctly in accordance with the law.

bill_summary: This bill expands the definition of a "crime of violence" to include sexual abuse of a minor when the offender is at least 21 years old and the victim is under 16. It also mandates that sentences for these offenders, as well as for adults convicted of second-degree sexual offenses as they were defined prior to October 2017, include a term of lifetime sexual offender supervision.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Adults convicted of sexual abuse of a minor or second-degree sexual offenses, victims of sexual abuse, and the Maryland Division of Parole and Probation.
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland state general fund expenditures are expected to increase minimally, primarily in the out-years, due to longer prison stays resulting from the expanded "crime of violence" definition and the requirements for lifetime sexual offender supervision. While the Office of the Public Defender estimated a need for 110101 dollars for a new attorney, the Department of Legislative Services anticipates a minimal impact because the bill applies to a relatively small population. Local government operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Judicial Branch, which is responsible for implementing the bill's sentencing changes and imposing special conditions for lifetime sexual offender supervision as required by the modified Criminal Procedure statutes.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for oversight of the state's budget and will monitor the fiscal impact of increased incarceration and supervision costs identified in the fiscal note.

The expansion of the 'crime of violence' definition triggers statutory restrictions that prevent courts from committing these offenders to the Department of Health for substance abuse treatment until they have become eligible for parole.

The bill specifically addresses lifetime sexual offender supervision requirements within the juvenile court system, impacting the agency's management of youth who meet the criteria for registration and long-term supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary agency impacted as it manages state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation, which is responsible for the lifetime sexual offender supervision mandated by the bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including the public safety and criminal justice strategies implemented through this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, directly relating to the bill's changes to sentencing and supervision policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for representing indigent defendants who will face these expanded 'crime of violence' charges and the mandatory lifetime supervision requirements.
As the chief legal officer, the OAG provides counsel to state agencies on the enforcement of the bill and represents the state in appeals related to these revised sexual offense laws.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to provide energy efficiency and conservation programs for low-income electricity customers, setting specific incremental energy savings targets for the 2024-2026 program cycle. It establishes the Green and Healthy Task Force to coordinate resources for low-income housing needs and mandates the creation of a plan to provide energy efficiency retrofits to all low-income households by 2031. The bill also sets specific labor requirements for contractors and requires a disparity study to evaluate the inclusion of minority- and women-owned businesses in the energy efficiency sector.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
stakeholders: Low-income households, Maryland electricity ratepayers, building owners and managers, and minority-, women-, and veteran-owned energy efficiency contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, DHCD special fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $39,800,000 in FY 2024, rising to approximately $214,200,000 by FY 2028 to meet the bill's energy savings targets. These costs are recovered through the EmPOWER Maryland surcharge on electricity bills, leading to a corresponding increase in special fund revenues. Local governments and small businesses may see increased electricity rates but can also benefit from additional program funding for weatherization and energy efficiency projects. The Maryland Energy Administration and the Maryland Department of Transportation may also incur minor additional costs for staffing and disparity studies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, DHCD is responsible for procuring energy efficiency and conservation programs for low-income customers, meeting specific energy savings targets, submitting detailed implementation plans to the PSC, and chairing/staffing the Green and Healthy Task Force.

The Commission is responsible for reviewing and approving DHCD's energy efficiency plans, coordinating funding and data sharing with electric companies, and including low-income program data in its annual report to the General Assembly.

MEA is consulted by the PSC on annual energy efficiency reports, manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (a designated funding source in the bill), and is mandated to apply for federal funding to support the bill's objectives.
The bill specifically requires DHCD to coordinate with DBM to identify additional state and federal funding sources to support the expansion of whole-home energy efficiency and maintenance programs.

Identified in the fiscal note as the primary certification agency designated by the Board of Public Works, MDOT is tasked with conducting a disparity study on energy efficiency services in collaboration with GOSBA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is mandated by Section 2 of the bill to initiate a study regarding energy efficiency and conservation services to evaluate the need for remedial measures for minority and women-owned businesses.
The OPC, which represents residential utility consumers, is a statutory member of the Green and Healthy Task Force established to coordinate resources for low-income housing energy needs.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is a statutory member of the Green and Healthy Task Force created by the bill to address low-income community housing and energy needs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Green and Healthy Task Force, a specialized body tasked with aligning resources and developing policy recommendations for low-income housing retrofits.
The OAG must be consulted during the disparity study regarding minority and women-owned business participation in the energy efficiency services market.
The BPW designates the certification agency (MDOT) tasked with the disparity study and oversees the regulatory framework for minority business participation impacted by the bill.
The Governor's Office receives the coordinated funding plan and the annual findings and recommendations from the Green and Healthy Task Force.

The Secretary of Health receives mandatory annual reports from the Green and Healthy Task Force regarding findings and recommendations for improving the health and energy efficiency of low-income housing.
The Secretary of the Environment receives mandatory annual reports from the Green and Healthy Task Force regarding recommendations for low-emissions and energy-efficient housing developments.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes licensed athletic trainers in Maryland to perform dry needling as a specialized task, provided they obtain approval from the State Board of Physicians by completing at least 80 hours of specialized instruction and hands-on training.
stakeholders: Licensed athletic trainers, Maryland athletes and patients receiving athletic training services, and the Maryland Board of Physicians.
