Special fund revenues may increase if the Maryland Board of Physicians establishes an application fee for dry needling approval. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physicians, which is a unit within the Maryland Department of Health, is the primary body responsible for approving licensed athletic trainers to perform dry needling and overseeing the required educational standards and disciplinary actions.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Physicians, and would assist in drafting regulations and representing the board in disciplinary proceedings related to the bill.

The fiscal note indicates a need for increased special fund expenditures for a contractual licensure analyst and licensure system modifications, which falls under the budget and personnel oversight responsibilities of DBM.

The bill establishes disciplinary protocols and potential licensure denial, suspension, or revocation; contested cases involving these administrative actions may be adjudicated by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Athletic Trainer Advisory Committee, which operates under the State Board of Physicians, is responsible for providing expert recommendations and annual reports regarding the practice of licensed athletic trainers, including the new specialized task of dry needling.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and signed this legislation into law. The office also manages appointments to the regulatory boards involved.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain assistant State's Attorney with knowledge of the case to meet with a victim of sexually assaultive behavior or the victim's representative within 20 days after receiving a request from the victim regarding a decision by the Office of the State's Attorney  not to file a charging document or to dismiss charges against an alleged suspect; requiring the assistant State's Attorney, at the meeting, to explain the justification for a certain decision; and establishing certain requirements for the meeting.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Victims of Sexually Assaultive Behavior
bill_summary: This bill requires an assistant State's Attorney to meet with a victim of sexually assaultive behavior, or their designated representative, within 20 days of a request if the Office of the State's Attorney decides not to file charges or to dismiss existing charges. During this meeting, which may be conducted in person, by phone, or by other agreed-upon means, the assistant State's Attorney must explain the justification for the decision not to proceed with the case.
stakeholders: Victims of sexually assaultive behavior and their designated representatives; Assistant State's Attorneys and local State's Attorneys' Offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's requirements do not materially affect State finances or operations. Local State's Attorneys' offices can implement the meeting requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no projected impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and victim services. This bill directly impacts victim rights and criminal justice policy, areas GOCPP manages through state and federal funding and policy development.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the state on criminal procedure and represents the state in criminal appeals. Legislative changes to victims' rights and prosecutorial requirements often require legal guidance and interpretation from this office.

The AOC provides operational and legal support to the judicial branch. Because the bill relates to criminal procedure and the rights of victims within the court system (including notifications and informational pamphlets mentioned in the fiscal note), the AOC is involved in the procedural implementation of these rights.

The bill's definition of 'sexually assaultive behavior' includes the sexual abuse of minors. DHS is the primary agency responsible for child protection and works closely with law enforcement and State's Attorneys on these specific cases.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigate cases of sexually assaultive behavior. The bill's requirement for prosecutors to explain why charges were not filed or were dismissed is directly linked to the investigative work performed by law enforcement.

Synopsis: Authorizing the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital and operating budget matters; requiring certain members of the county board and the executive leadership of the Baltimore County public school system to develop a certain draft curriculum for budget training for student members of the county board and submit the draft curriculum to the county board for review; and requiring each student member of the board to complete the budget training within 2 months of the student's election to the board.
Title: Baltimore County Board of Education - Student Member - Voting and Training

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital and operating budget matters, provided the member completes a specific budget training program. It requires the board and school system leadership to develop a training curriculum focusing on the budget process, which student members must complete within two months of their election to be eligible to vote on budgetary items.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of Education and the Baltimore County Public School System's Division of Business Services
stakeholders: Student members of the Baltimore County Board of Education and the Baltimore County Public School System.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no impact on State finances. Locally, the Baltimore County Public School System and the Baltimore County Board of Education can develop and facilitate the required budget training using existing resources. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signed this bill into law. It is responsible for the overall coordination of policy initiatives, including the legislative framework governing local school boards.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) provides leadership and oversight for the state's public education system. This bill amends the Education Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland to alter the voting authority and training requirements for a student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education, which falls under MSDE's general regulatory purview.

The Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) oversees state funding and allocations for local school capital projects. By authorizing the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital budget matters, the bill impacts the local decision-making process for project requests submitted to the IAC for state funding.

Synopsis: Designating Maryland Rye or Maryland Rye Whiskey as the State spirit.
Title: State Designations – State Spirit – Maryland Rye

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.

bill_summary: This bill designates Maryland Rye or Maryland Rye Whiskey as the official State spirit, recognizing Maryland's historical and contemporary significance in the production of rye whiskey and its impact on local agriculture.
stakeholders: Maryland distillers, rye farmers, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates that designating a State spirit does not materially affect State or local finances. No small business effect is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for government records and is specifically responsible for maintaining the official list of State Symbols of Maryland, as noted in the fiscal note.

The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of the state's official records, laws, and executive orders, and oversees the administration of the Great Seal of Maryland used for official state designations.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing bills into law, including the formalization of new state designations.
The bill's preamble specifically identifies rye as a locally grown cover crop and states that this designation highlights local agriculture and supports local spirits production.
The preamble notes that the distillery industry is growing and contributing to the economy and prominence of the State; the Department of Commerce promotes Maryland's economic assets.
Official state designations like a 'State spirit' are used in tourism marketing and branding to promote Maryland as a travel destination and highlight cultural assets.
The Comptroller regulates the alcohol and distilled spirits industry in Maryland, which is the industry directly affected by this symbolic designation.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time within which a person is required to file a Maryland estate tax return for the purpose of allowing a surviving spouse to take into account the deceased spousal unused exclusion amount to be consistent with the time for making a federal election; and applying the Act retroactively to any decedents dying on or after January 1, 2019.
Title: Maryland Estate Tax - Portability - Time Period for Election
bill_summary: This bill alters the time period within which a person must file a Maryland estate tax return to allow a surviving spouse to claim the deceased spousal unused exclusion (DSUE) amount, aligning the state's filing window with the federal election period (currently five years). The bill applies retroactively to the estates of decedents who died on or after January 1, 2019.
stakeholders: Surviving spouses and the estates of married decedents who died on or after January 1, 2019
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease starting in fiscal 2024 because the alignment with the longer federal filing deadline is expected to increase the number of individuals utilizing the DSUE election. The Comptroller's Office can handle administrative costs associated with updating forms and processing returns using existing resources. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for collecting estate taxes, processing returns, and adopting the regulations required by the bill to align state filing periods with federal law.
The bill explicitly requires the Register of Wills to certify the amount of inheritance tax paid to the Comptroller for decedents filing amended estate tax returns.
The bill is expected to decrease General Fund revenue, which the Department of Budget and Management manages and estimates as the state's principal fiscal agency.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Comptroller regarding the adoption of new regulations and the interpretation of tax law changes.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the agencies implementing the bill and signed the legislation into law.
The Maryland Tax Court may be required to adjudicate disputes or appeals arising from the Comptroller's decisions regarding estate tax filings and the DSUE election.

Synopsis: Altering eligibility for and the amount of a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for a taxpayer who adopts a child during the taxable year.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Adoption Expenses - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Adoption - see also- Parents and Guardians

bill_summary: This bill alters the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for adoption expenses by increasing the subtraction to a flat amount of $12,000 for a child with special needs and $10,000 for a child without special needs. It also removes the requirement that the child be a Maryland resident at the time of adoption to qualify for the full subtraction amount.
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers who adopt children
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $91,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024. One-time general fund expenditures are expected to increase by $43,000 in fiscal 2024 for tax system updates. Additionally, local income tax revenues are projected to decrease by $54,000 annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for tax collection and administration in Maryland. The bill directly alters subtraction modifications under the Maryland income tax, and the fiscal note explicitly states that the Comptroller's Office will incur expenditures to update tax systems for these changes.

The Department of Human Services (DHS) oversees public child welfare agencies in Maryland, which are specifically mentioned in the bill as entities through which eligible adoptions are made. DHS was also consulted in the development of the bill's fiscal note.
The bill has a measurable impact on Maryland's general fund revenues, which the Department of Budget and Management monitors as part of its responsibility for revenue estimation and fiscal planning.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, regarding the interpretation and implementation of changes to the Tax-General Article.

The Governor's Office for Children coordinates efforts to improve the well-being of Maryland's children and families. Increasing financial support for adoption aligns with the office's mission to support family stability and children's welfare.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the policy initiatives regarding family support and the overall state budget, both of which are affected by this tax alteration.

Synopsis: Authorizing a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification to an unlawfully restrictive covenant for a property within the boundaries of the county or municipality after providing persons with an ownership interest in the property with 30 days' written notice; and providing that persons with an ownership interest in property that is subject to an unlawfully restrictive covenant may decline action by a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification.
Title: Real Property - Unlawfully Restrictive Covenants - Modification by Counties or Municipalities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to identify and record modifications to property records to strike out unlawfully restrictive covenants based on race, religious belief, or national origin. Local governments must provide written notice to property owners at least 30 days before recording the modification, and owners may decline the action.
responsible_party: Maryland counties, municipalities, County Attorneys, and Clerks of the Circuit Court
stakeholders: Property owners with deeds containing unlawfully restrictive covenants and local government jurisdictions in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances. Local government impacts are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. No specific dollar estimates are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is directly responsible for providing the restrictive covenant modification intake sheet required by the bill and oversees the operations of the clerks of the circuit court who must process and record these modifications.

The bill addresses unlawfully restrictive covenants based on race, religious belief, or national origin, which directly relates to the commission's mission of enforcing anti-discrimination laws in housing.

The Maryland State Archives serves as the central depository for permanent government and judicial records, including the historical land records and recorded instruments that this bill seeks to modify.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and coordinating policy initiatives, including the implementation and enforcement of newly enacted real property and civil rights legislation.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Judiciary and all state agencies regarding the legal implications of new property laws and the enforcement of civil rights protections.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain employee or certain exclusive representative to initiate a grievance procedure under certain provisions of law; requiring certain decision makers in a grievance procedure in certain higher education systems to award certain damages under certain circumstances; requiring certain employee grievance procedures to include certain redress for certain violations; requiring the Secretary of Transportation to be consistent with certain provisions of law and include redress for certain violations; etc.
Title: State Personnel - Education and Transportation - Grievance Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill allows employees of the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) and public institutions of higher education to file grievances for unpaid wages or payroll reporting errors. It mandates the award of damages, which can reach up to three times the amount of the unpaid wages, and requires these agencies to align their grievance regulations with broader State personnel standards.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT), University System of Maryland (USM), Morgan State University (MSU), St. Mary's College of Maryland (SMCM), Baltimore City Community College (BCCC), and the Central Payroll Bureau.
stakeholders: State employees in the transportation and higher education sectors and their exclusive bargaining representatives.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund and higher education funds are expected to increase to cover potential damages and grievance costs. The Fiscal Note states that the exact financial impact is indeterminate but anticipated to be minimal. Additionally, the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) will see increased reimbursable revenues and expenditures, with costs estimated at $4,556 per case.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Central Payroll Bureau (CPB), which is housed within the Office of the Comptroller, is responsible for the payment of wages to employees across the state agencies and higher education institutions affected by this bill. The bill specifically addresses the reporting of payroll information to the CPB and the awarding of damages based on that reporting.

DBM is the principal personnel agency for the State and oversees the State Personnel Management System. The bill modifies grievance procedures and wage payment rights that align with policies managed by DBM, and the agency provided fiscal estimates for the impact on the Office of Administrative Hearings.

The bill explicitly amends the Transportation Article to require the Secretary of Transportation to adopt regulations regarding grievance procedures for payroll violations and damages, impacting MDOT's independent personnel system.
The bill specifically amends the Education Article (Title 14) pertaining to Morgan State University, requiring its grievance procedures to include redress and damages for wage withholding violations.

The bill explicitly applies to the University System of Maryland, amending the definition of a grievance and requiring decision makers in USM grievance procedures to award damages for payroll violations.
The bill specifically amends the Education Article (§ 14-408) to require Saint Mary's College's personnel system to include redress and damages for payroll-related grievance violations.

The OAH is responsible for adjudicating third-level grievance appeals for state employees. The bill increases the potential scope of these hearings and will result in increased reimbursable expenditures and revenues for the agency as cases are referred for adjudication.

The PERB (which now encompasses the former State Higher Education Labor Relations Board and State Labor Relations Board) is responsible for overseeing collective bargaining and labor relations. The bill specifically empowers 'exclusive representatives' to initiate grievances on behalf of employees, which falls under PERB's jurisdiction over public sector labor disputes.

The OAG serves as the legal representative for the state agencies and higher education institutions named in the bill. They would be involved in defending agencies in grievance proceedings and providing legal interpretation of the new requirements for damages and payroll reporting.

As the coordinating board for postsecondary education, the Commission is relevant to policies affecting the personnel and grievance systems of the state's public universities and colleges, including Baltimore City Community College (referenced in the bill text).

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Board of Education from issuing a certificate of approval to noncollegiate educational institutions that do not have a policy prohibiting the administration of corporal punishment; requiring regulations adopted by the State Board for the registration of family child care homes and large family child care homes and the licensing and operation of child care centers to prohibit corporal punishment; and requiring the State Board to identify certain methods in a certain overall plan.
Title: Nonpublic Schools and Child Care Providers - Corporal Punishment - Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits corporal punishment in nonpublic schools and child care settings in Maryland. It requires the State Board of Education to deny certification to nonpublic educational institutions that do not have a policy prohibiting staff from using corporal punishment and mandates that regulations for child care homes and centers explicitly forbid its use.
stakeholders: Nonpublic school students, children in family child care homes and child care centers, nonpublic school employees, and child care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland State Department of Education and the State Board of Education can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the State Board of Education are the primary entities responsible for implementing the bill. The bill requires the State Board to develop a plan to eliminate corporal punishment, update regulations for child care providers, and manage the certification process for nonpublic schools based on their corporal punishment policies.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Education and MSDE. It will be responsible for reviewing the new regulations and ensuring that the certification requirements for nonpublic schools comply with state and federal law.

The Office of Administrative Hearings would be responsible for adjudicating contested cases if a nonpublic school's certificate of approval is denied or a child care provider's registration is revoked due to violations of the corporal punishment policies established under the bill.

The Governor's Office for Children coordinates policies dedicated to the well-being and safety of Maryland's children. This bill's focus on eliminating corporal punishment in educational and care settings aligns with the office's mission to improve support networks and services for children.

The bill mandates that noncollegiate institutions (nonpublic schools) without a certificate of approval may not receive State funds. As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for managing state payments and ensuring that institutions ineligible for funding do not receive state disbursements.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including MSDE, and is responsible for the final approval and signing of the bill. The office also coordinates the broad policy initiatives related to child welfare and education represented in this legislation.

Synopsis: Providing for the stable funding and support of trauma-informed, high-quality programs and services for victims of crime; requiring the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to help support certain programs providing services for victims of crime; requiring the Office to consult with certain individuals and organizations regarding the allocation of certain funding; and requiring the Governor to include certain funding in the State budget.
Title: Victim Services Programs – Supplementing Federal Funding and Support (Victim Services Stabilization Act)

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crime Prev., Youth, and Victim Service, Governor's Office of
Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Elder Abuse and Neglect -see also- Vulnerable Adults
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Trauma Informed Approach -see also- Mental&Behavioral Health

bill_summary: The Victim Services Stabilization Act ensures consistent funding for crime victim services by requiring the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual budget that, when combined with federal Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) funding from the prior year, totals $60,000,000. The bill mandates the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (GOCPYVS) to support programs providing trauma-informed services to victims of crime and to award grants to public or private nonprofit organizations for this purpose.
responsible_party: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (GOCPYVS)
stakeholders: Victims of crime in Maryland, public and private nonprofit victim services organizations, State's Attorneys' offices, health care providers, and legal services organizations assisting victims.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a mandated appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2025, ensuring that the total of State funds and federal Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) funds from the prior year equals $60,000,000. According to the fiscal note, while the fiscal 2024 budget already included $35,000,000 in general funds for victim assistance, this bill requires the State to increase general fund expenditures if federal VOCA funding decreases to ensure the $60,000,000 aggregate total is met. Local government revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names this agency (under its prior name Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) as the primary entity responsible for supporting victim services programs, awarding grants, consulting with stakeholders, and submitting annual reports on the funding and grantees.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific appropriation in the annual budget bill that, when combined with federal VOCA funds, totals $60 million for victim services programs.

As the agency responsible for developing the state's budget and supervising budget execution, DBM must ensure the mandated $60 million aggregate appropriation is correctly integrated into the annual budget process starting in FY 2025.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG will likely provide legal counsel to the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy regarding grant administration, compliance with state/federal regulations, and the interpretation of the new Victim Services Stabilization Act.
The Treasurer's Office manages and protects state funds and property. The establishment of a $60 million mandated funding pool involves the management and distribution of significant state revenues.

The Comptroller functions as the state's chief financial officer and pays state bills and employees. This agency will be involved in the financial reporting and disbursement of the $60 million in victim services funding.

OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance audits. The distribution of $60 million in state and federal funds will be subject to their oversight and auditing procedures to ensure financial accountability.

The bill requires consultation with health care providers assisting victims of crime. MDH regulates health care professionals and facilities and manages public health services, making them a relevant stakeholder in trauma-informed victim services.

DHS is the primary social service provider and handles cases of child abuse and neglect. The bill specifically focuses on services for survivors of child abuse and requires coordination with organizations serving these populations.

The bill mandates consultation with organizations providing services to survivors of elder abuse. The Department of Aging oversees programs and advocacy for older adults and handles rights protection, making them relevant to the stabilization of services for this population.

Synopsis: Increasing the membership of the Wildlife Advisory Commission; requiring the Governor to appoint a member to the Wildlife Advisory Commission who is an academic researcher with expertise in wildlife biology, wildlife conservation, wildlife management, or ecology; and requiring the membership of the Commission to include representation from the farming, hunting, wildlife preservation, and passive wildlife recreation communities.
Title: Natural Resources - Wildlife Advisory Commission - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds

bill_summary: This bill increases the membership of the Wildlife Advisory Commission from nine to 10 members. It requires the Governor to appoint one member who is an academic researcher with expertise in wildlife biology, conservation, management, or ecology. Additionally, the bill mandates that the commission's membership include representation from the farming, hunting or fishing, wildlife preservation, and passive wildlife recreation communities.
stakeholders: Academic researchers, farmers, hunters, fishers, wildlife preservationists, and passive wildlife recreationists.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State finances and has no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Wildlife Advisory Commission is a body within the Department of Natural Resources. The bill directly increases its membership and changes the stakeholder representation requirements for the commission, which provides advice on wildlife management and conservation within the department's jurisdiction.

The Governor is the appointing authority for the members of the Wildlife Advisory Commission. The bill mandates the appointment of a tenth member with specific academic credentials and dictates the stakeholder composition for the commission's membership.

As the office that assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards and commissions, the Office of Appointments will be responsible for identifying and recommending an academic researcher and representatives from the specified stakeholder communities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Wildlife Advisory Commission is an advisory body within the executive branch. This legislation directly modifies its statutory membership, term structures, and specific representation requirements.

The bill mandates that the farming community be represented on the Wildlife Advisory Commission, which is relevant to the department's mission of promoting the economic viability of farming and agribusiness in relation to wildlife management.

Synopsis: Clarifying the language of provisions of law requiring the expungement of certain records maintained by the State or a political subdivision of the State relating to the charging of certain offenses under certain circumstances and notification of a certain right to expungement.
Title: Automatic Expungement - Clarification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill clarifies the statutory language regarding the automatic expungement of records for certain civil and criminal offenses. It specifies that automatic expungement after three years applies to civil offenses involving possession of cannabis and crimes other than Transportation Article violations for which a defendant is not required to appear, provided the disposition was acquittal, dismissal, not guilty, or nolle prosequi (except for those requiring drug or alcohol treatment).
stakeholders: Individuals with records of specific civil cannabis offenses or non-must-appear crimes; Maryland State and local law enforcement agencies; Maryland Judiciary
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as it clarifies existing law and rearranges statutory language without substantively changing state activities or operations. The Judiciary advises that the bill does not have a fiscal or operational impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) oversees the judicial operations and court records for the State of Maryland. The bill explicitly tasks the court with sending notices of dispositions and required expungement dates to several parties, including the Central Repository and law enforcement units.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages the Criminal Justice Information System's Central Repository, which is the primary recipient of the expungement notices generated by the courts. The department is responsible for ensuring that criminal records are expunged in accordance with the law.

As a primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police maintains police records that are subject to the automatic expungement requirements outlined in the bill. They are also a recipient of the disposition notices from the court.

The bill clarifies specific exemptions and inclusions for violations of the Transportation Article. MDOT, specifically through the Motor Vehicle Administration, maintains records regarding these violations and is identified as an information source for the legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent clients who are the primary beneficiaries of automatic expungement laws. They have a direct interest in the legal clarification of which records qualify for expungement without the need for a formal petition.
The OAG serves as the legal counsel for state agencies, including law enforcement and the judiciary, and is involved in the interpretation and enforcement of state criminal procedure laws.

The bill includes exceptions for cases involving drug or alcohol treatment, which is administered and overseen by the Maryland Department of Health. The department was also consulted as an information source for the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain persons subject to campaign finance regulation from making or accepting monetary contributions or monetary donations using any currency other than United States currency; prohibiting a campaign finance entity or a person acting on behalf of a campaign finance entity from making a monetary expenditure using any currency other than United States currency; authorizing the State Administrator of Elections or the Administrator's designee to investigate certain potential violations of the Act; etc.
Title: Currency - Campaign Finance Prohibitions - Disclosures by Financial Institutions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill prohibits campaign finance entities and persons involved in independent expenditures or electioneering communications from making or accepting contributions, donations, or expenditures using any currency other than United States currency, such as cryptocurrency. It grants the State Administrator of Elections the authority to investigate violations and issue subpoenas, and it expands the Comptroller's authority to include virtual currency money transmitters under the definition of financial institutions for the purpose of enforcing tax laws and satisfying tax liens.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Campaign finance entities, political candidates, donors, persons making independent expenditures or electioneering communications, and virtual currency money transmitters.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund revenues may increase starting in fiscal 2024 due to the collection of tax liens from virtual currency accounts and the imposition of penalties for campaign finance violations. Civil penalties are set at up to $1,000 per violation, and criminal fines can reach up to $25,000; however, the total fiscal impact is indeterminate as it depends on the number of violations and recoverable assets. The State Board of Elections and the Comptroller are expected to manage the bill's requirements using existing resources. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Board of Elections by prohibiting campaign finance entities from using non-U.S. currency (cryptocurrency) and granting the State Administrator of Elections new investigative and subpoena powers to enforce these regulations.

The bill expands the Comptroller's tax enforcement authority by redefining 'financial institution' to include virtual currency money transmitters, allowing the Comptroller to request information and seize property for tax liens.

The bill authorizes the State Board of Elections to refer potential willful and knowlingly violations of the campaign finance prohibitions to the State Prosecutor for criminal investigation and prosecution.

The bill pertains to virtual currency money transmitters regulated under Title 12 of the Financial Institutions Article, which falls under the regulatory purview of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and the Comptroller regarding the implementation and enforcement of the new prohibitions and authorities granted by the bill.

The bill grants the State Administrator of Elections subpoena power and stipulates that circuit courts may compel compliance. It also requires that filings regarding these subpoenas be sealed, affecting court administrative procedures.

As the primary fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for oversight of the general and special fund revenue increases projected from tax lien collections and campaign finance penalties mentioned in the fiscal note.

The Treasurer manages state funds, including the Fair Campaign Financing Fund, which the fiscal note indicates may receive increased revenue from the civil or criminal penalties established by the bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (such as SBE and the Comptroller) implementing this law and is responsible for appointing members to the State Board of Elections.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to stay the entering of a conviction, defer further proceedings, and place a certain defendant on probation subject to reasonable conditions if the court finds facts justifying a finding of guilt; authorizing the State and a certain defendant to enter into a probation agreement under certain circumstances; providing that the entry of a probation agreement under the Act shall be considered a probation before judgment for all other purposes under State law; etc.
Title: Probation Before Judgment - Probation Agreements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill authorizes a court to stay the entering of a conviction and place a defendant on probation before judgment if the defendant pleads not guilty and the court finds facts justifying a finding of guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. It establishes a framework for a probation agreement between the State and the defendant where the defendant accepts probation without admitting guilt, effectively creating a path for probation before judgment that avoids certain federal immigration consequences associated with traditional guilty pleas or findings of guilt.
responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Criminal defendants, non-citizen residents, State's Attorneys, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $33,400 in fiscal 2024 only to account for necessary programming changes. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect local finances or other State operations or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) is directly named in the bill and tasked with maintaining a list of approved treatment programs and notifying judges. The fiscal note also identifies a $33,400 expenditure for the Judiciary to implement necessary programming changes.

The bill requires defendants in specific cases (DUI/Drug offenses) to participate in treatment programs approved by the Maryland Department of Health. The department is responsible for the review, approval, and monitoring of these programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the legal options for defendants, allowing for probation agreements that avoid traditional findings of guilt. As the primary provider of legal representation for indigent defendants, the Office of the Public Defender is significantly impacted by changes to plea procedures and sentencing options.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees the Division of Parole and Probation, which is responsible for the supervision of defendants placed on probation. The bill's expansion of probation before judgment (PBJ) agreements directly impacts their supervisory operations and home detention programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's primary coordinating body for criminal justice policy. This bill introduces a significant change in criminal procedure regarding probation agreements, falling directly within their policy and strategic oversight role.

The bill specifically references probation procedures for violations of the Transportation Article (DUI/DWI). The MVA is responsible for maintaining driving records and managing license sanctions based on these court dispositions.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to the implementing agencies (MDH, AOC) and represents the state in appeals. The bill's provisions regarding the waiver of appeal rights for these agreements are of direct legal interest to the OAG.

Synopsis: Authorizing the creation of a State Debt in the amount of $1,218,639,000, the proceeds to be used for certain necessary building, construction, demolition, planning, renovation, conversion, replacement, and capital equipment purchases of the State, for acquiring certain real estate in connection therewith, and for grants to certain subdivisions and other organizations for certain development and improvement purposes; etc.
Title: Creation of a State Debt – Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2023, and the Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loans of 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2022
bill_summary: The Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2023 authorizes the creation of State Debt through the issuance of general obligation bonds to fund capital improvements. These funds are used for the planning, construction, renovation, and equipping of State-owned facilities, as well as providing grants to local governments and nonprofit organizations for various community, educational, and historical projects. The bill also amends previous capital bond acts from 2011 through 2022 and provides preauthorizations for capital debt in 2024, 2025, and 2026.
stakeholders: Maryland state agencies and departments, local governments, nonprofit organizations, public and nonpublic schools, community colleges, and higher education institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill authorizes $1,218,639,000 in State Debt for fiscal year 2024, though net new debt is limited to $1,205,000,000 after accounting for $13,639,000 in reductions to prior authorizations. Additionally, it provides $29,100,000 in bond premium proceeds. The act also sets preauthorizations for future debt: $629,689,000 for 2024; $239,789,000 for 2025; and $32,307,000 for 2026. Debt service is funded by an annual tax on all assessable property in the State.

Synopsis: Authorizing or altering the distribution of certain revenue; repealing a certain required appropriation to the Revenue Stabilization Account; altering the areas in which certain faculty must specialize to be assigned to provide clinical care at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center; reducing the budgeted Medicaid Deficit Assessment for fiscal year 2024; etc.

bill_summary: The Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2023 executes actions to provide mandate relief, contain costs, change the use of special funds, and swap funds in the fiscal 2024 Maryland operating budget. Key provisions include altering the specialization requirements for faculty at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center, reducing the Medicaid Deficit Assessment for fiscal year 2024, repealing certain repayment requirements for the Local Reserve Account, and transferring $500,000,000 from the Revenue Stabilization Account to the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund.

stakeholders: State agencies, Maryland hospitals, homeowners receiving property tax credits, recipients of Department of Human Services assistance payments, and natural gas customers in the Washington Gas service territory.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, general fund expenditures increase by $49,500,000 in FY 2024 and decrease by $500,500,000 in FY 2027. Special fund revenues decrease by $50,000,000 in FY 2024, and special fund expenditures decrease by $40,800,000 in FY 2024. The bill also reduces the FY 2023 general fund appropriation for the Assistance Payments Program within the Department of Human Services by $7,500,000.

Synopsis: Altering the eligibility requirements for the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program and publicly funded prekindergarten programs to include certain operational requirements, staff credentials, and student-to-staff ratios; requiring Montessori schools and programs to maintain a student-to-classroom personnel ratio of no more than 10 to 1, with a maximum of 20 students if all the students are under the age of 5 years; requiring a classroom teacher to hold a bachelor's degree and be certified by certain organizations; etc.
Title: Early Childhood Education - Prekindergarten Programs - Montessori Schools and Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Primary Schools -see also- Education; Private or Public Sch.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the eligibility criteria for Montessori schools and programs to participate in the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program and other publicly funded prekindergarten initiatives. It establishes specific requirements for staff credentials, requiring teachers to hold a bachelor's degree and a recognized Montessori credential, and sets unique student-to-staff ratios and classroom size limits tailored to the Montessori educational model.
stakeholders: Montessori schools and programs, prekindergarten students and their families, and the Maryland State Department of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates there is no anticipated material impact on State or local funding. While the bill alters eligibility requirements for Montessori schools and programs, it is not expected to change the overall levels of State or local expenditures or revenues. Montessori programs that are small businesses may benefit from the specific eligibility requirements established by the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the state budget and the execution of funding for the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program, which this bill modifies.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions governing the issuance of stock, convertible securities, and scrip; clarifying the authority of corporations to hold annual meetings by remote communication; clarifying the application of certain provisions of law to the conversion of a corporation; requiring a real estate investment trust that voluntarily dissolves to file a notice of termination with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation; etc.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

bill_summary: This bill makes several technical and administrative revisions to Maryland's Corporations and Associations laws. Key provisions include prohibiting the issuance of stock, scrip, or limited liability company membership certificates in bearer form; clarifying that stockholder meetings can be held partially or entirely by remote communication; and requiring Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) to file a formal notice of termination with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation when undergoing voluntary dissolution. It also allows nonstock corporations to include ex officio directors in their charter or bylaws and applies the Maryland Control Share Acquisition Act to certain statutory trusts.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
stakeholders: Maryland corporations, stockholders, limited liability company (LLC) members, nonstock corporation directors, and Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) trustees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. While the bill introduces new filing requirements for REIT dissolutions and modifies various corporate governance procedures, these changes are largely technical and are not expected to result in significant changes to revenue or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly grants the Attorney General the authority to institute proceedings to dissolve a real estate investment trust (REIT) that has abused or misused its powers. Additionally, the Office of the Attorney General's Securities Division is listed as a primary information source for the fiscal note, reflecting its interest in provisions related to the issuance of stock and convertible securities.

The bill makes significant revisions to the Corporations and Associations Article, which governs the legal structure and operations of businesses in Maryland. These provisions, including those related to remote meetings, stock issuance, and REIT dissolution, are subject to judicial interpretation and enforcement in state courts. The bill also specifies the venue for judicial proceedings regarding REIT dissolutions.

As the chief executive, the Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (such as the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, though not on this list) that implement corporate filing requirements. The Governor also signed this bill into law.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Commission on Public Health to make recommendations for improving the delivery of foundational public health services in Maryland. The Commission is tasked with assessing the capabilities of the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments in areas such as communicable disease control, chronic disease prevention, and emergency preparedness. It requires the Commission to submit an interim report by December 2023 and a final report by December 2024.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, the Maryland Department of Health, local health departments, State academic institutions, and public health professionals.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no fiscal impact in FY 2023. Any impact on the Maryland Department of Health and other State agencies can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. Higher education expenditures for State academic institutions providing staff support to the Commission may increase in FY 2024 and 2025, but specific dollar estimates are unavailable. Local health departments can absorb any impact within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary subject of the commission's assessment and foundational public health capability review. Furthermore, three senior MDH officials—the Deputy Secretary for Public Health, the Deputy Secretary for Behavioral Health, and the Director of the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities—are designated members of the Commission.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission is a statutory member of the new Commission on Public Health, and the commission is explicitly required to consult with the MHCC in performing its duties.

The Executive Director of the Health Services Cost Review Commission is a member of the Commission on Public Health, and the bill requires the Commission to consult with the HSCRC to inform its recommendations for public health reform.

The bill requires a faculty member from a public health program at an HBCU (such as Morgan State) to co-chair the commission. Additionally, the academic institutions represented by the co-chairs are mandated to provide the primary staff support for the commission's work.

The commission must include representatives from State academic institutions with public health expertise to serve as co-chairs. These institutions (typically USM members like UMB or UMCP) are required to provide the staff support necessary for the commission to function and conduct its assessment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill creates a new Commission on Public Health, which falls under this category of temporary or permanent bodies established to study and make recommendations on specific government policy issues.

The bill explicitly requires the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Department of Budget and Management while performing its duties and making recommendations for reform in public health funding and organization.
The commission is mandated by the bill to consult with the Department of General Services to assist in its assessment of foundational public health capabilities and organizational reforms.

The commission is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Disabilities to ensure that recommendations for the delivery of foundational public health services account for the needs of individuals with disabilities.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several specific members to the commission, including local health officers and public health experts, and receives the commission's interim and final reports.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment and vetting of the diverse set of stakeholders required to be appointed to the commission, including local health officers and members of the public with specialized expertise.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state agencies involved in the commission and would likely provide legal guidance to the newly created commission regarding its regulatory and statutory duties.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a landlord from using a lease or form of lease that contains a provision that limits a tenant's ability to summon, or penalizes a tenant or another individual solely for summoning, the assistance of law enforcement or emergency services; prohibiting a landlord from taking certain retaliatory actions because a tenant or another individual summons the assistance of law enforcement or emergency services for certain purposes; prohibiting a local jurisdiction from enacting certain laws; etc.
Title: Real Property - Limitations on Summoning Law Enforcement or Emergency Services - Prohibition

Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
