Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: This bill prohibits landlords from including lease provisions that limit or penalize tenants for summoning law enforcement or emergency services and forbids retaliatory actions, such as evictions or rent increases, for such calls. Additionally, it prohibits local jurisdictions from enacting ordinances that use emergency call thresholds to designate properties as nuisances or penalize residents and owners for seeking emergency assistance.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and local governing bodies of counties and municipalities
stakeholders: Residential tenants, landlords, property owners, and local government authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the impact is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new affirmative defenses and claims for damages that must be adjudicated in court. It also provides for specific judicial remedies, including the awarding of damages, attorney's fees, and the reinstatement of rental licenses, directly impacting court proceedings and the Judicial Branch.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division often handles disputes related to landlord-tenant law. Additionally, as the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to agencies regarding the enforcement of real property laws and the impact of the bill on local jurisdictions.

As the primary agency for ensuring safe and secure housing, DHCD is impacted by policies that regulate residential leases and prevent retaliatory actions against tenants, which are intended to preserve housing stability and community vitality.

The bill specifically defines 'emergency services' to include mobile crisis teams as defined in the Health - General Article. The Department of Health oversees these behavioral health units and public health services that tenants may be summoning.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are one of the core entities whose assistance tenants are explicitly protected in summoning under this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office advises on public safety strategies and manages funds for law enforcement and victim services. This bill impacts public safety coordination by ensuring residents can contact law enforcement without fear of housing-related penalties.

Individuals with disabilities may rely more frequently on emergency medical services or mobile crisis teams; this bill protects their right to access these services without risking their housing or facing nuisance designations.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that an application for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County include certain petitions of support signed by at least three residents who are owners of real property and registered voters in the district where the business is to be conducted.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages - Repeal of Petition of Support Requirement Ho. Co. 12-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement that applicants for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County include a petition of support signed by at least three local property owners and registered voters. It also preserves the ability of the Howard County Board of License Commissioners to waive county residency requirements for certain license applicants, such as purchasers of existing businesses or those who have owned the premises for at least two years.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Applicants for alcoholic beverages licenses in Howard County and the Howard County Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal impact on State or local government. Howard County can implement the changes to the license application process using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal regulator for the alcohol industry. As this bill amends the 'Alcoholic Beverages' Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland, it falls under the broad regulatory subject matter overseen by this agency, even though the primary impact is on local licensing procedures in Howard County.
The Governor's Office is responsible for overseen the executive branch and has the constitutional authority to sign bills into law, as occurred with House Bill 218.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the State of Maryland, including the interpretation and enforcement of laws regarding alcoholic beverages and local government authority.

Synopsis: Requiring the St. Mary's County Board of County Commissioners to produce a report recommending and describing the areas of St. Mary's County that the County Board considers appropriate for the operation of unregistered golf carts on public highways, subject to certain standards; and requiring the County Board to submit the report to certain committees of the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
Title: St. Mary's County - Golf Carts on Public Highways - Report

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the St. Mary’s County Board of County Commissioners to study and produce a report recommending specific areas in the county suitable for the operation of unregistered golf carts on public highways. The report must include detailed maps and consider factors such as geographic isolation, proximity to docking facilities, tourism viability, and road speed limits. The final report must be submitted to the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: St. Mary’s County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Residents and visitors of St. Mary's County, and the St. Mary's County Board of County Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. St. Mary’s County can produce and submit the required report using existing resources, and no changes to state or local revenues are expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is relevant as the administrative support for the Governor, who signed this bill into law and oversees the executive branch's adherence to state legislative reporting requirements.

The bill requires a report concerning the operation of vehicles on public highways and potential exceptions to registration requirements, which falls under the broad policy and operational oversight of MDOT.

The MVA is responsible for vehicle registration and driver licensing. Although this bill only mandates a study, the subject matter—unregistered golf carts and driver's license requirements—directly impacts the regulations and laws administered by the MVA.

The bill's criteria for suitable golf cart areas include the presence or absence of State highways and specific speed limits (under 30 mph), both of which are under the jurisdiction and management of the SHA.

The criteria for the required report emphasize the viability of areas as destinations for the boating public and their inclusion in a network of tourist attractions, which aligns with the mission of the Office of Tourism Development.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "person in a position of authority" applicable to sexual offense in the fourth degree; altering a certain prohibition against a certain person in a position of authority engaging in certain conduct to prohibit a person in a position of authority from engaging in a sexual act, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with a minor who is enrolled at a school or participating in a certain program for which the person in authority works; authorizing the imposition of a certain sentence;  etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Person in a Position of Authority - Sexual Offenses With a Minor

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill expands the legal definition of a 'person in a position of authority' to include individuals aged 21 or 22 and older who work or volunteer for schools or various youth-oriented programs, such as sports, arts, tutoring, and religious activities. It prohibits these individuals from engaging in sexual acts, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with minors participating in those programs. Additionally, the bill specifies that these offenses are not considered lesser included crimes of other offenses unless specifically charged and allows for sentences to be served consecutively or concurrently with other crimes based on the same act.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and local State's Attorneys' offices
stakeholders: Minors enrolled in schools or youth programs, and adults who work or volunteer in supervisory or instructional roles within those schools and programs
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. According to the Fiscal Note, there will be a minimal increase in State general fund revenues from fines and a minimal increase in expenditures due to incarceration costs. Local revenues and expenditures are also projected to increase minimally. Misdemeanor convictions for fourth-degree sexual offenses carry a fine of up to $1,000 and/or imprisonment for up to one year, or up to three years for subsequent offenders.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the executive authority over state agencies, the Governor's Office oversees the units of government whose employees, contractors, and volunteers are newly defined as 'persons in a position of authority' subject to the bill's criminal prohibitions.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding the interpretation and application of the revised criminal statutes and represents the state in appeals related to these offenses.

The department oversees programs like 4-H and other agricultural activities involving minors; its employees and volunteers in these programs will be classified as 'persons in a position of authority' under the bill.

As the central personnel agency, DBM is responsible for state employee policies; the bill expands criminal liability for state employees who interact with minors as 'persons in a position of authority.'

MSDE oversees public schools, preschools, and secondary schools, which are primary environments addressed by the bill's expanded definitions of 'persons in a position of authority' and prohibited conduct.
MDH regulates child care facilities and operates various health programs and facilities that serve or supervise minors, making its staff subject to the bill's requirements.

DHS oversees child care facilities, after-school care, and other social service programs for minors, all of which fall under the bill's expanded definition of 'programs' where authority figures are restricted.
DJS staff work directly with minors in residential and community-based settings; they are specifically included as 'persons in a position of authority' within a state government unit.
DNR manages state parks and recreational programs that serve minors; its employees and volunteers in these settings are impacted by the new 'position of authority' definitions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the incarceration of individuals convicted under the bill's expanded criminal provisions, leading to a potential increase in inmate populations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI manages volunteer and service programs (e.g., Service Year Option) that may place participants in positions of authority over minors in schools or community programs.
The Guard operates youth-focused programs such as the Freestate ChalleNGe Academy, where staff and volunteers will be considered 'persons in a position of authority' under the bill.
As a state agency providing education to minors, its faculty, staff, and volunteers are directly affected by the bill's expanded protections and definitions for school environments.

The Judicial Branch is responsible for adjudicating the new criminal cases, managing the sentencing changes, and implementing the procedural requirements for subsequent offenders established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates state public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy, including the sexual offense statutes modified by this bill.
MCSS provides a coordinated approach to school safety and training; the bill's focus on school-based authority figures and minor safety is central to its mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD is responsible for defending indigent individuals charged with fourth-degree sexual offenses under the bill's expanded definitions, leading to a direct increase in caseload.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for investigating and enforcing the criminal laws regarding sexual offenses against minors.
The university hosts various instructional, sports, and enrichment programs for minors; staff and volunteers in these programs fall under the bill's expanded definition of authority figures.
USM institutions frequently operate summer camps, clinics, and outreach programs involving minors, making their employees and volunteers subject to the bill's criminal provisions.

Synopsis: Requiring the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to release certain personal information of a minor who has a work permit to employers and apprenticeship sponsors, educational programs and institutions, and local workforce development boards that have requested and have registered with the Maryland Department of Labor for the purpose of receiving the information, if a parent or legal guardian of the minor or the minor elects to allow the sharing of the information.
Title: Employment for Minors - Opportunities for Work

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to share the contact information (name, home address, and telephone number) of minors at least 16 years old who have work permits with registered employers, apprenticeship sponsors, educational institutions, and local workforce development boards, provided the minor or their parent or guardian explicitly opts in to allow the information sharing.
stakeholders: Minors at least 16 years old with work permits, their parents or guardians, employers, apprenticeship sponsors, educational programs and institutions, and local workforce development boards.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Labor can release the required information and adopt necessary regulations using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Commissioner of Labor and Industry (within the Maryland Department of Labor) to manage the release of minor work permit data, handle registrations of organizations seeking the data, and adopt necessary regulations to implement the opt-in process.

The bill explicitly includes local workforce development boards as authorized recipients of minor work permit data to facilitate information sharing with employers and apprenticeship sponsors. The GWDB is the primary body coordinating these boards and state workforce strategy.

The bill identifies educational programs and institutions as recipients of work permit data and specifically references county school systems in the context of work-study and student-learner programs, which fall under MSDE's oversight.

Postsecondary educational programs and institutions, which are overseen and regulated by the Maryland Higher Education Commission, are designated in the bill as entities eligible to register for and receive the work permit information of minors.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This department focuses on workforce pathways and service opportunities for recent high school graduates; access to work permit data for 16- and 17-year-olds aligns with their mission of developing the state's talent pipeline.

As the legal counsel for the Department of Labor and MSDE, the OAG would be involved in drafting and reviewing regulations regarding the privacy and legal implications of releasing the personal information of minors to third parties.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations on or before December 1, 2023, establishing requirements for the sale of new zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles in the State; defining a "heavy-duty vehicle" as one with a gross vehicle weight rating equal to or greater than 14,001 pounds; requiring the Department, in consultation with certain units of State government, to prepare and submit to the General Assembly a certain needs assessment and deployment plan by December 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Department of the Environment - Zero-Emission Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles - Regulations (Clean Trucks Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: The Clean Trucks Act of 2023 requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations by December 1, 2023, establishing sales requirements for new zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, incorporating California's Advanced Clean Trucks standards beginning with model year 2027. It also requires a comprehensive needs assessment and deployment plan, and increases mandated funding for the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to $10,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2024 through 2027.
stakeholders: Commercial and industrial vehicle owners and operators, truck manufacturers, electric utilities, and residents of overburdened or underserved communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates an annual appropriation of at least $10,000,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund for fiscal years 2025 through 2027 for zero-emission vehicle grants. In FY 2024, general fund expenditures increase by $474,200 for administrative and contractual costs at the Department of the Environment, while special fund expenditures increase by $5,250,000 for grant funding. Local governments and State agencies may face increased vehicle procurement costs but decreased long-term operating expenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the Clean Trucks Act of 2023. It is tasked with adopting regulations for zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, incorporating California's standards, and lead-authoring the required needs assessment and deployment plan.

The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) is mandated to administer the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program, oversee the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) appropriations adjusted by the bill, and serve as a primary consultant for the state's needs assessment and deployment plan.

The Department of Transportation (MDOT) is a key consultant for the needs assessment and deployment plan. It is directly impacted by the bill's requirements to assess the transition of the state's vehicle fleet and the infrastructure needed for zero-emission transit and trucking.

The Department of General Services (DGS) manages the state's vehicle fleet and real estate. It is named as a required consultant for the needs assessment, specifically regarding the timeline and feasibility of transitioning the state fleet and installing charging infrastructure at state facilities.

The Public Service Commission (PSC) is a named consultant required to assess the additional electrical capacity, transmission, and distribution demands resulting from the widespread adoption of zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles on the state's electric grid.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is responsible for state budget development and personnel. It is relevant due to the bill's mandated $10 million annual appropriation from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) and the fiscal impact on state personnel and fleet budgets.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which must include the specific mandatory appropriations for zero-emission vehicle grants required by the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to MDE and other agencies in developing the required regulations and ensuring they align with both state law and federal Clean Air Act requirements.

The Board of Public Works (BPW) approves significant state procurements and contracts. It will be relevant as state agencies transition their medium- and heavy-duty vehicle fleets to zero-emission models through new state-wide contracts.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works and regulates the motor fuel industry. The transition away from traditional fuels to electricity and hydrogen for heavy vehicles will impact state revenues and regulatory frameworks under the Comptroller's purview.

The State Treasurer's Office is a member of the Board of Public Works and manages state funds. The agency is relevant to the oversight of expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund and potential bond-funded infrastructure projects related to zero-emission vehicles.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the public education system, which utilizes a significant fleet of heavy-duty school buses. The transition to zero-emission vehicles and the availability of grant incentives directly impact local school system logistics and funding.

The Maryland Environmental Service (MES) operates heavy-duty equipment and vehicles for state and local government clients. As a major operator of such machinery, it is directly impacted by the new regulatory standards and potential grant opportunities for equipment upgrades.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office is relevant because the bill mandates that the Maryland Energy Administration give preference for grants to entities engaged in business activities that impact public health or infrastructure in overburdened or underserved communities.

Synopsis: Providing that the use of cannabis by a parent or certain other individuals who care for a child does not qualify as neglect except in certain circumstances for purposes of provisions of law relating to children in need of assistance.
Title: Child in Need of Assistance – Neglect – Cannabis Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: This bill modifies the legal definition of neglect in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) cases to clarify that a parent's or caregiver's use of cannabis does not, by itself, constitute neglect. Cannabis use only qualifies as neglect if it results in actual harm or creates a substantial risk of harm or mental injury to the child.
responsible_party: The Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Parents and legal guardians, children involved in CINA proceedings, and Maryland State courts.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services is the primary state agency responsible for child welfare and the protection of children from abuse and neglect. Since the bill narrows the definition of 'neglect' regarding cannabis use in Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) cases, it directly impacts the investigations, case management, and court petitions handled by local departments of social services.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article of the Maryland Code, specifically affecting the standards used by judges and magistrates in CINA proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational and legal support to the judicial branch which must implement these changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation to indigent parents and children in CINA proceedings. This bill changes the legal definition of neglect, which is a core element in the defense and advocacy work performed by this agency in family and juvenile courts.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Human Services, and represents the state in civil and criminal appeals. They would be responsible for interpreting and defending the new legal standard for neglect in court.

The Governor's Office for Children is focused on the well-being of Maryland's children and the coordination of support networks. This bill aligns with policy goals regarding child welfare and the prevention of unnecessary family separation or state intervention based solely on legal cannabis use.

As the independent agency overseeing the regulated cannabis industry, the Maryland Cannabis Administration has an interest in ensuring that the legal use of cannabis by adults is consistent with state laws regarding parental rights and family welfare.

The Department of Health oversees behavioral health and general health policy. The bill touches on the intersection of public health (cannabis use) and child safety, which may require coordination with the department regarding health-based standards for harm or risk.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to take disciplinary action against an applicant or a licensee for failing to comply with a Board order; authorizing the Board to grant a stay of enforcement of a Board order in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act; prohibiting a Board order from being stayed pending judicial review; authorizing the Board to reinstate a suspended or revoked license only in accordance with the terms and conditions of the order or an order of reinstatement issued by the Board; etc.
Title: State Board of Chiropractic Examiners - Disciplinary Actions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to take disciplinary actions against applicants or licensees who fail to comply with any board order. It also establishes that a board order may not be stayed pending judicial review, allows the board to appeal court decisions that reverse or modify its orders, and specifies the conditions under which a suspended or revoked license may be reinstated.
stakeholders: Chiropractic license applicants, licensed chiropractors, and chiropractic assistants.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not affected. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Chiropractic Examiners is a regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This bill directly expands the Board's disciplinary authority and modifies its procedures for stays of enforcement and license reinstatement.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for all state agencies, including health boards. The bill's provisions regarding judicial review, the authority of the Board to appeal court decisions, and legal stays of enforcement would be executed by the OAG.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies under the Administrative Procedure Act. Because this bill deals with disciplinary actions and stays of enforcement under that Act, OAH is relevant to the implementation of the board's disciplinary process.

The bill explicitly prohibits the staying of Board orders pending judicial review and authorizes the Board to appeal judicial decisions that reverse or modify its orders, directly affecting the workflow and procedural rules of the state's courts regarding these specific administrative appeals.

Synopsis: Prohibiting in all counties, rather than Baltimore City only, a holder of a certificate of sale from filing a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption for owner-occupied residential property until 9 months from the date of sale; prohibiting in all counties, rather than Baltimore City only, a certain notice from being sent to certain persons with an interest in owner-occupied residential property sold at tax sale until 7 months after the date of sale; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Owner-Occupied Property - Foreclosure, Notice, and Reimbursement of Expenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: This bill extends the timeframe for tax sale proceedings on owner-occupied residential properties statewide. It increases the waiting period before a holder of a certificate of sale can file a foreclosure complaint from six to nine months and delays the first required notice and expense reimbursement eligibility from four to seven months after the date of sale, applying standards previously unique to Baltimore City to all Maryland counties.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and local tax collectors
stakeholders: Owners of owner-occupied residential properties and holders of tax sale certificates
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances, as indicated in the Fiscal Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the legal timeline for filing complaints to foreclose the right of redemption in Maryland's court system, which the Administrative Office of the Courts supports operationally and technologically.

The bill addresses housing security and foreclosure prevention for owner-occupied residential properties, aligning with this agency's mission to ensure residents have access to secure and affordable housing.

As the primary social service provider, this agency serves residents in economic need; extending the timeline to redeem property in a tax sale helps prevent homelessness among the vulnerable populations they assist.
The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and enforces tax laws; the bill amends sections of the Tax-Property Article regarding the procedures for tax sales.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly on the interpretation of the Tax-Property Article and state laws regarding residential property rights.

The bill provides additional time for homeowners to redeem properties, which significantly impacts the quality of life and housing stability for older adults, a core advocacy focus for the Department of Aging.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives related to tax relief and housing stability, as reflected in the Governor's approval of the act.

Synopsis: Expressing the intent of the General Assembly that at least 2% of the balance in the Homeowner Protection Fund be spent each year to conduct outreach in a certain manner to homeowners in tax sale to encourage the homeowners to enroll in the Homeowner Protection Program; authorizing the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to conduct outreach using State employees and resources or to contract with a private vendor; requiring that certain State and local government agencies provide certain information to facilitate outreach efforts; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protection Program - Outreach

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to conduct outreach to homeowners whose properties have been sold at tax sale to encourage enrollment in the Homeowner Protection Program. The outreach must prioritize live telephone calls or other non-mail methods and is funded by the Homeowner Protection Fund, with a legislative intent that at least 2% of the fund's balance be used for this purpose annually.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman (State Department of Assessments and Taxation)
stakeholders: Homeowners in tax sale, the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, local tax collectors, and the Comptroller of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Homeowner Protection Fund are estimated to increase by $204,200 in FY 2024, followed by annual expenditures between approximately $187,100 and $202,100 through FY 2028. These costs cover the hiring of a coordinator, a call center vendor contract, and data programming. Special fund revenues may decrease starting in FY 2025 as outreach costs are not recoverable, unlike funds used to purchase liens. Local government fiscal impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Comptroller provide the telephone numbers of homeowners (from tax returns) to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman or its vendor to facilitate the outreach campaign. The Comptroller is also responsible for accounting for the Homeowner Protection Fund used to finance the program.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, which includes the State Tax Sale Ombudsman (housed within SDAT). Additionally, the bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations for the Homeowner Protection Fund in the annual budget bill.

The State Treasurer is responsible for holding the Homeowner Protection Fund separately and investing the money of the fund. This fund is the exclusive source of funding for the outreach campaign and program activities described in the bill.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for the oversight of budget execution for the Homeowner Protection Fund and would manage the personnel requirements for the additional staff position identified in the fiscal note to coordinate the outreach campaign.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state contracts and expenditures. The Ombudsman's authority to contract with a private vendor for a statewide outreach campaign would likely require approval or oversight from the Board.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Ombudsman and SDAT. The agency would likely be involved in reviewing the contract with the private vendor and ensuring compliance with privacy laws (such as Tax-General Article § 13-202) when sharing data.

The bill requires the Ombudsman to collaborate with social service providers to reach vulnerable homeowners. Older adults are a key demographic impacted by tax sales, and the Department of Aging provides housing assistance and long-term care advocacy that aligns with the program's goals.

The Department of Housing and Community Development is the state's lead agency for homeownership support and community revitalization. The bill specifically mentions referring homeowners to housing counseling, a core service provided or funded by this department.

DHS is the primary social service provider for Marylanders in economic need. The bill requires the Ombudsman to collaborate with social service agencies and refer homeowners to public benefits, which falls directly under DHS's operational scope.

The outreach campaign is timed to occur before a holder of a certificate of sale can file a complaint in court to foreclose the right of redemption. The AOC provides support for these judicial proceedings and is noted as a potential source of information for the Ombudsman.

Synopsis: Extending, until July 1, 2036, the termination date applicable to an exemption from the sales and use tax for certain construction material or warehousing equipment purchased for use in a certain target redevelopment area in Baltimore County.
Title: Sales and Use Tax Exemption - Redevelopment Areas in Baltimore County - Sunset Extension
bill_summary: This bill extends the expiration date of a sales and use tax exemption from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2036, for construction materials and warehousing equipment purchased for use in a specific target redevelopment area in Baltimore County, which includes property previously owned by the Bethlehem Steel Corporation.
stakeholders: Businesses and developers purchasing construction materials or warehousing equipment for use in the designated target redevelopment area in Baltimore County (the former Bethlehem Steel site).
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will continue to decrease through fiscal 2036 due to the extension of the tax exemption. The fiscal note indicates that the exact revenue decrease is indeterminate as it depends on the value of eligible purchases made within the redevelopment area. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for tax collection and administration in Maryland. The bill specifically requires that buyers provide vendors with evidence of eligibility for the sales and use tax exemption issued by the Comptroller.

As the state's primary economic development agency, Commerce is relevant because the bill extends a tax incentive designed to stimulate the redevelopment of a major industrial site (the former Bethlehem Steel plant) into a warehousing and distribution hub.

DBM is responsible for estimating revenues and overseeing the state budget. The fiscal note indicates that this bill will result in a continued decrease in general fund revenues through FY 2036, impacting DBM's fiscal planning.

The 'target redevelopment area' is explicitly defined by its participation in the Voluntary Cleanup Program under Title 7, Subtitle 5 of the Environment Article, which is overseen by the Maryland Department of the Environment.

MEDCO provides financing and real estate development services for industrial and economic prosperity projects. This bill impacts large-scale industrial redevelopment, which is central to MEDCO's mission.

The target redevelopment area (formerly Bethlehem Steel/Sparrows Point) is a critical maritime and logistics hub adjacent to the Port of Baltimore. The expansion of warehousing equipment and construction there directly impacts waterborne commerce and port-related activities.
The Treasurer manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works. The bill's impact on general fund revenue totals is relevant to the office's oversight of the state's fiscal health.

The Governor's Office oversees executive policy and state revenue priorities. The extension of this tax exemption is a legislative policy choice affecting the state's annual budget proposed by the Governor.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, the Maryland Tax Court would be the body responsible for hearing appeals if there were disputes regarding the eligibility or application of the sales and use tax exemption.

MDP promotes sustainable growth and land use planning. The redevelopment of a brownfield site like Sparrows Point into a productive warehousing area aligns with state planning visions for infrastructure development and community revitalization.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to grant a stay of enforcement of a Board order in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act; prohibiting an order of the Board from being stayed pending judicial review; authorizing the Board to appeal a decision that reverses or modifies its order; altering the grounds for disciplining massage therapists and procedures related to the discipline of massage therapists, including appeals procedures and reinstatement procedures; etc.
Title: Massage Therapy - Discipline

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Massage Therapy Act by modifying disciplinary grounds and procedures for massage therapists and practitioners. It adds failure to comply with a Board order as a ground for discipline, authorizes the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to grant stays of enforcement for its orders, and removes the requirement to publish disciplinary notices in the Maryland Register within 24 hours. It also establishes a six-month grace period for individuals with expired licenses before they are subject to criminal penalties for practicing without authorization.
responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill's changes using existing budgeted resources. The bill does not affect State revenues and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners is a regulatory board housed within the Department of Health. This bill directly alters the board's disciplinary procedures, licensing definitions, and enforcement mechanisms.

The bill governs disciplinary actions and contested cases for massage therapists. Such cases are typically heard by Administrative Law Judges from the Office of Administrative Hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Board of Massage Therapy Examiners and represents the board in judicial reviews and legal appeals of its decisions.

The bill specifies the process for judicial review of board orders and modifies criminal penalties (misdemeanors) for practicing massage therapy without a license, which are handled by the state's judicial system.

The bill explicitly authorizes law enforcement officers to demand proof of licensure from individuals practicing massage therapy and involves the enforcement of criminal penalties for unauthorized practice.

The bill repeals a requirement for the Board to file notices of license revocation or suspension for publication in the Maryland Register, which is an official record maintained under the Secretary of State's jurisdiction.

Synopsis: Establishing the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force to survey and document a representative sampling of the variety of ordinances, laws, codes, and policies regarding the development and operation of accessory dwelling units in areas zoned for single-family residential use; and requiring the Task Force to report to the Governor and General Assembly on its activities on or before November 1, 2023, and its findings and recommendations on or before June 1, 2024.
Title: Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 798

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force to study state and local efforts regarding the creation of accessory dwelling units (ADUs) on land zoned for single-family residential use. The task force is charged with surveying existing laws, identifying best practices for streamlining permit processes, and making policy recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly regarding the practical issues of ADU development and their impact on housing markets and neighborhood livability.
stakeholders: Homeowners, local governments (Maryland Association of Counties and Maryland Municipal League), the Maryland Building Industry Association, the Maryland Association of Realtors, architects, interior designers, and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in fiscal 2024 for the Maryland Department of Planning to hire a consultant to assist the task force with its research and recommendations. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Planning is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. The Secretary of Planning is a mandatory member of the Task Force, the department is required to provide staff for the Task Force, and the fiscal note assigns a $50,000 cost to the department for hiring a consultant to support the Task Force's work.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a mandatory member of the Task Force. The bill's focus on Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) as a solution for affordable housing and community development aligns directly with the department's core mission.

The Governor is responsible for appointing eleven members of the Task Force and designating the chair. Additionally, the Task Force is required to submit two reports detailing its activities, findings, and recommendations directly to the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force, a temporary body composed of appointed public servants and private citizens tasked with conducting a study and providing policy recommendations to the executive and legislative branches.

The Office of Appointments will be responsible for recruiting, vetting, and recommending the eleven candidates for the Governor-appointed positions on the Task Force, ensuring they meet the specific professional and geographic criteria outlined in the bill.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM will oversee the $50,000 general fund expenditure identified in the fiscal note for the consultant services required by the Department of Planning to support the Task Force.

ADUs are a significant housing strategy for 'aging in place' for older adults. While the department is not a mandatory member, the Task Force includes a representative from AARP, and the policy recommendations will impact the housing options for the population the Department of Aging serves.

Accessory Dwelling Units are often utilized to provide accessible, integrated housing for individuals with disabilities. The Task Force's study of permit standardizing and building codes is relevant to the department's mission of advancing accessible housing.

The Task Force includes a mandatory member with professional experience in the planning and development of roads and highways. This expertise is relevant to assessing the impact of increased ADU density on local traffic, parking, and transportation infrastructure.

Synopsis: Authorizing an application for special death benefits to be made for the death of certain members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Special Death Benefits - Applicability

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: This bill allows the surviving spouse of a Correctional Officers’ Retirement System member who died in the line of duty by homicide on or after June 1, 2001, to apply for a special death benefit. The benefit includes a retroactive lump sum payment with 4% annual interest, adjusted for any previously received general death benefits. The legislation is specifically intended to provide benefits to the family of Officer Gregory Collins, who was killed in 2001 before special death benefits were established for the system in 2006.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Surviving spouses and beneficiaries of members of the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System who died in the line of duty by homicide on or after June 1, 2001.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is expected to apply to only one individual; consequently, it has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or employer contributions. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, which is managed by the Maryland State Retirement Agency, to administer and award special death benefits for specific individuals in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill pertains to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System, whose members are employed by this department. The fiscal note specifically identifies the agency's involvement in providing information regarding the performance-of-duty deaths that prompted the legislation.
As the central personnel and fiscal agency for the state, DBM is responsible for managing state employee benefits and policies, including those related to the state retirement systems.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies, including the Maryland State Retirement Agency, and would be responsible for ensuring the legal eligibility of claimants under the retroactive provisions of this bill.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "massage therapy"; altering the date after which the option to be registered by the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to practice massage therapy in a setting that is not a health care setting will no longer be available; and repealing a provision of law that provides that certain provisions of law do not require a nonprofit health insurance plan, an insurer, a health maintenance organization, or a person acting as a third party administrator to reimburse certain individuals for services rendered.
Title: Massage Therapy - Definition, Registration, and Reimbursement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: This bill updates the definition of massage therapy and extends the deadline by one year, until September 30, 2024, for individuals to qualify as registered massage practitioners. It also removes a provision in existing law that explicitly stated health insurance plans and carriers were not required to reimburse massage therapists or practitioners for their services.
responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, health insurance carriers (insurers, HMOs, and third-party administrators), and massage therapy clients.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill's changes using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no fiscal impact on local governments. The impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners is a regulatory board housed within the Department of Health. The bill directly modifies the Board's statutes, including the definition of massage therapy and the timeline for phasing out the registered massage practitioner credential.

The bill repeals a specific provision of the Health Occupations Article (Section 6-403) that explicitly stated health insurance plans and insurers were not required to reimburse massage therapists. This change directly impacts the insurance regulations and policy forms overseen by this agency.

The Office of the Attorney General provides primary legal counsel to the Department of Health and its professional licensing boards, ensuring that the changes to definitions and regulatory requirements are legally implemented and enforced.

The bill relates to the qualifications for massage therapy licensure and registration, which require applicants to graduate from programs approved or accredited by the commission and other educational bodies.

The commission is responsible for health system planning and monitoring health care financing; the repeal of reimbursement exemptions for health services provided by massage therapists relates to their interest in health care cost and accessibility.

The exchange manages the state's health insurance marketplace. Removing the statutory exclusion for massage therapy reimbursement may affect the coverage requirements and benefit structures of the health plans offered through the exchange.

Synopsis: Transferring the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency;  requiring program grant applicants to include the distribution of books to children in low-income zip codes within the applicants' areas of service; requiring the Governor to include $350,000 in the annual budget bill for the Program; requiring the State Library Board, beginning December 1, 2024, to report every other year to the General Assembly on the effectiveness of the Program; etc.
Title: Baltimore City Young Readers Program and Young Readers Matching Grant Program - Alterations (Young Readers Program Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: This bill transfers the administration of the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program from the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to the Maryland State Library Agency. It expands the Young Readers Program to be a statewide initiative, allows public libraries to apply for matching grants, and increases the mandated annual appropriation for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program from $250,000 to $350,000. Additionally, it requires the Maryland State Library Board to report biennially on the effectiveness of the matching grant program.
stakeholders: Maryland children (especially those in low-income zip codes), public library systems, nonprofit early reader organizations, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures will increase by $100,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to account for the increased mandated appropriation for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program. In fiscal 2024, existing funds for the programs (totaling approximately $746,193) are transferred to the Maryland State Library Agency. Administrative costs for a half-time staff member at the agency are estimated at $42,300 annually, which are expected to be covered by the mandated appropriation. Local library systems and counties may see increased revenues and expenditures if they apply for and receive matching grants under the program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly transfers the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency. The State Librarian is tasked with administering the programs, and the Maryland State Library Board must report on their effectiveness.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers administrative authority and existing funding for the Young Readers programs away from this office (formerly known as GOCPYVS) to the Maryland State Library Agency.

The bill increases a mandated annual appropriation for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program from $250,000 to $350,000 and requires the creation of a new half-time administrative position to manage the grants.

The Governor's Office for Children originally implemented the Young Readers Program. The program's mission to distribute books to children, particularly in low-income areas, aligns with the agency's focus on child well-being and reducing child poverty.
The bill requires the Governor to include specific mandated appropriations for these literacy programs in the annual state budget bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a register of wills to accept certain documents filed electronically through a system established by the register of wills; and prohibiting a register of wills from refusing to accept a document based on the manner in which it was signed.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Registers of Wills - Electronic Filing and Signatures
bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland registers of wills to accept documents filed electronically through an established system, with the exception of original wills. It prohibits registers from refusing documents based on the manner of signature and specifies that paper filings remain an acceptable option. The bill also aligns these processes with the Maryland Rules.
stakeholders: Individuals and legal professionals involved in estate administration, probate court users, and the Registers of Wills in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are expected to increase by a relatively minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2024 due to reduced administrative costs associated with paper filings. For illustrative purposes, the Howard County register estimates statewide savings of at least $40,000 annually. Local government operations and finances are not affected, and the electronic filing system is already included in the budget.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Registers of Wills to accept electronic filings (excluding original wills) and prohibits them from refusing documents based on the type of signature used, fundamentally altering their filing and administrative procedures.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judicial Branch; since Registers of Wills serve as clerks for the Orphans' Courts and the bill requires electronic filings to comply with Maryland Rules, there is a strong operational and procedural link.

The Comptroller oversees state revenue collection. The bill is expected to increase general fund revenues through administrative savings at the Register of Wills' offices, which collect inheritance taxes and probate fees.

As the principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management monitors revenue changes to the General Fund, such as the administrative cost reductions projected in the fiscal note for this bill.

The Maryland State Archives is responsible for preserving permanent judicial and state records. The transition to electronic filing for estate documents impacts the long-term preservation and accessibility protocols for these records.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Registers of Wills, regarding statutory compliance and the legal standards for electronic signatures and digital records.

The Department of Information Technology oversees state IT strategy and data governance. While the registers are building an independent system, the department's role in setting statewide standards for electronic signatures and secure digital platforms remains relevant.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to include an attestation that all units required to report are represented in its annual report beginning December 31, 2023; requiring the Office to conduct a certain periodic audit to ensure the accuracy of the attestation; requiring a certain annual report to be submitted to the Joint Committee on Fair Practices and State Personnel Oversight; etc.
Title: Minority Business Enterprise Program - Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor’s Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA) to include an attestation in its annual Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) report that all required State units are represented. GOSBA must conduct an audit of the Executive Branch every three years to identify which entities are required to report, and the Office of State Procurement must maintain a list of these units. The bill also updates reporting requirements for State agencies and provides for legislative oversight through the Joint Committee on Fair Practices and State Personnel Oversight.
responsible_party: Governor’s Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs and the Office of State Procurement in the Department of General Services
stakeholders: State Executive Branch units, certified minority business enterprises (MBEs), and prime contractors involved in State procurement.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no financial impact on State or local governments. The Governor’s Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs can fulfill the bill's requirements, including periodic audits and reporting, using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing the Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program, GOSBA is responsible for the annual report, including the new attestation and the triennial audit of the Executive Branch mandated by the bill.

The Office of State Procurement (OSP) within DGS is required by the bill to maintain the official list of reporting units and must be consulted by GOSBA regarding regulations for debarring non-compliant contractors.
The BPW receives the annual MBE reports, must approve the reporting forms, and is a consulting body for regulations concerning the persistent failure of prime contractors to meet MBE goals.
The OAG is consulted on the development of regulations for identifying failing contractors and handles the subsequent debarment process for those referred by GOSBA.
MDOT serves as the state's MBE certification agency mentioned in the bill's reporting requirements and is one of the primary units whose procurement data is audited and reported.
GOSBA is a coordinating office within the Executive Department. The Governor also serves as a member of the Board of Public Works which has oversight duties under the bill.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller reviews the annual reports and is consulted on regulations regarding the MBE program and contractor debarment.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer reviews the annual reports and is consulted on regulations regarding the MBE program and contractor debarment.
As an executive unit, MDH is required to report annual MBE procurement data and is subject to the triennial audit by GOSBA.
As an executive unit, MSDE is required to report annual MBE procurement data and is subject to the triennial audit by GOSBA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is a major executive unit subject to the bill's reporting and audit requirements, noted for significant MBE participation in the fiscal note.
The University System of Maryland is a reporting entity specifically mentioned in the fiscal note as subject to MBE participation reporting.
As a state university, Morgan State is a unit required to report its MBE participation data to GOSBA.
As a state college, St. Mary's is a unit required to report its MBE participation data to GOSBA.
DBM is a reporting unit and, as the state's fiscal and personnel agency, has an interest in the administrative compliance of other executive departments.
As an executive unit, MDA is required to report annual MBE procurement data and is subject to the triennial audit by GOSBA.
As an executive unit, MDE is required to report annual MBE procurement data and is subject to the triennial audit by GOSBA.
As an executive unit, DJS is required to report annual MBE procurement data and is subject to the triennial audit by GOSBA.
As an executive unit, DoIT is required to report annual MBE procurement data and is subject to the triennial audit by GOSBA.

Synopsis: Extending to October 1, 2028, the authority of the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to impose a transfer tax on certain instruments of writing.
Title: St. Mary's County - Transfer Tax - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill extends the authority of the County Commissioners of St. Mary’s County to impose a transfer tax on instruments of writing, such as property deeds recorded or filed in the county, from its previous termination date of October 1, 2024, to October 1, 2028.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary’s County
stakeholders: Real estate buyers and sellers in St. Mary’s County
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal impact. Locally, the bill maintains St. Mary's County transfer tax revenues of approximately 8000000 dollars annually through fiscal 2028. In fiscal 2029, revenue is estimated to be 2000000 dollars to reflect the final three months of collection before the October 1, 2028 sunset. These revenues are dedicated to the county's capital improvement fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the recording of instruments of writing with the Clerk of the Circuit Court for St. Mary’s County. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides the operational, legal, and financial support necessary for the clerks to process these recordings and ensure the transfer tax is correctly applied according to the extended authority.
As the chief executive, the Governor signed this bill into law and oversees the administration of state policy, including legislation that authorizes local jurisdictions to exercise taxing authority.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County to issue a Class B-ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) license for use at certain Towson University events.
Title: Baltimore County - Class B-ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) License - Towson University

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class B–ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) beer, wine, and liquor license for use at Towson University events. The license allows for the sale of alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption at university-related events catered by the university's campus dining services contractor, with profits deposited into the university's auxiliary services account.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County
stakeholders: Towson University, the university's campus dining services contractor, and attendees of university-related events in Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore County revenues are estimated to increase by $2,500 in fiscal 2024 due to initial application and license fees, and by $2,000 annually thereafter for license renewal fees. There is no fiscal impact on the State, and Baltimore County is expected to handle enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes Towson University, which is a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, to receive a Class B-ECF/DS alcoholic beverages license. It also clarifies regulations for the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (another USM institution), and requires that profits from the license be deposited into the respective university auxiliary services accounts.
The Comptroller's Office is the primary state agency responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state revenues, including taxes and fees related to alcoholic beverage licenses.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person who applies for certain property tax exemptions for real property in Baltimore City to request that the exemption be applied retroactively for up to 3 taxable years, subject to certain requirements; requiring Baltimore City and the State to pay a refund of excess real property taxes paid due to a retroactive exemption that is granted; and requiring the Baltimore City Department of Finance to submit a report on the number of requests made and the amounts refunded by December 1 each year from 2023 to 2027.
Title: Baltimore City - Property Tax - Retroactive Exemption
bill_summary: This emergency bill allows property owners in Baltimore City to apply for retroactive property tax exemptions for up to three years for properties owned by nonprofit or religious organizations. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation must grant the exemption upon approval by the Baltimore City Solicitor and Department of Finance, and both the State and Baltimore City are required to refund any excess taxes paid due to the retroactive status.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation, Baltimore City Solicitor, and Baltimore City Department of Finance
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, religious organizations, and small businesses in Baltimore City eligible for property tax exemptions.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State Annuity Bond Fund revenues are expected to decrease by approximately $14,200 annually from FY 2023 through 2027, and Baltimore City property tax revenues will decrease by approximately $285,000 annually over the same period. The bill also requires Baltimore City to handle administrative reporting with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Baltimore City Department of Finance to submit an annual report to the Governor through 2027 detailing the number of requests for retroactive exemptions received and approved, as well as the total amounts refunded.

As the state's principal tax collector and chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing the collection of state revenues and the issuance of refunds, which the bill explicitly requires the State to pay for retroactive exemptions.

The bill impacts the Annuity Bond Fund (ABF), which is the dedicated fund for state real property tax revenues used to pay debt service on general obligation bonds. The Treasurer manages state funds, bond sale revenue, and the issuance of State bonds.

DBM is responsible for estimating revenues and supervising budget execution. The bill is projected to decrease state property tax revenues flowing into the Annuity Bond Fund, requiring fiscal planning adjustments.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like SDAT and represents the state in tax-related appeals. The bill's requirement for a 'showing of good cause' may lead to legal challenges or requests for counsel on implementation.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes regarding tax exemptions and real property assessments. It would serve as the final administrative appeal level for taxpayers whose requests for retroactive exemptions are denied by state or local authorities.

The PTAAB hears appeals regarding property tax exemptions and credits. Disputes over the 'good cause' requirement for a retroactive exemption under this bill would likely be reviewed by this board after an initial determination by state assessors.

The Board, which includes the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees the state's fiscal integrity and general obligation bond issuances. The bill's impact on the Annuity Bond Fund affects the state's debt service capacity which falls under their broad oversight.

Synopsis: Repealing certain geographic and temporal restrictions on the issuance of Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Class A-7 Licenses
bill_summary: This bill removes geographic and time-based restrictions on Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City. Specifically, it repeals the prohibition against issuing these licenses in the 43rd legislative district and eliminates the July 1, 2022, deadline for license issuance. It continues to allow holders of Class B-D-7 licenses issued on or before July 1, 2018, to exchange them for Class A-7 licenses provided they receive approval from the Baltimore City Council.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders in Baltimore City, prospective license applicants in the 43rd legislative district, and the Baltimore City Council.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, Baltimore City revenues will increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024. New Class A-7 license applications result in a $2,100 revenue increase ($600 application fee plus $1,500 annual license fee) at the time of application. Exchanging a Class B-D-7 license for a Class A-7 license results in a $780 initial revenue increase ($600 application fee plus a $180 difference in annual fees) and a $180 annual increase thereafter. State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry in the state. Since this bill modifies the licensing structure for alcoholic beverages in Baltimore City, it falls under the Comptroller's broad regulatory and oversight duties regarding state-level alcohol laws and industry regulation.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions and represents the state in legal matters. This office would be responsible for interpreting the legal changes to the Alcoholic Beverages Article and providing guidance on the enforcement or litigation of the modified licensing rules.

As the chief executive, the Governor's Office is responsible for the overall administration of state laws and signed this specific bill into law. The office oversees the policy direction that informs changes to state-authorized local licensing regulations.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations that exempt on-farm composting facilities from certain permit requirements if the facility meets specific criteria, such as using 10,000 square feet or less for active food scrap composting and complying with record-keeping and feedstock restrictions. It also establishes requirements for construction and operation plans and mandates a report to the General Assembly by December 2028 on the impact of these facilities.
stakeholders: Farm owners and operators, on-farm composting facility operators, and the Maryland Department of the Environment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill, including the adoption of regulations and the submission of a report, using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local governments. Small businesses, particularly farms, may benefit from a reduced regulatory burden and potential savings in solid waste costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Department of the Environment to adopt new regulations establishing permit exemptions for on-farm composting, manage notices from farm operators, and submit a comprehensive impact report to the General Assembly by 2028.

The bill governs on-farm composting and requires facilities to comply with Nutrient Management Plans and Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plans, which are administered or overseen by the Department of Agriculture.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of the Environment and the Department of Agriculture in drafting the mandated regulations and ensuring the permit exemptions comply with state law.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the implementing agencies and coordinates the state's broader environmental and agricultural policy initiatives addressed by this bill.
The Department of Health has a secondary interest in the public health aspects of composting regulations, particularly concerning the management of food scraps and animal manure pathogens.
The Council advocates for agricultural and economic development in rural counties, where the majority of farms benefiting from these composting permit exemptions are located.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO supports the economic viability of the agricultural industry, which is enhanced by reducing regulatory barriers and costs for on-farm composting activities.

Synopsis: Requiring that a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Caroline County be a resident of the State rather than a resident of the county; and requiring that a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Queen Anne's County be a resident of the State rather than a resident of the county.
