DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public lands and state parks. The agency through the Natural Resources Police often regulates parking and issues citations within these areas.
MDOT is the parent agency for several modal administrations (MVA, MTA, MAA, SHA) that manage parking facilities and are responsible for the verification process through the MVA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts third-party contractors authorized to conduct parking enforcement, many of whom are assumed to be small businesses. This office monitors socioeconomic procurement programs affecting such contractors.
MAA operates BWI and Martin State Airport, which include extensive parking facilities where citations are issued. The agency must update its citations and verification procedures.
MFCA manages regional food distribution facilities, including wholesale markets with parking areas. As a state agency managing real estate and traffic flow, it may issue parking citations.
MPA manages state-owned port facilities, including terminals with regulated parking areas. The agency is responsible for complying with the new citation format and verification requirements.
MSA manages sports and entertainment complexes like Camden Yards, which involve significant parking operations and enforcement actions that must comply with the bill.

MSP is a primary law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing motor vehicle laws and issuing citations. They were also identified as an information source for the fiscal note regarding citation logistics.
MTA manages transit-related parking lots for buses, light rail, and MARC trains. They will need to modify their citations and verification processes for parking violations in these lots.
MDTA maintains its own police force and manages toll facilities and related property where parking enforcement occurs. They must adapt their citations to include the required checkbox.
As a state agency with its own campus and parking enforcement authority, Morgan State must comply with the new requirements for parking citations issued on its property.

The bill explicitly requires that issuing entities verify citation discrepancies through 'the Administration' (MVA). The MVA provides the interface and data needed to verify if registration plates match the vehicle described.
The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies and boards. They would likely advise agencies on the proper implementation of the new verification and dismissal procedures required by the bill.
As an independent state unit with campus parking, the college must update its parking citation forms and establish the required verification process with the MVA.
SHA manages state-numbered highways and adjacent public property where parking enforcement and citation issuance may occur.
USM institutions manage extensive campus parking systems and issue citations. They must adopt the new citation format and comply with the MVA verification requirement.

Synopsis: Altering the means by which the State Treasurer may send notice of a denial of a claim made under the Maryland Tort Claims Act to authorize notice by e-mail or, if it is the only available means, by regular mail.
Title: Maryland Tort Claims Act - Denial of Claims - Notice

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Torts -see also- Libel and Slander; Med Malp; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland Tort Claims Act to allow the State Treasurer to provide notice of a claim denial via e-mail or regular mail, rather than requiring certified mail.
stakeholders: Individuals filing tort claims against the State of Maryland and the Maryland State Treasurer's Office.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, general fund expenditures for postage and handling will decrease by approximately $17,800 annually starting in FY 2024. This is due to the shift from certified mail to e-mail or regular mail for claim denial notifications. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the administrative procedures of the Maryland State Treasurer's Office by authorizing the Treasurer or their designee to notify claimants of a tort claim denial via email or regular mail, rather than certified mail. The Treasurer's Office is the primary agency responsible for managing claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act (MTCA) and will realize the fiscal savings identified in the bill's fiscal note.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) serves as the chief legal representative for the State and is specifically required to be consulted by the Treasurer regarding the compromise and settlement of MTCA claims. As the OAG represents state agencies in civil litigation following the denial of such claims, changes to the statutory notice requirements for denials directly affect the legal procedures and timelines managed by the OAG.

Synopsis: Requiring a principal department of the Executive Branch to give certain notice to the public, the General Assembly, and any exclusive representative with certain bargaining unit employees, hold a public hearing, submit a certain report, make the report publicly available, and allow the submission of certain comments before changing the use, purpose, or function of a State facility or closing a State facility.
Title: State Government - State Facilities Changes and Closures - Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee

bill_summary: This bill requires principal departments of the Executive Branch to follow specific procedures before closing or materially changing the use, purpose, or function of a State facility. These procedures include providing public notice at least 90 to 180 days in advance, holding a public hearing, and for closures, submitting a detailed report to the Governor and the General Assembly justifying the action. It also expands the definition of 'State facility' to include any location where 25 or more State employees are regularly assigned.
responsible_party: Principal departments of the Executive Branch of State government
stakeholders: State employees and their exclusive bargaining representatives, members of the Maryland General Assembly, and patients, inmates, or residents of State health, juvenile, or correctional facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's requirements can be handled within existing budgeted resources. While State operations and finances could be affected if the new procedural requirements delay the closure or change of a facility, such impacts are expected to be minimal and absorbable. Local governments are not impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires principal departments to submit a report justifying or explaining any facility closure directly to the Governor. As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the departments implementing these new procedures.

The bill's definition of a 'State facility' specifically includes those providing health services. MDH operates numerous facilities that are directly subject to the new notice, hearing, and reporting requirements for closures or changes in use.

The bill's definition of a 'State facility' specifically includes those providing juvenile services. DJS operates residential and detention facilities that are directly impacted by the mandated procedures for facility changes and closures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's definition of a 'State facility' specifically includes those providing correctional services. DPSCS operates a large network of prisons and detention centers subject to these stringent closure and modification procedures.

DGS is the primary agency for planning, design, and management of state-owned and leased facilities. It handles real estate leasing and acquisitions, which are subject to the bill's notice and hearing requirements.

DBM is responsible for the state's personnel management and fiscal planning. The bill requires closure reports to address budgetary impacts and plans for assisting affected state employees with finding other employment.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures, including the acquisition, lease, and transfer of state property. Facility closures or changes in use typically result in property transactions requiring BPW approval.

The bill requires notice to be sent to the 'exclusive representative' (unions) of state employees. PERB is the agency responsible for administering collective bargaining and labor relations for these employees.

OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies. It will be responsible for advising executive departments on compliance with the new statutory notice, hearing, and reporting timelines established by the bill.

As a principal department with a vast network of facilities (MVA, SHA, Transit) often housing more than 25 employees, MDOT must comply with the bill's procedures when closing or changing the use of those sites.
As a principal department with numerous barracks and facilities housing 25 or more employees, the State Police are subject to the bill's requirements for facility closures and use changes.

The department oversees the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, which provides health services. This facility falls under the specific definition of 'State facility' and the associated closure/change procedures.
As a principal department, the Department of Aging must comply with the bill's procedures if it seeks to close or change the use of a facility regularly assigned 25 or more state employees.
As a principal department, MDA must comply with the new notice, reporting, and hearing requirements for any facility changes or closures meeting the bill's criteria.
As a principal department, the Department of Commerce is subject to the bill's mandates for facility closures or changes in use for sites with 25 or more employees.
As a principal department, it is subject to the requirements for facility closures and changes, particularly if it operates centers for people with disabilities that meet the bill's criteria.
As a principal department, MSDE must follow the bill's procedures for any of its facilities that meet the definition (e.g., those with 25+ employees).
As a principal department, MDEM is subject to the new statutory requirements for closing or changing the use of its facilities.
As a principal department, MDE must comply with the bill's mandates for facility changes or closures for sites with 25 or more employees.
As a principal department, DHCD is subject to the bill's mandates for facility closures or changes in use for its regional offices or centers with 25 or more employees.
As a principal department that operates numerous local offices and service centers, DHS is significantly impacted by the bill's requirements regarding facilities with 25 or more employees.
As a principal department, DoIT is subject to the bill's mandates for facility closures or changes in use for its operational centers with 25 or more employees.
As a principal department, DNR must follow the bill's procedures for its various regional and administrative facilities that meet the criteria of having 25 or more employees.
As a principal department, MDP is subject to the requirements for facility closures and modifications. Additionally, MDP's planning visions relate to state land use and resource management.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a newly established principal department, DSCI is subject to the bill's mandates for any facility closure or change in use meeting the statutory definition.
As a principal department with significant employee headcounts at various centers, the Department of Labor must comply with the bill's hearing and notice requirements.

Synopsis: Repealing the limitations on investment in certain commercial paper in which the Treasurer may invest or reinvest certain unexpended or surplus funds; requiring the Treasurer to adopt regulations to establish a State investment policy with certain thresholds; and requiring the Treasurer to notify certain officials and governing bodies of certain local governmental units about the provisions of the Act.
Title: State Investment Portfolio - Investment Thresholds - Alterations

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill removes the 10% cap on State investments in commercial paper and requires the State Treasurer to establish new investment thresholds for all authorized asset classes through regulation. It also requires the Treasurer to notify local government units of these changes to allow them to review and revise their own investment policies accordingly.
stakeholders: Maryland State Treasurer, local government units, and the State of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2024 to the extent that higher investment returns are realized through increased investment in commercial paper. No impact on State or local expenditures is anticipated. Local government revenues may also be minimally affected by the increased flexibility in their investment policies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office is the primary agency responsible for managing the State Investment Portfolio. The bill directly alters the Treasurer's authority regarding investment thresholds, requires the Treasurer to adopt new regulations, and mandates the Treasurer notify local governments of these changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Treasurer to work with this office to develop guidelines for identifying and evaluating qualified minority business enterprises for brokerage and investment management services. The Treasurer must also submit an annual report to this office regarding MBE participation.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller has a significant interest in the management of state revenues and the fiscal health of the investment portfolio, which impacts the overall state treasury.

DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues and long-term fiscal planning. The bill's potential to increase general fund revenues through optimized investment returns directly impacts the state's budget and revenue forecasting.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, coordinates policy initiatives, and is the recipient (via the sub-office for small and minority business) of required annual reports. The Governor also signed the bill into law.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Treasurer and will be responsible for reviewing the mandated regulations for legal sufficiency.

OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies. The new investment policy and regulatory thresholds established under this bill will become part of the future audit scope for the Treasurer's Office.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "hearing aid dispensary" to include certain actions taken for the purpose of ordering certain hearing instruments and specifying that certain hearing instruments include prescription hearing aids; altering the definition of "practice audiology" for the purposes of certain provisions of law governing the licensure of audiologists; and providing that certain provisions of law do not apply to certain actions taken with respect to certain over-the-counter hearing aids.
Title: Maryland Audiology, Hearing Aid Dispensing, Speech-Language Pathology, and Music Therapy Act - Definitions and Application

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill updates the definitions of 'hearing aid dispensing' and 'practice audiology' to include the ordering of prescription hearing aids and the management of osseointegrated devices such as cochlear implants. It also specifies that state licensing and regulatory requirements do not apply to over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids, aligning Maryland law with federal Food and Drug Administration regulations.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
stakeholders: Licensed audiologists, hearing aid dispensers, speech-language pathologists, music therapists, and consumers of hearing aid instruments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists can update regulations with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Audiology, Hearing Aid Dispensing, Speech-Language Pathology, and Music Therapy Act, which is administered by the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists, an entity under the Maryland Department of Health. The department is responsible for updating regulations and overseeing the licensure and practice of these health professionals.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions, including the Board of Examiners for Audiologists, and would be responsible for advising the board on the statutory changes and ensuring that new regulations align with federal law regarding over-the-counter hearing aids.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and appoints members to the various professional licensing boards affected by this legislation. The Governor also signed this bill into law.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Kent County Board of Education to include a student member; providing for the initial term of the student member of the county board; requiring the student member to attend the Maryland Association of Boards of Education new student board orientation and all regular meetings of the county board; prohibiting the student member's attendance at an executive session of the county board; etc.
Title: Kent County - Board of Education - Student Member

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.

bill_summary: This bill alters the composition of the Kent County Board of Education to include a nonvoting student member. The bill specifies that the student member must be a resident of Kent County, a junior or senior at Kent County High School, and a member of the student government. It outlines the application and election process by the high school student body and defines the student member's advisory role and term of office.
stakeholders: Students of Kent County Public Schools and the Kent County Board of Education
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, there is no impact on State or local finances because the bill codifies the Kent County Board of Education's existing practice of having a nonvoting student member.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) provides oversight for the state's public education system. This bill directly amends the Education Article regarding the composition of a local board of education and specifies the authority of the State Board (within MSDE) to remove members.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signs bills into law. This bill was enacted as Chapter 675 and affects local board governance, which falls under the executive branch's broad oversight of education policy.

The bill provides for a de novo review by the Circuit Court for Kent County in the event that a board member is removed under the specified administrative procedures, involving the judicial branch in the resolution of board membership disputes.

The State Ethics Commission is responsible for overseeing the ethics laws of local school boards. Adding a student member to the board involves potential ethics compliance and regulatory standards governing board members.

The Secretary of State is the custodian of the state's official records, including the laws passed by the General Assembly and signed by the Governor. This bill alters the codified laws of Maryland which the SOS manages.

While the student member is elected by the student body, the bill modifies the statutory structure of an elected board where the voting members are chosen in general elections supervised by the State Board of Elections.

The Governor's Office for Children promotes the well-being and engagement of Maryland youth. Codifying student representation in educational governance aligns with the agency's mission to support child and youth interests at the state and local levels.

As Kent County is one of Maryland's 18 rural counties, the Rural Maryland Council is relevant to policy changes affecting the governance and institutional health of its local entities, including its public education system.

Synopsis: Authorizing counties and municipal corporations to alter a certain limitation on the combined gross income of a homeowner for purposes of a local supplement to the homeowners' property tax credit; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Property Tax - Local Homeowners' Credit Supplement - Limitation on Combined Gross Income

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland counties and municipal corporations to increase the income eligibility limit for local supplements to the homeowners' property tax credit, which is currently set at a combined gross income of $60,000. This allows local governments to grant property tax credits to homeowners whose incomes exceed the previous state-defined threshold.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and local governing bodies of counties and municipal corporations.
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners with combined gross incomes exceeding $60,000 and local government jurisdictions.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on State finances as the State Department of Assessments and Taxation can administer the local supplement with existing resources. Local property tax revenues are expected to decrease beginning in fiscal 2024 to the extent that local governments choose to expand eligibility for their property tax credit supplements. The specific dollar amount of the revenue decrease is indeterminate and depends on the adoption of new income limits by local jurisdictions and the number of newly eligible applicants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The PTAAB is the independent agency responsible for hearing second-level administrative appeals regarding property tax assessments and credits. This bill allows local jurisdictions to alter income eligibility for homeowners' tax credit supplements, which directly impacts the criteria the board must use when adjudicating disputes over tax credit eligibility.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from the PTAAB. It is responsible for making factual determinations on real property assessments and tax credits, including the local supplements modified by this bill.

The Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program is a critical resource for older adults living on fixed incomes. By allowing local governments to expand income limits for these credits, the bill supports the Department of Aging's mission to improve housing stability and the quality of life for Maryland's senior population.

The DHCD is tasked with ensuring residents have access to safe, affordable, and secure housing. Tax credits that reduce the financial burden on homeowners directly align with the agency's goals of community revitalization and maintaining homeownership stability.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Assessments and Taxation (which administers these credits) and the Judiciary. It would be responsible for representing the state in legal challenges or interpreting the expanded local authority granted by this bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the administration of tax programs and the appointment of members to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards. The Governor also signed this bill into law as part of the state's executive policy implementation.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors all legislation with fiscal impacts on state and local governments. Although the bill primarily affects local revenues, DBM tracks these changes as part of the broader state fiscal and personnel landscape.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and has a general interest in tax policy and revenue collection, although the specific administration of local property tax supplements is handled by the Department of Assessments and Taxation and local jurisdictions.

Synopsis: Requiring a person who is not required to be licensed or permitted under certain provisions of law to obtain a free Department of Natural Resources identification number before using a snare, a trap, or another similar device to capture wildlife; and requiring a person who uses a snare, a trap, or another similar device to capture wildlife to ensure the person's Department identification number is stamped on the device or on a metal tag affixed to the device.
Title: Hunting - Snares, Traps, and Other Similar Devices - Identification Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill requires individuals who are exempt from hunting license requirements to obtain a free identification number from the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) before using snares, traps, or similar devices to capture wildlife. The identification number must be stamped on the device or a metal tag affixed to it, although DNR may waive this requirement for devices used on private property owned or rented by the user. The bill also allows individuals to report unidentified traps to the DNR or the Natural Resources Police Force.
stakeholders: Hunters and trappers exempt from licensing (such as landowners protecting property), wildlife control operators, and the Natural Resources Police Force.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances. The Department of Natural Resources can issue the required identification numbers using its existing online COMPASS licensing system and current budgeted resources. The application of existing misdemeanor penalties to violations of the bill is not expected to significantly impact state revenue or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is the primary agency responsible for implementing and enforcing the bill. It must issue identification numbers through its COMPASS electronic system, manage the tagging requirements, and oversee enforcement through its Natural Resources Police Force.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the State and provides counsel to the Department of Natural Resources regarding the implementation and enforcement of hunting and trapping regulations.

Violations of the bill's trapping identification requirements are categorized as misdemeanors under Title 10 of the Natural Resources Article. The Judicial Branch, supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, would be responsible for adjudicating these cases.

The bill requires the use of the state's electronic licensing system (COMPASS) to issue identification numbers. As the agency responsible for the state's IT strategy and infrastructure, DoIT oversees the systems utilized by executive branch departments like DNR.

The bill impacts the agricultural community, as farmers and landowners who use traps to protect property or livestock from wildlife may now be required to obtain and display a DNR identification number on their devices.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Natural Resources, and coordinates the policy initiatives that led to the enactment of this legislation.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a local board of elections from voting to change the location of a polling place without first holding a meeting to discuss the proposed change and providing an opportunity for individuals and organizations to testify; requiring each local board to submit a polling place plan to the State Board of Elections at least 6 months prior to each statewide primary election; altering the date of the 2024 statewide primary election and the primary election for municipal offices in Baltimore City to the second Tuesday in May; etc.
Title: Elections - Polling Place Plan, Prohibited Acts, and 2024 Primary Election Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill establishes new procedures for local boards of elections regarding polling place changes, requiring public meetings and testimony opportunities before a change is approved. It mandates that local boards submit a comprehensive polling place plan to the State Board of Elections for approval at least six months before statewide primary elections, requiring detailed demographic and impact analysis if the number of polling places is reduced from 2018 levels. The bill also expands the prohibition against influencing a voter's decision to include voting by mail or other lawful means and shifts the 2024 primary election date to the second Tuesday in May.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, historically disenfranchised communities, local boards of elections, and state and local elected officials
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $156,400 in FY 2024 for the State Board of Elections to hire a program administrator and procure mapping services. Future years see varying expenditure increases between $109,400 and $164,500. Local government expenditures increase collectively by at least $37,500 in FY 2024 and in subsequent primary election years due to cost-sharing requirements for mapping services and potential additional personnel or consulting costs for polling place plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, including the review and approval of polling place plans from local boards and managing the administrative shift of the 2024 primary election date.

The bill expands the definitions and prohibitions regarding the illegal influence of voters through force, fraud, or intimidation; the Office of the State Prosecutor is specifically tasked with investigating and prosecuting offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversaw this policy initiative and the Governor signed the bill into law. The office also provides administrative support and policy coordination for the State Board of Elections.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative and counsel for the State Board of Elections and will be responsible for providing legal interpretations and defending the new regulations regarding polling place plans and voter influence.
The bill creates and modifies misdemeanor penalties and civil penalties related to election law violations, which will be adjudicated within the state's judicial system managed by the AOC.

The bill explicitly requires local boards to utilize demographic reports published by the Maryland Vital Statistics Administration, which is a unit of the Department of Health, to conduct impact analyses for polling place plans.

The fiscal note identifies significant general fund expenditure increases for new personnel and mapping services at the State Board of Elections, which must be managed and approved by DBM as the state's principal fiscal agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD would be responsible for providing legal representation to indigent individuals charged with the election-related misdemeanors or civil penalties established or expanded by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines misdemeanors subject to imprisonment for up to five years, potentially impacting state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a certain incarcerated person from violating a condition of pretrial or posttrial release or other pretrial or posttrial condition prohibiting the person from contacting, harassing, or abusing an alleged victim or going in or near an alleged victim's residence or place of employment.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Violation of Pretrial or Posttrial Condition by Incarcerated Person - Victim Contact

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse & Neg.; Elder Abuse & Neg., etc
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom

bill_summary: This bill prohibits incarcerated individuals from violating pretrial or posttrial release conditions that forbid contacting, harassing, or abusing an alleged victim, or visiting the victim's home or place of employment, when the individual is charged with specific crimes including violence, stalking, sexual offenses against minors, or domestic abuse.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals charged with specific violent or sexual crimes and their alleged victims
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The judicial branch is responsible for setting and enforcing the pretrial and posttrial conditions that this bill addresses. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides support for these judicial functions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency manages incarcerated individuals and oversees pretrial and posttrial supervision (Parole and Probation). The bill specifically applies to incarcerated persons violating conditions regarding victim contact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent defendants who may be charged with the misdemeanor crime established or clarified by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the coordinating body for public safety and victim services, this office is relevant to policies aimed at protecting victims from harassment by incarcerated or supervised individuals.
The OAG represents the state in criminal appeals and provides legal guidance on the implementation of criminal procedure laws.
As a primary law enforcement agency, the State Police may be involved in investigating or charging individuals who violate the conditions specified in the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund to provide reimbursement for costs associated with educating, training, certifying, recruiting, placing, and retaining behavioral health professionals and paraprofessionals; and requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission, in coordination with certain entities, to conduct a comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment on or before October 1, 2024, and submit the assessment to certain committees of the General Assembly by October 15, 2024.
Title: Mental Health - Workforce Development - Fund Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund to provide reimbursement for costs associated with educating, training, certifying, recruiting, placing, and retaining behavioral health professionals and paraprofessionals in Maryland. It also requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct a comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment by October 1, 2024.
stakeholders: Behavioral health professionals, paraprofessionals, healthcare providers, and Maryland residents requiring mental health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund expenditures for the Maryland Health Care Commission increase by $75,000 in FY 2024 to conduct a workforce assessment. General fund expenditures and special fund revenues are estimated to increase by at least $1,000,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 to capitalize the fund, with corresponding special fund expenditures for reimbursements. Local government revenues may increase if local health departments are eligible for reimbursement from the fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for administering the newly established Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund and is required to submit annual reports on the fund's activities and expenditures.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is specifically mandated by the bill to lead and conduct a comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment in coordination with other state agencies.
The Department of Labor is named as a coordinating partner for the behavioral health workforce needs assessment and oversees workforce development programs that intersect with the bill's objectives.

The Higher Education Commission is required to coordinate on the workforce needs assessment and may see fiscal impacts as a potential recipient of fund distributions for student training and education programs.
The bill explicitly subjects the Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and personnel oversight; the bill establishes a new special fund requiring general fund appropriations and focuses on state workforce recruitment and retention.
The Comptroller is statutorily required by the bill to account for the Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund separately and invest its money in accordance with state law.
As a provider of behavioral health education and training, the University System of Maryland is a potential recipient of reimbursements and special fund revenues from the new investment fund.
Morgan State University provides professional health training and is identified as a potential recipient of funds to support behavioral health workforce development.
As a state educational institution, Saint Mary's College is a potential beneficiary of the fund's resources for training and educating the behavioral health workforce.
MSDE oversees career and technical education (CTE) and coordinates with the CTE Committee, which is a named partner in the mandated workforce needs assessment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Career and Technical Education Committee, which falls under this category, is named as a coordinating stakeholder for the behavioral health workforce needs assessment.
As the state's chief policy body for workforce strategy, the GWDB has a strategic interest in the bill's focus on expanding the pipeline for behavioral health professionals and paraprofessionals.

Synopsis: Requiring that the Health Services Cost Review Commission exercise its authority to consider certain standards when determining the reasonableness of certain rates in a manner that is consistent with the all-payer model contract.
Title: Health Services Cost Review Commission - Hospital Rates - All-Payer Model Contract

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: This bill requires the Health Services Cost Review Commission to ensure that its methods for determining whether hospital rates are reasonable—specifically when using standards for efficiency and effectiveness—align with the requirements of Maryland's all-payer model contract with the federal government.
stakeholders: Maryland hospitals and purchasers of health care facility services
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal impact on state or local governments because it codifies existing practices currently followed by the Health Services Cost Review Commission under the All-Payer Model Contract and its successor, the Total Cost of Care Model.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The HSCRC is the primary agency responsible for the hospital rate-setting system and the implementation of the All-Payer Model Contract (and its successor, the Total Cost of Care Model) mentioned in the bill. The bill directly regulates how the Commission determines the reasonableness of hospital rates.

The HSCRC is an independent agency located within the Maryland Department of Health. Furthermore, the bill specifies that the HSCRC may assist the Secretary of Health in the implementation of federally approved model programs.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its various departments, including the Department of Health. The Governor also signed this bill into law and is responsible for overall state policy regarding healthcare cost containment and federal contract compliance.

The OAG serves as the chief legal counsel to all state agencies, including the HSCRC and the Department of Health. They would be responsible for ensuring that the HSCRC's rate-setting investigations and standards remain legally consistent with the All-Payer Model Contract as required by the bill.

The MHCC is a sister regulatory agency within the Department of Health that works alongside the HSCRC to plan for health system needs and improve access and quality. While the bill is specific to HSCRC, changes to hospital rate-setting frameworks are relevant to the MHCC's broader health planning and accountability mission.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors the execution of state programs and fiscal practices. While the fiscal note indicates no direct impact on state funds, DBM oversees the budget and personnel of the implementing agencies involved in the All-Payer Model.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain rate of interest on certain member contributions in active members' nonvested accounts in the State Retirement and Pension System if the members have not withdrawn contributions from the nonvested accounts and are not eligible to receive a certain vested allowance; providing for the retroactive application of the Act; etc.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Nonvested Accounts - Regular Interest

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Retirement and Pension System to pay regular interest on member contributions held in nonvested accounts for former members who rejoin the system as active members in any of the state's retirement or pension plans. It applies retroactively to accounts of individuals who are active members on the bill's effective date and have not withdrawn their previous contributions.
stakeholders: Nonvested former members of the State Retirement and Pension System who return to service as active members and have not withdrawn their prior contributions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is estimated to increase State and local pension liabilities by approximately 514000 due to retroactive interest payments on roughly 1,600 identified accounts. This results in a minimal or negligible increase in annual pension contributions for the State and participating governmental units. There is no impact on state or local revenue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the operation and management of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), the Maryland State Retirement Agency is the lead implementing body for this bill. It will be responsible for identifying eligible nonvested accounts, calculating the required interest, and managing the retroactive application of these payments.

As the principal personnel and fiscal agency for the state, DBM manages state employee benefits and policies. It is responsible for overseeing the fiscal impact of pension liabilities and ensuring that state personnel records align with pension system requirements.
The bill specifically amends the State Police Retirement System (Section 24-206), affecting how interest is calculated for former members of that specific system who rejoin the SRPS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically amends the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System (Section 25-204), affecting how interest is calculated for former members of that specific system who rejoin the SRPS.
The bill specifically amends the Judges’ Retirement System (Section 27-203), affecting how interest is calculated for former members of the judiciary who rejoin the SRPS.
The bill specifically amends the Teachers’ Retirement System and the Teachers’ Pension System (Sections 22-215 and 23-213), which are overseen in coordination with educational system personnel.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the SRPS and state agencies. It would be involved in interpreting the retroactive application of the law and ensuring the statutory changes are implemented in accordance with state law.
The Comptroller serves as a key member of the Board of Public Works and as a trustee of the SRPS, overseeing the state's financial integrity and revenue flow.
The Treasurer serves as a trustee of the SRPS and is responsible for the management and protection of state funds, which include the assets within the retirement system.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget, which includes state contributions to the retirement systems impacted by changes in liability.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions relating to immunity from criminal arrest, charge, or prosecution for a person experiencing a medical emergency after ingesting or using alcohol or drugs.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Medical Emergency - Immunity

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: This bill expands and clarifies immunity from criminal arrest, charge, prosecution, and sanctions for violations of pretrial release, probation, or parole for individuals experiencing a medical emergency due to alcohol or drug use, as well as those who assist them, provided the evidence was obtained solely through seeking or receiving medical assistance.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Individuals experiencing medical emergencies from alcohol or drug use, persons assisting those individuals, and individuals on pretrial release, probation, or parole
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly prohibits the sanctioning of individuals for violations of conditions of pretrial release, probation, or parole if the evidence was obtained solely due to seeking or receiving medical assistance for a drug or alcohol emergency. This department oversees the Division of Parole and Probation and pretrial detention.

The judicial branch is responsible for the court proceedings where these immunities from prosecution and mitigating factors in criminal cases are applied, as well as the administration of pretrial release conditions.
As Maryland's primary law enforcement agency, the State Police are directly affected by the statutory changes to immunity from criminal arrest for specific drug and alcohol violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent clients in criminal and juvenile cases who will utilize these expanded immunity provisions as a critical legal defense.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, including policy development related to reducing drug and alcohol-related crimes and recidivism.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on criminal law interpretation and represents the state in appeals regarding statutory immunity and criminal procedure.
The department manages juvenile probation and aftercare services; the bill's provisions regarding immunity from sanctions for supervision violations apply to the youth under their jurisdiction.
The department oversees behavioral health and drug-related public health policies which provide the clinical context for the medical emergencies and drug use addressed in the bill.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies implementing these changes, signs the legislation, and coordinates the state's overall public safety and health policy initiatives.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to authorize a certain grant for the student member serving in the first year of the student's term on the Board of Regents.
Title: University System of Maryland - Board of Regents - Student Member Grant

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to provide a grant to a student member during the first year of their two-year term. The grant is funded by restricted funds from private donors through the University System of Maryland Foundation or a constituent institution and is capped at the cost of tuition and fees incurred by the student, ensuring total financial aid does not exceed the cost of attendance.
responsible_party: Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Student members of the University System of Maryland Board of Regents
fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education revenues and expenditures increase by an offsetting amount as private donor funds are received and distributed as grants to student board members. While specific total funding depends on donations and the students enrolled, the fiscal note indicates that per-student costs could range from approximately 10100 for in-state undergraduates up to 92500 for certain graduate programs. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the University System of Maryland (USM) Board of Regents, authorizing them to provide grants to student members and establishing the criteria for these grants and tuition waivers.

The bill explicitly states that the grants or tuition waivers provided to student regents are not to be considered gifts or compensation under the Maryland Public Ethics Law (Title 5 of the General Provisions Article), which the Commission enforces.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and is responsible for appointing members to the USM Board of Regents; the bill changes the financial benefits associated with these gubernatorial appointments.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the USM Board of Regents; the availability of grants for student members is relevant to the recruitment and selection process.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Board of Regents and state agencies regarding compliance with state law, including the interpretations of 'compensation' and 'gifts' as modified by this bill.
As the central personnel agency, DBM is interested in the bill's provision that ensures student regents receiving these grants are not classified as employees of the state.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Procurement Improvement Council to include the Comptroller and the Attorney General; authorizing certain members to send a designee to attend certain meetings under certain circumstances; and clarifying the duties of the Council to include discussion of strategies to increase the participation of small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses in procurement contracts.
Title: Procurement Improvement Council - Membership and Duties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill expands the membership of the Procurement Improvement Council to include the Comptroller and the Attorney General, allowing them to send designees to meetings. It also specifies that the Council must provide a forum for discussing strategies to increase the participation of small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses in State procurement contracts.
responsible_party: Chief Procurement Officer and the Procurement Improvement Council
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, the Comptroller, the Attorney General, and small, minority-, and women-owned businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not affect State or local finances. It has no projected impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly adds the Comptroller as a member of the Procurement Improvement Council and authorizes the Comptroller to send a designee to meetings.
The bill explicitly adds the Attorney General as a member of the Procurement Improvement Council and authorizes the Attorney General to send a designee to meetings.

The Chief Procurement Officer, who serves as the Chairman and principal staff for the Procurement Improvement Council, is located within the Department of General Services. The agency is also responsible for managing procurement resources like eMaryland Marketplace mentioned in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Special Secretary is a member of the Council, and the bill adds a specific duty for the Council to provide a forum for discussing strategies to increase participation of small, minority-, and women-owned businesses in state procurement.
The Council is tasked with advising the Board of Public Works on procurement problems and recommendations. Additionally, the Board's Procurement Advisor is a statutory member of the Council.
The State Treasurer is a statutory member of the Council, and the bill clarifies the Treasurer's authority to designate the Deputy Treasurer to attend meetings.
The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland is a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Health is a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Human Services is a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Information Technology is a statutory member of the Council, reflecting the agency's role in IT procurement.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services is a statutory member of the Council.
The Secretary of Transportation is a statutory member of the Council, representing the state's significant transportation procurement interests.
The State Superintendent of Schools (head of MSDE) is a statutory member of the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Procurement Improvement Council is a statutory advisory body within the executive branch that conducts studies and provides recommendations, fitting the description of this agency category.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and procurement policy; the Council advises the Board of Public Works (chaired by the Governor) and includes several of the Governor's cabinet secretaries.

Synopsis: Increasing from four to five the number of full-time assistant sheriffs provided to the Sheriff of Prince George's County; and providing that the Fraternal Order of Police will negotiate on behalf of deputy sheriffs in benefit matters not related to salary.
Title: Prince George's County - Office of the Sheriff - Deputy Sheriffs and Labor Organizations PG 308-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: This bill increases the number of full-time assistant sheriffs for the Prince George’s County Sheriff's Office from four to five. It also transfers the responsibility for negotiating benefits (other than salary increases) for deputy sheriffs from the Deputy Sheriffs’ Association to the Fraternal Order of Police and clarifies that the Sheriff's Office is authorized to investigate domestic violence calls and is not required to transfer those investigations to another law enforcement agency.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Office of the Sheriff
stakeholders: Prince George's County Sheriff's Office, deputy sheriffs, the Fraternal Order of Police, and Prince George's County residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no impact on State finances. Prince George’s County expenditures increase by approximately $331,600 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 to account for the salary and fringe benefits of the additional assistant sheriff position. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article of the Maryland Code, which is the primary statutory framework supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts. The legislation also affects the staffing and duties of the Prince George's County Sheriff's Office, which provides critical security and prisoner transportation services for the state's judicial system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references training requirements for deputy sheriffs to be set by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, an entity administratively housed within this department. It also updates language to align with the Public Safety Article regarding law enforcement standards and officer rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As Maryland's primary coordinating body for public safety policy, this office is impacted by legislation that clarifies or expands the investigative authority of law enforcement officers, particularly concerning domestic violence calls.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal representative for the State of Maryland and provides legal counsel to the Judiciary and state agencies. It would be responsible for providing guidance on the legal implications of the changes to law enforcement duties and the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including those related to public safety. The Governor is also responsible for signing the legislation into law.

Synopsis: Increasing the maximum number of speed monitoring systems that may be placed and used on Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) in Prince George's County from three to six; requiring the State Highway Administration in conjunction with a certain entity to report annually its recommendations for solutions to address accidents, injuries, and fatalities on the highway; extending the termination date for a provision of law granting the authority to place speed monitoring systems on Maryland Route 210 in Prince George's County; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) PG 304-23

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: This bill increases the number of mobile or stationary speed monitoring systems permitted on Maryland Route 210 in Prince George's County from three to six and extends the program's expiration date from 2023 to September 30, 2028. It also mandates that the State Highway Administration, in coordination with Prince George’s County, provide annual reports on highway safety findings and the allocation of fine revenues collected from these systems.
responsible_party: Prince George's County and the Maryland State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Maryland Route 210 and residents of Prince George's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill maintains and increases State Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures through fiscal 2029 due to the program extension and addition of cameras; specifically, $140,200 was remitted to the State Highway Administration in fiscal 2022. There is no net fiscal impact on Prince George’s County as fine revenues are used to cover implementation costs, with any remaining funds remitted to the state. General fund revenues may increase from fines paid in contested District Court cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Highway Administration to perform safety examinations of Maryland Route 210, use remitted fine revenues for safety solutions, and submit annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, MDOT is responsible for the state's highway network, including MD 210, and is noted in the fiscal note as an affected agency.
The bill requires that fines collected from the speed monitoring systems on MD 210 be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration.
The fiscal note indicates that the bill will likely increase the number of contested speed camera citations in the District Court, impacting court operations and revenues.
The bill requires the State Highway Administration to report its findings, recommendations, and fund usage regarding MD 210 safety to the Governor annually.
As the primary law enforcement agency for state highways, the Maryland State Police is a stakeholder in traffic safety and speed enforcement on Maryland Route 210.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County, notwithstanding a certain prohibition on the transfer of a license with an off-sale privilege, to approve the transfer of a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license to a premises located in a certain alcoholic beverages district under certain circumstances; authorizing the Board to issue a Class B-DD beer, wine, and liquor license with an off-sale privilege to certain restaurants in certain areas; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Licensing PG 305-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill permits the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners to transfer Class A beer, wine, and liquor licenses to specific districts if no other similar license exists within a one-mile radius. It also authorizes the issuance of Class B-DD (Development District) licenses with off-sale privileges for certain large restaurants located outside the Capital Beltway that meet specific seating, size, and investment requirements. Additionally, the bill modifies the geographical areas and caps for B-DD licenses, specifically for the South Lake mixed-use development and areas along Central Avenue.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurant owners, alcoholic beverage license applicants, and consumers in Prince George’s County.
fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George’s County revenues increase beginning in fiscal 2024 to the extent that new Class B-DD alcoholic beverages licenses are issued. The annual fee for a standard Class B-DD license is $3,025, while the fee for a Class B-DD license with off-sale privileges is $5,000. The exact revenue increase is indeterminate as it depends on the number of licenses issued. There is no impact on State finances, and local enforcement costs are expected to be covered by existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly empowers the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County, which is a state-authorized regulatory body, to issue and transfer specific alcoholic beverages licenses as part of their administrative duties.
The Comptroller functions as the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry and oversees the legal and regulatory framework within which local boards of license commissioners operate.

The bill focuses on the issuance of licenses within 'Development Districts' to stimulate local economic growth and support restaurant development, aligning with the department's mandate to attract and retain businesses.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state-authorized boards and commissions, including providing interpretations of the Alcoholic Beverages Article which this bill amends.

The Governor's Office is responsible for the appointment of members to the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners, the primary body tasked with implementing the changes described in the bill.
This office assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the local Board of License Commissioners to ensure leadership positions are filled by qualified individuals.

Synopsis: Changing the title of the Chief Executive Officer of the Prince George's County public school system to the County Superintendent of the Prince George's County public school system; establishing the Office of Integrity and Compliance in the Prince George's County public school system to evaluate, examine, investigate, report on, and make recommendations on certain issues related to the Prince George's County public school system; requiring the County Council of Prince George's County to appoint an Integrity and Compliance officer; etc.
Title: Prince George's County Public Schools - Alterations to Title of Chief Executive Officer and Establishment of Office of Integrity and Compliance PG 501-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse & Neg.; Elder Abuse & Neg., etc
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill changes the title of the Chief Executive Officer of the Prince George's County public school system back to the County Superintendent and establishes the Office of Integrity and Compliance (OIC). The OIC is responsible for investigating fraud, waste, and abuse, as well as evaluating the effectiveness, productivity, and internal controls of the county's public school system. The bill outlines the appointment process for an Integrity and Compliance Officer by the County Council and establishes protections for whistleblowers.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Council and the Prince George's County Board of Education
stakeholders: Prince George's County Public Schools employees, officials, vendors, and the general student and parent population of Prince George's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local school board expenditures in Prince George's County are estimated to increase by at least 741,041 dollars annually beginning in fiscal 2024. This figure is based on the assumption that the school system will repurpose existing internal audit staff while adding three new positions: an Integrity and Compliance Officer, a financial administrator, and a financial analyst. If the office is established without repurposing existing staff, costs could be significantly higher as the current Office of Internal Audit has a budget of approximately 2.4 million dollars.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary oversight body for Maryland public schools, MSDE is directly impacted by changes to the Education Article. The bill requires the State Superintendent to chair the search committee for the PGCPS Superintendent and mandates written approval from the State Superintendent for the final appointment.

The Governor has a direct statutory role in the selection of the PGCPS Superintendent by appointing two residents to the search committee. The Governor also oversees the executive branch and approved the enactment of this administrative policy change.

The bill explicitly requires the newly established PGCPS Integrity and Compliance Officer to report serious violations of law to the State Ethics Commission, integrating the commission into the school system's new accountability framework.

OLA performs fiscal compliance and performance audits of local school systems. The creation of a local Office of Integrity and Compliance with overlapping investigative and auditing powers creates a significant new coordination requirement for OLA's oversight work.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and other state boards on the interpretation and enforcement of the Education Article. The creation of local investigative powers, including subpoena authority, may require legal guidance and coordination from the OAG.

The OSP investigates criminal offenses related to the integrity of public institutions. The bill establishes an office to investigate fraud, waste, and abuse and requires it to report violations to law enforcement agencies, which include the OSP's jurisdiction.

The bill mandates that the PGCPS Superintendent enter into a memorandum of understanding for policy analysis and advice with several USM institutions, including the University of Maryland, College Park, UMGC, and Bowie State University.

The bill authorizes courts of competent jurisdiction to compel compliance with subpoenas and orders issued by the local Integrity and Compliance Officer, directly involving the judicial branch in the school system's new investigative process.

PERB oversees labor relations for local public school system personnel. The bill establishes whistleblower protections for school employees, and PERB would be responsible for adjudicating related claims of retaliation or unfair labor practices.

OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases, including those involving local school systems. Findings by the new Office of Integrity and Compliance regarding personnel or regulatory matters may lead to cases heard by OAH.

The IAC oversees state funding for public school capital projects. The new Office of Integrity and Compliance will audit vendor contracts and procurement, which directly supports the IAC's mission of ensuring fiscal responsibility in school facility projects.

Synopsis: Altering the alcoholic beverages that may be sold under a certain stadium license in Prince George's County; authorizing the holder of a Class B-Stadium (baseball stadium) beer, wine, and liquor license to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption; altering a provision of law providing that the profit from the sale of certain alcoholic beverages under the license may accrue to the use of the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission or the concessionaire; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B-Stadium (Baseball Stadium) Beer, Wine, and Liquor License PG 306-23
bill_summary: This bill allows the holder of a Class B-Stadium license for a baseball stadium in Prince George's County to sell liquor for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine. It also updates the names of stadium licenses to distinguish between baseball and football stadiums and specifies that profits from alcohol sales may accrue to the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission or its contracted concessionaires.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission, private concessionaires, and stadium patrons in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect Prince George's County finances or operations. While it expands the types of alcohol that can be sold under a baseball stadium license, the annual license fee remains $2,420.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal tax collector and regulates the alcohol, tobacco, and motor fuel industries. This bill alters the scope of Class B-Stadium licenses (expanding from beer and wine to include liquor) in Prince George's County, which directly impacts the agency's regulatory oversight and enforcement responsibilities regarding alcoholic beverages and state revenue collection.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the State and provides legal counsel to the Governor, the General Assembly, and state agencies. It is relevant here for its role in interpreting and providing legal guidance on changes to the Alcoholic Beverages Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives across the state. The Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the general enforcement of state laws, including those related to local commissions such as the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission mentioned in the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a court to schedule a hearing on a certain petition regarding the proposed relocation of a child who is the subject of a custody or visitation order on an expedited basis under certain circumstances.
Title: Child Custody - Relocation of Child - Expedited Hearing (Assurance of Child's Safety Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Child Custody -see also- Parents and Guardians

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland courts to schedule expedited hearings for petitions regarding the proposed relocation of a child who is the subject of a custody or visitation order, specifically in cases where the relocation is 40 or more miles away or would significantly interfere with the established parenting time schedule.
stakeholders: Parents and guardians involved in child custody or visitation proceedings and the children subject to those orders.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations, although there may be minimal expenditures associated with scheduling and conducting expedited hearings in circuit courts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the courts schedule hearings on an expedited basis for child custody relocation petitions, which falls under the operational and administrative support duties of the AOC for the Judicial Branch.

As the state's primary social service provider for children and families, DHS is a key stakeholder in child custody and welfare matters and was specifically consulted for the fiscal note analysis of this bill.

The bill's focus on child relocation, parenting time, and the 'Assurance of Child's Safety Act' aligns with the office's mission to coordinate statewide efforts and support networks for the well-being of Maryland's children.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the state agencies and the Judiciary; they would be responsible for advising on the implementation and legal interpretation of these changes to family law and court procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD provides legal representation in parental defense and juvenile proceedings; changes to custody relocation procedures and the scheduling of expedited hearings may impact their caseload and representation strategies in relevant cases.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, coordinates child-related policy initiatives, and the Governor signed this legislation into law.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors legislation for fiscal impacts on state operations, although the fiscal note indicates this bill's impact is minimal.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Prince George's County to enter into a payment in lieu of taxes agreement with an owner of real property that is used for low-income housing that is financed through the county's Right of First Refusal program or acquired, constructed, or rehabilitated for the purposes of operating the low-income housing.
Title: Prince George's County - Payment in Lieu of Taxes Agreements - Low-Income Housing PG 403-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Prince George’s County to enter into payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements with owners of low-income housing developments. The authorization applies to properties financed through the county’s Right of First Refusal program or those acquired, constructed, or rehabilitated specifically to provide rental housing for lower-income individuals.
stakeholders: Owners and developers of low-income housing in Prince George's County, lower-income residents seeking rental housing, and the Prince George's County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on state finances. At the local level, Prince George’s County property tax revenues may decrease starting in FY 2024 due to new property tax exemptions. The exact amount of the revenue decrease is indeterminate and depends on the number of eligible properties and their assessed values; however, these losses will be partially mitigated by the negotiated payments required under the PILOT agreements.
