agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, signs legislation into law, and coordinates state-level policy initiatives regarding affordable housing and local government relations.

The agency is responsible for financing and supporting affordable rental housing and community revitalization; the bill expands the use of PILOT agreements for low-income housing projects that may be supported by state or federal programs.

The office is dedicated to reducing child poverty and youth homelessness, making the authorization of new financial tools for low-income housing in Prince George's County highly relevant to its core mission.
The team focuses on addressing child poverty and enhancing economic mobility, both of which are central goals of expanding and preserving affordable rental housing for lower-income residents.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body for hearing appeals related to property tax disputes, which may include challenges to the local property tax exemptions authorized under this bill.

This board is responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax exemptions and credits; it would adjudicate disputes concerning the eligibility of specific housing projects for the PILOT agreements authorized by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to adopt regulations to ensure that children with disabilities who need special education and related services that cannot be provided in a public county, regional, or State program be placed in an appropriate nonpublic educational program that offers these services; requiring the State and certain counties to pay for costs of salaries for teachers at certain nonpublic schools in a certain amount and proportion; etc.
Title: Nonpublic Education - Placements of Children With Disabilities - Teacher Salaries (Teacher Pay Parity Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: The Teacher Pay Parity Act requires nonpublic schools that provide special education placements for children with disabilities to pay their teachers salaries equivalent to those of public school teachers with similar training and experience in the same county. This pay parity is phased in over three years beginning in fiscal year 2024. The additional funding required for these salary increases is shared by the State and local county governments based on a specific cost-sharing formula.
stakeholders: Teachers at nonpublic special education schools, children with disabilities in nonpublic placements, nonpublic educational facilities, and local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by 3500000 in FY 2024, rising to 11400000 by FY 2028. Local county government expenditures increase by 5000000 in FY 2024, reaching 16300000 by FY 2028. These increases represent the State and local shares of the additional funding needed to achieve teacher salary parity at nonpublic special education schools.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for K-12 oversight, MSDE is responsible for administering the nonpublic special education placement program, adopting regulations to carry out the teacher pay parity requirements, and managing the funding formulas that calculate the State and local shares of these costs.

The bill creates a mandated general fund expenditure that reaches $11.4 million annually by FY 2028. DBM is responsible for budgeting these mandated funds and oversees the fiscal personnel policies that the nonpublic salaries must now mirror.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. This bill establishes a significant new mandated appropriation that must be included in future executive budgets to fund teacher salary parity.

The bill specifically addresses the quality of education and support for children with disabilities. The Department of Disabilities coordinates services and policies for this population and has a direct interest in the financial stability of special education placements.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Department of Education and the State Board of Education regarding the implementation of the new salary parity mandate and ensuring compliance with the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA).
The Comptroller's office manages the collection and distribution of state revenues and will be responsible for the actual disbursement of mandated funds to support nonpublic teacher salaries.

The Treasurer's Office is responsible for the management and distribution of state funds, including those allocated for educational programs and special education placements under the revised funding formula.
The MLDS links student and workforce data; it may be used to analyze the impact of the Teacher Pay Parity Act on teacher retention and workforce outcomes in the special education sector.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board to place a licensee on emeritus status under certain circumstances; requiring the Board, under certain circumstances, to reinstate the license of an individual who is on inactive or emeritus status; exempting licensees who are on inactive status or emeritus status from continuing medical education requirements; repealing the requirement that the Board issue a license to an individual who is on inactive status under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: State Board of Physicians - Inactive and Emeritus Status

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Board of Physicians to establish an emeritus status for retired physicians who have practiced in the state for at least 10 years and meet specific conduct requirements. It updates the inactive status process and exempts both statuses from continuing medical education requirements and the standard three-year license term. Licensees on inactive or emeritus status are prohibited from practicing medicine or delegating medical acts, though emeritus physicians may continue to use titles such as 'Dr.' or 'M.D.' as long as they do not represent themselves as authorized to practice.
stakeholders: Licensed physicians in Maryland, particularly those retiring or seeking inactive license status
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Board of Physicians can handle the additional workload with existing budgeted resources. Any net impact on the board's special fund revenues from emeritus or inactive status fees is expected to be minimal. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physicians is a regulatory body within the Maryland Department of Health. This bill directly alters the Board's licensing procedures by establishing a new emeritus status, modifying inactive status requirements, and setting associated fees and continuing education exemptions.

The OAG serves as the chief legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Health and its professional boards. The OAG would be involved in drafting regulations for the new license status and providing legal guidance on the enforcement of practice prohibitions for inactive or emeritus physicians.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. If a physician is denied emeritus status or is charged with practicing medicine while on inactive or emeritus status, the resulting legal disputes would be heard by Administrative Law Judges at the OAH.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a health occupations board from requiring that an applicant provide proof that the applicant is lawfully present in the United States or have a Social Security number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number as a condition for licensure, certification, or registration; requiring each health occupations board to require each applicant for a license to disclose the Social Security number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number of the applicant or, as permitted by federal law, provide alternative documentation; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Licenses, Certificates, and Registrations - Lawful Presence and Identification Numbers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland health occupations boards from requiring applicants to provide proof of lawful presence in the United States or a Social Security number as a condition for professional licensure, certification, or registration. Instead, it allows applicants to provide an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) or other alternative documentation. The bill also updates data collection and reporting requirements for these boards to include ITINs for child support enforcement and tax assessment purposes.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and State health occupations boards
stakeholders: Immigrants residing in Maryland seeking healthcare professional licenses, the State Board of Nursing, the Child Support Administration, and the Department of Assessments and Taxation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for health occupations boards will increase by an indeterminate amount starting in fiscal 2024 due to potential additional license applications. Special fund expenditures for the State Board of Nursing are estimated to increase by $100,000 in fiscal 2024 for one-time programming costs. The Board of Nursing also estimates additional staffing costs of approximately $293,587 in fiscal 2024 and over $337,100 annually thereafter, though the Department of Legislative Services notes that the precise staffing need depends on actual application volume.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) as it prohibits health occupations boards, which operate within MDH, from requiring proof of lawful presence or a Social Security number for licensure. The fiscal note highlights significant impacts on the State Board of Nursing within MDH.

The bill amends the Family Law Article regarding child support enforcement by the Child Support Administration (CSA), which is a unit of the Department of Human Services. It modifies the identification data (adding ITINs) that licensing authorities must collect and share with CSA.

The bill specifically amends Section 10-119.3(b)(2) of the Family Law Article, which details the Social Security number disclosure requirements for recreational hunting and fishing licenses issued by the Department of Natural Resources.

The bill lists 'clerks of the court' and the 'Court of Appeals' as licensing authorities subject to the identification disclosure requirements in the Family Law Article, which are overseen and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Comptroller is designated as a 'licensing authority' under the Family Law provisions being amended and is subject to the updated requirements for recording and disclosing applicant identification numbers to the Child Support Administration.

The Department of Agriculture is listed as a 'licensing authority' whose procedures for recording applicant identification information (SSNs/ITINs) for child support enforcement are updated by this bill.
The State Department of Education is listed as a 'licensing authority' subject to the bill's updated identification disclosure requirements in the Family Law Article.

The Department of Labor is designated as a 'licensing authority' in the bill, meaning its licensing units must comply with the modified requirements for collecting and sharing Social Security numbers or ITINs.
The Department of Transportation is listed as a 'licensing authority' subject to the bill's changes regarding the disclosure of identification numbers for child support enforcement purposes.
The Department of the Environment is identified as a 'licensing authority' and is required to follow the bill's updated protocols for recording applicant identification information.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is listed as a 'licensing authority' affected by the bill's changes to the Family Law Article regarding the collection of Social Security numbers and ITINs for licensing.
The Office of the Attorney General is listed as a 'licensing authority' in the bill and provides legal counsel to the health occupations boards that must implement the new licensure criteria.
The Public Service Commission is designated as a 'licensing authority' subject to the updated applicant identification disclosure requirements for child support enforcement.
The Secretary of State is identified as a 'licensing authority' whose identification number collection procedures are modified by the bill's amendments to the Family Law Article.

The bill facilitates the entry of immigrants into the health workforce by removing lawful presence and Social Security number barriers, which aligns with the board's mission to develop innovative workforce solutions and talent pipelines.

Synopsis: Altering the authority of the Ocean Downs Race Course to use certain Purse Dedication Account funds generated from video lottery terminal proceeds for operating loss assistance to support a certain minimum number of live racing days at the racecourse.
Title: Video Lottery Terminal Proceeds - Purse Dedication Account - Ocean Downs Race Course Operating Loss Assistance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill modifies and makes permanent the financial assistance provided to Ocean Downs Race Course for operating losses from the Purse Dedication Account. It replaces a fixed annual limit of $1,200,000 with a formula of $30,000 per live racing day, provided the racecourse maintains a minimum of 40 live racing days per year.
stakeholders: Ocean Downs Race Course, standardbred racing industry participants, and the Maryland State Racing Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on overall State revenue or total special fund expenditures because it only redirects funds within the Purse Dedication Account (PDA). According to the fiscal note, the annual grant to Ocean Downs is expected to increase to approximately $1,410,000 (based on 47 racing days). This increase reduces the PDA funds available for standardbred purses by approximately $210,000 in 2023 and 2024, and by the full $1,410,000 annually thereafter as the original subsidy was set to expire.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Racing Commission, which is responsible for the authority and administration of the Purse Dedication Account described in the bill, is an entity within the Department of Labor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency regulates the video lottery terminals (VLTs) that generate the revenue distributed into the Purse Dedication Account, which this bill alters.
As the chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the collection and distribution of state revenues, including the proceeds from gaming that fund the Purse Dedication Account.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for implementing the bill's provisions and signed the legislation into law.
The department supervises budget execution and fiscal planning, including the oversight of special fund accounts like the Purse Dedication Account.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Pharmacy to adopt regulations necessary to ensure that individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled have appropriate access to prescription labels, bag tags, and medical guides; requiring the Board to give visually impaired individuals an opportunity to comment on the regulations; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to report by December 1, 2023, to the General Assembly on the implementation process for providing accessible labels for visually impaired persons.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Accessible Prescription Labels, Bag Tags, and Medical Guides for Blind, Visually Impaired, and Print Disabled Individuals - Regulations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Pharmacy to adopt regulations ensuring that blind, visually impaired, or print disabled individuals have access to accessible prescription labels, bag tags, and medical guides at no extra cost. It also mandates that the Maryland Department of Health submit a report on the potential costs and processes for implementing enhanced dispensing fees for these accessible materials.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Blind, visually impaired, and print disabled individuals; Maryland pharmacists and pharmacies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the State Board of Pharmacy and Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected. Small business pharmacies may incur additional expenses to provide accessible materials, though the exact impact depends on the regulations adopted by the Board.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Board of Pharmacy, which is overseen by the Department of Health, to adopt new regulations. Furthermore, Section 3 of the bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit a report to the General Assembly regarding the costs and process for implementing enhanced professional dispensing fees for accessible packaging.

The bill focuses on improving accessibility and service delivery for Marylanders with visual impairments and print disabilities. This aligns with the department's mission to coordinate services and ensure programs are inclusive and provided in integrated settings.

The Maryland State Library Agency directly oversees the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled (LBPD), which serves the specific population addressed by the bill and manages resources related to accessible formats.

A significant portion of the population that is blind or visually impaired consists of older adults. The bill's requirements for accessible prescription labels directly impact the quality of life and healthcare autonomy of Maryland's aging population.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to the Department of Health and the State Board of Pharmacy and will be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new regulations mandated by the bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (MDH and the Board of Pharmacy) responsible for implementing the bill and coordinates the policy initiatives that led to this legislation.

As the independent agency that hears contested cases for the Department of Health, the OAH would be responsible for adjudicating any regulatory enforcement disputes or appeals involving pharmacies failing to comply with the new label requirements.

The Commission is responsible for improving access to health care and promoting informed decision-making. The bill's requirement for accessible prescription information is a direct effort to improve health literacy and access for a specific patient population.

Synopsis: Repealing the School Safety Grant Program and the Aging Schools Program as of June 30, 2026; altering provisions relating to school construction approvals by the State Superintendent of Schools; altering provisions related to a public-private partnership agreement in Prince George's County; establishing that the Interagency Commission on School Construction is an independent unit of State government; repealing the requirement for the Board of Public Works to approve grants awarded under a certain capital grant program; etc.
Title: Public School Construction - Programs, Approvals, and Administration - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Interagency Commission on School Construction as an independent unit of State government and increases the state's annual funding commitment to the Prince George’s County public-private partnership for school construction from $25 million to $27 million starting in fiscal 2025. The bill also raises the cost thresholds for school remodeling projects and change orders that require approval from the State Superintendent of Schools and repeals the School Safety Grant and Aging Schools programs effective June 30, 2026, redirecting those funds to high-priority construction projects. Additionally, it mandates that local school boards perform life-cycle cost evaluations for major school construction or renovation projects.
stakeholders: Maryland local school systems, the Prince George's County Board of Education, the Maryland State Department of Education, and public school students.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $123,300 in FY 2024 for a new human resources position, and by approximately $2.1 million annually starting in FY 2025 to cover staffing and a $2 million backfill of Education Trust Fund revenues redirected to Prince George's County. Local revenues for the Prince George's County Board of Education will increase by $2 million annually beginning in FY 2025 for school construction. The repeal of the School Safety Grant and Aging Schools programs in FY 2027 is expected to be revenue-neutral, as approximately $16.1 million will be redirected to the Nancy K. Kopp Public School Facilities Priority Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill primarily concerns the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC), establishing it as an independent unit of State government, altering its membership removal process, and modifying its responsibilities regarding program administration, reporting, and life-cycle cost evaluations.

The bill alters the school construction approval authorities of the State Superintendent of Schools, moves the IAC out from being a unit within the Department, and requires coordination on life-cycle cost analysis standards.

The bill requires the Maryland Stadium Authority (MSA) to manage and deposit significant funds into the Prince George’s County Public–Private Partnership Fund and requires MSA to review P3 agreements and report on construction progress.

The Secretary of General Services is a member of the IAC. Additionally, the bill mandates that DGS develop life-cycle cost analysis standards in coordination with the IAC and the Department of Education.

The bill repeals the requirement for the Board of Public Works to approve certain grants awarded under school construction programs, reducing its direct oversight role in those specific funding allocations.

The Governor appoints and may remove certain members of the IAC. The bill also authorizes the Governor to process budget amendments related to the Supplemental Public School Construction Financing Fund.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) is a statutory member of the Interagency Commission on School Construction, which is restructured and given new mandates by this bill.

The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works and is responsible for holding, investing, and managing the special funds mentioned in the bill, such as the Prince George's County Public-Private Partnership Fund.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works and is responsible for accounting for the Prince George's County Public-Private Partnership Fund and depositing funds from the Education Trust Fund into the Financing Fund.
As the state's fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is impacted by the IAC's transition to an independent unit and the associated staffing requirements and budget amendments authorized by the bill.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting the public members of the IAC, for whom the bill establishes new removal protocols.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state agencies involved in the restructuring and the development of new life-cycle cost standards and P3 agreement reviews.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Architects in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2028, the termination provisions relating to certain statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Architects - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date for the State Board of Architects within the Maryland Department of Labor, allowing the board to continue its operations until July 1, 2028, in accordance with the Maryland Program Evaluation Act.
responsible_party: State Board of Architects, Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Individuals seeking architectural licensure, businesses practicing architecture, and the Maryland Department of Labor.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Architects are maintained through fiscal 2028. There is no impact on local government or small businesses. Specific dollar estimates for the maintained revenues and expenditures were not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is a regulatory body located within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the board's termination date, directly enabling the department to continue its mission of licensing and regulating the architectural profession.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is a permanent regulatory body that falls under this collective entity of executive-created boards and commissions. The bill specifically extends the statutory and regulatory authority of this board.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signed HB 463 into law. The Governor is responsible for the overall administration of the agencies and boards that regulate professional services in Maryland.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in filling vacancies on state boards. Extending the termination date of the State Board of Architects ensures that the office will continue to recruit and vet members for this board until 2028.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution. The bill maintains the board's special fund revenues and expenditures in the state budget for an additional five years, impacting long-term fiscal planning.

The bill is part of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act process, which requires evaluations of state boards. OLA is the agency responsible for conducting fiscal and performance audits that ensure these boards are operating efficiently and within the law.

Synopsis: Authorizing an individual under the age of 16 years to use a collapsible trap, net ring, handline, or dip net when catching or attempting to catch crabs in the waters of the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries without a recreational crabbing license.
Title: Natural Resources - Recreational Crabbing Gear - Individuals Under the Age of 16 Years

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill allows individuals under the age of 16 to catch crabs for recreational purposes in the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries using specific gear, such as collapsible traps, net rings, handlines, or dip nets, without the requirement of obtaining a recreational crabbing license.
stakeholders: Individuals under the age of 16 engaged in recreational crabbing and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a negligible impact on State finances. While there may be a slight decrease in license fee revenue from individuals under 16 who previously purchased licenses, this loss is considered immaterial. There is no fiscal impact on local governments, and the effect on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency, as it manages Maryland's fisheries and is responsible for adopting the regulations that will define the specific gear allowed for youth recreational crabbing.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources and will be responsible for reviewing the new crabbing regulations for legal sufficiency.
The Comptroller is the state's chief tax collector and revenue manager, responsible for overseeing the accounts into which recreational crabbing license fees are deposited.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state revenue estimation and budget execution, including monitoring any fiscal impacts on the state's special funds from changes in license fee requirements.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Natural Resources, and coordinates the implementation of policy initiatives related to natural resource management.

The Judicial Branch, supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, adjudicates citations and legal disputes related to natural resources violations, including potential enforcement issues involving recreational crabbing gear.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to allow a person in Worcester County to hunt game birds and game mammals on a Sunday, subject to certain time restrictions, during the open season for that game bird or game mammal; authorizing the Department to allow a person in Worcester County to hunt on public land designated for hunting on Sundays, subject to certain time restrictions; and altering the safety zone from 150 to 50 yards from certain buildings occupied by human beings within which archery hunting may not take place.
Title: Worcester County - Natural Resources - Hunting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill allows the Department of Natural Resources to authorize Sunday hunting for game birds and mammals in Worcester County on both private property and designated public land, typically restricted to the hours between 30 minutes before sunrise and 10:30 a.m. except during certain deer hunting seasons. Additionally, the bill reduces the required safety zone for archery hunting in Worcester County from 150 yards to 50 yards from occupied buildings.
stakeholders: Hunters in Worcester County, private landowners, agricultural businesses, and local retail and hospitality businesses catering to hunters.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances. While specific dollar estimates for increased revenue or expenditures are unavailable, the bill may have a minor positive economic impact on small businesses in Worcester County through increased hunter spending and potential reductions in agricultural crop damage.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department of Natural Resources is authorized by the bill to allow Sunday hunting in Worcester County and to manage the designation of public lands for such activities. The department is also responsible for regulating hunting safety zones.
The fiscal note indicates that the bill may affect businesses such as farms by potentially reducing deer populations and subsequent crop damage in Worcester County.

The Council is responsible for advocating for rural interests and addressing challenges in Maryland's rural counties, such as Worcester County. The expansion of hunting and its economic impact on local rural businesses falls within its scope of interest.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy coordination for all state agencies, including the Department of Natural Resources, which will implement the bill's provisions.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources regarding the implementation and enforcement of hunting regulations and statutory changes.
The Judiciary may be involved in the adjudication of violations related to the new hunting time restrictions or safety zone regulations established by the bill.

While the Natural Resources Police (within DNR) are the primary enforcers, the Maryland State Police provides support to allied law enforcement agencies and enforces state laws, which may include safety regulations related to the discharge of firearms.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the setting on fire or burning of oriented strand board for certain fire-fighting training; and establishing an administrative penalty not exceeding $500 for a first violation of the Act and a civil penalty not exceeding $1,000 for a second or subsequent violation of the Act.
Title: Environment - Fire-Fighting Training - Oriented Strand Board - Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits any person from setting on fire or burning oriented strand board (OSB) for the purpose of fire-fighting training. It establishes administrative penalties of up to $500 for a first violation and civil penalties of up to $1,000 for subsequent violations.
stakeholders: Fire departments, fire fighters, fire marshals, local environmental health agencies, and manufacturers or sellers of oriented strand board.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $57,100 in FY 2024 to hire one contractual environmental compliance specialist within the Maryland Department of the Environment for outreach, investigation, and enforcement. This cost is expected to continue through FY 2026. Local governments may experience increased costs to purchase alternative training materials; for instance, Prince George's County estimates an annual increase of $15,000. Potential minimal State and local costs may also arise from disposing of noncompliant materials. Penalty revenues are not expected to have a significant impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new section to the Environment Article and identifies the Department of the Environment (MDE) as the primary agency for enforcement, outreach, and investigations, necessitating a new contractual environmental compliance specialist position.

The Maryland State Police includes the Office of the State Fire Marshal, which regulates fire-fighting training and open burning; the agency was consulted regarding its training practices and the bill's impact on those operations.

The Department of Natural Resources oversees the Maryland Forest Service, which conducts fire management and training; the agency was consulted to determine if it uses oriented strand board for fire-fighting training.

The Department of Transportation, through the Maryland Aviation Administration, manages firefighting training for airport operations and was consulted as an information source regarding the bill's potential impact.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of the Environment and other state agencies regarding the implementation of the bill's new prohibitions and the enforcement of administrative and civil penalties.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for the state's personnel and budget oversight, specifically regarding the general fund expenditures and contractual staff required for MDE to implement the bill.
The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for the fiscal note as the bill establishes new civil penalties which may be adjudicated through the state court system.
The Department of General Services, which manages state facilities, was consulted as an information source for the fiscal note, although it reported no direct impact.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time that an area may be designated as a Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) zone from 5 to 10 years; increasing the number of RISE zones that the Secretary of Commerce may approve in Baltimore City to not more than four; extending the termination date of the RISE Program to January 1, 2030; and authorizing a political subdivision to pledge certain revenues to secure the payment of obligations to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation for infrastructure improvements located in a RISE zone.
Title: Economic Development – Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Zone Program – Alterations and Financing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone Program by extending its expiration date to January 1, 2030, and increasing the duration of a zone designation from 5 to 10 years. It increases the limit of RISE zones allowed in Baltimore City from three to four and authorizes local governments to pledge tax revenues to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) for infrastructure projects within these zones. The Department of Commerce is required to study the program's effectiveness and report its findings by December 15, 2024.
stakeholders: Qualified higher education institutions, innovative start-up businesses, Baltimore City, and Maryland counties and municipal corporations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected through fiscal 2028, although the fiscal 2024 budget includes $750,000 for rental assistance. Local revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 due to property tax credits, while MEDCO-related provisions may increase local and nonbudgeted State revenues and expenditures starting in fiscal 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for the RISE Zone Program. The Secretary of Commerce designates the zones, the department provides rental assistance matching funds, and is mandated by the bill to conduct a study on the program's effectiveness.

The bill explicitly adds RISE zones to the definition of 'MEDCO obligation' and authorizes political subdivisions to pledge revenues to secure MEDCO bonds for infrastructure improvements within these zones.
USM member institutions serve as 'qualified institutions' that can apply for RISE zone designations and participate in the program's rental assistance grants for businesses.
Morgan State is a 'qualified institution' that may anchor a RISE zone and benefit from the program's incentives for innovation-based businesses in its proximity.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College is a 'qualified institution' eligible to anchor a RISE zone and engage in associated economic development activities.
The Comptroller administers the state's tax laws and is responsible for managing the enhanced biotechnology and innovation investment incentive tax credits associated with the RISE Zone Program.
DBM oversees state budget execution, including the general fund appropriations for the Department of Commerce's rental assistance matching funds.
MHEC is the regulatory board for the higher education institutions that act as the anchor 'qualified institutions' for the RISE Zone Program.
The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Commerce, and the bill requires a report on program effectiveness to be submitted to the General Assembly.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Commerce and MEDCO, regarding the implementation and statutory changes of the RISE Zone Program.
The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and debt; the bill's provisions regarding the pledging of local revenues for MEDCO obligations intersect with state financial oversight.
The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and fiscal integrity, which may include infrastructure projects or state-backed financing tied to RISE zones.
RISE zones are targeted for increased economic and community development, which aligns with DHCD's mission regarding community revitalization and infrastructure financing.
The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and land use, which are relevant to the geographic designation and infrastructure development of RISE zones.

Synopsis: Requiring, on or before August 1, 2024, certain public senior higher education institutions, in consultation with students, to develop and implement a reproductive health services plan to provide at the institution or to refer students to a comprehensive range of reproductive health services; requiring the University of Baltimore, in lieu of developing and implementing a reproductive health services plan, to provide students with access to over-the-counter contraception through certain on-campus means; etc.
Title: Public Senior Higher Education Institutions - Reproductive Health Services Plans - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland public senior higher education institutions to develop and implement reproductive health services plans by August 1, 2024, in consultation with students. These plans must include access to or referrals for services such as FDA-approved contraception, STI prevention and treatment, and abortion care, as well as 24-hour access to over-the-counter contraception on campus. The University of Baltimore is permitted to provide access to over-the-counter contraception through retail outlets or vending machines in lieu of a full plan. The Maryland Department of Health is required to provide assistance to institutions in developing these plans upon request.
responsible_party: Public senior higher education institutions (including the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland) and the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Students attending Maryland public senior higher education institutions
fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures will increase to implement the required reproductive health plans, with material impacts likely in fiscal 2024 for one-time costs like vending machine installation. To offset these costs, higher education revenues may increase if institutions choose to charge student fees. The Maryland Department of Health can likely provide assistance using existing budgeted resources, though more extensive consultation could lead to an increase in general fund expenditures. Specific dollar estimates for the total impact are not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill may impact higher education expenditures and revenues, particularly related to the setup costs for reproductive health services and vending machines. As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the budget execution for these state institutions.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide assistance to public senior higher education institutions in developing their reproductive health services plans upon request.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the various public senior higher education institutions (USM, Morgan State, and St. Mary's College) tasked with implementing these plans.
As the state's coordinating board for higher education, the Commission establishes statewide policies and was listed as an information source regarding the impact on institutions.
The agency serves as the regulatory and coordinating board for Maryland's colleges and universities and is responsible for establishing statewide policies that affect these institutions.
The bill explicitly names Morgan State University as one of the public senior higher education institutions required to develop and implement a reproductive health services plan.

The Office of Legislative Audits is responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of state agencies, which would include the public universities' adherence to the funding and execution requirements of these plans.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Health and the public higher education institutions, regarding the implementation and legal compliance of reproductive health services plans.
The bill explicitly names St. Mary's College of Maryland as one of the public senior higher education institutions required to develop and implement a reproductive health services plan.

The bill explicitly names the constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (with specific requirements for the University of Baltimore) as entities required to develop and implement reproductive health services plans.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Veterans Affairs to bury the eligible spouse or dependent of a veteran in a State veterans' cemetery without charge.
Title: Department of Veterans Affairs - Burial in State Veterans' Cemeteries - Spouses and Dependents

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs to provide burial services and grave liners for the eligible spouses and dependents of veterans in State veterans' cemeteries at no cost, prohibiting the department from charging fees for opening and closing the burial plot.
stakeholders: Eligible spouses and dependents of veterans, and Maryland veterans.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately 1240000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 because the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs will no longer collect burial fees for spouses and dependents. General fund expenditures are expected to increase by an equivalent amount to backfill the Cemetery Program and maintain its operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary implementer of the bill, responsible for the burial program and cemetery management, and faces a significant loss of special fund revenue and increased general fund reliance.
As the principal fiscal agency, it must manage the $1.24 million annual general fund expenditure increase required to backfill the MDVA Cemetery Program due to the loss of burial fee revenue.

The Governor oversees the executive branch including the Department of Veterans Affairs and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which must now account for this program's funding shift.
This body is explicitly required by the bill text (Section 9-906(c)) to approve any land acquisition or acceptance for the state veterans' cemeteries.
Provides legal counsel to state agencies and would assist the Department of Veterans Affairs in interpreting and implementing the federal eligibility standards cited in the bill.
Serves as the Governor's senior military advisor; the bill's definition of 'veteran' specifically includes members of the state militia under presidential orders.
As the state's chief financial officer, the agency oversees the collection of revenues and expenditures impacted by the shift from special fund fees to general fund support for burials.
Responsible for the management of state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works, which approves the acquisition of land for the state veterans' cemeteries.
Responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of state agencies, including the Department of Veterans Affairs, to ensure proper handling of the new fee-free burial requirements.
Provides operational support, facilities management, and real estate services for state-owned properties, which include the five veterans' cemeteries managed by MDVA.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain previous convictions for drunk or drugged operation of a vehicle or vessel and grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel under certain provisions of law constitute prior convictions for the purpose of determining certain enhanced subsequent offender penalties.
Title: Grossly Negligent or Drunk or Drugged Operation of Vehicle or Vessel - Prior Convictions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes that prior convictions for specified drunk or drugged driving offenses and grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel count as prior convictions for determining enhanced subsequent offender penalties for operating a vessel while under the influence or impaired. Reciprocally, convictions for operating a vessel while under the influence or impaired count as prior convictions for determining subsequent offender penalties for drunk or drugged driving violations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources and Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Operators of motor vehicles or vessels in Maryland with current or prior convictions for impaired operation or gross negligence manslaughter
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates a potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from fines and a minimal increase in general fund expenditures due to longer sentences in State facilities. Local revenues may increase minimally from fines, while local expenditures may decrease minimally if individuals are shifted from local detention to State correctional facilities. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the volume of individuals subject to these enhanced penalties is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the Judicial Branch as judges must determine if a defendant is a subsequent offender based on the new criteria establishing prior convictions across vehicle and vessel operation offenses.
The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article, which the department oversees, specifically regarding the penalties for operating a vessel while under the influence or impaired.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is responsible for the supervision and incarceration of justice-involved individuals; the bill's enhanced penalties for subsequent offenders may affect the length of sentences and correctional facility populations.

The bill directly amends the Transportation Article regarding drunk and drugged driving offenses, establishing how prior convictions from vessel operation are counted toward subsequent offender penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and advises on criminal justice strategies, including sentencing and recidivism policies impacted by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent defendants who will be subject to the expanded criteria for subsequent offender penalties established by the bill.
The State Police are responsible for enforcing motor vehicle and criminal laws related to impaired driving and are essential in the investigation and reporting of these offenses.

As part of the Department of Transportation, the MVA maintains driving records and handles vehicle services; these records are essential for determining the prior conviction history required for subsequent offender sentencing.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Police, DNR, and MDOT, regarding the enforcement and interpretation of the amended criminal and transportation laws.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation to collect information from each local board of education on nonpublic school student busing programs other than for the transportation of students in special education; and requiring the Task Force to report by December 15, 2023, to certain committees of the General Assembly any recommendations as to how the State may support a reduction in the use of passenger vehicles for nonpublic school students and policies for certain busing programs.
Title: Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation

Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation. The task force is charged with collecting information from local boards of education regarding existing nonpublic student busing programs, evaluating the potential impact of various transportation models (such as tax credits or the use of public school buses for nonpublic students) on state revenue and safety, and making recommendations to the General Assembly regarding policies to support nonpublic student transportation.
stakeholders: Nonpublic school students and their families, nonpublic school administrators, local boards of education, and school bus drivers and contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Any expense reimbursements for task force members and staffing costs for the Maryland State Department of Education are expected to be absorbed into current budgets. There is no projected impact on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for the Task Force. Two of its directors are named members, the Director of the Office of Pupil Transportation and Emergency Management chairs the Task Force, and the agency is mandated to provide staffing support.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation, which is a temporary body created by the General Assembly to address specific policy issues, fitting the definition of this collective entity.

The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee, is a designated member of the Task Force. The Task Force's work directly involves evaluating student transportation, traffic congestion, and safety goals within the state's transportation network.
The Task Force is specifically required to consult with the Comptroller to evaluate the potential impact of a State income tax credit for student bus transportation expenses.

The bill provides for reimbursement of Task Force member expenses under the Standard State Travel Regulations, which are overseen by DBM, and the agency manages the state budget through which these funds are allocated.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the departments (MSDE, MDOT) involved in the Task Force and signed the bill into law.

Synopsis: Altering the number of years that a school vehicle may be operated in Anne Arundel County from 12 years to 15 years.
Title: Anne Arundel County - School Vehicles - Duration of Operation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum duration a school vehicle may be operated in Anne Arundel County from 12 years to 15 years, provided the vehicle meets applicable safety standards and maintenance requirements.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Public School System
stakeholders: Students, school bus contractors, and the Anne Arundel County Public School System.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State finances or the finances and operations of the Anne Arundel County Public School System.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article of the Maryland Code, specifically regarding the operational lifespan of school vehicles. The State Superintendent of Schools, who leads this department, is responsible for granting the final approval for school vehicles to operate beyond the standard 12-year limit.

The MVA is directly tasked with approving preventive maintenance plans, approving independent experts for structural repair certifications, and performing mandatory semi-annual inspections for school vehicles in their 13th through 15th years of operation.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT oversees the regulatory framework and safety standards for all motor vehicles in Maryland, including the school buses affected by the operational duration changes in this bill.

The bill requires the Automotive Safety Enforcement Division of the Maryland State Police to jointly approve preventive maintenance plans for school vehicles that are authorized to operate for more than 12 years.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education focused on comprehensive school safety, this agency has a peripheral interest in the mechanical safety and maintenance standards of vehicles used to transport students.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies responsible for implementing these vehicle standards and the Governor signed this specific legislation into law.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Department of Education from increasing the copayment levels, reducing the reimbursement rates, reducing the income eligibility requirements, or implementing an enrollment freeze for the Child Care Scholarship Program in effect as of January 1, 2023, unless certain conditions are met.
Title: Early Childhood Development - Child Care Scholarship Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland State Department of Education from increasing copayments, reducing reimbursement rates, lowering income eligibility, or freezing enrollment for the Child Care Scholarship Program without following a specific legislative notification process. It further mandates that, starting in fiscal year 2025, the Governor must include enough funding in the state budget to provide subsidies for all eligible individuals.
stakeholders: Low-income families eligible for child care assistance and private child care providers (small businesses).
fiscal_impact_summary: The State fiscal impact is indeterminate but potentially significant starting in fiscal 2025. While there is no anticipated impact in fiscal 2024, the bill limits the state's ability to reduce program costs through enrollment freezes or rate adjustments, which may increase general fund expenditures once supplemental federal funding expires. No local impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary administrator of the Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program, MSDE is responsible for conducting market rate surveys, setting reimbursement rates, determining income eligibility, and notifying the Comptroller for provider payments.
The bill mandates that the Governor include sufficient funds in the annual state budget starting in FY 2025 to cover all eligible individuals and maintain specific reimbursement percentiles.
The bill grants MSDE the authority to bypass legislative waiting periods for program alterations if the Board of Public Works approves budget reductions for the program.
The bill establishes a strict statutory timeline requiring the Comptroller to pay child care providers within 5 days of receiving notice from MSDE.

DBM oversees budget execution and development; the bill's requirement for 'sufficient' funding for all eligible individuals poses significant long-term fiscal planning and sustainability implications for the agency.
Eligibility for copay waivers is linked to participation in DHS-administered programs like SNAP and Temporary Cash Assistance, requiring inter-agency coordination for eligibility verification.
Eligibility for copay waivers is linked to participation in the WIC program, which is typically supported or coordinated by public health departments.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which has a specific role in approving budget reductions that allow for immediate program adjustments.
The bill directly addresses child care affordability and access, which are core components of GOC's mission to reduce child poverty and improve child well-being.

Synopsis: Repealing the provisions of law establishing and governing the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot; and requiring the Governor to provide an appropriation in the State budget for fiscal year 2024 and each fiscal year thereafter to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.
Title: Rural Health Collaborative Pilot Repeal and Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill repeals the laws establishing the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot and instead requires the Governor to provide an annual budget appropriation to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition starting in fiscal year 2024.
responsible_party: The Governor and the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Residents, health care providers, and local health departments in the mid-shore region, specifically Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Talbot counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, general fund expenditures of $150,000 annually are maintained beyond fiscal year 2023 but shift from the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot to the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. Local revenues and expenditures are likewise maintained but redirected to the coalition.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot, which was established as an independent unit within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). It also adds a new subtitle to the Health - General Article requiring budget funding for the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition, which falls under the department's public health purview.

The bill mandates an annual appropriation in the State budget for the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. DBM is responsible for developing the state's budget and was previously involved in personnel classification for the pilot being repealed.

The bill specifically requires the Governor to provide an annual appropriation in the State budget for the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. The Governor is also responsible for oversaw the executive branch units being modified by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot, which functioned as a regional collaborative body created by the General Assembly to coordinate health services and expertise in the mid-shore region.
The MHCC is explicitly mentioned in the repealed sections of the bill regarding its authority to regulate health care facilities in conjunction with the pilot program being abolished.
The HSCRC is explicitly mentioned in the repealed sections of the bill regarding its regulatory authority over health care institutions in conjunction with the pilot program being abolished.

The Rural Maryland Council is tasked with addressing challenges in rural counties, specifically healthcare access. The bill fundamentally alters the funding and governance of a rural health initiative across five Eastern Shore counties.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Public Works, for meetings held on or after October 1, 2024, to allow members of the public to submit certain public comments electronically except under certain circumstances; requiring public comments to be included in certain meeting materials and posted and retained online; and requiring an additional staff position at the Board to carry out requirements of the Act.
Title: Board of Public Works Public Comment Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: This bill requires the Board of Public Works to allow members of the public to submit electronic comments on agenda items for meetings held on or after October 1, 2024. These comments must be included in meeting packets, posted on the board's website at least 24 hours before the meeting, and retained online. To implement these requirements, the Board is mandated to hire at least one additional staff position.
stakeholders: Members of the public wishing to comment on Board of Public Works agenda items and the staff and members of the Board of Public Works.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $227,417 in FY 2024 for the Board of Public Works to hire one computer operator manager and cover one-time technology costs for a new web portal. Ongoing general fund expenditures are estimated at $92,200 in FY 2025, rising to $105,900 by FY 2028 to cover salary, benefits, and operating expenses. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill is the primary subject of the legislation, which mandates changes to its meeting procedures, requires the creation of an electronic public comment system, and authorizes an additional staff position to manage these requirements.
The Governor is one of the three members of the Board of Public Works; the Governor's Office provides administrative support for the Governor's executive duties, including their role on the Board.
The Comptroller is one of the three members of the Board of Public Works and will be directly affected by changes to meeting procedures and the inclusion of public comments in board materials.
The State Treasurer is one of the three members of the Board of Public Works and will be directly affected by changes to meeting procedures and the inclusion of public comments in board materials.
As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is involved in the authorization of the new staff position mandated by the bill and the allocation of general funds for its implementation.
The fiscal note indicates that DoIT will likely be responsible for administering the new web portal required for electronic public comments on a fee-for-service basis for the Board of Public Works.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions and would advise the Board of Public Works on compliance with the new public comment requirements and the Open Meetings Act.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Human Services to restore to a beneficiary any benefits lost due to theft; authorizing certain households to request a hearing within 90 days after a certain determination; requiring the State to give preference to certain vendors in the procurement process for electronic benefits distribution or administration; authorizing the Department to restore certain benefits; requiring the Department to take certain actions to reduce the vulnerability of Electronic Benefits Transfer cards to theft; etc.
Title: Department of Human Services - Electronic Benefits Transfer Cards - Theft of Benefits (Prevent Electronic Benefits Theft Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) to reimburse or restore benefits lost by households due to the theft or fraudulent use of Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cards, including theft through skimming, cloning, or physical theft. It mandates that DHS automatically restore benefits upon verification, provide a new EBT card within 10 days of a report, and implement security enhancements such as embedded microchips and two-way fraud alerts. The bill also establishes a process for administrative hearings and requires annual reporting to the General Assembly on EBT card security and theft statistics.
stakeholders: Recipients of EBT-based benefits (including SNAP, TCA, TDAP, and PAA), the Department of Human Services, EBT distribution vendors, and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are estimated to increase by up to $1,900,000 in FY 2023, $6,200,000 in FY 2024, and $4,200,000 annually thereafter for benefit restorations. Federal fund revenues increase to offset specific SNAP-related restorations through FY 2025 ($1,130,000 in FY 2023 and $4,400,000 in FY 2024). The FY 2024 budget included $11,400,000 for these reimbursements. Local law enforcement agencies can handle reporting requirements with existing resources. Procurement preferences for vendors with identity theft insurance may impact contract costs, though specific estimates for these costs are currently unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary agency responsible for administering the Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) system in Maryland. The bill directly mandates DHS to restore stolen benefits, establish investigation protocols, provide new EBT cards, and report annually on benefit theft statistics.

The bill explicitly requires DHS to consult with the Maryland State Police to establish points of contact for investigations, screen for unusual charges, and develop annual reports on the security of EBT cards and the frequency of fraudulent use.

As the central procurement authority, DGS is responsible for the contracting changes mandated by the bill, including establishing templates and guidelines for EBT vendor solicitations that prioritize insurance and identity protection technologies.

DoIT oversees state cybersecurity and IT infrastructure. The bill requires significant technical upgrades to EBT systems, including embedded microchips, multifactor authentication, and two-way fraud alerts, which fall under DoIT's strategic and security oversight.

DBM is responsible for the state's fiscal planning. The bill has a significant fiscal impact, increasing expenditures by millions of dollars annually for benefit restoration, which requires coordination with DBM for budget execution and planning.

The bill allows EBT beneficiaries to request administrative hearings to dispute DHS decisions regarding benefit restoration. OAH is the independent agency that adjudicates these types of contested cases for state departments.

The Board of Public Works must approve the significant state procurement contracts for EBT distribution and administration. The bill’s new requirements for vendor preferences and insurance will directly affect the procurement approvals overseen by the Board.

The OAG provides legal counsel to DHS. It will likely assist in drafting regulations for the new reimbursement process, ensuring compliance with the 'Prevent Electronic Benefits Theft Act,' and representing the state in legal challenges or appeals.

The Department of Aging supports older adults who are frequent recipients of the benefits (like SNAP) managed via EBT cards. The bill specifically requires reporting on demographic data for households with members at least 60 years old.

Many individuals with disabilities rely on the cash and food assistance programs mentioned in the bill (such as TDAP). The protections against benefit theft directly impact the financial security of the population this department serves.

The GOC focuses on reducing child poverty. The bill's restoration of EBT benefits for families is a direct mechanism for economic mobility and food security for households with children, which are a specific demographic mentioned in the bill's reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety and criminal justice strategies. EBT theft and skimming are specific criminal activities that fall under the office's broader mandate to advise the Governor on crime reduction and victim services.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies. OLA will likely review DHS's compliance with the bill's reimbursement mandates and the management of the multi-million dollar funds allocated for benefit restoration.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments (DHS, MSP, DoIT) implementing this act and is responsible for the policy initiatives and annual budget proposals that will include these benefit restoration costs.
