bill_summary: This bill establishes the Greenspace Equity Program within the Department of Natural Resources to provide grants to local governments and nonprofit organizations for the purpose of preserving, creating, and enhancing community greenspaces—such as parks, gardens, and urban farms—in overburdened and underserved communities.
stakeholders: Residents of overburdened and underserved communities, local governments, land trusts, and nongovernmental organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,000 in FY 2024 and $365,700 in FY 2025 for administrative staffing. Program Open Space special funds are redirected for program grants, with annual allocations of $5,000,000 in FY 2025, $7,000,000 in FY 2026, and up to $10,000,000 starting in FY 2027. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase if they apply for and receive grants under the program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department of Natural Resources is responsible for establishing, administering, and staffing the Greenspace Equity Program and its Advisory Board.
The agency operates the Maryland State Clearinghouse for Intergovernmental Assistance required for grant reviews, and its Secretary must approve any future land conversions under the program.
The Board of Public Works is mandated to review and provide final approval for all grant awards recommended by the program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board as a new advisory body within the executive branch to oversee program implementation.
The Secretary of Budget and Management must approve land conversions, and the agency oversees the redirection of Program Open Space funds required to finance the grants.
The Department is a statutory reviewer required to provide comment and expertise on grant applications for the Greenspace Equity Program.
The Department is designated as a statutory reviewer to evaluate how greenspace projects impact public health in underserved communities.
The agency is a statutory reviewer for grant applications, reflecting its role in community revitalization and urban development.
The Governor serves on the Board of Public Works for grant approvals and is responsible for appointing members to the new Advisory Board.
The Comptroller serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which must approve all grant expenditures under the program.
The State Treasurer serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which must approve all grant expenditures under the program.
The Commission shares Program Open Space fund allocations that are being redirected to finance the new Greenspace Equity Program.
The bill utilizes definitions of 'overburdened' and 'underserved' communities based on environmental health indicators managed by this Department.
This office assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the newly established Greenspace Equity Advisory Board.
The program aligns with this initiative's mission to coordinate multi-agency efforts for sustainable land use and community preservation.
This agency will be responsible for fiscal and performance audits of the new grant program as part of its oversight of DNR and Program Open Space.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council as an independent unit of State government with the authority to conduct and support advocacy, systems change, and capacity-building efforts to promote inclusive communities and equity in services for individuals with disabilities in the State, research best practices and provide related training and technical assistance to communities in the State, and inform State and local leaders about disability issues.
Title: Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council - Establishment

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council as an independent unit of State government. It codifies the council's duties, which include developing and implementing a five-year strategic plan, conducting advocacy and systems change efforts, researching best practices, and advising state and local leaders on policies affecting individuals with developmental disabilities and their families.
stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities and their families, guardians, and advocates, along with state agencies and nonprofit organizations involved in disability services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill codifies an existing council that is fully funded under the federal Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act of 2000. According to the fiscal note, there is no additional State fiscal impact because the council's budget and staff are already supported by federal funds administered through the Governor’s Office of Financial Administration. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing all members of the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council. Furthermore, the council serves in an advisory capacity to the Governor, and the Governor's Office of Financial Administration currently manages the federal funds allocated to the council.

Multiple officials from the Department of Health are mandated members of the council, including the Deputy Secretary of the Developmental Disabilities Administration and representatives from the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill's provisions are also codified within the Health - General Article of the Annotated Code.

The Secretary of Disabilities is a statutory member of the council. The council's mission to conduct research and advocacy for individuals with disabilities directly intersects with the department's role as the principal state agency for disability services and policy coordination.
The bill mandates that both the State Superintendent of Schools and the Assistant State Superintendent of the Division of Rehabilitation Services (or their designees) serve on the council.

The Secretary of Aging is designated as a member of the council. The fiscal note indicates that this represents a new requirement for the department to participate in this specific council's activities.

This office assists the Governor in fulfilling the statutory requirement to appoint qualified individuals to the council, ensuring the membership meets the specific demographic and professional criteria outlined in the bill and federal law.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to independent units of government and state agencies, including the newly codified Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council.

As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is relevant to the council's operations as an independent unit of government, though the bill includes provisions protecting the council from interference in its budget and personnel management.

Synopsis: Establishing that an elevator installed in a privately owned single-family residential dwelling on or after October 1, 2023, is subject to certain inspection and registration requirements; prohibiting the Commissioner of Labor and Industry from disclosing to the public any information regarding a registered elevator unit installed in a privately owned single-family residential dwelling; and requiring the Commissioner to delete certain registration information on the completion of the final acceptance inspection on a certain unit.
Title: Elevator Safety - Privately Owned Single-Family Residential Elevators - Inspection and Registration Requirements
bill_summary: This bill requires that elevator units installed in privately owned single-family residential dwellings on or after October 1, 2023, be registered with the Commissioner of Labor and Industry and undergo a final acceptance inspection before being placed into service. The bill also provides privacy protections by prohibiting the public disclosure of registration information and requiring the deletion of registration records once the final inspection is complete.
stakeholders: Owners and lessees of single-family residences with new elevator installations, elevator mechanics and contractors, and the Maryland Department of Labor.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Maryland Department of Labor special fund expenditures increase by $171,928 in FY 2024 to hire two inspectors and cover administrative costs, with annual expenditures rising to $235,500 by FY 2028. Special fund revenues from inspection fees are estimated to increase by $109,700 in FY 2024 and approximately $146,300 annually thereafter. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Commissioner of Labor and Industry, a division of the Department of Labor, to register and perform final acceptance inspections for newly installed residential elevators. The department is responsible for enforcing these safety standards, managing registration data, and hiring additional inspectors as specified in the fiscal note.

According to the fiscal note, the Maryland Department of Labor's Elevator Safety Inspection Unit is funded via an appropriation from the Workers' Compensation Commission. The bill's implementation requires additional expenditures and personnel, which may necessitate an increase in employer assessments by the Commission to cover these costs.

As the state agency responsible for budget development and personnel management, DBM will oversee the creation of two new inspector positions and manage the fiscal execution of the special fund expenditures and revenues associated with the bill's implementation.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor. It would be responsible for advising the department on the implementation and enforcement of the new safety regulations and the specific non-disclosure and data deletion requirements for residential registrations.

Synopsis: Requiring a county or municipal corporation to define, by law, who is a law enforcement officer or rescue worker; altering eligibility for the tax credit to include certain disabled law enforcement officers or rescue workers who were domiciled in the State as, or any time within the 5 years before the officer or worker died or was determined to be disabled; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Property Tax Credit - Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers - Definition and Eligibility

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland counties and municipal corporations to legally define 'law enforcement officer' and 'rescue worker' for the purpose of property tax credit eligibility. It also expands eligibility for the local property tax credit to include disabled law enforcement officers, rescue workers, or their surviving spouses and cohabitants who were Maryland residents at any point within the five years preceding the individual's death or permanent disability.
responsible_party: Local governing bodies (counties and municipal corporations)
stakeholders: Disabled law enforcement officers, rescue workers, surviving spouses, cohabitants of fallen officers/workers, and Maryland local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Local property tax revenues may decrease starting in fiscal 2024 to the extent that local governments authorize the credit and additional taxpayers become eligible. The specific fiscal impact is indeterminate as it depends on the number of qualifying individuals and the assessed value of their properties within each jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the executive head of state, the Governor signed this bill into law and oversees the administrative support for the executive branch, which includes the agencies employing the law enforcement and correctional officers referenced in the bill.
The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, maintaining a high-level interest in all tax-related legislation, including local property tax credits.
The department employs the Natural Resources Police; these law enforcement officers and their families could be beneficiaries of the property tax credit addressed in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references correctional officers in the definition of those eligible for the disabled or fallen officer tax credit. As the employer of these officers, the department has a significant interest in the benefits available to its workforce.
MDOT oversees several law enforcement units, including the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) Police, whose members are eligible for the property tax credit modified by this bill.
As the state's primary law enforcement agency, its officers (State Troopers) are key subjects of the bill's provisions regarding disability and line-of-duty death property tax credits.
The Tax Court adjudicates appeals from final decisions of state and local taxing authorities, which could include disputes over eligibility for this specific property tax credit.

This agency specifically handles administrative reviews for property tax assessment disputes and disputes over property tax credits, making it highly relevant to any conflicts arising from the implementation of this credit.

The agency manages disability benefits for law enforcement and correctional officers; it may serve as the administrative body mentioned in the bill that determines if an officer is permanently and totally disabled.
The Commission adjudicates claims for compensation from workplace injuries and determines disability status, which is a prerequisite for eligibility for the property tax credit described in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency oversees the state's EMS network. EMS personnel fall under the 'rescue worker' category defined in the bill, meaning the agency's constituent workforce is directly impacted by the eligibility changes.
The OAH may conduct hearings for administrative disputes involving state agencies' determinations of disability for their employees, which is a core eligibility requirement for the credit.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to publish municipal election results on its website immediately after a municipality submits its election results; and requiring, within 30 days after the results of a municipal election are certified, the municipality to submit to the State Board an electronic copy of the election results for each office or question voted on at the election.
Title: State Board of Elections - Municipal Elections - Publication of Results on Website

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland municipalities to submit electronic copies of their election results to the State Board of Elections (SBE) within 30 days of certification. The SBE is required to establish an electronic portal on its website for these submissions and must publish the results, organized by election year and municipality, immediately upon receipt. The reports must include vote totals by method (early voting, mail-in, provisional, and election day) and candidate party affiliations for partisan elections.
stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, municipal candidates, the Maryland State Board of Elections, and Maryland voters.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. The State Board of Elections and local municipalities are expected to manage the requirements for portal maintenance, submission, and publication of results using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, including establishing an electronic portal and publishing municipal election results on its website.
As the agency responsible for the state's IT strategy and digital services, they oversee the standards and infrastructure for the new portal and web publication mandated by the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for assessing the fiscal impact of the bill and overseeing the budget execution for the State Board of Elections as it implements the new portal.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections regarding compliance with statutory requirements and the legal implementation of the portal.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies, including the State Board of Elections, and coordinates policy initiatives related to government transparency and election integrity.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to enforce certain prevailing wage requirements for contractors and subcontractors working on projects involving and traffic control activities related to underground gas or electric infrastructure of an investor-owned gas company, electric company, or gas and electric company; requiring certain contractors and subcontractors to request from the Department a copy of a certain wage determination and ensure that employees are paid in compliance with existing prevailing wage rates; etc.
Title: Investor-Owned Utilities - Prevailing Wage - Enforcement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Labor to enforce prevailing wage requirements for contractors and subcontractors working on underground gas or electric infrastructure projects for investor-owned utilities. It mandates that these employers request wage determinations from the department and ensures employees are paid accordingly, while providing a grace period for compliance through March 2024 to avoid civil penalties.
stakeholders: Contractors, subcontractors, and employees working on underground gas or electric infrastructure projects for investor-owned gas and electric companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, primarily through complaint investigations by the Division of Labor and Industry. There is no material impact on state revenues or local government finances. Small business impacts are expected to be minimal as the requirement for these utilities to pay prevailing wages already existed under previous law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Maryland Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry with enforcing prevailing wage requirements for investor-owned utility projects, providing guidance to contractors, and conducting wage surveys.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article and clarifies that enforcement of prevailing wage for underground utility projects rests with the Department of Labor rather than through Public Service Commission regulatory mechanisms.

The OAG serves as the legal representative for the State and provides counsel to both the Department of Labor and the Public Service Commission regarding the enforcement and interpretation of these laws.
The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies; disputes regarding prevailing wage enforcement or civil penalties issued by the Department of Labor would likely be heard by this agency.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives related to labor standards and ensures interagency coordination between Labor and the Public Service Commission.

DBM oversees the fiscal and personnel resources of state agencies; while the fiscal note indicates the bill can be handled with existing resources, DBM is responsible for monitoring these budget impacts.

Synopsis: Altering the date from February 1, 2020 and each February 1 thereafter, to July 1 each year, on which the Department of Agriculture must submit to the General Assembly a certain annual report regarding the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry to the General Assembly.
Title: Agriculture - Use of Antimicrobial Drugs - Reporting Deadlines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill changes the annual deadline for the Maryland Department of Agriculture to submit its report to the General Assembly regarding the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry, moving the date from February 1 to July 1.
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Agriculture, licensed veterinarians, and owners of farm operations raising cattle, swine, or poultry.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the change is procedural and does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary agency responsible for collecting data on antimicrobial drug use in livestock and submitting the annual report to the General Assembly. This bill directly alters the agency's statutory reporting deadline.

The bill regulates reporting on medically important antimicrobial drugs. Because antimicrobial resistance is a significant public health concern, the data collected and reported by the Department of Agriculture is highly relevant to the Department of Health's mission to protect public health and set health policy.
The Council advocates for rural and agricultural interests. Changes to the reporting deadlines for livestock drug use affect the agricultural community and stakeholders that the Council represents.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Agriculture and coordinates the state's policy initiatives, including the approval and implementation of legislative changes to agency mandates.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Agriculture, assisting the agency in complying with statutory reporting requirements and interpreting legislative changes.

The Office of Legislative Audits conducts compliance audits of state agencies. A change in the statutory deadline for a required report alters the compliance criteria used during audits of the Department of Agriculture.

Synopsis: Establishing an art establishment beer and wine license in the City of Annapolis; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to sell or serve beer and wine for on-premises consumption to a nonprofit organization primarily engaged in certain arts-related activities; and providing for a license fee of $1,000.
Title: City of Annapolis - Alcoholic Beverages - Art Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill creates a new art establishment beer and wine license in the City of Annapolis, which allows eligible nonprofit organizations primarily engaged in the arts—such as those involved in art display, instruction, or live performances—to sell or serve beer and wine for on-premises consumption. The annual fee for this license is set at $1,000.
responsible_party: City of Annapolis Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Nonprofit art organizations and live performance venues in the City of Annapolis.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not affected. For the City of Annapolis, local revenues are expected to decrease because nonprofit organizations may switch from purchasing multiple special event licenses to a single $1,000 annual license; for context, the city received approximately $9,950 from 138 event license applications in 2022. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state agency responsible for regulating the alcohol, tobacco, and motor fuel industries. As this bill establishes a new class of alcoholic beverage license, it falls under the general regulatory and revenue-collection oversight of the Comptroller's Office.

The Maryland Department of Commerce oversees the state's tourism and arts sectors. This bill specifically impacts nonprofit art establishments and live performance venues, which are core components of the arts and cultural economy that the Department is tasked with promoting.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland Stadium Authority; establishing the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund and the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund to enable the Maryland Stadium Authority to take certain actions; requiring the Authority to administer the funds; altering the amount the Comptroller is required to distribute from the State Lottery Fund to certain funds; establishing the Bus Rapid Transit Fund to provide grants to eligible grantees; etc.
Title: Maryland Stadium Authority - Camden Yards Sports Facilities Funds and Bus Rapid Transit Fund

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill establishes two supplemental financing funds for the Maryland Stadium Authority (MSA) to manage lottery revenue for Camden Yards' baseball and football facilities. It also creates the Bus Rapid Transit Fund (BRTF) within the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to provide grants for transit systems, requiring a minimum annual distribution of $20 million to Montgomery County if eligible. Additionally, the bill increases the membership of the MSA, modifies the definition of the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor, and adjusts lottery revenue distribution schedules.
responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority and Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Maryland residents, local governments (particularly Montgomery and Prince George’s counties), the Maryland Stadium Authority, the Maryland Department of Transportation, and professional sports teams in the Baltimore metropolitan region.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by $14.2 million in FY 2024 due to a reduction in lottery distributions to the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT). MDOT special fund revenues and expenditures decrease by a corresponding $14.2 million in FY 2024. The bill reallocates up to $90 million in annual lottery revenues to new stadium financing funds. Locally, Montgomery County revenues and expenditures decrease by $14.2 million in FY 2024, but the county is guaranteed a minimum $20 million annual grant from the Bus Rapid Transit Fund starting in FY 2025, provided it remains an eligible grantee.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Stadium Authority is the primary subject of the bill, which alters its membership, establishes and requires it to administer the Camden Yards Football and Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Funds, and adjusts definitions related to the Prince George’s County Blue Line Corridor facilities.

The bill establishes the Bus Rapid Transit Fund within the Department of Transportation and mandates the department to administer the fund and award grants to eligible grantees, including specific distribution requirements for Montgomery County.

The Comptroller is responsible for distributing State Lottery Funds to the newly established stadium supplemental financing funds and the Bus Rapid Transit Fund, and is tasked with accounting for these funds.
The State Treasurer is mandated to hold the Camden Yards and Bus Rapid Transit Funds separately and invest the money in these funds in the same manner as other state funds.
The fiscal note indicates that the Board of Public Works must approve Maryland Stadium Authority bond issues and comprehensive financing plans, which are central components of this bill.

The Governor is responsible for appointing seven members to the Maryland Stadium Authority (an increase of one) and oversees the executive departments (MDOT, Comptroller, and MSA) implementing the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the distribution of revenue from the State Lottery Fund, which is regulated and operated by this agency.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment and vetting of candidates for the expanded membership of the Maryland Stadium Authority board.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is involved in the long-term fiscal planning and budget execution related to the mandated lottery fund distributions and the establishment of new special funds.

Synopsis: Establishing the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program in the State Department of Education to license outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs to expand access to affordable, high-quality early learning and child care programs and investigate the benefits of outdoor, nature-based classrooms; requiring the Department to submit a final report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2027, with recommendations for modifying or expanding the Program; etc.
Title: Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds
Primary Schools -see also- Education; Private or Public Sch.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program within the Maryland State Department of Education to license outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs. The program aims to expand access to affordable, high-quality care and research the educational benefits of outdoor classrooms.
stakeholders: Outdoor nature-based early learning and child care providers, children, and families.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the pilot program using existing resources. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances. Participating small businesses in the child care sector may experience a meaningful positive benefit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency tasked with administering the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program, the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is responsible for promulgating regulations, selecting pilot participants, and submitting reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
The bill requires the Department of Education to submit both interim and final reports to the Governor regarding the implementation and findings of the pilot program.
The bill specifies that priority for the pilot program should be given to existing outdoor nature-based programs that are currently licensed as camps by the Maryland Department of Health.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Education, which will be necessary as the department is mandated by this bill to promulgate new rules and regulations for the licensing and operation of outdoor preschools.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Department of Education to convene an advisory group of outdoor, nature-based early learning practitioners to inform and support the implementation of the pilot program.

Synopsis: Transferring all the functions, powers, and duties of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County and certain personnel to the Child Support Administration of the Department of Human Services.
Title: St. Mary's County - Transfer of Child Support Unit and Personnel to the Child Support Administration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill transfers the operations, duties, and personnel of the Child Support Unit within the Office of the State’s Attorney for St. Mary’s County to the Child Support Administration of the Maryland Department of Human Services. It requires that transferred employees be placed into the State Personnel Management System with comparable positions, salary rates, and seniority credits.
stakeholders: Employees of the St. Mary’s County Child Support Unit and the St. Mary’s County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $236,300 in FY 2024 and $251,900 in FY 2025 to cover the State's share of child support enforcement costs. State general fund revenues decrease by $24,200 in FY 2024 and $32,300 annually thereafter as the county stops paying administrative fees. St. Mary’s County expenditures decrease by an estimated $249,200 in FY 2024 and at least $332,300 annually due to the transfer of personnel and operational costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the functions, powers, duties, and personnel of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County to the Child Support Administration, which is an entity within the Department of Human Services.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Budget and Management to increase and establish Position Identification Numbers (PINs) for the transferred employees and oversee their integration into the State Personnel Management System.
The bill provides for the Office of the Attorney General to potentially appoint Assistant State's Attorneys from the county to continue providing child support legal services as state employees.
The bill requires an actuarial valuation by the pension system's actuary and the transfer of employer contributions and interest from the municipal pool to the State pool for the affected employees.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversaw the inclusion of funding for this transfer in the state budget and is responsible for the overall administrative transition of these local functions to a state department.

Synopsis: Making certain members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System eligible to receive creditable service at retirement for unused sick leave accrued by the member in the State Employees' Retirement System or State Employees' Pension System; and requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to transfer certain individuals' Employees' Retirement System or Employees' Pension System service to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System on June 30, 2024.
Title: Correctional Officers’ Retirement System – Transfer of Membership – Modifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill allows certain members of the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System (CORS) to receive retirement credit for unused sick leave earned while they were members of the State Employees’ Retirement or Pension Systems. It also requires the State Retirement and Pension System to automatically transfer service credit from the old systems to CORS for eligible individuals unless they explicitly choose to opt out by June 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Current members of the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System whose membership was transferred from the Employees’ Retirement or Pension Systems, including approximately 300 employees of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Department of Juvenile Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities and contributions across all funds are expected to increase minimally beginning in fiscal year 2025. However, specific dollar estimates are unavailable because unused sick leave credit is only communicated to the State Retirement Agency at the time of retirement, and individual data for all 300 affected members is not currently feasible to calculate. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the administrative body for the State Retirement and Pension System, the SRA is directly responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, including transferring service credits, processing opt-out elections, and calculating unused sick leave for members of the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly affects multiple cohorts of DPSCS employees (including case management specialists, parole and probation agents, and counselors) who were transferred into the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System, modifying their eligibility for creditable service and sick leave benefits.

The bill impacts several categories of DJS employees (including community detention officers, resident advisors, and case management specialists) whose membership was moved to the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System, affecting their pension service transfers and sick leave credits.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency. The bill is expected to increase state pension liabilities and employer contributions, directly impacting the state budget and personnel policies managed by DBM.

The State Treasurer serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, which is tasked with the mandatory transfer of service credits under this bill.
The Comptroller serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, providing oversight for the pension system modifications mandated by this bill.

Synopsis: Altering the distribution of certain funds from local impact grants to Baltimore City; and altering the appointment process for certain members of the Pimlico Community Development Authority.
Title: Gaming - Video Lottery Terminals - Local Impact Grants and Pimlico Community Development Authority Membership - Baltimore City

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles

bill_summary: The bill modifies the distribution of video lottery terminal local impact grants within Baltimore City, increasing the percentage allocated for capital projects consistent with the Park Heights Master Plan from 75% to 85% for fiscal years 2024 through 2032. It also changes the appointment process for certain members of the Pimlico Community Development Authority, requiring that mayoral appointments receive the advice and consent of the Maryland Senate.
responsible_party: Mayor of Baltimore City and the Maryland Senate
stakeholders: Residents and business owners in the Park Heights Corridor and surrounding Baltimore City neighborhoods near the Pimlico Race Course.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on State finances. At the local level, the total amount of local impact grants distributed to Baltimore City remains unchanged; however, the internal allocation shifts. Beginning in fiscal 2024, approximately 363,500 dollars will be redirected to projects under the Park Heights Master Plan from other specified areas in the city, with this shift projected to reach 424,200 dollars by fiscal 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Pimlico Community Development Authority (PCDA) by altering its membership appointment process (requiring Senate advice and consent for mayoral appointees) and changing the distribution formulas for the local impact grants that the Authority oversees and advises on.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency regulates video lottery terminals (VLTs) and the commercial gaming industry that generates the revenue for the local impact grants affected by the bill's redistribution.

As the state's chief financial officer and revenue collector, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing the distribution of state funds and is specifically mentioned in the bill's reporting requirements regarding the continuation of funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Pimlico Community Development Authority is a state-mandated advisory body that falls under this collective category, and the bill significantly alters its governance and operational mandate.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and relevant departments (like Gaming and DBM) that manage these funds, and the Governor signed the bill into law.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and commissions, including the PCDA and the Gaming Control Agency, and would be responsible for advising on the legal implications of the altered appointment and distribution processes.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state, managing the budget and overseeing the allocation of state revenues, including the gaming proceeds redistributed by this bill.

The Baltimore City Planning Director is a statutory member of the PCDA, and the bill mandates that grant funds be distributed in a manner consistent with the Park Heights Master Plan, which involves land use and community planning oversight.
The bill introduces a Senate confirmation process for certain members of the PCDA, a task often coordinated by the Office of Appointments for state-mandated boards and commissions.

Synopsis: Requiring a local board of elections to send, not later than 43 days before an election, a ballot to voters who have made a request and qualify to vote by absentee ballot; altering the procedures for the canvassing of and curing of errors on absentee and provisional ballots; prohibiting the tabulation of absentee ballot vote totals before the polls close; requiring that the statewide primary election and the primary election for the municipal offices of Baltimore City in 2024 be held on the second Tuesday in May; etc.
Title: Election Law - Ballot Issuance, Processing, and Reporting Procedures and 2024 Primary Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland's election laws by requiring local boards to send mail-in ballots at least 43 days before an election and allowing them to begin processing these ballots eight business days before early voting begins. It establishes a process for voters to cure unsigned ballot envelopes via text, email, or an online portal and mandates that precinct-level election results include separate reporting for early, mail-in, and provisional votes. Additionally, the bill moves the 2024 statewide and Baltimore City primary elections to the second Tuesday in May.
stakeholders: Maryland voters, local boards of elections, and political candidates
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state general fund expenditures increase by at least $84,100 in FY 2024, and by over $100,000 annually in subsequent years, primarily to hire an IT programmer to manage the ballot-curing system. Local government expenditures also increase for personnel costs related to early canvassing and hardware such as flash drives and scanners; equipment costs are shared 50/50 between the state and local boards. Most counties estimate personnel cost increases of less than $5,000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the State Board of Elections is responsible for overseeing the new absentee ballot curing process, adopting required regulations, managing the statewide voter registration system updates, and reporting election results by precinct.
The bill alters the date of the statewide primary election, which directly affects the executive branch's electoral timeline and coordination of policy initiatives by the Governor.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections regarding the drafting of new regulations for ballot curing and ensures that the altered procedures comply with state and federal election laws.

The fiscal note indicates a need for increased general fund expenditures for personnel, specifically an IT programmer, and the management of state/local cost-sharing for new election equipment and software.

DoIT coordinates the state's IT strategy and security, which is relevant as the bill requires the development of an online portal and text-messaging systems for voters to cure signature omissions on ballots.

The bill requires local boards to transmit certified copies of election results to the clerk of the circuit court and addresses provisional ballots cast during court-ordered extensions of poll closing times.

The OLA is responsible for conducting fiscal compliance and performance audits of state agencies, including the State Board of Elections, ensuring they adhere to the bill's new statutory requirements.
The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works, which would oversee the procurement of the required hardware (scanners and flash drives) and IT services mentioned in the fiscal note.

The Archives is the central depository for government records of permanent value and would be responsible for preserving the certified election results and reports generated under the new reporting requirements.

Synopsis: Specifying that the definition of "earnable compensation" does not include certain payments requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to pay a nonvested former member's accumulated contributions to the nonvested former member's designated beneficiary or estate if the nonvested former member dies before withdrawing the member's contributions; and providing a list of individuals who immediately vest on taking certain offices.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Earnable Compensation, Nonvested Former Members, and Immediate Vesting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: The bill excludes certain retroactive lump sum salary payments from the definition of "earnable compensation" for the State Retirement and Pension System, requires the system to pay a deceased nonvested former member's accumulated contributions to their beneficiary or estate, and provides a specific list of high-level State officials who receive immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Members and former members of the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System, their beneficiaries, and high-level State government officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates. Provisions related to deceased nonvested members conform statute to current administrative practice, and the list of officials for immediate vesting is clarifying in nature. The exclusion of certain payments from earnable compensation represents a potential but negligible reduction in pension liabilities. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary entity impacted, as the bill directly amends the laws governing the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). It modifies the definition of earnable compensation, establishes rules for contributions of deceased nonvested members, and specifically grants the Executive Director immediate vesting rights.

Section 3 of the bill specifically addresses retroactive salary increases and lump sum payments made by the Maryland Department of Transportation, exempting certain MDOT payments from the new earnable compensation restrictions under specific conditions.

The Comptroller serves on the SRPS Board of Trustees, which is granted authority under the bill to determine what constitutes earnable compensation. Additionally, the Comptroller oversees the state's payroll and tax collection systems, which are affected by retroactive salary definitions.
The State Treasurer chairs the SRPS Board of Trustees. The bill directly impacts the SRPS and the Board's authority to define compensation and manage member contributions.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM is responsible for managing state employee benefits and compensation policies. The bill's changes to pension definitions and vesting rights for department heads directly affect state personnel administration.
The bill explicitly names the Adjutant General as one of the officials who receives immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the Director of the Office of Homeland Security as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the Director of the Office of Performance Improvement as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Director of the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Director of the Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the Director of the Maryland Energy Administration as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the Insurance Commissioner as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the State Archivist as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Chair of the State Board of Contract Appeals as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Director of the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the Chief Administrative Law Judge as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the State Prosecutor as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the Chair of the Public Service Commission as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill explicitly names the Chair of the Workers' Compensation Commission as an official receiving immediate vesting rights.
The bill clarifies vesting for various executive department heads and appointments made by the Governor.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the SRPS Board of Trustees regarding the interpretation and implementation of these pension law changes.

As the highest administrative body overseeing state fiscal policy, and including the Comptroller and Treasurer, the BPW is concerned with the fiscal integrity and pension liabilities impacted by the bill.

Synopsis: Increasing certain dollar thresholds of spending for the purposes of defining "small procurement" for State procurement contracts.
Title: State Procurement - Small Procurement - Definition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement

bill_summary: This bill raises the maximum dollar thresholds for 'small procurements' in Maryland. It increases the general limit from $50,000 to $100,000 and doubles thresholds for specific construction and maintenance contracts for the Department of General Services, Maryland Department of Transportation, and Department of Natural Resources.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works, Department of General Services, Maryland Department of Transportation, Department of Natural Resources, and the State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Maryland state agencies and government contractors, including small and minority-owned businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no material effect on State finances, though agencies may realize administrative efficiencies from using simplified procurement methods for more contracts. There is no local fiscal impact and minimal impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Board of Public Works to review the prevailing costs of labor and materials every three years and recommend appropriate adjustments to the small procurement ceiling to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly increases the small procurement threshold for construction contracts managed by DGS from $100,000 to $200,000. As a primary procurement unit and the central procurement authority for the state, DGS is directly responsible for implementing these threshold changes.
The bill explicitly increases the small procurement threshold for construction contracts managed by MDOT from $100,000 to $200,000.
The bill explicitly increases the small procurement threshold for DNR capital projects or maintenance contracts from $100,000 to $200,000.
The bill explicitly increases the small procurement threshold for the agency's expenditures on independent medical evaluations and related physician testimony from $50,000 to $100,000.

As the principal fiscal agency and a primary procurement unit, DBM is responsible for overseeing budget execution and procurement efficiency. The increase in the general small procurement threshold from $50,000 to $100,000 directly impacts their administrative processes and fiscal planning.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office monitors the state's socioeconomic procurement programs. Changes to small procurement thresholds affect how agencies solicit bids from Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) and Small Business Reserve (SBR) participants, as small procurements have simplified solicitation requirements.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is responsible for the triennial review and recommendation of procurement ceiling adjustments mandated by the bill.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the State Treasurer is responsible for the triennial review and recommendation of procurement ceiling adjustments mandated by the bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding procurement law. They will be responsible for ensuring that updated regulations and contracts comply with the new statutory definitions of small procurements.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of state agencies and will use these new dollar thresholds as the legal criteria for auditing procurement activities and ensuring agencies do not engage in artificial division of contracts.

Synopsis: Altering the percentage of the federal earned income tax credit used for determining the amount that an individual may claim as a refund under the Maryland earned income tax credit under certain circumstances; repealing a certain limitation on the amount certain individuals may claim as a refund under the credit; altering the definition of "qualified child" and income eligibility requirements for purposes of qualifying for a certain credit against the State income tax for certain dependent children; etc.
Title: Family Prosperity Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: The Family Prosperity Act of 2023 permanently extends temporary expansions to the Maryland earned income tax credit, including maintaining the refund percentage at 45% for general claimants and 100% for individuals without qualifying children. It also expands eligibility for the State child tax credit by increasing the income limit to $15,000, broadening the definition of a qualified child to include all children under age 6, and removing the requirement to offset the credit with federal child tax credit amounts.
stakeholders: Low- to moderate-income Maryland residents, particularly those with children under age 6 or children with disabilities, and workers without qualifying children eligible for the earned income credit.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund revenues decrease by $172.3 million in FY 2024, with decreases projected to reach $186.5 million by FY 2028. Local income tax revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $6.1 million in FY 2024. Additionally, general fund expenditures increase by $36,533 in FY 2024 (and approximately $60,000 to $70,000 annually thereafter) for the Comptroller's Office to hire a revenue examiner to process and validate child tax credit claims.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering state income tax credits, processing returns, and issuing the refunds mandated by the bill. The fiscal note explicitly identifies the need for an additional revenue examiner within this agency to process the increased volume of claims.

This is an Administration bill introduced at the request of the Governor. It represents a major executive policy initiative aimed at reducing poverty and implementing the Governor's fiscal and social agenda.

The bill has a significant impact on state general fund revenues, with an estimated decrease of over $172 million annually. DBM is responsible for revenue estimation, budget development, and long-term fiscal planning, all of which are directly affected by this legislation.

The bill's primary objective is to address child poverty and support low-income families, which directly aligns with the core mission and the ENOUGH Initiative led by the Governor's Office for Children.

The Innovation Team is specifically charged with addressing the Governor's priorities of reducing child poverty and enhancing economic mobility. This bill is a key legislative tool used to achieve those specific outcomes.
The bill provides substantial financial support to low-income residents and families in economic need, a population that DHS serves through its social service and assistance programs.

The bill contains specific provisions and eligibility criteria for children with disabilities, directly impacting a demographic that the Department of Disabilities is responsible for supporting and advocating for within state policy.

The bill references definitions for 'child with a disability' as established under the Education Article, which is governed by the policies and standards set by the Maryland State Department of Education.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State for purposes of developing opportunities for banking institutions and credit unions to better serve the needs of low- to moderate-income tracts; providing for certain assessment offset credits for certain banking institutions and credit unions in certain areas; authorizing the use of the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Financial Regulation - Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund - Establishment (Access to Banking Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State to develop financial innovations and enhance access to capital for businesses in low- to moderate-income areas. It authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to invest up to $2,500,000 in initial equity and $250,000 for administrative expenses from the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund, while providing assessment offset credits to banks and credit unions that establish or maintain branches in underserved tracts.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Maryland-chartered banking institutions, credit unions, and businesses and residents in low- to moderate-income census tracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund expenditures will increase by approximately $2,838,500 in FY 2024 to cover initial investments, administrative costs, and matching funds. Special fund revenues from assessments on financial institutions are estimated to decrease by $171,000 in FY 2024, with annual decreases growing to $310,000 by FY 2028 due to the assessment offset credits authorized by the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is implemented by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, who is a part of the Maryland Department of Labor. The agency is responsible for establishing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, managing assessment offset credits for banks and credit unions, and overseeing the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund.

The State Treasurer is explicitly named as the custodian of the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund, from which the bill authorizes an initial investment of $2.5 million and $250,000 for administrative expenses.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the state budget and the execution of special fund expenditures. The bill involves significant special fund expenditures and changes to assessment revenue that impact the State's fiscal planning.

This is an 'Administration' bill initiated by the Governor to address 'banking deserts' and enhance economic mobility in low- to moderate-income areas, aligning with the Governor's top policy priorities.

The bill's purpose is to enhance access to capital and financial services for businesses in low- to moderate-income tracts, which directly overlaps with the Department of Commerce's mission to stimulate the economy and support business expansion.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill focuses on providing credit and investment capital for small businesses in underinvested (LMI) communities, which aligns with this office's mission to connect the small business community to economic opportunities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and commissions. They would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the establishment of the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State.

Synopsis: Altering the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Program by extending the duration of the Program through fiscal year 2026, repealing the rebates that may be issued to retail service station dealers, and increasing the limitation on the total amount of rebates that the Maryland Energy Administration may issue in each fiscal year; altering the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program by altering the definition of "grant"; etc.
Title: Maryland Energy Administration – Energy Programs – Modifications (Clean Transportation and Energy Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill modifies and extends clean energy programs administered by the Maryland Energy Administration. It extends the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program through 2026, increases its annual funding cap to $2,500,000, and raises individual rebate limits. It also increases the mandated annual appropriation for the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to $10,000,000 through 2027, focusing on commercial vehicles and prioritizing projects in underserved communities. Additionally, the bill raises the administrative expense cap for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to $7,500,000 and modifies the use of alternative compliance payments to benefit environmental justice and low-income communities.
stakeholders: Electric vehicle owners, commercial and industrial fleet operators, local governments, small businesses in the green energy sector, and residents of low-income or overburdened communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund expenditures increase by $7,750,000 in FY 2024, $7,500,000 in FY 2025 and 2026, and $5,000,000 in FY 2027. These increases primarily stem from raising the mandated annual appropriation for the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to $10,000,000 and increasing the annual cap for electric vehicle recharging rebates to $2,500,000. The bill also increases the administrative expense cap for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund from $5,000,000 to $7,500,000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is the primary agency responsible for administering the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program, the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program, and the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF).
This is an Administration bill submitted by request of the Governor to advance executive policy priorities regarding clean energy and transportation.
DBM is responsible for supervising the budget execution of the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) and managing the $10 million mandated annual appropriation required by the bill.
DHS is a major beneficiary of the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), receiving at least 50% of proceeds from the sale of RGGI allowances for its energy assistance programs.
The bill focuses on the transportation sector, including electric vehicle infrastructure and zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles, which impacts state transportation policy and fleet management.

The bill utilizes statutory definitions from the Environment Article regarding overburdened and underserved communities and relates to the SEIF, which is funded by MDE's regulation of carbon allowances.
DGS manages state facilities and fleets that are eligible for recharging equipment rebates and zero-emission vehicle grants, and serves as the state's central procurement authority.
OAG provides legal counsel to MEA and other state agencies regarding the implementation and regulatory enforcement of the modified energy programs.
The BPW oversees and approves significant state expenditures, which may include major procurement contracts or grant awards authorized under these programs.
The Comptroller serves as a member of the Board of Public Works and is responsible for the fiscal oversight and payment of state rebates and funds.
The Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works and manages the investment and distribution of state funds, including those within the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of Statewide Broadband within the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study as to how the State can incentivize broadband service providers to expand broadband infrastructure to communities that are unserved or underserved; and requiring the Office to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
Title: Office of Statewide Broadband - Study of Broadband Expansion Incentives

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill requires the Office of Statewide Broadband (OSB) within the Department of Housing and Community Development to study and make recommendations on incentives to expand broadband infrastructure to unserved or underserved communities. The study must also examine how to best deploy federal grants and evaluate broadband network investment models from other states, with a final report due to the Governor and General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Office of Statewide Broadband within the Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Broadband service providers and residents of unserved or underserved Maryland communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase by an estimated $100,000 to $150,000 in fiscal 2024 if the Office of Statewide Broadband requires contractual consultant assistance to complete the required study. The Department of Legislative Services notes these costs may be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. The bill has no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Statewide Broadband, which is housed within DHCD, is the primary agency mandated to conduct the study and report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
The bill is an administration request, and the Governor's Office is the direct recipient of the required study and recommendations to help coordinate statewide broadband policy.
As the agency responsible for the state's information technology and telecommunications strategy, DoIT is a critical stakeholder in the expansion of broadband infrastructure.
The study must explore regulatory incentives for utility and broadband expansion, which falls under the broader expertise and regulatory scope of the PSC.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller provides expertise on the financial and tax-based incentives being considered to encourage infrastructure investment.
DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and may be required to facilitate the allocation of additional general funds for DHCD to complete the study.
Broadband expansion is a core economic development strategy used to attract businesses and stimulate growth, aligning with the department's primary mission.
The council advocates for the 18 rural counties that are the primary focus of efforts to expand broadband to unserved and underserved communities.
The study specifically tasks the Office of Statewide Broadband with ensuring that federal broadband infrastructure grants are deployed effectively, an area of expertise for the GGO.
The OAG will likely provide legal counsel to DHCD regarding the proposed regulatory or financial incentives to ensure compliance with state and federal laws.
The OPC represents the interests of residential utility consumers, who are the primary beneficiaries of efforts to improve broadband access and affordability.

Synopsis: Establishing the Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program in the Department of Commerce to provide funding for certain costs for infrastructure projects in eligible technology sectors; requiring certain grantees to provide matching funds and to demonstrate certain abilities; and requiring the Department to report to the Governor and the General Assembly on the projects funded through and the economic impact of the Program by July 1, 2026.
Title: Economic Development - Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund (Innovation Economy Infrastructure Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
