bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee to establish and publish online specifications for the procurement of compost, mulch, soil amendments, and aggregate produced from recycled or organic materials such as food waste, yard waste, and construction waste. State agencies must include these specifications in their procurement solicitations if the products are competitively priced, of satisfactory quality, and readily available.
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, local governments responsible for public land maintenance, and suppliers of recycled or organic soil and aggregate products.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Green Purchasing Committee can develop the required specifications with existing resources. The overall fiscal effect on State expenditures is indeterminate as it depends on the future pricing and availability of recycled materials relative to inorganic materials. Local governments may see a minimal increase in revenues if the State purchases more municipal solid waste products from them.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of General Services (DGS) provides staff support to the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee, and its Secretary chairs the committee, which is tasked with establishing and publishing the required specifications. The bill also updates DGS's specific goals for composting landscape waste on State property.

The Department of Natural Resources manages extensive state parks and public lands requiring compost and mulch. The fiscal note explicitly mentions DNR's concerns regarding the safety and quality of products derived from solid and food waste for use on state lands.

The Department of Transportation is a major user of aggregate for highway construction and maintenance, and it uses mulch and compost for roadside landscaping. It must incorporate the new specifications into its large-scale procurement solicitations.

The Maryland Environmental Service provides technical expertise in solid waste management, recycling, and composting. It is listed as an information source and operates facilities that produce or manage the organic materials mentioned in the bill.
The State Treasurer is a statutory member of the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee, which is responsible for establishing the environmentally preferable specifications required by the bill.

The Department of the Environment regulates the organic materials specified in the bill, such as sludge, food waste, and municipal solid waste, and was consulted as an information source for the fiscal note.
The Department of Agriculture oversees soil conservation and fertilizer quality, making it a relevant stakeholder for specifications involving compost and soil amendments.

The University System of Maryland maintains numerous campuses and facilities that require the procurement of mulch and compost for grounds maintenance, thus falling under the bill's requirements for state units.
As a state agency that maintains its own urban campus, Morgan State University must include the specified organic material requirements in its procurement of landscaping materials.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services maintains various correctional facilities with significant grounds, requiring the procurement of soil amendments and mulch according to the new specifications.
The Department of Juvenile Services operates residential facilities that require landscape maintenance and must comply with the new procurement specifications for organic materials.
This agency manages state veteran cemeteries and the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, which involve extensive grounds maintenance requiring the procurement of mulch and compost.
The Maryland School for the Deaf maintains campuses in Frederick and Columbia and is listed as an impacted agency that must follow the bill's procurement standards for land maintenance.
The Board of Public Works oversees state procurement regulations and policies, including those related to the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee and general preference standards.
The Department of Housing and Community Development was identified as an information source and may be impacted when maintaining properties or coordinating community revitalization infrastructure.
The Maryland Department of Planning provides data and policy guidance related to sustainable growth and land use, making it a stakeholder in the use of recycled materials for state land maintenance.

Synopsis: Authorizing, for a certain period of time, the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to exchange a Class B-D-7 beer, wine, and liquor license in a certain area for a Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor license under certain circumstances; repealing certain geographic and temporal restrictions on the issuance of Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City; and altering a certain period of time during which a certain alcoholic beverages license may be issued.
Title: Baltimore City - 41st District - Alcoholic Beverages - Licenses
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to exchange Class B-D-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses for Class A-7 licenses for specific locations on Frederick Avenue and removes geographic and temporal restrictions on Class A-7 licenses in the 43rd legislative district. Additionally, it modifies the requirements for 'marketplace' licenses in the 41st legislative district by extending the allowed opening window for establishments from 6 to 24 months and authorizing off-premises consumption sales.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders in Baltimore City, specifically those in the 41st and 43rd legislative districts and the 4000 block of Frederick Avenue, and marketplace business owners.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no impact on State finances and does not materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations. While it establishes or maintains annual license fees ($1,500 for Class A-7 and $6,000 for marketplace licenses), the overall fiscal effect is considered minimal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City—a state-authorized regulatory body categorized under this entity—to exchange specific liquor licenses and manage new provisions for marketplace licenses in the city. The Board is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's provisions.

As the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry and chief tax collector, the Comptroller oversees the legal and fiscal framework in which alcoholic beverages are sold. Modifications to license classes and sales authorizations in Baltimore City intersect with the Comptroller's regulatory and oversight duties.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in appointing members to the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners. This bill expands and alters the statutory authority of that Board, making the appointment of qualified individuals to these positions a matter of continued relevance to the office's work.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the state-appointed boards that regulate alcoholic beverages. Governor Wes Moore signed this bill into law and is responsible for its overall execution.

Synopsis: Altering a certain provision to prohibit a court from assessing certain costs on a certain person or governmental unit for recording and indexing an order of restitution issued by any court in the State instead of the court in which the judgment of restitution was entered.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Restitution Orders - Recording Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland courts from charging recording or indexing fees to individuals or government agencies when they file a restitution order as a money judgment, regardless of which court in the state issued the order.
stakeholders: Crime victims, governmental units, and third-party payors to whom restitution is owed, as well as the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is a potential minimal decrease in State fee revenues, but it is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances. No specific dollar estimates are provided for the revenue decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency affected by this bill, as it provides operational support for the state's judicial system. This bill directly prohibits courts from assessing specific recording and indexing fees for restitution orders, which falls under the AOC's administrative and financial oversight.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency manages victim services and coordinates public safety strategies. Since restitution orders are a critical component of victim compensation in criminal proceedings, the policy changes regarding the ease of recording these judgments as money judgments are highly relevant to their mission.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Judiciary and all state agencies. They may be required to offer guidance on the implementation of these procedural changes or represent the state's interest when government units are the recipients of restitution orders.

As the state's chief financial officer responsible for collecting state revenues, the Comptroller is relevant because the bill alters the collection of court-related fees, though the fiscal note indicates the impact on state revenue is minimal.

Synopsis: Repealing the $500,000 cap on grants that may be awarded by the Maryland Transit Administration under the Maryland Senior Rides Program; repealing the $400,000 cap on the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program; establishing the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation to examine transportation needs of the elderly, persons with disabilities, and residents requiring transportation assistance to jobs, appointments, citizen programs, and other engagements; etc.
Title: Health and Human Services Transportation Improvement Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill removes the annual funding caps for the Maryland Senior Rides Program and the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program. It also establishes the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation within the Maryland Department of Transportation to assess and coordinate transportation services for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and transportation-disadvantaged residents.
stakeholders: Low-to-moderate-income seniors, individuals with disabilities, and transportation-disadvantaged residents requiring access to medical services, jobs, and health-related programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by 180,000 dollars in FY 2024 and 80,000 dollars annually thereafter for consultant services to assist the new coordinating committee. The bill repeals the previous funding caps for the Maryland Senior Rides Program (500,000 dollars) and the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program (400,000 dollars), though it does not mandate specific funding increases for these programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. The Maryland Transit Administration (a unit of MDOT) administers the Maryland Senior Rides Program and the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program. The Secretary of Transportation chairs the new State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, and the department provides the committee's staff and funding.

The Secretary of Health is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, as the bill focuses on transportation to medical and health-related appointments.

The Secretary of Human Services is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation. The bill addresses the needs of transportation-disadvantaged individuals, many of whom are served by DHS programs.

The Secretary of Aging is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation. Additionally, the bill impacts the Maryland Senior Rides Program, which specifically serves low-to-moderate income seniors.

The Secretary of Disabilities is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation. The bill specifically addresses the transportation needs of residents with disabilities.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Secretary of Planning is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Secretary of Veterans Affairs is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.

The Secretary of Labor is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation. The committee is tasked with examining transportation needs for individuals requiring access to jobs and training.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of the Governor's Office for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Executive Board Chair of the Rural Maryland Council is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.

The Governor is responsible for appointing additional members to the State Coordinating Committee and the bill mandates that the Governor include funding for specific programs in the annual budget bill.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is involved in the budget execution and revenue estimation related to the bill's removal of funding caps and requirements for state budget appropriations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the correction of the designated beneficiary election for certain retirees of the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, or Judges' Retirement System who retired on or before December 31, 2012, if the retiree named an individual of the same sex to be a designated beneficiary and the retiree married the designated beneficiary on or after January 1, 2013.
Title: State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System, and Judges’ Retirement System – Surviving Spouse Benefit – Same–Sex Spouses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: This bill allows retirees of the State Police Retirement System, the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System, and the Judges’ Retirement System who retired on or before December 31, 2012, to convert their actuarially reduced optional retirement allowances into unreduced basic allowances if they subsequently married a same-sex designated beneficiary. It provides for retroactive lump-sum payments (including 4% interest) to account for the difference between the reduced and unreduced benefits from the date of retirement or marriage.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Retirees of the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System, and Judges’ Retirement System and their surviving same-sex spouses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal effect on State pension assets and no discernible effect on State pension contribution rates. While the bill mandates retroactive adjustments and lump-sum payments for eligible retirees, the State Retirement Agency identified only 109 accounts that potentially meet the criteria. There is no impact on State or local revenues, and no discernible effect on local pension contribution rates for participating governmental units.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary implementing body for this bill, as it is responsible for the administration and management of the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and Judges' Retirement System. It must process the requested beneficiary conversions and calculate retroactive adjustments.

Retirees from the Maryland State Police are specifically covered under the State Police Retirement System, one of the three systems modified by this bill to allow survivor benefit corrections for same-sex spouses.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides support for the Judicial Branch, whose judges participate in the Judges' Retirement System, which is directly impacted by the bill's provisions regarding survivor benefits.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency for the state, DBM oversees employee benefits and long-term fiscal planning related to state pension systems and the financial impact of benefit adjustments.

The OAG serves as the chief legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland State Retirement Agency, and would likely provide guidance on the legal implementation of these benefit corrections and eligibility verification.

MDOT employs law enforcement officers (e.g., Maryland Transit Administration and Maryland Transportation Authority Police) who are members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System impacted by this bill.
DNR employs Natural Resources Police officers who participate in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, making this bill relevant to its former and current staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs various law enforcement and investigative officers who are eligible for the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System affected by the bill's changes to survivor benefits.
Certain law enforcement personnel within DJS are members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and are therefore eligible for the benefit adjustments described in the legislation.

OLA is responsible for auditing the financial and compliance operations of state agencies, including the Maryland State Retirement Agency, ensuring that benefit adjustments and lump-sum payments are executed correctly according to the law.

The Comptroller serves on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System and the Board of Public Works, overseeing the fiscal integrity and payments related to state retirement benefits.

The State Treasurer serves as a key member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System and manages state funds, which are impacted by changes to pension payouts and liabilities.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and protects the state's fiscal integrity; the bill's impact on pension liabilities, though minimal, falls under their broad administrative oversight.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from discriminating in the sale or rental of, or otherwise making unavailable or denying, a dwelling to an individual with a disability who has, obtains, or retains a certain service dog.
Title: Human Relations - Housing Discrimination - Service Dogs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill prohibits discrimination in the sale or rental of housing against individuals with disabilities who use service dogs or keep retired service dogs. It ensures these individuals are exempt from pet-related lease restrictions and additional fees, while maintaining their liability for any damages caused by the animal.
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities who use service dogs, individuals with retired service dogs, and housing providers including landlords and sellers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for enforcing Maryland's anti-discrimination laws in housing, MCCR will investigate complaints regarding housing discrimination against individuals with disabilities using service dogs and manage the conciliation process.
The OAH is responsible for conducting administrative hearings in cases where the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights finds that discriminatory housing practices have occurred.

The bill explicitly references regulations adopted by DHCD regarding handicapped accessibility standards and affects the agency's mission of ensuring safe, secure, and fair housing for state residents.

As the principal agency coordinating services and improving policy for residents with disabilities, this bill directly affects their mission to ensure integrated settings and equitable access to housing.
Individuals claiming to be injured by discriminatory housing practices may file civil actions in circuit court, which is supported operationally by the AOC.
Many veterans utilize service dogs for physical or psychological disabilities; the agency assists these individuals in securing benefits and resources related to housing.

The department protects the rights of older adults, many of whom have disabilities and may rely on service or retired service dogs, making the housing protections in this bill highly relevant to their advocacy work.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Many individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing utilize guide dogs; the agency advocates for equal access to public resources and community life for this population.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Commission on Civil Rights and the Department of Housing and Community Development regarding the enforcement and implementation of state housing laws.

The Department of Health supports individuals with developmental and behavioral disabilities who may require service dogs for assistance, making these housing protections relevant to their patient support networks.

DHS assists residents with economic needs and disabilities through local departments, and this bill provides protections for vulnerable individuals requiring housing assistance and service dog accommodations.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Nursing in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board; altering the exceptions to the registered nurse and licensed practical nurse licensure requirements; providing that, for a certain period of time, the Secretary of Health, rather than the Board, has authority over the infrastructure operations of the Board; etc.
Title: State Board of Nursing – Sunset Extension, Licensure Exceptions, and Board Operations and Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill extends the sunset date of the State Board of Nursing to July 1, 2025, and temporarily transfers authority over its infrastructure operations from the Board to the Secretary of Health until June 30, 2025. It also modifies licensure exceptions to allow nursing applicants to practice while their application is pending even after failing an examination once, requires an independent evaluation of the Board's operations, and implements a staggered termination of current Board member terms.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Nursing
stakeholders: Registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, nursing license applicants, nursing education programs, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $8,000,000 in FY 2024 to cover infrastructure operations for the State Board of Nursing, which were previously covered by special funds; special fund expenditures for these activities decrease correspondingly. Special fund expenditures also increase by at least $150,000 in FY 2023 to hire an external consultant for an independent evaluation. Board of Nursing special fund revenues continue as authorized. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers authority over the State Board of Nursing's infrastructure operations to the Secretary of Health through June 30, 2025. The Department is responsible for implementing the operational takeover and managing the general funds allocated for this purpose.

The Secretary of Budget and Management must be consulted on setting compensation for Board of Nursing staff and the department is a named partner in developing the independent action plan for the Board's long-term sustainability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the membership, operations, and statutory termination date of the State Board of Nursing, which is an ongoing regulatory body within this category.
DoIT is a specified partner in the development of the Board's action plan, specifically addressing infrastructure needs, new workflows, and technical resource identification.
The Governor receives annual reports from the Board and is responsible for appointing members to the Board, whose terms are specifically terminated and staggered by this bill.
This office will assist the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates to fill the Board of Nursing vacancies created by the bill's mandatory termination of current member terms.

The bill requires an independent evaluation that coordinates with the ongoing performance evaluation of the Board of Nursing conducted by OLA's Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability (OPEGA).

As the legal representative for all state agencies, the OAG provides counsel to the Board of Nursing and the Department of Health regarding the transition of authority and regulatory changes to licensure exceptions.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures, which may include the procurement of the external consultant and IT infrastructure upgrades required by the bill.
The Comptroller manages state revenues and the Board of Nursing Fund, which is subject to specific spending prohibitions regarding infrastructure operations under the bill.
The Treasurer's Office manages the state funds and accounts, including the transition of funding for the Board's operations from special funds to general funds as mandated by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Aging to oversee long-term care and train the staff of long-term care and dementia care navigation programs; requiring each area agency to establish a long-term care and dementia care navigation program; and requiring the Department to submit a report by October 1, 2024, and each year thereafter, to the Governor, the President of the Senate, the Speaker of the House, and certain committees of the General Assembly about the services provided by the program and to publish the report on its website.
Title: Department of Aging - Long-Term Care and Dementia Care Navigation Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Long-Term Care -see also- Continuing Care; Nursing Homes

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Aging to oversee and train staff for long-term care and dementia care navigation programs, which each local area agency on aging must establish. These programs are designed to provide information, referrals, cognitive screenings, and support services for individuals with dementia and their caregivers, with the Department required to report annually on program activities and outcomes.
stakeholders: Maryland residents with dementia or cognitive changes, their caregivers, and local Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs)
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $79,733 in fiscal 2024 for a program manager. Beginning in fiscal 2025, the bill mandates an annual appropriation of $2,400,000 to manage navigation programs statewide and fund them locally. For local governments that operate Area Agencies on Aging, revenues and expenditures will increase starting in fiscal 2025 to establish and manage the navigation programs using the provided funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Aging (MDoA) to oversee and train staff for the new Long-Term Care and Dementia Care Navigation Programs, collect interaction data, and submit annual reports on program efficacy. It also requires Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs), which MDoA oversees, to establish these programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires that the work of the long-term care and dementia care navigation programs be guided by the recommendations of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council, which is an executive advisory body within this category.

The bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation of $2.4 million beginning in FY 2025. DBM is the principal agency responsible for developing the state budget and managing personnel costs associated with the new program manager position required by the bill.

The Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council, which guides the navigation programs, is established under the Health - General Article. Additionally, the department partners with the Department of Aging on chronic disease and dementia outreach.
The Governor is required to include the mandated $2.4 million appropriation in the annual budget bill and is the recipient of the annual progress reports submitted by the Department of Aging.

Synopsis: Extending the reporting and termination dates, to July 1, 2024, and June 30, 2025, respectively, for the Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals.
Title: Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals - Extension of Dates

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill extends the reporting and termination dates for the Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals. The workgroup is now required to submit its findings and recommendations by July 1, 2024, and the act's termination date is extended to June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: The Maryland Department of Health and the University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and other underrepresented behavioral health professionals; students pursuing behavioral health careers; and underserved communities in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for staffing and member expense reimbursements are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources for the Maryland Department of Health and the University System of Maryland. No local fiscal impact is expected, and specific dollar estimates for the extension were not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is mandated to jointly staff the Workgroup, the Secretary of Health appoints several members and designates the chair, and the bill focuses on behavioral health professionals, which falls under the department's primary mission.

The University System of Maryland is mandated to jointly staff the Workgroup and is represented on the body through the presidents of several member institutions (Bowie State, Coppin State, and UMES).
The President of Morgan State University, or their designee, is a named member of the Workgroup established by the underlying legislation being amended.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the reporting and termination dates for a state-mandated workgroup, which falls under the category of temporary bodies established to conduct studies and provide recommendations.
The Workgroup is required to report its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor, who also oversees the executive agencies tasked with staffing the body.
The bill involves the expenditure of state funds for travel reimbursements for workgroup members and utilizes personnel resources from executive agencies which DBM oversees.

Synopsis: Establishing the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program in the Department of Commerce to provide grants to certain small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises to assist those manufacturers with implementing new Industry 4.0 technology or related infrastructure for certain purposes; establishing the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund; and requiring the Governor to include in the budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028 an appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Fund.
Title: Economic Development - Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program and Fund within the Maryland Department of Commerce to provide grants to small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) for implementing advanced technologies such as robotics, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity. The program provides grants between $25,000 and $500,000 on a competitive basis to enhance the productivity and competitiveness of Maryland's manufacturing sector.
stakeholders: Small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) with business operations in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.1 million annually from fiscal 2025 through 2028, which includes a $1 million mandated appropriation to the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund and approximately $123,176 for administrative staff and operating expenses. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund increase by $1 million annually during this period as mandated funds are received and distributed as grants. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program and Fund within the Department of Commerce. The Secretary of Commerce is responsible for administering the fund, awarding grants to manufacturing enterprises, and adopting necessary regulations.

The bill allows the Department of Commerce to enter into an MOU with a State-chartered corporation to administer the grant program. The fiscal note explicitly identifies TEDCO as a potential entity to serve as the program administrator.

The bill allows the Department of Commerce to enter into an MOU with a State-chartered corporation to administer the grant program. The fiscal note identifies MEDCO as a potential entity to serve as the program administrator.
The bill requires the Governor to include a mandated appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising the execution of the state budget, which includes managing the mandated annual appropriations and the establishment of the new special grant fund.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund separately and to invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other state money.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund, serving their role as the state's chief financial officer.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The grant program specifically targets small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) manufacturers, with a 20% set-aside for businesses with 50 or fewer employees, aligning with this office's mission to support small business economic opportunities.

Synopsis: Expanding the forms of financial assistance available under the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program; altering eligibility requirements for projects that may receive financial assistance under the Program; altering the time period when applications may be submitted under the Program; repealing certain restrictions on the amount of financial assistance that may be provided under the Program; etc.
Title: Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill alters the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program by expanding the types of financial assistance available to include loans, guarantees, and credit enhancements, rather than just grants. It allows developers to apply for assistance when a project is proposed instead of when it is completed, expands eligibility to include projects in sustainable communities, and removes previous restrictions on the maximum amount of financial assistance that can be provided per project.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
stakeholders: Affordable housing developers, individuals or business entities proposing construction or rehabilitation of residential properties in low-income census tracts and sustainable communities, and residents of historically redlined neighborhoods.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill's changes do not directly affect State operations or finances because funding for the Appraisal Gap from Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program has not been budgeted since the program’s enactment in 2021. There is no impact on local government finances. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the program is currently unfunded.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community is the primary agency responsible for administering the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program. The bill tasks the agency with developing application forms, processes for distributing assistance, and adopting necessary regulations.

The bill expands program eligibility to 'sustainable communities' and requires projects to comply with local land use plans. The Department of Planning is responsible for promoting sustainable growth, providing technical assistance for land use planning, and coordinating sustainable community designations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Housing and Community and would be involved in drafting and reviewing the new regulations and financial assistance instruments authorized by this bill.

As the principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management oversees the state budget and the execution of funding for programs like the Appraisal Gap Fund, which is critical given the fiscal note's mention of the program's historical lack of funding.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives related to housing and community revitalization. The bill also relates to existing reporting requirements for studies that must be submitted to the Governor.
This multi-agency initiative coordinates sustainable development and land use policy across departments, aligning with the bill's focus on 'sustainable communities' and local planning compliance.

The program's core mission of addressing 'historic redlining'—a form of systemic housing discrimination—directly aligns with the Commission's work in protecting civil rights and enforcing anti-discrimination laws in housing.

Synopsis: Establishing the Human-Relevant Research Fund under the administration of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to provide grants and loans to promote State-funded research intended to develop human-relevant alternatives to using nonhuman animals in medical and product testing and research; requiring, beginning January 15, 2024, research facilities that engage in animal testing or research to pay a contribution, based on a certain number of animals, to the Secretary of Health; providing a civil penalty for a violation of the Act; etc.
Title: Animal Testing and Research - Human-Relevant Research Funding and Animal Testing and Research Contributions

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Human-Relevant Research Fund and a grant and loan program administered by the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to support the development of human-relevant alternatives to nonhuman animal testing. It requires research facilities in Maryland that are required to submit certain federal animal research forms to pay an annual contribution to the Maryland Department of Health, with the proceeds funding the new research program.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) and the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Research facilities in Maryland using nonhuman animals for testing, public and private higher education institutions, and scientific researchers developing animal testing alternatives.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note estimates that special fund revenues for the Human-Relevant Research Fund (HRRF) will increase by up to $915,000 annually beginning in FY 2024, with corresponding expenditures for grants, loans, and administrative costs. State higher education expenditures are projected to increase by $120,000 annually due to required contribution payments from public universities. Additionally, local expenditures for the Community College of Baltimore County are expected to increase by $5,000 per year. TEDCO's annual administrative costs are estimated at $180,000, leaving approximately $735,000 for research grants and loans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates TEDCO as the primary administrator of the Human-Relevant Research Fund and the associated grant and loan program. TEDCO is responsible for contracting with a review board, adopting regulations, and reporting on the program's progress.
The bill requires research facilities to pay annual contributions to the Secretary of Health, who is responsible for collecting these fees and distributing them to the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

Multiple member institutions of the University System of Maryland, including UMCP, UMB, and Towson University, are required to pay annual contributions under the bill's provisions. These institutions are also potential recipients of the research grants and loans.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Human-Relevant Research Fund separately and invest the money in the fund, with interest earnings credited to the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a Human-Relevant Research Review Board to evaluate research proposals and make recommendations for the disbursement of grants and loans.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Human-Relevant Research Fund as established by the bill.
The Governor is authorized to include appropriations for the Human-Relevant Research Fund in the state budget and receives annual reports from TEDCO regarding the program's progress.
DBM is involved in the fiscal administration of the state budget, which may include appropriations to the Human-Relevant Research Fund as authorized by the bill.
MHEC oversees the institutions of higher education that are both required to pay the research contributions and eligible to apply for the grants and loans provided by the bill.

As a major public urban research university, Morgan State University may be impacted by the contribution requirements if it uses nonhuman animals in research and is an eligible entity to receive grants or loans for human-relevant research.

Synopsis: Specifying that a certain surviving spouse of a member of the armed forces is eligible to apply for a scholarship under the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program if the service member died, suffered a service connected disability, or was declared to be a prisoner of war or missing in action under certain circumstances.
Title: Higher Education – Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program – Surviving Spouses of Service Members

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility criteria for the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program to include surviving spouses of U.S. Armed Forces members who died as a result of military service after December 7, 1941, or who were declared a prisoner of war or missing in action during the Vietnam conflict.
stakeholders: Surviving spouses of U.S. Armed Forces members who died in military service or were prisoners of war/missing in action during the Vietnam conflict, and eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures are expected to increase by an estimated $7,700 per additional award granted annually. While there is a mandated $4,000,000 appropriation for the scholarship fund beginning in fiscal 2024, expanding eligibility will likely cause program expenditures to exceed this amount, necessitating additional general fund support. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund, verifying student eligibility reported by institutions, and allocating the scholarship funds.

The University System of Maryland (USM) oversees many of the public four-year institutions where these scholarships are used. These institutions are responsible for verifying student eligibility and awarding the scholarships directly to students.
As a public state-run university, Morgan State University is an eligible postsecondary institution that awards these scholarships to its students and reports eligibility data to MHEC for funding.
Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible public institution that directly implements the scholarship program for its students and coordinates with MHEC for fund allocation.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families is the principal state agency for assisting veterans and their families in securing benefits. This bill expands a specific state educational benefit for the surviving spouses of service members.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state's fiscal planning. This bill expands eligibility for a mandated scholarship program, which the fiscal note indicates will increase general fund expenditures.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including MHEC, and would likely be involved in updating regulations to reflect the bill's changes to eligibility criteria.

The Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives and the executive branch. This bill aligns with executive priorities regarding veterans' benefits and education, and required the Governor's approval.

Synopsis: Authorizing an account holder who is the victim of abuse to terminate, and requiring a utility to allow for the termination of, the account holder's future liability under a utility contract if the account holder provides the utility with certain written notice requesting termination of the account holder's future liability under the contract; requiring a utility to allow an account holder who terminates a utility contract under the Act to open a new utility account notwithstanding a certain account balance or arrearage; etc.
Title: Utility Account Holders - Victims of Abuse - Protections
