bill_summary: This bill allows utility account holders who are victims of abuse to terminate their future liability under a utility contract by providing written notice and documentation, such as a protective order or a report from a qualified third party. Utilities are required to allow these terminations and must permit the account holder to open a new account at a different location regardless of any outstanding balances or arrearages from the previous premises.
stakeholders: Utility account holders who are victims of abuse and utility companies (including electric, gas, water, and sewage disposal companies).
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Public Service Commission can handle the bill’s requirements with existing budgeted resources and the bill does not otherwise materially affect State finances or operations. Local utilities are also expected to manage the requirements within existing resources. Specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditures are unavailable as the bill is not expected to have a significant fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory body for the utility companies (electric, gas, water, and sewage disposal) affected by this bill. The PSC is responsible for overseeing utility compliance with the new mandates regarding account termination and new account opening for victims of abuse.

The Office of the People's Counsel (OPC) represents the interests of Maryland's residential utility consumers. This bill establishes significant new consumer protections and rights for utility account holders who are victims of abuse, making it highly relevant to the OPC's advocacy mission.

The bill's implementation relies on documentation from the judicial system, specifically final peace and protective orders issued under the Family Law and Courts articles. The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the court systems that issue these orders.

The Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) is the state's primary social service provider for victims of abuse. The bill defines social workers and caseworkers from public agencies as 'qualified third parties' who can provide documentation for utility account termination.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates statewide strategies for public safety and victim services. It was consulted as an information source for the fiscal note and oversees policy and funding related to domestic violence and sexual assault prevention programs.

The bill defines licensed physicians and psychologists as 'qualified third parties.' The Department of Health regulates these health care professionals and oversees behavioral health programs that serve victims of abuse.

The Secretary of State administers the 'Safe at Home' address confidentiality program for victims of domestic violence and human trafficking. The bill's protections for victims seeking to relocate and open new utility accounts align with the goals of this program.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and other state agencies. It also enforces consumer protection laws, which are relevant to the bill's utility account protections.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the various agencies tasked with implementing these protections and signed the bill into law (Chapter 566).

Synopsis: Requiring that the credential reappointment process for physician staff included in certain minimum standards for hospitals licensed in the State be conducted in accordance with standards of the accreditation body that accredits a hospital, rather than every 2 years.
Title: Hospital Credentialing - Reappointment Process for Physician Staff - Modification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill updates the minimum standards for the hospital physician credentialing process. Specifically, it changes the frequency of the formal reappointment process for physician staff from a biennial requirement (at least every two years) to a process conducted in accordance with the standards of the specific accreditation body that accredits the hospital.
stakeholders: Licensed hospitals and physicians in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources. No local government fiscal impact or small business impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Secretary of Health with establishing regulations for hospital credentialing standards and enforces these standards through the hospital licensure process, including the authority to impose fines or delicense facilities for noncompliance.

As an independent regulatory agency within the Department of Health, the MHCC is responsible for health system planning and improving the quality of healthcare, which includes overseeing hospital performance and accountability standards related to physician credentialing.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health for the development of the required regulations and represents the state in litigation or appeals regarding hospital licensure and regulatory enforcement actions.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies; if a hospital contests a fine or delicensure action imposed by the Department of Health under this bill, the case would be heard by an OAH Administrative Law Judge.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "personal information" for purposes of certain provisions of the Public Information Act to include an individual's personal e-mail address; requiring certain custodians to deny inspection of certain records of personal e-mail addresses and telephone numbers except under certain circumstances; and requiring certain custodians to allow inspection of certain records of business e-mail addresses under the same circumstances as inspection of certain records of business addresses and telephone numbers.
Title: Public Information Act - Inspection of E-Mail Addresses and Telephone Numbers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Public Information Act to define an individual's e-mail address as "personal information." It requires public record custodians to deny inspection of personal e-mail addresses and telephone numbers for students and government employees, while establishing specific conditions for the inspection of business e-mail addresses for notaries public and licensed professionals.
responsible_party: Custodians of public records at Maryland State and local government agencies, including school districts and licensing boards.
stakeholders: Maryland students and their families, State and local government employees, notaries public, licensed professionals, and individuals or entities requesting public records.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. Any impact on activities related to the Public Information Act is expected to be minimal and handled within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC provides legal and operational support to the courts, which are custodians of public records and employers. The bill's restrictions on inspecting personal email addresses and telephone numbers of state employees (Section 4-331) apply to the judiciary's personnel.

The department is responsible for various regulatory and licensing activities (e.g., pesticide regulation and animal health). Section 4-333 of the bill establishes new rules for the inspection of email addresses and telephone numbers of individuals licensed in an occupation or profession.

As the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland, DBM manages state employee policies and resources. The bill's requirement that custodians deny inspection of state employees' personal email addresses and telephone numbers (Section 4-331) directly impacts the management of personnel records across the executive branch.

MSDE oversees the state's public education system. The bill specifically amends Section 4-313 to require custodians to deny the inspection of a student's personal email address and telephone number in school district records, while establishing specific exceptions for authorized entities.

The department is a major state employer and also regulates numerous healthcare professionals and facilities. The bill's provisions regarding the privacy of state employee records (Section 4-331) and occupational licensing records (Section 4-333) are highly relevant to its operations.

The Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of numerous professions and industries. The bill's amendments to Section 4-333 explicitly address the inspection of email addresses and telephone numbers for licensed individuals in these occupations.

The MCA is responsible for licensing and compliance within the cannabis industry. Section 4-333 of the bill, which governs the inspection of records related to the licensing of individuals in an occupation or profession, applies to the licensees regulated by this agency.

MHEC is explicitly named in Section 4-313 as an entity that may be authorized to inspect student records, while being strictly prohibited from using such information for commercial purposes or disclosing it further.

As the regulatory body for the state's insurance market, the MIA licenses insurance producers and other professionals. The changes to Section 4-333 regarding the disclosure of licensee email addresses directly impact the administration of these public records.

The State Archives is the central depository for government records. Changes to the Public Information Act, including the expanded definition of 'personal information' and new mandatory denials for emails and phone numbers, affect how the Archives manages public access to its collections.

As a public university and state agency, Morgan State handles both state employee records and student records, both of which are subject to the bill's new privacy protections for personal email addresses and telephone numbers.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies on Public Information Act (PIA) compliance and publishes the state's PIA Manual. It will be responsible for interpreting these new requirements and advising state custodians on implementation.

The PSC licenses various entities, including retail energy suppliers and common carriers. The bill's provisions in Section 4-333 regarding the inspection of occupational and professional licensing records apply to the commission's licensee data.

As a public honors college and independent unit of state government, the college is a custodian of both employee and student records, making the bill's privacy protections for email addresses and phone numbers directly applicable.

The Secretary of State is responsible for the commission and oversight of notaries public. The bill specifically amends Section 4-332 to establish rules for the inspection of a notary public's business and personal email addresses.

The USM and its constituent institutions are major state employers and maintain extensive student records. The bill's updates to Section 4-313 (students) and Section 4-331 (employees) regarding email and telephone privacy are directly relevant to its operations.

Synopsis: Altering the grounds on which a deputy sheriff having a rank of major or below in Washington County may be discharged after 2 years of continuous employment; providing that a special deputy sheriff in Washington County is not a State employee for certain purposes; authorizing sworn deputy sheriffs at the rank of sergeant and below and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below to engage in collective bargaining with the Washington County Sheriff and the County Administrator; etc.
Title: Washington County - Deputy Sheriffs and Correctional Deputies - Employment Conditions and Collective Bargaining

NarrowSubjects.Name: Termination of Employment -see also- Work, Labor, and Employ
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill authorizes full-time sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below in Washington County to engage in collective bargaining regarding wages and benefits with the County Sheriff and Administrator. It further defines 'police misconduct' as the sole grounds for discharging tenured deputy sheriffs and clarifies that special deputy sheriffs are not considered State employees for the purposes of employment security or benefits.
responsible_party: Washington County Sheriff, Washington County Administrator, and the Washington County Board of Commissioners
stakeholders: Sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below in Washington County, the Washington County Sheriff's Office, and the Washington County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. According to the fiscal note, Washington County expenditures may increase minimally due to potential costs associated with third-party arbitration for labor organization certification and any negotiated increases in wages or benefits, which are subject to approval by the County Commissioners. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signs all legislation. This bill concerns the administration and employment terms of the Washington County Sheriff's Office, where the Sheriff is a state constitutional officer under the Governor's general executive oversight.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and providing counsel to the General Assembly and state officials, including Sheriffs. The bill defines 'police misconduct' and clarifies the legal employment status of deputies, which are matters of legal interpretation and representation for the state.

As the state's principal personnel and benefits agency, DBM is impacted by the bill's explicit clarification that Washington County special deputy sheriffs are not state employees for the purpose of employee benefits, thereby excluding them from state-managed personnel systems.

The bill directly amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article of the Maryland Code. As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is relevant because Sheriffs are established as officers of the court within this statutory framework.

The SRA administers retirement and pension benefits for state employees and law enforcement. The bill's specification that certain deputies are not state employees for the purpose of employee benefits impacts their eligibility and categorization within state retirement systems.

PERB is responsible for standardizing collective bargaining across the public workforce. This bill creates a specific collective bargaining framework for Washington County deputies that utilizes the American Arbitration Association, creating an alternative process that differentiates these employees from those under standard PERB jurisdiction.

The bill clarifies that special deputy sheriffs are not state employees for 'employment security' purposes. Since the Maryland Department of Labor administers unemployment insurance (employment security), this clarification impacts their administration of state liability and claims.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references training standards designated by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (housed within DPSCS) and addresses the employment conditions of 'correctional deputies,' which overlaps with the department's general mission regarding correctional and law enforcement standards.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a Class B-GSF (golf simulator facility) license to a golf simulator facility under certain circumstances; authorizing the license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption under certain circumstances; requiring the license holder to submit an annual gross sales report to the Board before a license may be renewed; and establishing an annual license fee of $1,500.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Golf Simulator Facility
bill_summary: This bill establishes a Class B-GSF (golf simulator facility) license in Frederick County, allowing eligible golf simulator facilities with at least five simulator bays to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption. To maintain the license, facilities must meet specific revenue thresholds: simulator rental fees must account for at least 50% of annual gross sales, food must account for at least 15%, and alcoholic beverages cannot exceed 35%.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Golf simulator facility owners and operators in Frederick County, patrons of these facilities, and the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues increase by $2,250 for each new Class B-GSF license issued ($1,500 annual license fee plus a $750 initial application fee) and $1,500 for each annual renewal thereafter. The Frederick County government reports that at least one small business is interested in applying. There is no impact on state revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state agency responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and enforcing state tax laws related to the sale of beer, wine, and liquor.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and enforcing state laws. The Governor signed this legislation into law, authorizing the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners to issue the new Class B-GSF license.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and local boards of license commissioners regarding the interpretation and enforcement of the Maryland Alcoholic Beverages Article.

Synopsis: Increasing, from $8 to $10, the auctioneer's fee for the tax sale of property in Garrett County for each property sold.
Title: Garrett County - Tax Sales - Auctioneer Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill increases the auctioneer's fee for the tax sale of property in Garrett County from $8 to $10 for each property sold.
stakeholders: Auctioneers, property owners facing tax sales, and property purchasers in Garrett County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates the bill has no State effect and does not materially affect Garrett County finances. The auctioneer's fee is typically paid by the purchaser of the property at tax sale and is included as a lien on the property.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing bills into law; the Governor approved this specific legislation on April 11, 2023.

The Administrative Office of the Courts (Judiciary) was a cited information source for the bill's fiscal note. Additionally, the judicial branch manages the legal proceedings related to tax sales, such as the foreclosure of the right of redemption, which may be impacted by changes in tax sale expense structures.

Synopsis: Updating certain provisions of law regarding Baltimore City alcoholic beverages districts to refer to the Legislative Districting Plan of 2022; and requiring the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to grant a certain exemption to certain persons under certain circumstances.
Title: Baltimore City – Alcoholic Beverages Districts – Legislative Districting Plan References
bill_summary: This emergency bill updates the statutory definitions of alcoholic beverages districts in Baltimore City to align with the boundaries of the 2022 Legislative Districting Plan, replacing references to the 2012 plan. It requires the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to exempt license holders from certain new prohibitions created by the district boundary changes if their activities were approved by February 1, 2022, and they have maintained continuous ownership of the licensed premises.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and business owners located in Baltimore City legislative districts 40, 41, 43, 44, 45, and 46.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill has no State fiscal impact and a minimal local impact on Baltimore City. The changes are technical in nature, updating district references to maintain consistency with the 2022 Legislative Districting Plan, and do not directly affect city operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal regulator of the alcohol industry in Maryland, the Comptroller's office oversees the implementation of the Alcoholic Beverages Article. Updates to district boundaries for licensing in Baltimore City directly impact the agency's regulatory and oversight framework.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City, which is a state agency. The agency is responsible for providing legal guidance on the interpretation and enforcement of the bill's provisions, including the specific grandfathering clause for license holders.

The Department of Planning manages the data, technical analysis, and mapping associated with the Maryland Legislative Districting Plans. The bill updates statutory references to utilize the 2022 districting boundaries for alcohol licensing districts.

The Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City is a state-level board whose members are appointed by the Governor. This office manages the recruitment and vetting process for these positions, ensuring the board is properly staffed to implement the bill's requirements.

Synopsis: Altering the timing of the annual election of the officers of the Talbot County Board of Education to be at its last meeting at the end of each calendar year, or at the meeting in December each year.
Title: Talbot County - Board of Education - Election of Officers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting

bill_summary: This bill changes the timing for the Talbot County Board of Education to elect its president and vice president. Rather than electing these officers at the first meeting of the calendar year, the board must now conduct the election at its last meeting of the calendar year or during its meeting in December.
stakeholders: Members of the Talbot County Board of Education and the Talbot County Public Schools system
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State or local finances. As noted in the fiscal and policy note, the change is procedural in nature and does not affect Talbot County's revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article of the Maryland Annotated Code, which governs the state's public education system. As the agency responsible for leadership and oversight of the 24 local school systems, including the Talbot County Board of Education, MSDE is relevant to changes in the governing statutes and procedural requirements of these local boards.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing legislation passed by the General Assembly into law. This bill was passed and signed by the Governor to alter the procedural requirements for the internal election of officers within the Talbot County Board of Education.

Synopsis: Altering the requirements for the subject matter of continuing education courses for licensees issued an initial license by the Real Estate Commission.
Title: Real Estate Brokers, Salespersons, and Associate Brokers - Continuing Education Courses - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill alters the continuing education requirements for real estate brokers, salespersons, and associate brokers who have been issued an initial license by the State Real Estate Commission. It requires these new licensees to complete specific coursework in topics such as contract writing, escrow funds, property management, landlord and tenant laws, and real estate financing, while maintaining separate existing requirements for license renewals.
stakeholders: Newly licensed real estate brokers, salespersons, and associate brokers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund expenditures for the State Real Estate Commission increase by approximately $42,600 in fiscal 2024 for IT programming changes and consulting to track and enforce the new educational requirements. Small ongoing consulting costs ranging from $2,200 to $2,500 are expected in subsequent years. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for overseeing the licensing and regulation of various professions in Maryland. It manages the State Real Estate Commission, which is the entity responsible for implementing the continuing education requirements and course approvals mandated by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission, which is an ongoing regulatory body mentioned throughout the bill and fiscal note, falls under this category. The bill specifically directs the Commission to alter its approved subject matter for continuing education and results in a direct fiscal impact of $42,600 for the Commission's programming and consulting costs.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. The bill has a notable fiscal impact on special fund expenditures for the State Real Estate Commission, which falls under DBM's budgetary oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring the Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to confer to identify ways the Comptroller could collaborate with the Department to enhance access to certain property tax benefits administered by the Department; and requiring the Comptroller and the Department to submit a joint report of their findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Comptroller and State Department of Assessments and Taxation - Enhancing Access to Property Tax Benefits - Report
bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) to collaborate to identify ways to enhance access to and awareness of property tax benefits, including homeowners', homestead, and renters' tax credits, as well as exemptions for disabled veterans. The agencies must produce a joint report by December 1, 2023, outlining recommendations to simplify the application process and provide an implementation timeline and budget.
responsible_party: The Maryland Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners, renters, disabled veterans, surviving spouses of veterans, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and the Office of the Comptroller.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $18,000 in fiscal 2024 for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to hire a consultant to assist with the required report. The Comptroller’s Office is expected to handle its responsibilities within existing resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is explicitly named as a lead agency responsible for conferring with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to simplify tax credit applications, share income data to reduce redundant reporting, and submit a joint report to the General Assembly.

The bill specifically addresses enhancing access to property tax exemptions for disabled veterans, disabled active duty service members, and their surviving spouses, which are core benefit programs this department advocates for.

The Homeowners' and Renters' tax credits are critical financial supports for older adults on fixed incomes; the department's network often assists seniors in accessing these programs to ensure housing stability.

The bill targets improved access to property tax benefits for residents with service-connected disabilities, aligning with the department's mission to coordinate inclusive services and accessible housing for Marylanders with disabilities.

The board adjudicates disputes related to property tax assessments and credits; changes in how these benefits are administered or applied for may impact the volume or nature of appeals brought before the local boards.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the court is impacted by procedural changes in the administration of the property tax credits and exemptions addressed in the bill.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for oversight of the general fund expenditures identified in the fiscal note required to produce the study and implement potential policy recommendations.

The bill's mandate to eliminate waste, simplify application processes, and reduce redundant government reporting directly aligns with this office's mission to enhance the efficiency and responsiveness of state operations.

The team's focus on economic mobility and evidence-based strategies to support Maryland families is relevant to the bill's goal of enhancing access to financial property tax benefits for vulnerable populations.
The property tax benefits discussed (Renters' and Homeowners' credits) are essential tools for housing affordability and community revitalization, which are central to this department's mission.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for a real estate appraisal license and for a certificate for residential or general real estate appraisal to include completion of certain criteria in the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal program.
Title: Real Estate Appraisers - Licensing and Certification - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill establishes an alternative qualification pathway for individuals seeking licensure or certification as real estate appraisers. It allows applicants to complete the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) program as a substitute for the existing requirement to complete 1,000 or 1,500 hours of supervised trainee experience.
responsible_party: State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors
stakeholders: Prospective real estate appraisers, appraiser trainees, and the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures are expected to increase due to an influx of additional licensure and certification applicants following the establishment of the alternative pathway. However, the Department of Legislative Services indicates that a reliable fiscal estimate is not feasible because the number of individuals who will use this pathway is unknown. The Commission is required by statute to adjust licensing fees to cover any increase in operating expenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors is housed within the Department of Labor. This agency is the primary regulator responsible for implementing the new licensure and certification qualifications, managing the application process, and overseeing the special fund that receives licensing fees.

The bill explicitly identifies the Secretary of State as the official upon whom service of process is binding for non-resident applicants seeking certification for residential or general real estate appraisal.

The bill is expected to increase special fund revenues and expenditures. DBM oversees the state's budget and would be involved if the Department of Labor requires additional personnel to handle an influx of new applicants or a higher volume of consumer complaints resulting from the expanded pool of licensees.

OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. If the influx of new licensees leads to more consumer complaints or if applicants challenge the Commission's determination of their qualifications under the new criteria, OAH would preside over those hearings.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers and would advise on the implementation of the new qualifications and the integration of federal standards (FIRREA) into state regulation.
The Governor's Office has general oversight of the executive branch agencies (such as the Department of Labor) implementing this legislation and is responsible for signing the bill into law.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County to meet at least twice a month; authorizing the Board to hold public meetings in person or through live video streaming; and prohibiting the Board from meeting solely through live video streaming for more than two consecutive meetings without a formal declaration of a state of emergency.
Title: Garrett County - Board of County Commissioners - Meetings
bill_summary: This bill requires the Garrett County Board of Commissioners to meet at least twice monthly instead of weekly and authorizes these public meetings to be held via live video streaming. It also restricts the Board from meeting solely through live video streaming for more than two consecutive meetings unless a state of emergency is declared.
responsible_party: Garrett County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Garrett County residents and the Garrett County Board of County Commissioners
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. According to the fiscal note, altering the meeting frequency and format for the Garrett County Commissioners will not affect county finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office manages intergovernmental relations with local entities and oversees the executive branch's role in the legislative process, including signing public local laws. Furthermore, the bill's remote meeting exception is triggered by a formal declaration of a state of emergency, which is an executive action of the Governor.

The bill permits the Garrett County Board of Commissioners to meet solely through live video streaming under a formal declaration of a state of emergency. The Department of Emergency Management is the primary agency responsible for coordinating the state's emergency response and supporting local jurisdictions during such declarations.
The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of the state's official records, including the laws and executive orders that this bill modifies or references.

The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for government records of permanent value from county and municipal governments. Changes to the frequency and format of the Garrett County Board of Commissioners' public meetings affect the documentation and records that the Archives is mandated to preserve.

Synopsis: Repealing certain requirements that the Maryland Transit Administration increase fares for certain transit services according to the Consumer Price Index; and repealing certain provisions prohibiting the Administration from increasing fares under certain circumstances.
Title: Maryland Transit Administration – Fare Price Requirements – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill repeals the statutory requirement that the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) increase its base fare prices every two years and every five years based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and other factors. It preserves the MTA's authority to modify transit fares through a public hearing process.
stakeholders: Maryland transit users, including passengers of local bus lines, light rail, Metro subway, commuter buses, MARC trains, and mobility/paratransit vehicles.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are expected to decrease as the bill repeals mandated fare increases. Estimated revenue losses include $6.9 million in FY 2024, $7.1 million in FY 2025, $18.1 million in FY 2026, $17.6 million in FY 2027, and $19.8 million in FY 2028. These losses could be mitigated if the MTA exercises its discretionary authority to adjust fares after public hearings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory requirements for the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) regarding how it sets and increases fare prices for mass transit services.

As the parent department of the MTA, the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is responsible for the overall transit system and the Transportation Trust Fund, which the fiscal note indicates will see a significant decrease in revenue due to this bill.

DBM is responsible for state revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The bill's multi-million dollar impact on the Transportation Trust Fund affects the state's overall fiscal picture and budget execution.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like the MTA and MDOT regarding statutory changes and the legal requirements for public hearings when revising fare prices.
Changes to public transit fare requirements directly impact the affordability and accessibility of transportation services for Marylanders with disabilities, a key focus area for this department.
The Department of Aging advocates for older adults, who are significant users of public transit. Changes to fare increase mandates impact the economic well-being of this population.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors state revenue streams. The repeal of mandated fare increases represents a notable change in projected state revenues.

Synopsis: Altering the uses of the Historic Preservation Loan Fund; and authorizing the Maryland Historic Trust to transfer funds from the Fund to a qualified cooperating nonprofit organization to pay for the acquisition, restoration, or rehabilitation of certain historic properties, to provide loans for the acquisition, rehabilitation, restoration, or refinancing of certain properties, and for necessary administrative and programmatic expenses.
Title: Maryland Historic Trust - Historic Preservation Loan Fund - Qualified Cooperating Nonprofit Organizations - Transfers

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Historic Trust (MHT) to transfer funds from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund to qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations. These nonprofit organizations can use the funds to acquire, restore, or rehabilitate historic properties, or to provide loans to individuals, business entities, and political subdivisions for historic preservation purposes.
stakeholders: Qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations, Maryland Historic Trust, individuals, business entities, and political subdivisions involved in historic preservation.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures may increase and special fund revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2024. The Maryland Historic Trust estimates that the Loan Fund will have expenditures of $204,000 and revenues of $176,208 in fiscal 2024. Revenue decreases occur because funds transferred to nonprofits are not recovered through loan payments, unlike traditional program loans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historic Trust (MHT) is a unit within the Department of Planning. The bill directly impacts the Maryland Historic Trust by altering the uses of the Historic Preservation Loan Fund and authorizing MHT to transfer funds to nonprofit organizations.
The bill explicitly states that the Comptroller shall account for the MHT Loan Fund, which is being modified by this legislation.
The bill mandates that the State Treasurer shall hold the MHT Loan Fund and invest its money in the same manner as other State money.
The Board of Public Works is required to approve certain loans or expenditures from the MHT Loan Fund, particularly those financed through the sale of State general obligation bonds.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is tasked under the referenced statutes with determining if properties will be occupied by individuals of limited income, which affects the interest rates of the loans managed under this program.
As the agency responsible for budget development and fiscal planning, DBM is involved in the appropriation process for the MHT Loan Program and was consulted on the bill's fiscal impact.

This multi-agency initiative includes the Department of Planning and focuses on community revitalization and historic preservation, which are the core objectives of the MHT Loan Program and the transfers authorized by the bill.
The bill requires the Maryland Historic Trust to report to the Governor annually on the financial status and activities of the MHT Loan Program.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland to study the adequacy of trauma center funding across the State for operating, capital, and workforce costs; and requiring the Commission to reports its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
Title: Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland to examine the adequacy of funding for the state's trauma centers regarding operating, capital, and workforce costs. The commission is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS) and the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC)
stakeholders: Maryland trauma centers (including Level I, II, III, pediatric, and primary adult resource centers), trauma physicians, the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems, the Maryland Health Care Commission, the Maryland Department of Health, and the General Assembly.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS) and the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) can staff the commission using existing budgeted resources. Expense reimbursements for commission members are expected to be minimal, and the bill has no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees the budget and personnel resources for the agencies tasked with staffing the commission and will manage any potential fiscal impacts or state employee expense reimbursements identified in the fiscal note.
The Secretary of Health is a designated member of the commission and is responsible for appointing several of its other members representing various trauma center levels and health organizations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland, a temporary body created to conduct a specific study and provide recommendations to the state government.
The commission is required to report its findings and recommendations regarding trauma center funding to the Governor by December 1, 2023.
The HSCRC is a designated member of the commission and co-administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, which is a primary subject of the commission's study.
The MHCC is required to co-chair the commission and jointly provide staffing; the agency also co-administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund being studied.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is required to co-chair the commission and jointly provide staffing; the agency's primary mission involves designating and regulating the trauma centers that are the subject of the study.

Synopsis: Making certain provisions of law governing cemeteries applicable to pet cemeteries; providing that a certain registered cemeterian, registered crematory operator, or permit holder who sells or offers to sell to the public certain services for pet remains owes a duty of perpetual care for the cemetery in which certain pet remains are interred; and requiring the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight to adopt regulations to enforce certain provisions of the Act.
Title: Cemeteries - Interment - Pet Remains
bill_summary: This bill extends Maryland's cemetery regulations to pet cemeteries and defines pet remains. It requires registered cemeterians, crematory operators, and permit holders offering pet burial or cremation services to provide perpetual care for the cemetery where pet remains are interred. Additionally, it updates preneed burial contract requirements to include pet-specific information.
responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight within the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Pet owners, pet cemetery operators, registered cemeterians, registered crematory operators, and permit holders.
fiscal_impact_summary: State fiscal impact is expected to be minimal. The Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO) can implement the bill with existing resources, and special fund revenues may increase slightly if additional pet cemeteries register with OCO. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO) is housed within the Department of Labor. The bill explicitly requires the Director of OCO to adopt regulations and enforce the new perpetual care requirements for pet cemeteries, making it the primary implementing agency.

The OAG serves as the chief legal counsel for state agencies, including the Department of Labor. It will be responsible for providing legal guidance and reviewing the new regulations required by this bill for legal sufficiency.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases involving state agencies. Any enforcement actions or disputes regarding the new pet cemetery regulations and registrations would be heard by administrative law judges at this agency.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and approved the bill. The legislation impacts the regulatory duties of an executive official (the Director of Cemetery Oversight) within a principal department.

DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and oversight. The fiscal note indicates that the bill will have a minimal impact on the Department of Labor's special fund revenues and administrative resources, which falls under DBM's monitoring purview.

Synopsis: Extending until fiscal year 2028 the appropriation of $500,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund that the Governor is required to include in the annual budget bill for the operation of the replica sailing vessel known as the Pride of Baltimore II.
Title: Pride of Baltimore II - Appropriations - Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill extends and reestablishes a mandated annual appropriation of $500,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund for the operation of the Pride of Baltimore II, a replica sailing vessel. The mandate and its associated reporting requirements are extended to cover fiscal years 2024 through 2028, requiring the Governor to include these funds in the annual State budget and the recipient to submit detailed expenditure and itinerary reports.
stakeholders: Operators of the Pride of Baltimore II, Maryland maritime education and tourism sectors, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund increase by $500,000 annually from fiscal 2024 through 2028. This reflects a mandated appropriation for fiscal 2025 through 2028 and an assumed discretionary appropriation for fiscal 2024. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $500,000 (referenced as $600,000 in the bill text) specifically from the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which is managed by the Maryland Department of Transportation. Additionally, the department is designated to receive annual expenditure reports, itineraries, and strategic business plans from the recipient entity.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for budget development and execution. The bill establishes a mandated appropriation that DBM must incorporate into the Governor's annual budget and supervise for fiscal 2024 through 2028.
The bill requires the Governor to include the mandated appropriation for the operation of the Pride of Baltimore II in the annual state budget for a period extended through fiscal year 2028.

The vessel's operation is explicitly intended to foster economic development, aligning with the department's role as Maryland's primary economic development agency. The vessel serves as a promotional tool for the state's assets.

The operation of the Pride of Baltimore II is mandated to foster tourism and represent the citizens of Maryland in every port visited, which directly supports the office's mission to stimulate the tourism economy and promote the state as a travel destination.

Synopsis: Requiring in Frederick County a license holder to frame and conspicuously display an alcoholic beverages license on the licensed premises.
Title: Frederick County – Alcoholic Beverages Licenses – Display of License
bill_summary: This bill modifies the requirements for displaying alcoholic beverages licenses in Frederick County by removing the statewide mandate that licenses be framed under glass. Instead, license holders in Frederick County are simply required to frame the license and display it conspicuously on the premises.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. It is not anticipated to materially affect Frederick County finances or operations, and there is no impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller's Office is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry in Maryland. This bill alters the specific requirements for how alcoholic beverages licenses must be displayed on-premises in Frederick County, which falls under the Comptroller's regulatory and enforcement purview for the industry.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller and any state bodies overseeing alcoholic beverages, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of statutory changes to the Alcoholic Beverages Article.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, coordinates policy initiatives, and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation, including local bills that modify state law for specific counties.

Synopsis: Increasing the total amount of credits against the State income tax that the Maryland Higher Education Commission may approve in a taxable year for certain individuals with certain student loan debt amounts; requiring the Commission to reserve a certain amount of the tax credits that the Commission is authorized to approve for certain graduates; extending, from 2 years to 3 years, the period of time that an individual who claims the credit has to prove that they used the credit to repay the individual's student loan debt; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill increases the total amount of Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credits that the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) can approve from $9 million to $18 million annually. It mandates that $9 million of these credits be reserved for State employees, with priority given to those who graduated from Maryland institutions where at least 40% of students receive Pell Grants. Additionally, the bill extends the time a recipient has to prove they used the credit for loan repayment from two to three years and requires MHEC to conduct targeted outreach and marketing.
stakeholders: Qualified taxpayers with at least $20,000 in student loan debt, Maryland State employees, and graduates of Maryland higher education institutions with high Pell Grant eligibility.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund revenues will decrease by $9,000,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2024. This reduction is due to the increase in the maximum authorized amount of tax credits from $9,000,000 to $18,000,000. The fiscal 2024 revenue reduction is already assumed in the State budget. There is no impact on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Commission is responsible for certifying tax credit amounts, prioritizing applicants based on new criteria (such as Pell Grant eligibility), implementing an outreach and marketing plan, and providing an annual demographic report to the Governor and General Assembly.

As the state's chief tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for processing the student loan debt relief tax credits on income tax returns, managing the recapture of credits for non-compliance, and accounting for the estimated $9 million annual reduction in general fund revenues.

The department is the principal fiscal and personnel agency. It is relevant because the bill has a significant impact on state revenues ($9 million decrease) and creates a specific $9 million tax credit reserve and priority for State employees, whom the department manages.

As the state's public higher education system, its institutions and graduates are directly impacted by the bill's prioritization of in-state graduates and Pell Grant recipients. The bill also tasks the Commission with encouraging these institutions to advise new graduates about the credit.

As a public, historically black research university, its graduates are key targets for the bill's prioritization of Pell Grant-eligible institutions. The university is also expected to participate in the Commission's outreach plan to advise graduates of the credit.

As an independent public honors college, its graduates are eligible for the credit, and the institution is part of the state higher education network encouraged to advise new graduates of the program's availability.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires the Commission to report annually to the Governor regarding the number of applicants, award amounts, and demographic breakdowns of credit recipients.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to issue an apprentice hunting license to a person under the age of 17 years who has previously been issued an apprentice hunting license under certain circumstances.
Title: Natural Resources – Apprentice Hunting License – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue a second or subsequent apprentice hunting license to an individual under the age of 17, provided the applicant repeats a Department-approved short course on firearms and hunter safety.
stakeholders: Individuals under the age of 17 interested in hunting, apprentice hunters, and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances. According to the fiscal note, any potential impact on hunting license fee revenue—which is $10 for resident apprentice licenses and $20 for nonresident apprentice licenses—is anticipated to be minimal. The Department of Natural Resources can update regulations using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for issuing hunting licenses, including the apprentice hunting licenses altered by this bill. It also approves the safety courses and manages hunting regulations affected by this legislation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Natural Resources, and would be responsible for advising on the legal and regulatory implementation of these changes to the hunting license statutes.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for estimating and tracking state revenues. This bill impacts hunting license fee revenue, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state's fiscal health.

The Rural Maryland Council advocates for rural interests and natural resource stewardship. Hunting is a significant cultural and recreational activity in rural Maryland, and policies encouraging youth participation align with the Council's focus on rural quality of life.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. As the Department of Natural Resources is a cabinet-level agency, this legislative change to hunting policy falls under the Governor's administrative and policy oversight.

Synopsis: Eliminating requirements for collection agencies and certain non-depository financial institutions to maintain separate licenses for branch locations and authorizing them to conduct business at multiple licensed locations under a single license; and altering certain other requirements and provisions governing the licensing and regulation of collection agencies and certain non-depository financial institutions, including applications, assessments, and bond requirements.
Title: Financial Regulation - Modernizing Licensing of Non-Depository Institutions and Elimination of Branch License Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.

Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill eliminates the requirement for collection agencies and various non-depository financial institutions (such as consumer lenders, money transmitters, and mortgage lenders) to maintain separate licenses for branch locations. Instead, it creates a single licensing system where an institution obtains one license covering all its licensed locations. The bill also authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to impose annual assessments on licensees to cover regulatory costs and updates bonding requirements for these institutions.
responsible_party: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Collection agencies and non-depository financial institutions (including consumer lenders, installment lenders, sales finance companies, mortgage lenders, check cashers, money transmitters, and debt management companies) operating in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately 3,000,000 annually starting in FY 2024 because of the elimination of separate branch licensing fees. The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OCFR) intends to use this revenue reduction to draw down a large existing balance in the Non-depository Special Fund. If the fund balance falls below target levels in the future, OCFR is authorized to replenish it through annual assessments on licensees. There is no significant impact on state expenditures, and local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commissioner of Financial Regulation, an official within the Maryland Department of Labor, is the primary regulator responsible for implementing the modernized licensing system and managing the Non-depository Special Fund established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory requirements, fee-setting authority, and regulatory duties of the State Collection Agency Licensing Board, which falls under this collective agency designation.
The State Treasurer is designated as the custodian of the Non-depository Special Fund and is responsible for allocating interest earned on the fund's assets in accordance with the bill's provisions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and the State Collection Agency Licensing Board regarding the enforcement of financial services laws and consumer protection regulations.

The Comptroller accounts for net interest on State money and ensures that interest from the Non-depository Special Fund is properly credited to the fund rather than the General Fund, as required by the bill.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the annual state budget and budget amendment procedures that govern expenditures from the newly modified Non-depository Special Fund.

The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for the bill's implementation and is responsible for the final approval of the state's annual budget, which includes the special fund allocations defined in the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing rules governing the exercise of the decanting power to distribute the property of a first trust to one or more second trusts or to modify the terms of a first trust; and providing for the retroactive application of the Act.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Trusts - Decanting (Maryland Trust Decanting Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: The Maryland Trust Decanting Act establishes rules and procedures allowing a trustee or authorized fiduciary to distribute property from an existing trust into one or more new trusts or to modify the terms of the existing trust. This process, known as decanting, is subject to fiduciary duties, specific notice requirements for beneficiaries and settlors, and protections for vested interests and tax benefits. The act also includes provisions for special needs trusts and charitable interests.
responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Trustees, fiduciaries, trust beneficiaries, settlors, charitable organizations, and individuals with disabilities who are beneficiaries of trusts.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to have a material, direct effect on Maryland State or local government operations or finances. Specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditures are not provided because the fiscal impact is expected to be negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly grants the Attorney General the rights of a qualified beneficiary when a trust contains a determinable charitable interest. The Attorney General must receive notice of an intended exercise of decanting power and possesses the authority to object to or consent to changes in the governing law of such trusts.

The Maryland Trust Decanting Act establishes a framework for court involvement, allowing the judiciary to provide instructions to fiduciaries, appoint special fiduciaries, and adjudicate the effectiveness or validity of the exercise of decanting powers.

As the agency responsible for administrative probate and providing clerk services to the Orphans' Courts, the Register of Wills is directly involved in the oversight of estate and trust-related matters, including the collection of inheritance taxes which may be impacted by trust modifications.

The bill contains extensive provisions regarding 'Special Needs Trusts' and 'Special Needs Fiduciaries.' These sections govern how trust decanting can be used to protect the rights and eligibility of beneficiaries with disabilities for governmental assistance.

The management and modification of special needs trusts via decanting directly impact a beneficiary's eligibility for public health services and Medicaid (Health Care Financing), which are administered by this department.

Changes to trust structures and distributions through decanting can affect an individual's eligibility for asset-tested social programs, such as food and cash assistance (SNAP), which are managed by DHS.

The bill includes specific mandates to preserve various federal and state tax benefits (e.g., marital deductions, charitable deductions, and S corporation stock eligibility) during the decanting process, which falls under the Comptroller's oversight of state revenue and tax enforcement.

Synopsis: Requiring that each memorandum of understanding establishing a school in the Pathways in Technology Early College High (P-TECH) School Program ensures that each P-TECH student receives a high school diploma immediately following completion of high school graduation requirements.
Title: Pathways in Technology Early College High (P–TECH) School Program – High School Diplomas

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires that students enrolled in a Pathways in Technology Early College High (P-TECH) school receive their high school diploma immediately upon completing graduation requirements, regardless of whether they have finished the full six-year associate's degree pathway sequence. It mandates that all memoranda of understanding establishing P-TECH schools include provisions to ensure the timely awarding of diplomas.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local county boards of education
stakeholders: P-TECH students, local school systems, community colleges, and industry partners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $14,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland State Department of Education to update the student accountability system to allow continued tracking and funding for P-TECH students after they receive their diplomas. Local school systems may incur minimal costs to update their own student accountability systems. The bill specifically does not alter existing education funding formulas under Titles 5, 7, or 16 of the Education Article.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for overseeing public education and setting graduation requirements. The bill directly impacts MSDE by requiring it to update student accountability systems and guidance to ensure P-TECH students receive diplomas upon meeting graduation requirements, resulting in a fiscal impact of approximately $14,000.

The P-TECH program relies on partnerships with colleges regulated by the Higher Education Commission. The bill's changes to the graduation timeline and its continued reference to college credit and supplemental grants under Title 16 of the Education Article involve the commission's role in coordinating postsecondary education and student aid.

The Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center tracks student performance and workforce outcomes by linking data from MSDE, MHEC, and Labor. Changing the timing of high school diploma issuance for P-TECH students who remain in the program for additional years impacts how the center collects and analyzes graduation and longitudinal data.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the budget execution related to the $14,000 general fund expenditure required for MSDE to update its student accountability systems as a result of this bill.

The P-TECH program is a strategic workforce development initiative designed to align education with industry needs. The board, as the Governor's chief policy body for workforce strategy, is impacted by changes to the pathway and graduation milestones of students entering the talent pipeline.

The Department of Labor oversees workforce development programs and industry compliance. Since P-TECH is a dual-enrollment workforce pathway involving industry partners, the timing of high school graduation for these students is relevant to the department's monitoring of state labor pipelines.

The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch. P-TECH is a high-profile education and economic policy, and the Governor is responsible for signing the legislation and overseeing the agencies implementing the program's changes.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation.
Title: Maryland African American Museum Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill reduces the membership of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation from 37 to 25 members and modifies the board's composition, including adding appointments from the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House.
stakeholders: Members of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation, the Commission on African American History and Culture, and the Governor of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the governance and composition of the Corporation's Board of Directors, reducing the total membership from 37 to 25 and changing the appointing authorities for various seats.

The Governor is the primary appointing authority for the Board; this bill reduces the number of direct gubernatorial appointments from 36 to 22 and adjusts the specific qualifications required for those seats.
The bill requires the Board of Directors to include a representative from Morgan State University who must be approved by the university's Board of Regents.

As the office that assists the Governor in vetting and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions, it will manage the reduced number of appointments and new legislative requirements for the MAAMC board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Commission on African American History and Culture to approve a member to the MAAMC board to ensure coordination and consistency with statewide programs.

The Department of Planning oversees the state's historical and cultural programs and was specifically identified in the bill's fiscal note as a source of information regarding the impacts of these board changes.

Synopsis: Establishing that a county or a municipal corporation has the authority to approve or deny any local permit required under a certificate of public convenience and necessity issued by the Public Service Commission for generating stations, transmission lines, and qualified generator lead lines; requiring a county or municipal corporation to approve or deny the local permits in a certain manner; prohibiting a county or municipal corporation from conditioning the approval of the local permits on certain approvals; etc.
Title: Public Service Commission – Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity – Local Permits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: This bill establishes that local governments, including counties and municipalities, have the authority to approve or deny local permits for energy projects such as generating stations and transmission lines that have been issued a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) by the Public Service Commission. The bill requires local governments to process these permits within a reasonable time and prohibits them from conditioning approval on specific zoning actions, such as conditional use, special exception, or floating zone approvals.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission and local county and municipal governments
stakeholders: Local governments (counties and municipalities), energy infrastructure developers, and the Maryland Public Service Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State government finances or operations. The impact on local government finances and operations is expected to be minimal, primarily involving administrative changes to ensure local permits for projects with a CPCN are processed within a reasonable timeframe and without prohibited zoning conditions. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the fiscal note characterizes the overall effect as minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Public Utilities Article regarding Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN), which is the primary regulatory and licensing mechanism administered by the Public Service Commission for energy generating stations and transmission lines.

The fiscal note identifies the Department of Natural Resources and its Power Plant Research Program as integral participants in the comprehensive CPCN process, which this bill modifies by clarifying the scope of local permitting authority.

The Department of the Environment is a key state agency involved in the CPCN review process, evaluating the environmental impacts of projects that are the subject of the local permits and state certificates addressed in the bill.

The bill limits the ability of local governments to condition permits on zoning findings or consistency with comprehensive plans. The Department of Planning provides guidance to local governments on land use and planning, making this state preemption highly relevant to their work.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and other state agencies. This bill codifies and clarifies legal preemption issues following the Supreme Court of Maryland's decision in Perennial Solar, requiring legal interpretation and defense.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including the state's energy policy and the balance of authority between state regulators and local jurisdictions.

Generating stations and transmission lines are frequently sited on agricultural land. Changes to the CPCN and local permitting process affect land use and the economic viability of farming regions, which the department supports.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the State Board of Pharmacy to include a registered pharmacy technician; authorizing a licensed pharmacist, under certain circumstances, to delegate the entry of certain data into databases or patient charts to be performed at a remote location to a registered pharmacy technician and a registered pharmacy intern; prohibiting registered pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees from making decisions requiring the professional judgment of a pharmacist; etc.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Board Membership, Delegated Pharmacy Acts, and Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill adds a registered pharmacy technician to the State Board of Pharmacy and extends the board's termination date to July 1, 2025. It allows pharmacists to delegate remote data entry tasks to pharmacy technicians and interns under specific conditions. Additionally, it authorizes pharmacy technicians to administer specific vaccinations, including influenza, COVID-19, and pneumonia for adults, and RSV and shingles for individuals age 50 and older, while prohibiting pharmacy technician trainees from administering vaccines.
stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, registered pharmacy technicians, pharmacy interns, pharmacy technician trainees, and patients receiving vaccination services in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Pharmacy are maintained through fiscal 2025 due to the sunset extension. Special fund expenditures may increase minimally to cover the per diem and related expenses of the additional board member. Other administrative workloads on the Board can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Pharmacy is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Health. This bill directly impacts the Board's composition, the scope of practice for the professionals it regulates (pharmacists and pharmacy technicians), and extends its statutory authority under the sunset law.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the State Board of Pharmacy. This bill increases the board's membership by adding a registered pharmacy technician position which the Governor must fill.
