bill_summary: This bill protects the privacy of medical records related to reproductive health care, including abortion and other sensitive services. It establishes the Protected Health Care Commission to advise the Secretary of Health on identifying health services that require privacy protections. It prohibits health information exchanges and electronic health networks from disclosing specific abortion-related data to out-of-state entities without patient consent and mandates that certain insurance plans cover abortion services without cost-sharing.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Individuals seeking reproductive health services, health care providers, health information exchanges, electronic health networks, and insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Maryland Health Care Commission increase by 100,000 dollars in fiscal 2024 for contractual services to develop data privacy standards. The Maryland Department of Health is expected to implement its requirements, including staffing the Protected Health Care Commission, using existing resources. There is no significant impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primary impacts this commission by expanding its purpose to include establishing policies and standards for reproductive health data confidentiality. It also requires the commission to adopt emergency regulations to restrict the exchange of patient data related to legally protected health care through the state-designated health information exchange (CRISP).

The Secretary of Health is given significant regulatory authority under the bill to identify diagnostic and medication codes for abortion care and sensitive health services. Additionally, the department is responsible for providing staff to the newly created Protected Health Care Commission.

The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding abortion care services, prohibiting cost-sharing and establishing coverage requirements that the Insurance Commissioner must oversee and potentially exempt under specific federal funding conditions.

The Attorney General or their designee is a required member of the newly established Protected Health Care Commission. The office also serves as the legal counsel for MDH and MHCC as they navigate the complex legal landscape of reproductive health data protections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new permanent body, the Protected Health Care Commission, to advise the Secretary of Health on sensitive health services that should be classified as legally protected health care.

The bill's amendments to the Insurance Article affect health benefit plans and qualified health plans offered within the Exchange, specifically regarding the coverage of abortion care services notwithstanding federal essential health benefit restrictions.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the policy initiatives regarding reproductive rights and coordinates the interagency efforts of MDH, MHCC, and MIA in implementing these protections.

The bill requires MHCC to coordinate with the HSCRC in managing the state-designated health information exchange and ensures that policies regarding data confidentiality are integrated across state health agencies.
DBM is responsible for the fiscal oversight of the $100,000 in special fund expenditures identified in the fiscal note for MHCC to develop the required confidentiality policies and standards.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor criminal penalty for the knowing violation of health information disclosure prohibitions, which may result in new cases requiring adjudication within the state court system.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date of certain provisions of law that establish and govern the funding for the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program; and requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Administration, to conduct a study on available federal and State subsidies and report its findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2024.
Title: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange - State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program for two additional years, moving the sunset from June 30, 2024, to June 30, 2026. The program provides premium subsidies for young adults (typically ages 18 to 34) who purchase health benefit plans in the individual health insurance market. Additionally, the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange must conduct a study on available federal and State subsidies and report findings to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
stakeholders: Young adults in Maryland purchasing health insurance through the individual market, and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund expenditures for the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange increase by as much as 10000000 in FY 2024, 20000000 in FY 2025, and 10000000 in FY 2026 to provide young adult subsidies. These expenditures are funded by the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, which receives a mandated diversion of premium tax revenues. General fund revenues are affected only to the extent that unspent special funds, which would otherwise revert to the general fund at the end of the fiscal year, are instead used for program subsidies. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) is the primary agency responsible for implementing and managing the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Program, establishing eligibility parameters, and conducting the comprehensive study on federal and state subsidies required by the bill.

The bill requires the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) to consult with the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange on the implementation of the subsidy program and the required study regarding federal subsidies and the State's Section 1332 waiver.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is responsible for state budget development and oversight; the bill has a notable fiscal impact of up to $20 million annually in special fund expenditures from the MHBE Fund for the extended pilot program.

The bill affects the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, which also provides essential funding for the Department of Health's Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program.
The Maryland State Treasurer's Office is the principal custodian of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund and is statutory mandated to hold the fund separately.
The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for accounting for the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund and manages the distribution of premium tax revenues that support the fund.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the primary agencies (MHBE and MIA) concerning program regulations and the legal implications of amending federal health insurance waivers.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive departments involved, proposes the annual budget which includes fund transfers for health equity, and sets the overall policy priorities for the administration of the subsidy program.

Synopsis: Requiring insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for certain lung cancer diagnostic imaging and limiting the copayment, coinsurance, or deductible that the entities can require for lung cancer screening and diagnosis; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to conduct an assessment on certain outreach, education, and health disparities in cancer screening and report the results to the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
Title: Cancer Screening - Health Insurance and Assessment of Outreach, Education, and Health Disparities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers to cover recommended follow-up diagnostic imaging for lung cancer for individuals meeting specific criteria and prohibits cost-sharing for these services that exceeds what is charged for breast cancer screenings. Additionally, it directs the Maryland Department of Health to conduct an assessment of outreach, education, and health disparities in cancer screening and to establish a stakeholder workgroup to advise on these issues.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Individuals requiring lung cancer screenings, health insurance carriers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and underserved communities affected by health disparities in cancer care.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,921 in fiscal 2024 for the Maryland Department of Health to conduct the required assessment and lead the stakeholder workgroup. The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in special fund revenues from rate and form filing fees. Local governments may experience increased costs for employee health insurance plans, and the impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program is indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct a comprehensive assessment on cancer screening outreach, education, and health disparities. The department is also tasked with establishing a stakeholder workgroup and reporting findings to the General Assembly, which the fiscal note indicates will require additional general fund expenditures for contractual personnel.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating the state's insurance market. This bill creates new mandates for lung and breast cancer diagnostic imaging coverage and limits cost-sharing, requiring the MIA to review rate and form filings from carriers to ensure compliance with the new statutory requirements.

As the agency that manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM is impacted by any legislation that mandates new health insurance benefits or alters cost-sharing structures, which could lead to indeterminate costs for the state's employee health plan.

The bill affects health benefit plans issued or delivered in the state, including qualified health plans offered through the Exchange. The Exchange is involved in ensuring that plans sold on the marketplace align with state-mandated benefits.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration. It will likely provide legal guidance on the implementation of the new mandates and the interpretation of the defined diagnostic imaging requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the creation of a stakeholder workgroup composed of various community representatives and health professionals to advise the Department of Health on cancer screening and outreach plans for underserved communities.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop a scorecard to evaluate units of State government on the units' performance toward meeting certain participation goals under the Minority Business Enterprise Program and the Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise Program; establishing a certain grading scale for the scorecard; and requiring grades achieved by each unit to be published each year on the Office's website.
Title: Procurement - Minority Business Enterprises and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises - Participation Goal Scorecard

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA) to develop a scorecard with a weighted grading scale to evaluate state agencies on their performance toward meeting Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) participation goals. The grades achieved by each agency must be published annually on GOSBA's website and reported to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA)
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs), and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises (VSBEs)
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that GOSBA can implement the bill's requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no projected impact on state revenues or local government finances, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates GOSBA to develop the scorecard and grading scale, publish the results on their website, and report the findings to the General Assembly.

MDOT serves as the state's MBE certification agency and, along with its various administrations (Aviation, MVA, Port, SHA, MTA, MDTA), is a major procurement unit subject to evaluation under the new scorecard.
As the primary operational support and central procurement authority for the state, DGS is a key unit evaluated by the scorecard for its MBE and VSBE participation performance.
The OAG is consulted in establishing biennial MBE goals and is responsible for the debarment of contractors who fail to meet participation goals.
DBM is a principal fiscal and personnel agency involved in state procurement and is explicitly listed as an agency evaluated on its MBE participation performance.
The Governor's Office (Executive Department) is evaluated as a unit of state government on the scorecard and oversees the office (GOSBA) implementing the bill.
As a major cabinet-level agency with significant procurement activity, MDH is evaluated on its performance toward meeting MBE and VSBE participation goals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is identified in the fiscal note as a cabinet agency with high MBE participation rates that will be subject to the new scorecard evaluation.
MDE is specifically listed in the fiscal note as one of the cabinet agencies evaluated for its performance in meeting participation goals.
DHCD is listed as a cabinet agency evaluated for its performance in meeting participation goals, currently showing high participation rates.
MSDE is a cabinet-level agency evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
DJS is evaluated on its performance toward meeting participation goals and is subject to the grading scale established by the bill.
MSP is a principal department evaluated on its performance in meeting procurement participation goals for minority and veteran-owned businesses.
MDA is a cabinet-level agency evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
The Department of Commerce is evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
DoIT manages state IT infrastructure and procurement and is evaluated for its performance in meeting participation goals.
Maryland Labor is evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
DNR is a cabinet-level agency evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
DHS is a principal department that will be graded on its performance toward meeting participation goals; the fiscal note indicates previous data was unavailable for this unit.
MHEC is evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
The Military Department is evaluated on its performance toward meeting MBE and VSBE participation goals.
The Department of Aging is a cabinet-level agency evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
MDP is a cabinet-level agency evaluated for its procurement performance regarding MBE and VSBE participation goals.
As a large state-funded entity with significant procurement, USM is included in the statewide totals for MBE participation and subject to evaluation.
As a public university and state agency, Morgan State is included in the units evaluated for meeting MBE/VSBE participation goals.
As an independent state agency, the college is included in the units whose procurement performance is measured against state goals.
The BPW formerly administered the VSBE program and oversees significant state contracts that must comply with the participation goals being graded.
As a modal administration under MDOT, the MAA is specifically tracked and graded on its individual MBE participation rates.
The MVA is specifically tracked and graded on its individual MBE participation rates as part of the MDOT performance review.
The MPA is a unit of MDOT evaluated for its performance in meeting participation goals for state contracts.
SHA is a major procurement unit within MDOT that is tracked and graded for its performance in meeting minority business goals.
MTA is a unit of MDOT evaluated for its performance in meeting participation goals for state contracts.
The MDTA is specifically tracked and graded on its individual MBE participation rates as part of the transportation sector performance review.

Synopsis: Requiring the Division of State Documents to make at least the 15 most recent issues of the Maryland Register available to the public for online searching; altering the requirements for a unit of State government to submit certain proposed or emergency regulations, work plans, and evaluation reports to the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review, the Department of Legislative Services, and the Administrator of the Division of State Documents; etc.
Title: State Government - Regulation Procedures and the Maryland Register

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill updates the procedures for State agencies to submit proposed and emergency regulations. It requires the Division of State Documents to make at least the 15 most recent issues of the Maryland Register available for free online searching and mandates the development of an electronic filing system for submitting and tracking regulations. It also extends certain review periods for the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review and establishes formal procedures for notifying legislative bodies of changes to proposed regulations.
responsible_party: Administrator of the Division of State Documents
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, the general public, small businesses, and the General Assembly.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $124,200 in FY 2024 for contractual staff and to supplement lost revenue. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Division of State Documents are projected to decrease by $29,300 in FY 2024 and $39,000 annually thereafter because free online access to the Maryland Register will reduce paid subscriptions. Additional indeterminate costs may arise from fixing and finalizing the electronic filing system (ELF 2.0), with preliminary estimates suggesting costs could reach several million dollars.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Division of State Documents (DSD), which publishes the Maryland Register and the Code of Maryland Regulations (COMAR), is a unit within the Office of the Secretary of State. The bill places direct mandates on the Administrator of DSD to provide free online access to the Maryland Register and to lead the development of a new electronic filing system for state regulations.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to consult with and support the Division of State Documents in the development, maintenance, and security of a new electronic filing system for the submission and tracking of state regulations.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees all units authorized to adopt regulations. The bill fundamentally changes the procedures and electronic systems these executive units must use to propose and track regulations.

The fiscal note identifies specific general fund expenditure increases for personnel and revenue offsets for the Division of State Documents to implement the bill's mandates, which falls under the purview of DBM's fiscal and personnel management.

As a major 'unit' that adopts a high volume of regulations (COMAR Title 10), the Department of Health is significantly impacted by the bill's changes to the submission, tracking, and review procedures for proposed and emergency regulations.

The Department of Transportation and its modal administrations adopt extensive regulations. The bill's revised procedures for filing regulations and using the new electronic system directly impact MDOT's operational processes.

The Maryland State Department of Education is a primary regulatory unit. It must comply with the bill's new procedures for electronic filing and the revised submission requirements for the Maryland Register and the AELR committee.

The Department of the Environment is a major regulatory body. It is explicitly identified as an information source in the fiscal note and is impacted by the updated timelines and digital filing requirements for environmental regulations.

The Department of Labor oversees numerous boards and commissions that adopt regulations. It must transition to the new electronic filing system and follow the altered submission protocols mandated by the bill.
As a state unit that adopts regulations, the Department of Agriculture is impacted by the modified regulatory procedures and the requirement to use the new electronic tracking system.
The Department of Commerce is identified as a regulatory unit that must follow the bill's updated procedures for proposing, withdrawing, and tracking state regulations.
The Department of Emergency Management is impacted as a regulatory body that must comply with the revised procedures for both proposed and emergency regulations.

The Department of Housing and Community Development is a regulatory unit required to utilize the new electronic filing system and adhere to the updated submission and notice requirements for regulations.

The Department of Natural Resources adopts significant environmental and conservation regulations and is listed as an impacted agency regarding the changes to the regulatory submission and review process.

The Public Service Commission is an independent regulatory agency that must comply with the bill's procedures for submitting regulations to the Maryland Register and coordinating with the AELR committee.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state agencies regarding the regulatory process. OAG staff, particularly within the General Assembly Counsel, are specifically tasked by the bill to review substantive changes to regulations during the submission process.

As a principal law enforcement agency that also functions as a regulatory unit for matters such as firearms and traffic safety, the Maryland State Police must comply with the bill's new electronic filing and procedural requirements for regulations.

Synopsis: Altering the penalty for a violation of the prohibition on wearing, carrying, or transporting a handgun; requiring the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy to annually report certain information to the Governor and General Assembly; requiring the Department of State Police to transmit a certain summary of certain laws relating to firearms to certain persons; requiring the Secretary of State Police, in consultation with the Attorney General and the Maryland Department of Health, to develop a certain curriculum; etc.

Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland's laws regarding the possession and carrying of regulated firearms. It increases the maximum incarceration penalty for illegal handgun transport for first-time offenders and expands the list of disqualifying conditions for firearm possession. The legislation also modifies the process for obtaining a handgun permit by raising the minimum age to 21, increasing application and renewal fees, and requiring a modernized training curriculum that covers de-escalation and suicide prevention. Additionally, the Department of State Police must implement regular reviews of permit holders and provide electronic updates on firearm laws to registered owners.
stakeholders: Handgun permit applicants, owners of regulated firearms, firearms instructors, and law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are projected to increase by approximately 5294200 in FY 2024 due to increased handgun permit fees, with future revenues fluctuating based on renewal cycles. General fund expenditures are expected to increase by at least 2402200 in FY 2024 to support additional staffing and administrative requirements for the Department of State Police and the Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy. Local governments may see a minimal impact on revenues and expenditures from revised penalty provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Maryland State Police (headed by the Secretary of State Police) is responsible for the issuance, renewal, and revocation of handgun permits, conducting background investigations, and communicating law changes to the public.

The bill mandates that the Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicate appeals regarding denied, revoked, or limited handgun permits and requires them to submit detailed annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Department of Health is required to consult on the development of a firearms training curriculum, and its records regarding mental health admissions and facilities are central to the bill's expanded permit disqualifiers.
The Office of the Attorney General is specifically tasked with consulting on the development, publication, and update of the new firearms training curriculum mandated by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency manages the CJIS Central Repository used for permit eligibility reviews and will be affected by the bill's increase in the maximum incarceration penalty for handgun violations.
The Judicial Branch, supported by the AOC, provides data for the mandatory reporting on handgun-related charges and sentences and manages the legal proceedings for violations addressed in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This includes the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy, which the bill explicitly tasks with reporting annual data on handgun violations, convictions, and sentences.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments implementing this bill and receives multiple mandated reports on handgun permits and sentencing data.

The department oversees the significant fiscal impact on the general fund and the personnel requirements identified in the fiscal note for the implementation of the new permitting and reporting duties.
The department issues hunter safety certificates, which the bill identifies as a valid exemption for certain firearm possession prohibitions for minors.
Juvenile adjudications and records managed by the department are used as disqualifiers for the possession of regulated firearms and the issuance of handgun permits.
Convictions under the Transportation Article, such as DUI or DWI, are specifically listed as disqualifying factors for possessing firearms and obtaining handgun permits.
As the agency managing driver records and Transportation Article violations, the MVA provides the data used to determine applicant eligibility based on driving-related disqualifiers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

Military service status is used as a qualifying factor for certain age-based permit requirements and exemptions from training courses.

bill_summary: This bill grants the Town of Forest Heights in Prince George’s County the authority to carry out urban renewal projects for blight clearance in areas zoned for commercial use. The town is authorized to use eminent domain to acquire property, issue general obligation and revenue bonds to finance projects, and levy taxes to support redevelopment efforts.
stakeholders: Residents and owners of commercial property in the Town of Forest Heights, particularly in designated blighted areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State of Maryland may experience a minimal increase in income and sales tax revenue if redevelopment is successful. Local expenditures for the Town of Forest Heights will increase to cover legal fees and land acquisition costs, while revenues could increase through the sale of acquired properties and a broader tax base. Specific dollar estimates are not provided in the fiscal note as the impact depends on the town's implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development is responsible for community revitalization and economic vitality, which directly aligns with the bill's focus on urban renewal and blight clearance. The agency was also consulted in the preparation of the fiscal note.

The Maryland Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and technical assistance for local resource management. As the bill concerns municipal land use and redevelopment, and the agency was a contributor to the fiscal note, it is highly relevant.

The bill grants the Town of Forest Heights the power of eminent domain, which involves judicial proceedings, and specifically mentions obtaining entry orders from the Circuit Court and jury-awarded compensation.

The fiscal note indicates that successful redevelopment projects may result in a minimal increase in state tax revenues, including income and sales taxes, which the Comptroller is responsible for collecting.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel on constitutional authority and the interpretation of state laws, including the Urban Renewal Amendment of the Maryland Constitution referenced in the bill.

The bill's purpose is to facilitate redevelopment in commercial areas to improve economic activity, which relates to the Department of Commerce's mission of stimulating the economy and attracting businesses.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The Governor signed the bill into law, and the office manages the executive support functions for such legislative changes.
Redevelopment and blight clearance can lead to changes in property valuations and the assessable base, which may result in appeals handled by local boards under the PTAAB's oversight.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Prince George’s Gateway Development Authority to support and develop a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan for a target area consisting of Mount Rainier, Brentwood, Cottage City, Bladensburg, Colmar Manor, and North Brentwood. The Authority is required to report its revitalization strategy to the Governor and the General Assembly by October 31, 2025.
stakeholders: Residents, small businesses, and local governments within the City of Mount Rainier, the Town of Brentwood, the Town of Cottage City, the City of Bladensburg, the Town of Colmar Manor, and the Town of North Brentwood.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local finances. It is assumed that the Authority can be staffed and members reimbursed for expenses using existing resources. While the Authority is authorized to manage funds appropriated by the State, Prince George’s County, or target municipalities, the bill does not mandate any specific appropriations. Local expenditures may increase minimally if existing resources are insufficient for staffing needs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Commerce is a designated member of the newly established Authority. The agency's core mission aligns with the Authority's objective to support economic development within the target area of Prince George's County.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a designated member of the Authority. The agency's expertise in neighborhood revitalization and community development is central to the Authority's mandate.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new state-authorized body (the Authority) composed of appointed officials and citizens to study and provide recommendations for a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan.

The Authority is required to report its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to the Governor by October 31, 2025. The office also oversees the executive branch departments serving on the Authority.
The bill mandates that the Authority's revitalization plan specifically address transportation, including both motor vehicles and pedestrians, within the target area.
The Authority may manage state-appropriated funds and its members are entitled to reimbursement for expenses under standard state travel regulations, which are overseen by this department.
The agency promotes sustainable growth and community planning, which are key components of the comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan the Authority is tasked with developing.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions, including the newly established Authority and its executive branch members.

bill_summary: This bill requires new residential construction, including single-family detached houses, duplexes, and townhouses with a garage, carport, or driveway, to include either an installed electric vehicle charging station, an EV-ready parking space, or an EV-capable parking space. It also mandates that the Maryland Energy Administration conduct a study on the costs and logistics of requiring electric vehicle charging infrastructure in multifamily residential buildings, with a report due by December 1, 2023.
stakeholders: Residential builders, developers, prospective home buyers, and residents of single-family homes, duplexes, and townhouses.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund expenditures will increase by up to 250000 in fiscal 2024 only for the Maryland Energy Administration to hire a consultant to complete the required study. Local governments are expected to handle enforcement of the bill's requirements using existing resources, and there is no projected impact on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Energy Administration to report its study findings and recommendations directly to the Governor. Additionally, the Governor oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for implementing these new residential construction standards.

The bill and fiscal note mention rebate programs for electric vehicle charging stations, which are administered through the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. The Comptroller, as the state's chief financial officer, oversees revenue collection and distributions related to state funds.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state agencies involved in implementing this law (MEA and MDE) and ensures the statutory changes to the Public Safety Article are legally sound and enforceable.

The fiscal note identifies a special fund expenditure of up to $250,000 for the required study. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and fiscal planning related to these agency expenditures.

As the agency responsible for ensuring residents have access to safe and secure housing, DHCD is directly impacted by changes to construction and renovation requirements for new housing units and multifamily residential buildings.

The Maryland Department of Labor typically oversees building performance standards and regulates the construction industry; it was also identified as a source of information in the fiscal analysis of the bill.
The bill references definitions and standards from the Transportation Article and directly relates to the state's broader goals for electric vehicle adoption and charging infrastructure.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Energy Administration to consult with the Department of the Environment to estimate the number of electric vehicles in the state through 2050, specifically in the context of the California Advanced Clean Cars II regulations managed by MDE.

MEA is the primary agency impacted and responsible for the implementation of the bill. It is tasked with conducting a significant study on the costs and ratios for EV charging in multifamily buildings and reporting recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Public Service Commission regulates public utilities. The mandatory installation of EV charging infrastructure in residential construction significantly impacts electrical load, grid management, and utility service requests.

bill_summary: This bill directs the Public Service Commission (PSC) to expand the Electric Vehicle (EV) Pilot Program, enabling participating electric companies to install EV charging stations in multifamily dwellings located in underserved communities. It establishes mandatory uptime standards for public EV charging stations, typically requiring a 97% availability rate, and mandates quarterly reporting on usage, costs, and maintenance. Additionally, electric companies must maintain sufficient staff to monitor and repair these stations and may be subject to civil penalties for failing to meet performance standards.
stakeholders: Electric companies, residents of multifamily dwellings in underserved communities, electric vehicle owners, and Maryland electricity ratepayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can handle the bill's requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no anticipated material effect on State or local finances. However, electricity rates may increase as investor-owned electric companies recover the costs of installing and maintaining the infrastructure from ratepayers. The PSC is also authorized to impose civil penalties of up to $25,000 per violation against electric companies that fail to satisfy uptime requirements, which would be paid into various special funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory body responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, including expanding the EV Pilot Program, establishing uptime standards, receiving quarterly data reports, and imposing penalties for noncompliance.

As the advocate for residential utility consumers, the Office of the People's Counsel is highly relevant because the bill impacts utility rates (as noted in the fiscal note) and sets reliability standards for public EV charging infrastructure provided by electric companies.

The Maryland Energy Administration is dedicated to maximizing energy efficiency and promoting renewable energy; the regulation and reliability of EV charging infrastructure aligns closely with their mission to coordinate energy planning across state agencies.

The bill specifically targets the installation of EV charging stations in multifamily dwellings in underserved communities, which directly intersects with this department's mission to ensure safe, affordable housing and community revitalization.

The bill defines 'underserved community' based on U.S. Census Bureau data. The Department of Planning provides data analysis and technical assistance regarding land use and census information, making it relevant to the targeting of program expansion.

The Department of the Environment is responsible for state environmental laws and air quality; improving EV charging reliability supports the state's broader environmental and climate goals, which the agency oversees.

The Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation network and mobility; the expansion and reliability of electric vehicle charging infrastructure is a critical component of state transportation planning.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force to study and recommend improvements to the governance, management, and financing of water and wastewater systems in the Baltimore region. The task force is charged with reviewing existing business process reviews, assessing alternative governance structures, and recommending a model that ensures safe, efficient, and affordable service for the region.
responsible_party: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force, the Mayor of Baltimore City, and the Baltimore County Executive
stakeholders: Residents and ratepayers of Baltimore City and Baltimore, Anne Arundel, Carroll, Harford, and Howard counties who rely on the regional water and wastewater systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Environmental Service can fulfill their consultation requirements using existing budgeted resources. Baltimore City and Baltimore County are expected to absorb minimal staffing and member reimbursement costs within their existing budgets. No impact on state or local revenues is anticipated.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force as a temporary body to conduct a specific study and provide recommendations on regional water and wastewater governance.

The bill explicitly requires the Task Force to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) in developing its recommendations. MDE also has regulatory oversight over the 10-year water and sewerage plans that the Task Force's findings may impact.
The bill explicitly requires the Task Force to consult with the Maryland Environmental Service (MES), which provides technical and operational expertise in water and wastewater management.
The Governor is responsible for appointing two members to the Task Force and is a designated recipient of the Task Force's final report on findings and recommendations.

Under current law as cited in the fiscal note, the Public Service Commission has authority to approve water rates charged by Baltimore City to county consumers. The Task Force's evaluation of alternative governance models directly impacts the future rate-setting and regulatory framework overseen by the Commission.
The Office of Appointments within the Executive Department would be responsible for the recruitment and vetting of the two members appointed by the Governor to the Task Force.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions and may be involved in the legal review of the recommended governance models or the drafting of subsequent legislation.
The bill specifies that task force members are entitled to reimbursement for expenses under the Standard State Travel Regulations as provided in the state budget, which is overseen by DBM.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to create and maintain a website providing information on the legal rights and responsibilities of individuals living in common ownership communities (COCs), including condominiums, cooperatives, and homeowners associations. The website must feature links to local COC programs and annual summaries of newly enacted statewide legislation regarding COC governance.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Residents, unit owners, and governing boards of condominiums, cooperative housing corporations, and homeowners associations; local common ownership community programs; and the Department of Housing and Community Development.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,000 in fiscal 2024 for website development by the Department of Housing and Community Development. Future annual costs for maintenance and updates are indeterminate but expected to be less than $90,000. No significant impact on state revenues or local government operations is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirements. It is mandated to establish, maintain, and annually update a website providing information on the rights and responsibilities of individuals in common ownership communities, including hyperlinks to local programs and relevant legislation.

The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of state records and is specifically responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums. Since the bill requires a website for common ownership communities (which include condominiums), the Secretary of State's existing registry is a primary source of data and regulatory context.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division has statutory authority over violations of the Maryland Homeowners Association Act and other COC-related laws. The information provided on the new website regarding 'rights and responsibilities' will likely involve resources and guidance produced by the OAG.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact, requiring an estimated $90,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2024 for website development plus ongoing maintenance costs. DBM is responsible for managing the state's budget and personnel resources related to this appropriation.

As the agency responsible for the state's information technology strategy, infrastructure, and security, DoIT would likely provide technical oversight, guidance, or support for DHCD in the development and hosting of the new public-facing website.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of the Environment to authorize and regulate the use of reclaimed water as a source for drinking water treatment facilities. The program sets technical standards for water treatment, including pathogen removal and minimum residence time in environmental buffers, and requires a status report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2024.
stakeholders: Public water systems, local governments, drinking water treatment facilities, and Maryland residents served by these systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,022 in FY 2023 and $139,858 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire contractual engineers to manage the program. Expenditures continue through the program's termination in 2028. Local government expenditures may increase significantly if they choose to participate in the pilot program to upgrade their water treatment systems. There are no permit fees, so state revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment is the primary agency responsible for establishing, implementing, and regulating the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program, including issuing permits and reporting progress to the Governor.

The Maryland Department of Health's Laboratories Administration is identified in the fiscal note as responsible for complex water testing, specifically for PFAS, and the department oversees drinking water quality standards relevant to the pilot.

As a technical service provider for water and wastewater systems, MES is likely to assist local governments or private entities in designing and operating the infrastructure required for the potable reuse pilot program.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of the Environment for drafting regulations, establishing permit conditions, and enforcing compliance with the pilot program's requirements.
DBM is impacted as the bill requires significant fiscal expenditures and the hiring of contractual regulatory and compliance engineers at the Department of the Environment.
The Department of the Environment is required by the bill to report its findings and recommendations regarding the pilot program to the Governor by December 2024.

OAH would be responsible for adjudicating administrative appeals or contested cases resulting from MDE's issuance, denial, or revocation of potable reuse permits under Title 1, Subtitle 6 of the Environment Article.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates sustainable development and environmental protection efforts between MDE and other agencies, aligning with the pilot's goal of innovative water resource management.
The PSC regulates for-profit water utilities that may participate in the pilot program, potentially necessitating rate adjustments or regulatory oversight for new potable reuse infrastructure.

bill_summary: This bill extends the time period from 60 days to 180 days during which a 'person in interest' may request the medical examiner to correct findings and conclusions regarding the cause and manner of death on a death certificate, except in cases where the finding is homicide.
responsible_party: Chief Medical Examiner, Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Spouses, adult children, parents, adult siblings, grandparents, or guardians of deceased individuals (persons in interest).
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health and the Office of Administrative Hearings report that the extension of the request period can be managed with existing budgeted resources. There is no material effect on state revenues and no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner is a unit within the Department of Health. The bill directly impacts their operations by tripling the time period during which a person in interest can request corrections to autopsy findings and involves the Secretary of Health in the formal appeal and adjudication process.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Secretary of Health refer appeals regarding autopsy correction denials to the Office of Administrative Hearings for contested case hearings. Administrative Law Judges at this agency are responsible for conducting the hearings and submitting findings of fact to the Secretary.

The bill allows for the Secretary of Health's final decisions regarding autopsy corrections to be appealed to a circuit court. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides the operational and technological support for the judicial branch and the courts that handle these appeals.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and would represent the state's interests in both the administrative hearings at OAH and subsequent judicial review in the circuit courts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), which is a division of the Maryland Department of Health, to enter into a memorandum of understanding and a data-sharing agreement with the Division of Rehabilitation Services.

The bill directly mandates the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which is part of the Maryland State Department of Education, to enter into a memorandum of understanding and data-sharing agreement with the Developmental Disabilities Administration.

As the principal state agency responsible for coordinating and improving the delivery of services to residents with disabilities, the Department of Disabilities is impacted by changes to how client data is shared to expedite eligibility decisions for disability-related services.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and would likely be involved in the drafting, review, and legal validation of the mandated Memorandum of Understanding and data-sharing agreement to ensure compliance with privacy laws.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) to enter into contracts with the District of Columbia or the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority to provide water, sewer, or drainage services to certain "border properties" in Prince George's County. These properties must be located within one-half mile of a mass transit station and a regional transit district or neighborhood center, and they must lack the necessary frontage on a Prince George's County right-of-way for utility connections.
stakeholders: Property owners and developers of transit-oriented projects in Prince George's County located on the border with the District of Columbia, as well as the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission and D.C. water authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. Additionally, it does not materially affect the operations or finances of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC). Specific dollar estimates for expenditures or revenues are not provided as the impact is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically mentions the collection of the Bay Restoration Fee under the Environment Article, which is a state revenue item managed and monitored by the Comptroller's office in its role as the state's principal tax and revenue collector.

The legislation concerns infrastructure for multifamily housing and transit-oriented development projects within regional transit districts and neighborhood centers, aligning with the agency's mission to support community revitalization and affordable housing.

The bill targets properties that qualify as expedited transit-oriented development (TOD) projects. The Department of Planning is responsible for promoting sustainable growth and coordinating land use planning policies related to TOD across the state.

The bill's scope is defined by proximity to WMATA mass transit rail stations and regional transit districts. As the agency overseeing Maryland's transit strategy and coordination with WMATA, MDOT is directly impacted by changes to utility services for transit-adjacent developments.

The Department of the Environment regulates public water and sewer systems and oversees the administration of the Bay Restoration Fee, which the bill explicitly authorizes the WSSC to charge to the affected accounts.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (a state-created agency) and coordinates the policy initiatives related to transit-oriented development and regional infrastructure mentioned in the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies like the WSSC and is responsible for reviewing and ensuring the legal sufficiency of contracts between Maryland agencies and external entities like the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). The unit is authorized to investigate and prosecute criminal violations of State environmental and natural resources laws, as well as other criminal offenses discovered during these investigations. The bill grants the unit the powers of a State's Attorney, including the authority to use grand juries and issue subpoenas for records relevant to ongoing criminal investigations.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, businesses in resource-based industries, the Maryland Department of the Environment, and the Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $566,200 in FY 2024, which accounts for the bill's October 1, 2023 effective date. These funds cover the hiring of four positions: a Chief Counsel, two assistant Attorneys General, and one investigator, along with operating expenses. Expenditures are projected to grow to $796,000 by FY 2028. State and local revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount starting in FY 2024 due to the collection of monetary penalties and restitution resulting from the unit's prosecutions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General, making it the primary agency responsible for the unit's operations, staffing, and prosecution of cases.

The newly established unit is tasked with investigating and prosecuting violations of environmental laws under the department's jurisdiction, assisting the department on request, and advising the Secretary of the Environment on legal and policy matters.

The unit investigates and prosecutes violations of state natural resources laws, assists the department with civil actions on request, and provides legal and policy advice to the Secretary of Natural Resources.
The Attorney General must cooperate with the Secretary of Budget and Management to set minimum salaries, qualifications, and standards of training and experience for the unit's personnel.

The Attorney General is required to report annually to the Governor on the activities of the unit and the responsive actions taken by the Department of the Environment and the Department of Natural Resources.
The unit is mandated to cooperate with state and local law enforcement officials in investigating and prosecuting pollution and other environmental crimes.
The bill authorizes the unit to use grand juries and issue subpoenas through the state's courts, requiring judicial oversight and potential hearings in the event of non-compliance.

The bill makes this authority permissive, meaning the city is allowed but not required to accept these certificates in place of traditional bonds.
responsible_party: Baltimore City and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Contractors, nonprofit contractor associations, and Baltimore City government officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances as the Maryland Insurance Administration can handle any enforcement with existing resources. There is no impact on Baltimore City finances because the authorization to honor certificates of guarantee is optional. Small businesses may experience a minimal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the State Insurance Article to define and exempt certificates of guarantee from typical insurance regulation. The fiscal note explicitly mentions that the Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for enforcing the bill's requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Certificates of guarantee are often used as alternative bonding mechanisms to help small, minority, and women-owned businesses satisfy procurement requirements when they may not have the capacity to secure traditional surety bonds.
As the state's primary procurement and construction management agency, DGS is interested in bonding requirements and financial instruments used by contractors to secure public improvement projects.

The bill specifically defines 'contractors' as entities performing construction or maintenance on roads. MDOT, particularly through the State Highway Administration, oversees significant roadwork where such bonding instruments may be relevant.

The Maryland Stadium Authority manages extensive construction projects within Baltimore City, including professional sports venues and the 21st Century School Buildings Program, making local bonding authorizations highly relevant to their projects.

The IAC oversees the funding and planning of school construction projects across Maryland, including Baltimore City. Changes to how contractors can satisfy bond requirements for public improvements directly affect their oversight of these capital projects.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This board adjudicates bid protests and contract disputes. Disputes regarding the validity or acceptance of a certificate of guarantee during the bidding process for Baltimore City-related projects (where the state has an interest) could fall under their purview.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the defined term "related event" as it applies to a related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City includes events for which tickets are sold in advance or at the door or cover charges are imposed; reducing the number of days within which a person must apply for a permit, the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City must take certain actions relating to the permit, and alterations may be made to the permit; and altering the standards for determining the permit fee.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Related Event Promoter's Permit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill modifies the regulations for related event promoter's permits in Baltimore City, specifically for events associated with the CIAA Basketball Tournament. It expands the definition of 'related events' to include those where tickets are sold at the door or a cover charge is imposed, shortens the application and review timelines for the Board of License Commissioners, and changes the basis for permit fees from anticipated attendance to venue capacity as determined by the Baltimore City Fire Marshal.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Third-party event promoters, Baltimore City alcoholic beverage license holders, the Baltimore City Fire Marshal, Visit Baltimore, and attendees of the CIAA Basketball Tournament.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates there is no state impact. Local fiscal impact is not anticipated to be material to Baltimore City's operations or finances. The bill modifies the criteria for existing permit fees ($500 for capacity under 300; $1,500 for capacity of 300 or more) and maintains an application fee of $50 and potential fines between $1,000 and $3,000 for violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the operations of the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City, which is the primary body responsible for issuing and managing the related event promoter’s permits. Additionally, the bill clarifies authority for the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission. Both of these entities fall under this category of state-authorized boards and commissions.

The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages Article, which the Comptroller historically regulated. Specifically, Section 12-2802 is amended to update an obsolete reference to the Comptroller’s authority, reflecting the transfer of certain enforcement powers to the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for all state agencies, boards, and commissions, including the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, both of which are central to the bill's implementation and enforcement.

The Governor’s Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. As the state's chief executive, the Governor signed this legislation into law, which alters the regulatory and permitting framework for alcoholic beverages in the state's largest city.

The bill specifically addresses 'related events' associated with the CIAA Basketball Tournament, which is a major event for Maryland's tourism economy. The agency's work includes promoting the state as a travel destination and fostering recreational and cultural attractions.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in a certain area of the 40th alcoholic beverages district in Baltimore City to the holder of a Class C beer and light wine license under certain circumstances; prohibiting certain license holders in certain areas of the 40th alcoholic beverages district from selling alcoholic beverages at certain times of day; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - 40th District - Alcoholic Beverages
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue new alcoholic beverages licenses in specific areas of the 40th alcoholic beverages district, including a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in the 3600 block of Hickory Avenue and a Class A-7 license in the 1200 block of West North Avenue. It establishes specific operating hour restrictions (10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.) for certain licensees in designated blocks and provides exceptions to the 300-foot proximity rule for schools and places of worship for specific license types.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and holders in Baltimore City's 40th alcoholic beverages district, the Penn North Community Association, and local residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues are expected to increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024. The extent of the increase depends on the number of licenses issued; a Class C BWL license generates $1,150 in its first year and $600 annually thereafter, while a Class A-7 BWL license generates $2,100 in its first year and $1,550 annually thereafter. There is no impact on state finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry. Although the bill specifically empowers the local Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, the Comptroller oversees the general regulation and enforcement of alcohol laws and tax collection in the state.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel to state agencies and boards. They may be required to provide legal interpretation of these new provisions in the Alcoholic Beverages Article.
The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and signed this bill into law as part of the state's legislative process.

Synopsis: Requiring the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission to obtain the approval from the Commissioners of St. Mary's County before submitting a loan application where the Commission seeks to incur debt upon the full faith and credit of the county; requiring the Commission to cause studies, plans, and estimates to be made for new facilities in certain portions of the county; requiring any excess revenue made by the Commission in the sale or transfer of certain debt to be exempt from taxation; etc.
Title: St. Mary’s County – Metropolitan Commission – New Facilities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Sanitary Districts -see also- Wash Sub Sanitary District

bill_summary: The bill requires the St. Mary’s County Metropolitan Commission (MetCom) to obtain approval from the St. Mary’s County Commissioners for loan applications involving debt on the county's full faith and credit. It also mandates that MetCom conduct studies, provide public notice, and hold hearings regarding new water or sewerage facilities. Additionally, the bill updates definitions related to service areas and facilities and allows MetCom to pay for the costs of shifting or removing obstructions during the construction of water and sewerage systems, subject to certain conditions.
stakeholders: Residents and property owners in St. Mary’s County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Locally, it does not materially affect St. Mary’s County operations or finances, as the changes are primarily procedural and streamline existing practices. While the county provides full faith and credit for debt incurred by the Metropolitan Commission, the Commission remains responsible for paying all incurred debts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary state agency responsible for the oversight of public water and sewerage systems. The bill concerns the planning, cost estimation, and expansion of these facilities in St. Mary's County, which relates to MDE's regulatory authority and its role in approving county water and sewerage plans.

The bill redefines 'service area' based on the St. Mary's County Comprehensive Water and Sewerage Plan. The Department of Planning provides technical assistance and policy guidance to local governments regarding land use planning and coordinates the review of comprehensive infrastructure plans to ensure sustainable growth.

The bill specifies that excess revenue from the sale or transfer of debt by the St. Mary’s County Metropolitan Commission shall be exempt from state and local taxation. As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for enforcing tax laws and identifying exempt revenues.

Synopsis: Altering the application requirements for the homeowners' tax credit to allow homeowners with certain types of income to file an application every 3 years, subject to a certain certification requirement; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Homeowners' Property Tax Credit - Qualified Homeowner - Application and Certification Requirements
bill_summary: This bill streamlines the application process for the homeowners' property tax credit for certain individuals. Qualified homeowners whose income consists only of Social Security, pensions, or annuities are required to submit a full application only once every three years, provided they submit a simplified certification in the intervening two years confirming their residency, income sources, and household composition remain unchanged.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Homeowners whose gross income is derived exclusively from Social Security benefits, pensions, or annuities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the altered application and certification requirements using existing budgeted resources, as the total number of applications is not expected to change significantly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is specifically responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments and disputes over various property tax credits. Alterations to the application and certification requirements for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit could lead to disputes or appeals that fall under its jurisdiction.

The bill defines 'qualified homeowners' as those receiving income solely from Social Security, pensions, or annuities, a demographic primarily composed of older adults. The Department of Aging is the advocate for this population and focuses on housing assistance and quality of life for seniors.

The Department is responsible for developing the state budget, which includes the significant funding (approximately $56.5 million) allocated for the state-funded Homeowners' Property Tax Credit program.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from decisions regarding tax assessments and credits, including the property tax credits modified by this bill.
As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller has a general interest in all state tax credit programs and tax law enforcement.

Many veterans and their families receive pensions or Social Security benefits. This bill simplifies the property tax credit application process for individuals whose income is limited to these sources, directly impacting retired veterans.

The bill aims to enhance the efficiency of state government operations by streamlining and simplifying an application process, aligning with this office's mission to eliminate waste and improve service delivery.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Assessments and Taxation, regarding the implementation and interpretation of new tax laws and application requirements.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the agencies implementing this law and the broader policy initiatives related to tax relief and administrative efficiency.

Synopsis: Establishing that a hernia caused as a result of repetitive trauma may be considered an occupational disease and be compensable subject to certain provisions of the workers' compensation law.
Title: Labor and Employment - Workers' Compensation - Hernia

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill expands Maryland workers' compensation law by establishing that a hernia caused by repetitive trauma can be classified as a compensable occupational disease. It also specifies that for cases of athletic pubalgia hernia, the diagnosis must be reported to the employer within 45 days to be compensable.
stakeholders: Covered employees, employers, and workers' compensation insurers in Maryland, including the Chesapeake Employers’ Insurance Company.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. According to the fiscal note, hernias caused by repetitive trauma are relatively rare, and the requirement for employees to prove the injury was work-related remains in place, resulting in minimal fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicating claims. This bill directly amends the standards for compensable hernia claims, which the Commission must implement and adjudicate.

The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article of the Maryland Code. The Department of Labor is responsible for protecting workers and enforcing labor laws, making this change to compensation standards highly relevant to its mission.

The Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) is the third-party administrator for workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees. Changes to hernia compensability directly impact the claims they process and the state's liability.

The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions. Because the bill addresses the aggravation of pre-existing hernias and classifies certain hernias as occupational diseases, it affects the fund's investigations and potential liability.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM manages employee benefits and fiscal planning. Expansion of workers' compensation eligibility for state employees can have a fiscal impact on the state's personnel and insurance budget.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Workers' Compensation Commission and the Subsequent Injury Fund. It would be responsible for interpreting the new statutory language and representing state interests in related litigation.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the implementation of state laws; the Governor signed this bill into law and is responsible for the overall execution of the state budget, which includes workers' compensation costs.

Synopsis: Altering a certain condition under which the Board of License Commissioners of Garrett County may issue a certain alcoholic beverages license to a hotel or motel; authorizing a gift basket permit holder to purchase certain alcoholic beverages from a wholesaler; authorizing a holder of a Class C multiple day beer license, beer and wine license, or beer, wine, and liquor license to hold another license that is issued by the Board; etc.
Title: Garrett County Alcoholic Beverages Act of 2023
bill_summary: This bill modifies alcoholic beverages regulations in Garrett County by reducing the required number of rooms for hotel and motel licenses from 25 to 10, authorizing gift basket permit holders to purchase from wholesalers, and allowing certain club license holders to hold additional licenses. It also extends Sunday sale hours to begin at 6:00 a.m. and establishes a framework for the expiration and hardship extension of inactive licenses.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners of Garrett County
stakeholders: Hotel and motel owners, gift basket permit holders, social clubs, alcoholic beverage retailers, and consumers in Garrett County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact as the Judiciary can handle any workload changes with existing resources. Local finances and operations in Garrett County are not materially affected. Small businesses may see increased sales from the extension of Sunday hours.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry in the state. This bill alters regulations for alcoholic beverages licenses in Garrett County, including expanding the authority of gift basket permit holders to purchase alcohol from wholesalers, which falls under the Comptroller's regulatory and oversight domain.

The fiscal note explicitly mentions that the Judiciary can handle the workload associated with this bill. The bill establishes a framework for the expiration of alcoholic beverages licenses that includes timelines linked to final judgments of reviewing courts in cases of judicial review.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and boards and represents the state in appeals. Since the bill introduces new county-specific legal frameworks for license expiration and judicial review, the OAG may be involved in interpreting these provisions or representing the state's interests in related litigation.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversaw the signing of this bill into law. The bill modifies the Alcoholic Beverages Article, which the executive branch is responsible for enforcing.
