Synopsis: Making permanent the Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Pilot Program; requiring a community solar energy generating system to serve at least 40% of its kilowatt-hour output to low-income and moderate-income subscribers under certain circumstances; authorizing a subscription coordinator to act on behalf of a subscriber organization; altering requirements related to the siting and size of certain community solar energy generating systems projects; authorizing the use of consolidated billing for certain charges; etc.
Title: Electricity - Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Program and Property Taxes

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill makes the Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Pilot Program permanent and renames it the Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Program. It requires systems to serve at least 40% of their kilowatt-hour output to low- and moderate-income (LMI) subscribers, authorizes consolidated billing, and adjusts project siting and size requirements. The bill also mandates prevailing wage rates for certain large projects and extends personal property tax exemptions for eligible community solar systems approved through 2025.
stakeholders: Low- and moderate-income (LMI) electricity customers, solar energy developers, subscriber organizations, electric companies, and residential tenants in master-metered facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission (PSC) increase by $264,900 in FY 2024 and $297,500 in FY 2025 for new staff and consultant services, with special fund revenues increasing correspondingly through assessments on public service companies. Local government revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2026 due to the extension of the personal property tax exemption for certain community solar projects. The bill may also put upward pressure on electricity prices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller, as the state's principal tax collector, is relevant because the bill alters personal property tax exemptions for community solar systems and requires reporting on the number and location of exempt projects.
The bill defines and regulates 'agrivoltaics' (simultaneous land use for solar power and agriculture), referencing agricultural activities recognized by the Department of Agriculture.
The bill creates a new full-time personnel position (Position Identification Number) within the Public Service Commission, which falls under DBM's oversight of state employee resources and budgeting.
The bill references definitions for overburdened and underserved communities from the Environment Article and addresses the siting of solar systems on brownfields and clean fill sites.
The bill focuses on providing solar access to low-to-moderate income (LMI) residents and specifically mentions residents of affordable housing facilities.
Verification of a subscriber's LMI status includes participation in programs administered by DHS, such as SNAP and the Maryland Energy Assistance Program.
The bill establishes prevailing wage requirements for developers of community solar projects exceeding 1 MW, a standard enforced by the Department of Labor.
The bill requires solar projects to comply with the Forest Conservation Act and address Critical Area concerns, citing the Natural Resources Article.
The bill impacts land use policy through modified siting, co-location, and agrivoltaic requirements, which align with the Department's role in sustainable growth and resource management.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch operations, including policy coordination for the agencies implementing this bill and the creation of new staff positions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Public Service Commission to convene a stakeholder workgroup to provide recommendations on new regulations for the solar program.
This office connects residents with government resources; the community solar program is a significant resource for LMI communities targeted by the office's advocacy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO supports agricultural and rural business sustainability, which is directly impacted by the bill's provisions on agrivoltaics and solar siting on farmland.
The bill specifically exempts solar projects located at airports from certain co-location prohibitions, directly impacting facilities managed by the MAA.
The bill's focus on expanding and making permanent the community solar program aligns with MCEC's mission to advance clean energy and reduce emissions.
The MEA coordinates state energy policy and manages renewable energy incentives; this bill permanently establishes a core component of Maryland's solar energy strategy.
The bill's focus on economic mobility and reducing child poverty via LMI energy savings aligns with the Innovation Team's mandate to pilot strategies for these priorities.
The Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including those related to the property tax exemptions modified by this bill.
OAH provides impartial hearings for state agencies; new regulatory requirements for subscription organizations could lead to contested cases adjudicated by OAH.
The OPC represents residential utility consumers in PSC proceedings; they will be deeply involved in rulemakings regarding billing, subscription rates, and LMI protections.
PTAAB handles disputes regarding property tax assessments and exemptions, which are extended and modified for solar equipment under this bill.
The PSC is the primary agency responsible for establishing, maintaining, and regulating the permanent Community Solar Energy Generating Systems Program.
This multi-agency initiative promotes sustainable development and community revitalization, both of which are central goals of the expanded community solar program.
The bill permits the co-location of solar systems on or over transportation and public rights-of-way, which are managed by the SHA.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2026, the termination provisions relating to certain statutory and regulatory authority of the Commission; and requiring an independent evaluation of the Commission to be conducted in consultation with the Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability in the Department of Legislative Services.
Title: State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date for the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors by three years to July 1, 2026. It also requires the Maryland Department of Labor to hire a consultant to conduct an independent evaluation of the Commission’s adherence to diversity, equity, and inclusion guidelines in its regulatory activities.
stakeholders: Real estate appraisers, appraisal management companies, and home inspectors licensed or certified in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund expenditures will increase by between $50,000 and $75,000 in FY 2024 only to hire a consultant for the required evaluation. By extending the sunset date, the bill also maintains the Commission's existing special fund revenues and expenditures through FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors is a regulatory body within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department is directly responsible for hiring a consultant to conduct the mandated independent evaluation and must use its funds to cover the associated costs.

The bill mandates that the independent evaluation of the Commission be conducted in consultation with the Office of Program Evaluation and Government Accountability (OPEGA) within the Department of Legislative Services. The Office of Legislative Audits is the primary legislative agency on the provided list responsible for fiscal and performance oversight of state programs.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the Department of Labor and its subsidiary commissions. The Governor also signed this bill into law and is responsible for the overall administrative support of such executive entities.

The extension of the Commission's termination date ensures the continued existence of board positions that the Governor must fill. The Office of Appointments is responsible for recruiting and vetting the individuals who serve on this Commission.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to establish certain targets for the deployment of new energy storage devices in the State; requiring the Commission to establish and implement the Maryland Energy Storage Program to meet certain energy storage goals and develop a certain energy storage system in the State; and requiring the Commission to submit a certain report to the General Assembly by December 31, 2023, regarding the implementation of the Maryland Energy Storage Program and any needed statutory changes.
Title: Energy Storage - Targets and Maryland Energy Storage Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Clean Energy Credits -see also- Renewable Energy Sources
Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Public Service Commission to establish the Maryland Energy Storage Program and set targets for the cost-effective deployment of new energy storage devices, aiming for a cumulative capacity of 3,000 megawatts by 2033. It mandates that the commission develop procurement mechanisms, energy storage credits, and incentives to support a robust energy storage market in the state.
stakeholders: Investor-owned electric companies, energy storage developers, and Maryland electricity ratepayers including state and local governments and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission's special fund expenditures and revenues are estimated to increase by $649,600 in FY 2025 for program implementation and staffing. Additionally, state and local government electricity costs are expected to rise as utilities recover costs for storage projects, with total capital expenditures for the 3,000 MW goal estimated at approximately $3800000000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Public Service Commission to establish energy storage targets and implement the Maryland Energy Storage Program, making it the primary regulatory and implementing agency.
As the state's advisor on energy policy and coordinator of energy planning, the MEA is central to the deployment goals and is a recipient of reports regarding related energy storage pilot programs.
The OPC advocates for utility consumers and will be deeply involved in PSC proceedings regarding the program's design, procurement costs, and impact on ratepayer electricity prices.
As the state's green bank, the MCEC is tasked with advancing clean energy technology and leveraging capital, aligning with the bill's multi-billion dollar goal for energy storage infrastructure.
DGS manages state facility sustainability and energy procurement; it will be impacted by the large-scale integration of energy storage and potential changes to state energy contracts.
DBM oversees the state's budget and personnel; it must handle the PSC's staffing increases and monitor the bill's impact on statewide electricity expenditures for government operations.
The bill's goals of transitioning to a clean grid and reducing emissions through renewable energy resources directly support the environmental protection and climate goals managed by MDE.
The bill identifies the energy storage program as a driver for economic development and job creation, which falls under the primary mission of the Department of Commerce.
The Department of Labor is relevant due to its role in workforce development and oversight of professional industries, specifically as the bill aims to create jobs in the energy sector.
The Governor's Office coordinates state policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch; the bill requires the PSC to report to the General Assembly and involves high-level policy setting.
The bill's focus on grid reliability and resilience against shocks and stressors aligns with MDEM's mission to ensure state resilience against hazards and infrastructure failures.

Synopsis: Requiring student financing companies to register with the Commissioner of Financial Regulation before providing services in the State; requiring a student financing company to renew its registration on an annual basis; authorizing the Commissioner to adopt registration procedures for student financing companies, which may include certain fees; and requiring student financing companies to annually report certain information, to be made publicly accessible on a certain website, to the Commissioner beginning March 15, 2024.
Title: Financial Institutions - Student Financing Companies - Required Registration and Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: This bill requires student financing companies to register with the Maryland Commissioner of Financial Regulation and submit annual reports detailing their financial products, outstanding debt totals, and default rates. It authorizes the Commissioner, the Attorney General, and local State's Attorneys to enforce these requirements, and mandates that the reported data be published on a publicly accessible website.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Student financing companies, consumers residing in Maryland who utilize non-federal student financing products, and institutions of postsecondary education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OCFR) can implement the bill's requirements with existing resources. State revenues are likely not materially affected because registration fees are paid directly to the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System (NMLS), a third-party licensing system. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary regulator is the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, who is a key official within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department is responsible for the registration, reporting oversight, and enforcement of the new subtitle regarding student financing companies.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to enforce the registration and reporting requirements for student financing companies, including using investigative and enforcement powers.

The bill regulates financing products for students at institutions of postsecondary education. MHEC is the state's regulatory body for these institutions and coordinates policy regarding student financial aid and access to higher education.

The bill mandates the collection of detailed data on student debt, schools attended, and default rates. This information is highly relevant to the MLDS Center's mission to analyze student performance and workforce outcomes in Maryland.

As a provider of postsecondary education, USM's students are the primary consumers of the financing products regulated by this bill. Additionally, any USM institution offering its own financing products (such as income-share agreements) would be subject to the bill's registration and reporting requirements.

As an institution of postsecondary education, Morgan State's students are impacted by the regulation of student financing companies. The university itself could potentially be categorized as a student financing company if it extends credit or income-contingent financing.

Saint Mary's College students utilize financing products covered by this bill. The college must also ensure that any institutional financing it provides complies with the registration requirements for student financing companies.

The fiscal note identifies the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts as an affected entity. The courts will be involved in cases where student financing products are declared void and unenforceable due to violations of this subtitle.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a certain proceeding for judicial review of a final decision or order by the Public Service Commission may be instituted in a circuit court for a county in which the public service company that is a party to the proceeding provides service or in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City.
Title: Public Service Commission – Judicial Review – Proceedings
bill_summary: This bill clarifies the legal venues for seeking judicial review of a final decision or order from the Public Service Commission. It specifies that such proceedings must be filed in the circuit court for a county where the public service company involved in the case provides service, or in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City.
stakeholders: Public service companies, parties involved in Public Service Commission proceedings, the Office of People’s Counsel, and the Public Service Commission legal staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances. According to the fiscal note, the Public Service Commission (PSC) administrative expenditures may decrease or be reallocated due to a potential reduction in travel for legal staff as a result of limiting the venues for judicial review. Local government operations and finances are not significantly impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary agency affected by this bill, as the legislation governs the judicial review process for its final decisions and orders, specifying the jurisdictions in which these proceedings can be instituted.

The Office of the People's Counsel is specifically mentioned in the bill as a party that can seek judicial review of Public Service Commission decisions. The bill's changes to the venue for these proceedings directly impact how the office performs its advocacy in the court system.
The bill clarifies and limits the venues for judicial review within the Maryland circuit court system, which is supported operationally by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill text explicitly references the Secretary of Natural Resources' authority to seek judicial review of Public Service Commission orders related to the environmental aspects of power plant siting, making the bill relevant to their regulatory and legal standing.

The bill explicitly references the Secretary of the Environment's authority to seek judicial review of certain final decisions or orders of the Commission, making the venue clarification relevant to their operations.

The bill addresses judicial review of Commission orders that lead to the suspension or revocation of registrations by the Motor Vehicle Administration, specifically clarifying that the Commission's order is the subject of review in these instances.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT is relevant due to the bill's provisions regarding the judicial review of PSC orders affecting motor vehicle carrier registrations.

The Office of the Attorney General represents state agencies, including the Departments of Natural Resources and Environment, who are specifically empowered to seek judicial review under the sections mentioned in the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing procedures for the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City, in the case of an alleged complaint against a licensed establishment or license holder, to make an offer of a monetary penalty as a compromise in lieu of a hearing before the Board under certain circumstances; and altering the maximum penalty for certain alcoholic beverages violations.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Violation Procedures and Fines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to offer license holders a monetary penalty as a compromise instead of holding a formal hearing for alleged violations, provided the license holder waives their right to a hearing and admits to the facts. It also increases the maximum fine for subsequent violations and unauthorized pub crawl activities from $3,000 to $20,000.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders in Baltimore City, licensed establishments, pub crawl promoters, and the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Baltimore City revenues may increase due to the collection of monetary penalties from compromise offers and higher maximum fines (increased from $3,000 to $20,000) for subsequent offenses or unauthorized pub crawls. The procedural changes can be managed by the Board of License Commissioners using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry in the state. While this bill focuses on local procedures for the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, it pertains to the broader regulatory and enforcement framework for alcoholic beverages overseen by the Comptroller.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions. The Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City is a state-established entity that will require legal guidance to implement the new offer of compromise procedures and to draft the regulations mandated by the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. As the bill was signed into law by the Governor and involves the administrative procedures of a state-authorized board, it falls under the office's general executive oversight.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to approve a license expansion to a noncontiguous property with a second separate use permit issued by the City if a certain condition is met; authorizing the establishment and conversion of various alcoholic beverages licenses in the 46th alcoholic beverages district; extending for 1 year the expiration of an alcoholic beverage licenses issued for  certain areas for certain transferal and renewal purposes; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - 46th Alcoholic Beverages District - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill modifies alcoholic beverages laws in Baltimore City, specifically within the 46th district. It authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to allow license expansions for certain non-contiguous properties, creates new license opportunities for establishments with specific features like duckpin bowling or food trucks, and allows the conversion of Class D beer and light wine licenses to Class D beer, wine, and liquor licenses under specific conditions (including a $15,000 fee). It also extends the expiration dates for several specific licenses to allow for transfers or renewals and removes a requirement for the Downtown Commercial District Management Authority to contract for specific police patrols.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Establishment owners in the 46th alcoholic beverages district of Baltimore City, the Canton Community Association, and the Fells Point Neighborhood Association.
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally starting in fiscal year 2024. This increase would stem from the issuance of additional Class B and Class D beer, wine, and liquor licenses, as well as a special $15,000 transfer fee for license conversions. Specific total dollar estimates are not provided in the Fiscal Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and enforcing state tax laws related to it. Since this bill makes significant revisions to the Alcoholic Beverages Article, specifically regarding license types, expansions, and conversions in Baltimore City, it directly falls under the Comptroller's broad regulatory and tax collection oversight of the industry.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including intergovernmental relations with local entities like Baltimore City. As this bill involves changes to the Baltimore City Charter and specific local district licensing, it involves the Governor's role in managing state-local legal and policy frameworks.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies regarding the interpretation and enforcement of state laws. This bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages Article and the Baltimore City Charter, requiring legal oversight and potential guidance on compliance and implementation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP) coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor. The bill specifically alters a mandate in the Baltimore City Charter regarding police patrols by the Baltimore Police Department in a commercial district, which falls under the office's interest in public safety and law enforcement coordination.

Synopsis: Establishing consumer protections related to the repair or replacement of motor vehicle glass on motor vehicles equipped with an advanced driver assistance system; and establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice.
Title: Consumer Protection - Motor Vehicle Glass Repair or Replacement - Advanced Driver Assistance System Recalibration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes consumer protection requirements for the repair or replacement of motor vehicle glass on vehicles equipped with an advanced driver assistance system (ADAS). It requires motor vehicle safety glass facilities to inform customers if ADAS recalibration is necessary, provide written documentation that the work will meet or exceed manufacturer specifications, and prohibits charging for services not performed or successfully completed.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Motor vehicle safety glass repair facilities and owners of motor vehicles equipped with advanced driver assistance systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not have a material impact on State or local government finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division, can handle the bill's requirements with existing resources. Violations are considered unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices, subject to civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation and $25,000 for repetitions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that a violation of its provisions regarding motor vehicle glass repair and Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) recalibration is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is the primary entity responsible for enforcing this Act and investigating complaints.

The bill regulates services performed on motor vehicles and their safety equipment (ADAS), using definitions from the Transportation Article. The MVA is responsible for overseeing vehicle equipment, safety standards, and highway safety initiatives in Maryland.

Motor vehicle glass repair and replacement are frequently subject to insurance claims. As the regulator of the state's insurance market, the MIA has a significant interest in consumer protection and the standards of repair facilities that interact with policyholders and insurers.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and the primary body for transportation policy, MDOT was consulted for the fiscal note and is concerned with any regulations affecting vehicle safety systems and equipment on Maryland roadways.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing the legislation into law. The Governor also coordinates the policy initiatives that involve multiple departments like the OAG, MDOT, and MIA.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Department of Commerce from denying certain cannabis business entities conducting business in the State certain economic development program benefits under certain circumstances; clarifying the eligibility of certain cannabis business entities conducting business in the State under the Job Creation and One Maryland programs; authorizing certain cannabis business entities to reapply for benefits under certain economic development programs; etc.
Title: Economic Development - Program Participation - Cannabis Business Establishments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Cannabis Distribution -see also- Cannabis, Cannabis Prod.
Cannabis Production -see also- Cannabis, Cannabis Dist.
Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland Department of Commerce from denying state economic development or financial assistance program benefits to licensed cannabis businesses solely because of their industry, provided they meet other program requirements. It specifically expands eligibility for the Job Creation and One Maryland tax credit programs to include cannabis growers, processors, and dispensaries and allows businesses previously denied such benefits to reapply.
stakeholders: Licensed cannabis business establishments including growers, processors, and dispensaries, as well as small cannabis businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are projected to decrease, potentially significantly, starting in fiscal 2025 as cannabis dispensaries qualify for the Job Creation and One Maryland tax credits. The Job Creation Tax Credit is capped at 4000000 annually, while the One Maryland credit provides up to 5000000 per credit without an annual cap. Local highway user revenues will also decrease if credits are claimed against the corporate income tax.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for economic development, Commerce is responsible for administering the programs modified by the bill, including the Job Creation, One Maryland, and More Jobs for Marylanders programs, and is explicitly prohibited from denying benefits to licensed cannabis businesses.

The Comptroller administers the state's tax laws and processes the tax credits (Job Creation and One Maryland) expanded by this bill; the expansion of eligibility to cannabis businesses will directly impact tax revenue collection and auditing procedures.
The MCA is the licensing and regulatory body for the cannabis growers, processors, and dispensaries that this bill makes eligible for state economic development programs and tax credits.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning; the fiscal note indicates a potentially significant decrease in General Fund revenues starting in FY 2025 due to the expansion of these tax credits.

The Governor's Office oversees the Department of Commerce and coordinates the executive branch policy initiatives related to economic development and the implementation of cannabis-related legislation.

The fiscal note identifies a direct impact on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues, which MDOT manages, because tax credits claimed against the corporate income tax reduce the share of revenue allocated to the TTF.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office monitors socioeconomic procurement and assistance programs; the bill affects programs under Title 5 of the Economic Development Article, which includes the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Commerce and other state agencies regarding the implementation of new statutory requirements and non-discrimination provisions regarding licensed cannabis entities.

Synopsis: Providing that the Secretary of Higher Education is appointed by and serves at the pleasure of the Governor; requiring each institution of higher education to adopt a written policy that provides reasonable academic accommodations for students to practice sincerely held faith-based or religious beliefs; altering eligibility criteria for and the process for awards from the Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Program of Educational Excellence Awards; altering the administration of the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship; etc.
Title: Higher Education - Appointment of Secretary and Student Financial Assistance - Accommodations at Public Institutions for Religious Beliefs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the appointment process for the Secretary of Higher Education, making the position an appointee of the Governor who serves at the Governor's pleasure. It requires public institutions of higher education to implement policies for reasonable academic accommodations for students' religious beliefs, including excused absences and designated campus spaces for practice. Furthermore, the bill alters eligibility and administration for state financial aid programs, specifically shifting the responsibility for awarding and verifying certain grants and scholarships, like the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship and parts of the Howard P. Rawlings Program, from the Maryland Higher Education Commission to the individual colleges and universities.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission and individual Maryland public institutions of higher education
stakeholders: Students at Maryland public and private institutions of higher education, community college students, religious student groups, and the Governor of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $278,200 in FY 2024 for one-time contractual costs related to the Maryland College Aid Processing System. Higher education expenditures for Baltimore City Community College and other public institutions are expected to increase starting in FY 2024 and FY 2026 to manage new administrative and notification responsibilities. Locally funded community colleges will also face administrative costs for verifying scholarship eligibility. The bill references a mandated annual appropriation of at least $112,000,000 for the Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Higher Education Commission (MHEC) is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. It manages the student financial assistance programs (EEA and MCCP) affected by the bill, maintains the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) which requires significant updates, and its Secretary's appointment process is fundamentally altered.

The bill significantly increases the Governor's authority by making the Secretary of Higher Education an appointee who serves at the pleasure of the Governor, removing the requirement to select from a list of Commission-provided nominees.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) administers the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program, which is altered by the bill to expand eligibility and allow students who relocate to continue receiving services.

As a public institution of higher education, USM is mandated to adopt and post policies regarding religious accommodations, provide campus space for religious practices, and take on new responsibilities for notifying and awarding Guaranteed Access Grants to students.

As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is mandated to implement the bill's requirements for religious accommodations and the decentralized administration of state financial aid awards.

As Maryland's public honors college, the institution is required to implement the bill's mandates concerning academic religious accommodations and the new financial aid notification and awarding processes.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal agency. The bill expresses legislative intent for the Governor to include funding for financial aid offices at public institutions starting in FY 2026 and involves significant general fund expenditures for system updates.

The Office of Appointments will manage the altered recruitment and vetting process for the Secretary of Higher Education, who is now a direct gubernatorial appointee serving at the Governor's pleasure.

The OAG will provide legal counsel to MHEC for the drafting of new regulations and to public institutions regarding the implementation of policies for religious accommodations and the provision of dedicated prayer/practice spaces.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires MHEC to work with the Segmental Advisory Council and the Financial Assistance Advisory Council to establish regulations for implementing the decentralized financial aid award process.

Synopsis: Altering the hours during which a licensee may sell alcoholic beverages on Sundays in Frederick County.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages - Sunday Sales
bill_summary: This bill alters the hours during which various alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County may sell beer, wine, and liquor on Sundays, generally extending the start time to 6:00 a.m. to align with existing Monday through Saturday hours.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages licensees in Frederick County and consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state impact and will not materially affect Frederick County finances or operations. Small businesses holding the affected licenses may experience a meaningful increase in sales due to the extension of operating hours on Sundays.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal tax collector and regulates the alcohol industry. This bill directly modifies alcoholic beverages laws and license operating hours, and certain licenses mentioned (such as Class 7 micro-brewery licenses) are obtained directly from the Comptroller.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the State and provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, regarding the enforcement and interpretation of alcoholic beverages laws.

The Department of Commerce is responsible for economic development and business retention. The fiscal note indicates this bill has a potentially meaningful impact on small businesses by allowing additional sales hours for hospitality and retail entities.

This agency promotes Maryland as a travel destination and supports recreational and cultural attractions. The bill specifically alters hours for conference centers, dinner theaters, entertainment centers, and municipal golf courses, which are components of the state's tourism and leisure economy.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The Governor signed this legislation into law, and the office is responsible for the overall execution of state laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office connects small businesses to economic opportunities. The bill's extension of Sunday hours is noted as having a potentially meaningful impact on small business sales within the impacted industries.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County to issue up to five Class B-DD (Development District) beer, wine, and liquor licenses for restaurants located within the Main Street Laurel development.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Main Street Laurel Development PG 404-23
bill_summary: The bill authorizes the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners to issue up to five Class B-DD (Development District) beer, wine, and liquor licenses to restaurants located within the Main Street Laurel development area.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurant owners in the Main Street Laurel development and Prince George's County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: State impact is none. Prince George’s County revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 by $3,025 per license issued, totaling up to $15,125 annually if all five licenses are granted. Any additional enforcement activity can be handled using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state-level regulator of the alcohol industry. This bill modifies the Alcoholic Beverages Article of the Maryland Code by authorizing new license categories in Prince George's County, which falls under the regulatory purview of the Comptroller's office.

The Department of Housing and Community manages community revitalization initiatives and oversees the 'Main Street Maryland' program. This bill specifically facilitates business expansion and restaurant licensing within the Main Street Laurel development area, aligning with the department's mission of urban and community redevelopment.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is relevant because the bill aims to stimulate local economic activity and attract new business to a designated development district in Laurel.
The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and coordinating the final review and signing of this legislation into law.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Charles County to grant, by law, a  tax credit against the property tax imposed on the owner-occupied residence of certain emergency responders and their surviving spouses if the federal adjusted gross income of the emergency responder or the unmarried surviving spouse for the immediately preceding taxable years is $150,000 or less; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Charles County - Property Tax - Credit for Volunteer Emergency Responders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the governing body of Charles County to establish a property tax credit for the primary residences of active or retired volunteer emergency responders or their unmarried surviving spouses, provided their federal adjusted gross income for the preceding taxable year does not exceed $150,000.
responsible_party: The governing body of Charles County and the Charles County Treasurer's Office
stakeholders: Active or retired volunteer fire, rescue, or emergency medical services members in Charles County and their unmarried surviving spouses.
fiscal_impact_summary: Based on the Fiscal Note, Charles County property tax revenues are estimated to decrease by $347,300 in FY 2024 and by $375,900 in FY 2028 if the credit is granted. County expenditures are expected to increase by $115,900 in FY 2024 and by $130,400 in FY 2028 for administrative costs, specifically to hire an additional staff person in the County Treasurer’s Office. There is no impact on State revenue or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The PTAAB is the independent state agency responsible for hearing second-level administrative appeals regarding property tax assessments, including disputes over the application or eligibility for local property tax credits and exemptions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and regulates the statewide emergency medical services (EMS) network. The bill's tax credit specifically targets volunteer EMS responders, which impacts the recruitment and retention of the volunteer workforce MIEMSS regulates and coordinates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is tasked with promoting service and civic engagement across Maryland. This bill directly incentivizes volunteer service in the fire, rescue, and EMS sectors, aligning with the agency's mission to strengthen communities through service.

GOCI manages the state's volunteerism and community service efforts, including the Governor's Office on Service and Volunteerism. The bill supports volunteerism through financial incentives provided to county residents.

MDEM coordinates state-level emergency response and preparedness. The availability and health of volunteer fire and EMS companies are essential components of the state's localized emergency response infrastructure.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary coordinating body for public safety policy. Supporting volunteer first responders through tax incentives is a strategic element of maintaining public safety infrastructure in Maryland's counties.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector. While the credit is local, the eligibility criteria depend on federal adjusted gross income, which may require coordination or data verification related to state tax records.

The Council supports rural infrastructure and services. Volunteer fire and EMS companies are the primary providers of emergency services in Maryland's rural jurisdictions, and this credit aids their sustainability.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinated the bill's signing; it also supports the Governor's role in overseeing policy initiatives related to public safety and intergovernmental relations with local entities.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Native Plants Program to respond to the increasing demand for, use of, and sale of native plants at retail garden centers and wholesale nurseries and to educate the public on native plants; requiring the Department of Agriculture to administer the Program in coordination with the University of Maryland Extension and to establish the "Maryland Natives" marketing program; requiring the University of Maryland Extension to hire an extension agent to serve as a native plant specialist for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Maryland Native Plants Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Native Plants Program to promote the use and sale of Maryland native plants and educate the public on their ecological benefits. The program, jointly administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture and the University of Maryland Extension, involves creating a commercial native plant list, a voluntary certification program for growers and retailers, a 'Maryland Natives' marketing program, and the hiring of a specialized native plant extension agent.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture and University of Maryland Extension
stakeholders: Retail garden centers, retail and wholesale nurseries, landscapers, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $285,100 in fiscal 2025, covering salaries for a native plant specialist and a marketing specialist, logo development, and operating expenses. The bill establishes mandated annual appropriations starting in fiscal 2025 ($150,000 for the University of Maryland Extension and $100,000 for the Maryland Department of Agriculture), though the fiscal note estimate for actual costs is higher. Local government finances and State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Native Plants Program. MDA is tasked with creating a voluntary certification program for growers and retailers, developing a 'Maryland Natives' marketing program (including a logo and QR code), and maintaining the program's data on its 'Maryland’s Best' website.

The University of Maryland Extension (UME), which is part of the University System of Maryland, is mandated to hire a native plant specialist, administer the educational and training components of the program, and create the 'Maryland Native Plants' webpage. The bill includes a specific mandated appropriation for UME to hire an extension agent.

The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is required to provide expert input to the Department of Agriculture for the development and periodic review of the Commercial Maryland Native Plant List. Additionally, DNR must include a link to the new native plants webpage on its own website.

The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations ($150,000 for UME and $100,000 for MDA) in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2025 and each subsequent year to fund the program's staff and operations.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, the Department of Budget and Management will oversee the execution of the mandated appropriations and the creation of the new personnel positions at the Department of Agriculture and the University of Maryland Extension.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from disbursing or authorizing the disbursement of certain funds to a county if the county has not provided certain information concerning its tax sales; altering the taxable year for which the Department is required to obtain certain information concerning county tax sales; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Tax Sales - Data Collection - County Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland counties to submit detailed annual surveys regarding tax sales to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). It specifies that data must be collected for the second immediately preceding taxable year and prohibits SDAT from disbursing funds under the Tax-Property Article to counties that fail to comply with these reporting requirements.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland county governments and property owners subject to tax sales
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill is not expected to have a material impact on State or local finances. While the bill allows for the withholding of State funds from noncompliant counties as a penalty, no specific revenue or expenditure figures are provided because compliance is expected and the impact is considered non-material.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note specifies that SDAT must collaborate with the Administrative Office of the Courts to obtain data on properties for which the right of redemption has been foreclosed by private tax sale certificate holders.

As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller is involved in the physical disbursement and management of state funds that SDAT is mandated to withhold for county non-compliance.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like SDAT regarding the implementation of the law and the enforcement of statutory penalties like the withholding of county funding.
The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and distributions to local governments and would be involved in any fiscal process where state disbursements are withheld or authorized.
DBM supervises state budget execution and fiscal planning, making it responsible for monitoring the impact of withheld county funds on both state and local finances.
The BPW oversees significant state expenditures and protects the state's fiscal integrity, providing an oversight role for the mechanisms used to distribute or withhold funds to counties.
The bill requires the collection of specific data regarding dwellings owned by individuals who are at least 65 years old and have been withheld from tax sales.
The bill requires the collection of specific data regarding dwellings owned by disabled individuals that have been withheld from tax sales.
Tax sale data and the resulting loss of property are critical factors in the agency's mission to ensure housing stability, community revitalization, and affordable housing.
OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of executive agencies and would be responsible for ensuring that SDAT is correctly withholding funds from non-compliant counties as mandated.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments implementing the survey and fund-withholding protocols, and coordinates related policy initiatives on tax reform.
The Tax Court is the administrative body that reviews disputes related to tax assessments and property under the Tax-Property Article, which encompasses the tax sale processes mentioned.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor annually to proclaim October 5 as Dashain Day, a festival originating in Nepal that celebrates and symbolizes victory of good over evil.
Title: General Provisions - Commemorative Days - Dashain Day

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor of Maryland to annually proclaim October 5 as Dashain Day, a festival originating in Nepal that celebrates and symbolizes the victory of good over evil.
stakeholders: South Asian communities in Maryland, particularly those of Nepalese descent, and the general public of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal impact on State or local government finances, as commemorating Dashain Day does not affect expenditures or revenues according to the Fiscal Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically requires the Governor to annually proclaim October 5 as Dashain Day. The Governor's Office, as the executive support unit, is responsible for the drafting, coordination, and issuance of official gubernatorial proclamations.

The Secretary of State serves as the custodian of the state's official records, including executive orders and proclamations. This agency is responsible for processing, sealing, and recording the proclamations mandated by this bill.

This office manages the state's ethnic and cultural commissions and advises the Governor on community engagement. Since Dashain is a Nepalese and South Asian festival, this agency would likely lead outreach and coordination with the relevant cultural communities regarding the proclamation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to include on its staff one or more employees that are experts in cybersecurity to perform certain duties; requiring the Commission to establish, in coordination with the Office of Security Management, cybersecurity standards and best practices for regulated entities; requiring each public service company to report a cybersecurity incident to certain entities; requiring the State Security Operations Center to immediately notify certain agencies of a certain reported cybersecurity incident; etc.
Title: Public Service Commission – Cybersecurity Staffing and Assessments (Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC) to hire cybersecurity experts to oversee and advise on utility cybersecurity practices. It mandates that regulated public service companies, excluding common carriers and telephone companies, implement zero-trust cybersecurity standards, conduct biennial third-party assessments, and report cybersecurity incidents to the State. The PSC is further tasked with establishing standards in coordination with the Office of Security Management and reporting on the cybersecurity status of various utility sectors.
stakeholders: Public service companies (electric, gas, and water), municipal electric utilities, electric cooperatives, and the Maryland Public Service Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission increase by $364,400 in fiscal 2024 to support three new positions, with annual costs projected to reach $510,500 by fiscal 2028. These costs are expected to be recovered through assessments on regulated public service companies. Local governments operating municipal electric utilities may face significant compliance costs for mandatory cybersecurity assessments. The bill also authorizes the use of existing Dedicated Purpose Account funds by the Department of Information Technology for cybersecurity staffing and operational capacity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is the primary focus of the Public Service Commission (PSC), requiring it to hire cybersecurity experts, establish standards and best practices for regulated utilities, monitor compliance, and submit biennial reports to the State Chief Information Security Officer.

The bill mandates that the Public Service Commission coordinate with the Office of Security Management (within DoIT) to set standards. Additionally, public service companies must report cybersecurity incidents to DoIT's State Security Operations Center, and DoIT receives funding for increased staffing and capacity.

The bill and fiscal note specify that the State budget must provide money for the PSC to hire additional cybersecurity staff (IT director and technicians). It also authorizes the transfer of funds from the Dedicated Purpose Account via budget amendment, which DBM oversees.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and DoIT regarding the implementation and enforcement of the new cybersecurity regulations and standards established by the bill.

The bill requires the State Security Operations Center to immediately notify appropriate state agencies of reported cybersecurity incidents. As the agency responsible for disaster response and resilience against man-made hazards, MDEM is a key stakeholder in utility infrastructure security.

The office is responsible for coordinating homeland security efforts and advising the Governor on public safety issues, including disaster prevention for critical infrastructure. The cybersecurity of utilities is a core component of the state's readiness and disaster prevention strategy.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation to study information on mold assessment and remediation to determine the best practices for identifying mold, preventing the development of mold within indoor environments, and remediating indoor molding conditions harmful to public health; and requiring the Workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by October 1, 2024.
Title: Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Housing and Community Development, Department of
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation to study and identify best practices for identifying, preventing, and remediating mold in indoor environments. The workgroup is tasked with reviewing existing industry standards, EPA guidelines, and the potential impact of climate change on mold growth, with the goal of submitting a report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by October 1, 2024.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, the Maryland Department of the Environment, Maryland Department of Health, Department of Housing and Community Development, Department of General Services, Department of Labor, and professional industrial hygienists and mold remediation specialists.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state expenditures for staffing the workgroup and providing expense reimbursements for members are expected to be minimal and absorbable within the Maryland Department of the Environment's existing budgeted resources. The bill has no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of the Environment as the chair of the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation and requires the Department to provide staffing for the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes a new temporary body, the Workgroup on Mold Standards and Remediation, to conduct a study and provide policy recommendations.
The Secretary of General Services is a required member of the Workgroup, as mold remediation standards significantly impact the management and maintenance of state-owned facilities.
The Secretary of Health is a required member of the Workgroup, as the study focuses on remediating moldy conditions that are harmful to public health.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a required member of the Workgroup, reflecting the relevance of mold standards to safe and secure residential housing.
The Secretary of Labor is a required member of the Workgroup, as the agency oversees professional licensing and workplace safety standards which may be affected by new mold remediation guidelines.
The Workgroup is mandated to report its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor by October 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Establishing the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner in the Maryland Department of Health to advance forensic science and carry out other duties as provided by law; renaming the State Postmortem Examiners Commission to be the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee; requiring and authorizing the Department and the Office to perform certain duties and powers previously performed by the Commission; authorizing the Department to contract with a physician for employment with the Office on a per diem basis; etc.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - Office of the Chief Medical Examiner

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner as a formal unit within the Maryland Department of Health and renames the State Postmortem Examiners Commission to the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee. It transfers administrative authority over postmortem examinations to the Department of Health, authorizes the hiring of per diem medical staff, adjusts certification timelines for assistant medical examiners, and allows certain retired health care practitioners to be reemployed by the office without a reduction in their pension benefits.
stakeholders: Medical examiners, forensic pathology fellows, staff of the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, and retired health care practitioners seeking reemployment within the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's changes are procedural and do not materially affect State or local governmental finances. While the bill exempts certain retirees reemployed by the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner from pension benefit reductions, the Fiscal Note indicates this applies in a limited number of cases and has no material effect on pension liabilities or contribution rates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner within the Maryland Department of Health and transfers authority from the former Commission to the Secretary of Health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames the State Postmortem Examiners Commission to the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee and defines its membership, powers, and advisory role.

The bill includes a specific provision that prohibits the reduction of retirement allowances for retirees of the Employees' Pension System who are reemployed on a contractual basis as health care practitioners in the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.

The bill specifies that if the Chief Medical Examiner denies a request to correct findings on a certificate of death, the person may appeal to the Secretary of Health, who must refer the matter to the Office of Administrative Hearings.
The bill requires the Department of Health to set compensation for personnel within the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner with the approval of the Secretary of Budget and Management.
The Secretary of State Police is a mandated member of the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee, and the agency is involved in the notification protocols for medical examiner cases.
The Governor oversees the executive branch units involved in this restructuring and signed the bill into law; the bill modifies the administrative structure of an executive department unit.
The head of the Pathology Department of the University of Maryland School of Medicine (part of USM) is a mandated member of the Postmortem Examiners Advisory Committee.

In cases of child death involving suspected abuse or neglect, the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner is required to report findings to the local department of social services, which is overseen by DHS.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG provides counsel regarding the implementation of forensic science statutes and legal disputes involving the new Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.

Title: State Employees – Programs and Scholarships for Human Services Careers and Probation Agents and State Contributions to Supplemental Retirement Plans

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers and an associated scholarship to recruit students from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County into positions at the Department of Human Services. It expands existing police officer loan repayment and scholarship programs to include parole and probation agents. Furthermore, the bill mandates a State matching contribution of up to $600 annually for employees participating in supplemental retirement plans, including a match option for employees making student loan payments.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services, Maryland Higher Education Commission, and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Maryland State employees, parole and probation agents, high school students in Baltimore City and Baltimore and Prince George's counties, and State-employed student loan borrowers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note estimates a total State expenditure increase of $21.8 million in FY 2024, comprising $13.5 million in general funds, $4.1 million in special funds, and $4.1 million in federal funds. This total includes approximately $20.6 million for the State retirement matching contributions and $1.0 million for the Human Services Careers Scholarship. Additionally, the bill redirects $3.5 million in mandated annual appropriations from the Maryland Police Officers Scholarship Program to the Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP) for Police Officers and Probation Agents. Local school systems in the designated counties may incur minor costs to implement the pilot program curriculum.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers within the Department of Human Services, requiring the agency to collaborate with local school systems, prioritize hiring participants, assign mentors, and pay one-time stipends to qualifying employees.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and its Office of Student Financial Assistance are responsible for administering the new Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship and the expanded Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP) and Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program and the Maryland Police Officers Scholarship Program to include parole and probation agents, supervisors, and regional administrators employed by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates State matching contributions of up to $600 per fiscal year for State employees participating in supplemental retirement plans administered by this agency, including provisions for matching higher education loan payments.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for the budget execution of the State matching contributions for supplemental retirement plans and managing the personnel policies related to the student loan documentation and employer match.

The Comptroller's Office, as the state's chief financial officer and payor of state employees, is responsible for implementing the payroll deductions and State matching contributions mandated by the bill for supplemental retirement plans.

MSDE oversees the local school systems in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Prince George's County that are required to collaborate with DHS on the pilot program, curriculum development, and career counseling services.

The bill alters and renames programs originally designed for police officers and significantly reduces the mandated annual appropriation for the scholarship program that previously served police officers exclusively, which has a notable fiscal and programmatic impact on recruitment and retention tools for the agency.

The Governor is required to include mandated appropriations in the annual budget bill for the LARP and scholarship programs, and the office oversees the executive departments (DHS and DPSCS) implementing the pilot programs.
The bill's eligibility for retirement plan matching is defined by membership in the Employees' Pension System or Employees' Retirement System, which are managed by the SRA.
The bill requires DHS to negotiate mentor compensation with each exclusive representative (unions), a process overseen and regulated by the Public Employee Relations Board.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the implementing agencies (DHS, DPSCS, MHEC) regarding the development of Memorandums of Understanding and new regulations for the scholarship and pilot programs.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose of the Heritage Conservation Fund to include acquiring interests in land that can be used by the general public for hunting; establishing the Wildlife Conservation, Education, and Outreach Program to provide outreach and foster an interest in outdoor recreation and stewardship, hunting, and wildlife conservation; establishing a stamp for hunting sika deer; authorizing a nonresident attending a college or university in the State to purchase a resident hunting license; etc.
Title: Hunting, Wildlife Conservation, and Outdoor Recreation - Funding, Promotion, Management, Licenses, Permits, and Stamps

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Wildlife Conservation, Education, and Outreach Program within the Department of Natural Resources to promote hunting and outdoor conservation. It increases various hunting and trapping license fees, creates a new Sika deer stamp, allows nonresident college students in Maryland to purchase licenses at resident prices, and permits migratory game bird hunting on Sundays. Additionally, the bill requires the state to develop a plan to manage deer overpopulation, creates a cost-share program for farmers to plant crops that support wildlife, and clarifies liability protections for landowners who permit recreational hunting on their property.
stakeholders: Resident and nonresident hunters, Maryland college students, farmers, veterans, and residents in suburban or exurban areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund revenues and expenditures are projected to increase by $2,271,600 annually starting in FY 2024 due to license fee increases. Federal fund revenues are expected to increase by $6,814,900 annually starting in FY 2025 through federal matching grants. These funds will support eight new staff positions and a farmer cost-share program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for managing Maryland's wildlife, hunting licenses, and stamps, DNR is tasked with implementing the new Wildlife Conservation, Education, and Outreach Program, establishing new sika deer stamps, and developing the state's deer overpopulation plan.

DNR must consult with the Department of Agriculture to develop the deer overpopulation plan and coordinate a new farmer cost-share program to plant forage crops and reduce wildlife-related commercial crop loss.

The bill requires the creation of eight new Position Identification Numbers (PINs) for DNR staff and involves significant shifts in special and federal fund expenditures, which fall under DBM's oversight of personnel and budget execution.
The Governor signs the bill, provides overall policy direction for executive departments like DNR, and appoints members to the Migratory Game Bird Advisory Committee.
The bill explicitly states that the balance of migratory game bird stamp fees is paid over to and accounted for by the State Treasurer for the Wildlife Management and Protection Fund.
The new Wildlife Conservation, Education, and Outreach Program is required to develop a plan specifically to increase the engagement of veterans in outdoor recreation and hunting.
The bill allows nonresident students attending Maryland colleges or universities to purchase resident hunting licenses, a policy change affecting students overseen by MHEC-regulated institutions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill outlines the appointment and duties of the Migratory Game Bird Advisory Committee, which is a permanent advisory body within the executive branch.
The bill aims to promote outdoor recreation and hunting, which are key components of Maryland's tourism economy managed by this office.
The office assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the Migratory Game Bird Advisory Committee.
Nonresident students at USM institutions will be eligible to purchase resident hunting licenses under the bill.
Nonresident students at Morgan State will be eligible to purchase resident hunting licenses under the bill.
Nonresident students at St. Mary's will be eligible to purchase resident hunting licenses under the bill.
