agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services is a member of the Commission, which is tasked with assessing health infrastructure and services for the State's forensic population.
The bill's provisions regarding Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) explicitly include requirements to provide mental health care for military service members and veterans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, a multi-year body tasked with comprehensive study and recommendations.
The Governor appoints several members to the Commission, jointly designates the chair, and receives annual reports on findings and legislative recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the office (specifically named as the Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services in the bill) is a member of the Commission.
The Executive Director of HSCRC is a member of the Commission, and the bill preserves HSCRC's authority to set hospital facility fees for telehealth services.
MHCC's Executive Director is a member of the Commission, and the agency is specifically mandated to study and make recommendations regarding telehealth delivery and payment parity.
The Insurance Commissioner is a member of the Commission, and the bill extends telehealth reimbursement requirements for private insurers and health maintenance organizations regulated by the MIA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: A representative from the Office of the Public Defender is a mandated member of the Commission.
The office is responsible for assisting the Governor in recruiting and vetting the various professional and consumer representatives appointed to the new Commission.

Synopsis: Requiring certain Medicaid funding to be used to provide community services to individuals waiting for services through waiver programs; authorizing certain Medicaid funding to be used for expanding provider capacity in certain waiver programs; and altering the uses of certain funding appropriated to the Dedicated Purpose Account in the fiscal year 2023 budget bill.
Title: Medicaid Waiver Programs - Waitlist and Registry Reduction (End the Wait Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The 'End the Wait Act' requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide community services to individuals on waitlists for several Medicaid waiver programs, including the Brain Injury and Autism waivers. It broadens the use of a $30,000,000 fiscal year 2023 appropriation to support these expansions and allows funds to be used for increasing provider capacity through hiring, retention, and rate increases.
stakeholders: Individuals on waitlists or registries for Medicaid waiver programs and community-based service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill redirects $30,000,000 in fiscal year 2023 funding from the Dedicated Purpose Account for Medicaid waiver expansions. According to the Fiscal Note, there is no net impact on state expenditures as the bill authorizes funds already included in the budget; however, the Maryland Department of Health estimates the total cost to reduce waiver waitlists by 50% as required by law will exceed $1,000,000,000 through fiscal year 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Governor to include sufficient funds in the annual budget bill starting in fiscal year 2024 to carry out the waitlist and registry reduction plans. The Governor's Office also oversees the Executive Department which includes the Dedicated Purpose Account mentioned in the supplemental budget.

The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for administering the Medicaid waiver programs, developing the plans to reduce waitlists and registries, and overseeing the hiring and retention of providers.

The Maryland State Department of Education is explicitly required to collaborate with the Department of Health on plans relating to the Autism Waiver and receives budget transfers to support students with disabilities.
DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and processing budget amendments for the Dedicated Purpose Account, which this bill alters to expand funding uses for Medicaid waivers.

The bill directly impacts services and support systems for individuals with disabilities, which falls under the department's core mission to coordinate and improve service delivery for this population.

Several of the Medicaid waivers addressed in the bill, such as the Brain Injury Waiver and the Home- and Community-Based Options Waiver, are critical to the elderly and disabled populations served by the Department of Aging.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is involved in the oversight of state expenditures and revenues. The bill also includes specific budgetary items for disparity grant funding which the Comptroller's office manages.

The Treasurer's Office was identified as a source of information for the fiscal note and plays a key role in managing state funds and serving on the Board of Public Works, which oversees state procurements.
The bill includes specific provisions and restrictions on the use of funds for administrative costs associated with apprenticeship workgroups operated by the Department of Labor.
The supplemental budget section of the bill includes numerous line items for programs managed by Commerce, including tourism grants, arts grants, and small/minority/women-owned business accounts.
The bill's supplemental budget section reallocates and specifies funding for Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and the Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), which are managed by DHS.
The bill includes budget items for street and sidewalk improvements to comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act in Baltimore City, which involves MDOT programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allocates funds for the Division of Parole and Probation to review murders involving supervised offenders and requires annual reporting on these activities.
The supplemental budget section provides funding for the establishment of the Maryland State Police Gun Center and grants for license plate readers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill includes funding to expand the Maryland Corps Program, which is a central part of this department's mission.
The bill specifies funding for the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit and a redevelopment plan for State Center, which are planning-related initiatives.
The bill includes a grant for the Pride of Baltimore, which is administratively linked to the Department of Agriculture's budget codes (L00).
The bill details funding for a new unified financial aid system, loan assistance repayment programs for nurses, and other higher education grants managed or coordinated by the Commission.
The bill contains specific budget allocations for the Administrative Office of the Courts for prosecutorial transparency reporting.
The bill includes a specific appropriation for public communications for the general election overseen by the State Board of Elections.

Synopsis: Making certain shared appreciation agreements subject to the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law and other provisions of law that regulate certain loans of single extensions of closed end credit and revolving credit plans; and authorizing the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to adopt certain regulations regarding the enforcement of and compliance with provisions of law that regulate shared appreciation agreements.
Title: Commercial Law and Financial Institutions - Credit Regulation - Shared Appreciation Agreements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill classifies shared appreciation agreements as mortgage loans and subjects them to the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law. These agreements involve a consumer receiving money or value in exchange for a future interest in a dwelling or an obligation to repay based on events such as a property transfer, death, or maturity date. The bill authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to oversee these transactions and adopt necessary regulations for enforcement and compliance.
responsible_party: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners/consumers entered into shared appreciation agreements and financial entities or businesses offering these products.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill codifies and clarifies existing regulatory practices and is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. While some small businesses not currently licensed as mortgage lenders may face costs for licensure, including a 1,000 dollar annual fee, the overall financial impact to the State is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly grants the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, an official within the Department of Labor, the authority to adopt regulations and oversee the enforcement of and compliance with shared appreciation agreements under the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law.

The Office of the Attorney General enforces consumer protection and financial regulation laws. This bill impacts consumer credit regulation, and the OAG's Consumer Protection Division is directly identified as a stakeholder in the bill's fiscal analysis.

The bill regulates financial agreements tied to owner-occupied residential real property and home equity, which directly aligns with this department's mission to ensure access to safe and secure housing for Maryland residents.

The bill establishes a civil cause of action allowing borrowers to sue lenders for damages resulting from violations of the shared appreciation agreement regulations, potentially increasing litigation within the state court system.

As the independent agency responsible for hearing contested cases from state regulatory bodies, the OAH would adjudicate appeals and disputes arising from the Department of Labor's enforcement of shared appreciation agreement regulations.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies responsible for implementing these financial regulations and coordinates the state's broader policy agenda regarding consumer protection and commercial law.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, the Maryland Children's Health Program, and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for all services rendered to an enrollee by a licensed pharmacist within the pharmacist's lawful scope of practice to the same extent as services rendered by any other health care practitioner; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed by January 1, 2024.
Title: Health Insurance - Reimbursement for Services Rendered by a Pharmacist

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), the Maryland Children’s Health Program (MCHP), and private health insurers to provide coverage for all services rendered by a licensed pharmacist within their lawful scope of practice to the same extent as other licensed health care practitioners. It prohibits conditioning pharmacist reimbursement on whether the pharmacist is employed by a physician or acting under a physician's orders.
stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, Medicaid and Maryland Children’s Health Program enrollees, and individuals with private health insurance plans in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures (approximately 51% federal funds and 49% general funds) will increase by an indeterminate amount starting in fiscal 2024 due to increased billing for services already covered by Medicaid and MCHP. Federal fund revenues will increase correspondingly to match federal expenditures. Local government expenditures for health insurance may increase if the bill leads to higher costs for fully insured plans. There is no material impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP). The bill specifically amends the Health - General Article to require these programs to provide coverage for services rendered by licensed pharmacists and mandates that MDH apply for federal waivers or amendments to implement these changes.

The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) regulates health insurance carriers in the state. The bill amends the Insurance Article to require that insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations provide reimbursement for services rendered by a licensed pharmacist within their scope of practice to the same extent as other health care practitioners.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) oversees the health insurance marketplace where individual and small group plans are sold. These plans are subject to the bill's requirements regarding pharmacist reimbursement, and MHBE was consulted for the fiscal analysis of the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note assesses the potential impact of the bill's reimbursement mandates on the state health plan's expenditures.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the MDH and MIA. It will be involved in advising these agencies on the legal requirements of the new statutes and the drafting of any necessary regulations or federal waiver applications.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (MDH, MIA) implementing this bill and coordinates health policy initiatives. Governor Wes Moore signed this bill into law as part of the administration's health policy agenda.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations that establish certain food service facility standards that are appropriate to residential programs that have less than 17 residents.
Title: Behavioral Health Programs - Residential Programs - Food Service Facility Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing specific food service facility standards for certain small residential behavioral health programs that have fewer than 17 residents. This applies to programs licensed for low-intensity, medium-intensity, high-intensity, and intensive residential substance-related treatment levels.
stakeholders: Residential behavioral health programs with fewer than 17 residents and individuals receiving substance-related treatment services within those programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can adopt the required regulations using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues. Local government finances are not materially affected, and small businesses operating these residential programs may see a meaningful benefit from the tailored food service standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Health adopt regulations to establish food service facility standards appropriate for specific residential behavioral health programs with fewer than 17 residents. MDH is the primary agency responsible for the licensure and oversight of these behavioral health programs.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and is responsible for reviewing new regulations for legal sufficiency before they are adopted.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its departments, including the Department of Health. The Governor approved the bill, and the office coordinates the policy initiatives that these regulations reflect.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and estimating the fiscal impact of legislation; the fiscal note for this bill confirms that MDH can implement the required changes within existing resources.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. It could be called upon to resolve disputes or appeals regarding the enforcement of the new food service standards for behavioral health programs.

Synopsis: Providing that a therapy management contract may be entered into in writing or orally; requiring, if a therapy management contract is entered into orally, the parties to the therapy management contract to reduce the contract to writing within 30 days after entering into the therapy management contract; and providing that a therapy management contract may be in electronic form.
Title: Pharmacists - Therapy Management Contract - Form

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: This bill authorizes therapy management contracts between pharmacists, authorized prescribers, and patients to be entered into orally or in electronic form. If a contract is entered into orally, it must be reduced to writing within 30 days. The bill updates the definition of a therapy management contract by removing the requirement that it be written and signed, replacing it with a requirement that the parties agree to the contract.
stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, authorized prescribers, and patients receiving treatment under drug therapy management protocols.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State governmental operations or finances. There is no local impact, and the impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates health care professionals, including pharmacists. The State Board of Pharmacy, which operates under MDH, is responsible for the oversight of therapy management contracts and the Drug Therapy Management Program. The bill directly modifies the statutory requirements for the form of these contracts.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to all state agencies and boards, including the State Board of Pharmacy. The OAG would be involved in interpreting the legal shift from purely written contracts to those that can be entered into orally or electronically.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its departments, including the Maryland Department of Health. The Governor signed this bill into law, and the office maintains administrative support for the implementation of legislation affecting state regulatory bodies.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which a dentist who is a faculty member at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry and was trained at a foreign dental school must be qualified by the State Board of Dental Examiners to take an examination offered by the American Board of Dental Examiners, Inc., or its successor organization.
Title: State Board of Dental Examiners - University of Maryland School of Dentistry Faculty - Qualifying for Examination

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility for foreign-trained faculty at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry to qualify for the American Board of Dental Examiners (ADEX) dental exam. It allows general dentists who have completed a general dental practice residency, advanced education in general dentistry, or board certification by the American Board of General Dentistry to take the exam, provided they have served as full-time faculty for at least seven consecutive years and have institutional support.
stakeholders: Foreign-trained general dentists who are faculty members at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Dental Examiners special fund revenues will increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2024 from license fees collected from additional applicants. The board's administrative workload and expenses related to the bill can be managed with existing budgeted resources. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the qualifications and procedures for the State Board of Dental Examiners, which is a regulatory board situated within the Department of Health. The department is responsible for overseeing the licensure of health care professionals.

The bill specifically alters the criteria for faculty members at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry (UMSOD) to qualify for professional licensure. UMSOD is a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, and the bill directly affects their faculty recruitment and professional development.

The Commission is the state's coordinating board for higher education, responsible for establishing statewide policies and ensuring adherence to academic standards at public universities like the University of Maryland.

As the state's regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, this agency establishes policies for public universities and ensures academic programs meet state standards, which is relevant to the training requirements for university faculty licensure mentioned in the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and representation to all state agencies and regulatory boards, including the State Board of Dental Examiners and the University System of Maryland, regarding the interpretation and implementation of new statutes.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the Department of Health and its various regulatory boards. The Governor also officially signed this legislation into law.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer responsible for collecting revenues. The fiscal note indicates that this bill will result in a minimal increase in special fund revenues through license fees collected by the Board.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor, in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to conduct a study on the utilization of the expedited licensing process for service members, veterans, and military spouses for certain occupational and professional licenses in the State; and requiring the Maryland Department of Labor, in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by June 30, 2024.
Title: Study on the Utilization of the Expedited Licensing Process for Service Members, Veterans, and Military Spouses

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Labor, in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs, to conduct a study on how service members, veterans, and military spouses utilize the state's expedited occupational and professional licensing process. The study must examine the number of individuals using the process, the types of military experience credited toward licensure, and outreach efforts, with a report due by June 30, 2024.
stakeholders: Service members, veterans, and military spouses seeking professional or occupational licenses in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of Labor and the Department of Veterans Affairs can conduct the required study using existing budgeted resources. No impact on state revenues or local government finances is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for conducting the study and submitting the report on the utilization of the expedited licensing process for service members, veterans, and military spouses, as it oversees the professional licenses subject to the study.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Labor to consult with the Department of Veterans & Military Families (formerly the Department of Veterans Affairs) to conduct the study and report findings, as the agency advocates for the service members and veterans targeted by the legislation.

The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the study's findings and recommendations, and the office oversees the executive departments responsible for implementing these licensing and workforce policies.

Synopsis: Correcting certain references to the Comptroller of Maryland to be the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, as appropriate; and clarifying certain powers and duties of the Executive Director of the Commission relating to alcoholic beverages regulation and enforcement.
Title: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission – Technical Corrections and Clarifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills

bill_summary: This bill makes technical corrections and clarifications by replacing references to the Comptroller of Maryland with the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission (ATC). It updates and specifies the ATC's concurrent enforcement and regulatory authority over matters related to alcoholic beverages and tobacco, reflecting the transfer of responsibilities from the Comptroller's Office, and repeals an obsolete reference to alcoholic beverage tax stamps.
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage and tobacco licensees (manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers), common carriers, local licensing boards, and the Maryland Comptroller.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no fiscal impact on state or local government operations or finances. According to the Fiscal Note, the legislation codifies existing practices and technical transfers of authority from the Comptroller's Office to the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission that were initiated by previous legislation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly impacts the Comptroller by stripping its former regulatory and enforcement authority over the alcohol and tobacco industries, transferring these powers to the Executive Director of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, and clarifying cooperative duties between the two agencies regarding tax administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly relates to the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission and its Executive Director, while also specifically renaming the 'Governor’s Wine and Grape Advisory Commission' to the 'Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing.'

The bill amends the Health – General Article regarding the enforcement of tobacco laws, requiring local health departments to report violations to the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission and requiring the Department of Health to collaborate with the Commission on enforcement strategies.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish immunity from liability for the Executive Director and officers of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission during contraband seizures and clarifies the judicial review process for contested cases.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG is relevant to the interpretation and enforcement of the clarified regulatory powers and may represent the Commission in judicial reviews of final decisions.

The bill includes the Field Enforcement Division of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission in the statutory definition of law enforcement agencies alongside the State Police and involves coordinated efforts between peace officers for the seizure of contraband.
The bill requires the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission to verify with the Secretary of Labor that applicants for license renewals have paid required unemployment insurance contributions.

The bill requires applicants for alcoholic beverage licenses to provide the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission with certificates of compliance or policy numbers related to the Maryland Workers’ Compensation Act.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and signs legislation impacting the administrative structure and authority of state commissions like the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State's Attorney of Calvert County to designate county attorneys or assistant county attorneys to prosecute civil infractions; and authorizing the designated attorneys to exercise the powers of the State's Attorney when prosecuting civil infractions.
Title: Calvert County - Civil Infractions - Prosecutorial Designations
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State’s Attorney of Calvert County to designate the county attorney or an assistant county attorney to prosecute civil infractions, provided the designation is approved by the county commissioners.
stakeholders: Calvert County State’s Attorney, the Calvert County Attorney’s Office, the Calvert County Commissioners, and individuals involved in civil infraction cases in Calvert County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Maryland State operations or finances. Any operational impact for Calvert County is assumed to not materially affect local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes changes to who may prosecute civil infractions in Calvert County. Since these infractions are adjudicated within the state court system, the Administrative Office of the Courts is relevant as it provides the operational and administrative support for the judiciary where these cases are heard.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor signed this bill into law and oversees the administration of state laws. The office also manages the appointment of various officials, though the primary impact of this bill is at the local county level.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to file a petition for expungement of certain criminal records based on a conviction for certain hunting offenses.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Hunting Offenses - Expungement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes a person to file a petition for the expungement of criminal records for specific misdemeanor hunting offenses, such as hunting without a license, failing to wear fluorescent clothing, or trapping furbearers without a nonresident trapper's license.
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of specific misdemeanor hunting offenses under the Natural Resources Article.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally from $30 filing fees per petition. State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Judiciary increase through fiscal 2026 to process additional expungements. Although the total expenditure is indeterminate, the Judiciary indicated that hiring 23 additional clerks would cost 1400000 dollars if petition volume is high. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary entity responsible for processing expungement petitions; the fiscal note projects a significant increase in workload and expenditures for judicial clerks to manage these new petitions.

The bill concerns expunging convictions for hunting offenses specifically listed in the Natural Resources Article. The DNR's Natural Resources Police is the primary enforcement and record-keeping body for these violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This department oversees the supervision of justice-involved individuals and manages the state's central repository of criminal records, which must be updated following any court-ordered expungements.
As a primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police maintain records that may be subject to expungement orders resulting from the expansion of eligibility for these hunting offenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals and will likely be responsible for assisting eligible clients in filing petitions for the expungement of their records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates state public safety and criminal justice policy, making the expansion of expungement eligibility and its impact on criminal record management highly relevant to its strategic oversight.

The Maryland State Archives preserves permanent government and judicial records; since the bill allows for the expungement of old convictions, the Archives may need to process orders for archived records.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the various state agencies and the Judiciary that must interpret and implement the revised expungement procedures.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for the final approval and signing of this legislation into law.
The Department of Budget and Management handles state fiscal planning, which is relevant due to the Judiciary's projected need for additional funding and personnel to manage the bill's requirements.

Synopsis: Altering a certain benefit amount for certain fire and rescue volunteers; and authorizing the board of commissioners to approve an increase in benefit payment for certain fire and rescue volunteers.
Title: Calvert County - Length of Service Award Program - Benefits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill increases death and burial benefits for volunteer fire, rescue, and dive team members in Calvert County under the Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP). It also authorizes the Calvert County Board of County Commissioners to approve cost-of-living increases for these benefits that align with those given to county employees.
responsible_party: Calvert County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Qualified volunteer fire company members, rescue squad members, and rescue dive team members in Calvert County
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on State operations or finances. However, Calvert County expenditures are estimated to increase by a minimum of 450000 annually starting in fiscal 2024. This increase is largely attributed to the authorization of cost-of-living adjustments for LOSAP benefits. Increases to specific death and burial benefits are expected to have a minimal fiscal impact based on historical data.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office is responsible for the final review and signing of legislation, and the Governor signed this bill into law on May 16, 2023.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and coordinates the statewide emergency medical services (EMS) network. Since the bill alters the benefits and recruitment/retention incentives (LOSAP) for volunteer rescue squads and dive teams within that network, it is relevant to the agency's mission of ensuring a robust EMS system.

The bill explicitly tasks the State Workers' Compensation Commission with determining whether a qualified volunteer died 'in the line of duty,' which is a necessary certification for receiving the enhanced death benefit. The Commission also certifies permanent disability for volunteers under existing law related to these benefits.

Synopsis: Defining "generating station" as it relates to the requirement to obtain a certificate of public convenience and necessity or approval from the Public Service Commission for a person who constructs a generating station that has the capacity to produce more than 2 but not more than 14 megawatts of electricity from a solar photovoltaic system; requiring an electric company to provide meter aggregation for certain eligible customer-generators under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Public Utilities - Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity and Meter Aggregation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: This bill modifies the definition of a "generating station" to exempt certain solar photovoltaic systems and combinations of units from the requirement to obtain a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN). Specifically, it allows combinations of units on the same or adjacent properties with a cumulative capacity up to 14 megawatts to bypass the CPCN process under certain conditions. Additionally, the bill requires electric companies to provide meter aggregation for eligible customer-generators used for agriculture, nonprofits, state and local governments, and public senior higher education institutions.
stakeholders: Solar energy developers, electric companies, nonprofit organizations, state and local government units, public senior higher education institutions, and agricultural businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State government operations or finances, though state agencies such as the Public Service Commission, the Department of Natural Resources, and the Maryland Department of the Environment may have fewer CPCN applications to review. Local governments may experience significant expenditure impacts if they choose to more actively regulate or study electric generation projects that bypass the state-level CPCN process. Specific dollar estimates for these impacts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary agency responsible for defining generating stations, issuing certificates of public convenience and necessity (CPCN), and regulating the meter aggregation policies of electric companies.

The Department of Natural Resources, through its Power Plant Research Program, is a key participant in the CPCN review process, conducting scientific and technical evaluations of proposed generating facilities.
The bill specifically references closed landfills regulated by MDE in its definition of brownfield sites and involves MDE in the multi-agency review of CPCN applications for environmental impacts.
The agency manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is designated to receive abandoned application deposits under the bill's provisions regarding solar generating stations.

The OPC represents the interests of residential utility consumers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission, including those involving certificates for generating stations and meter aggregation rules.
Agriculture is one of the specific sectors for which electric companies are mandated to provide meter aggregation, directly impacting the economic viability of farms and agricultural operations.
As the agency responsible for state facility management and sustainability initiatives, DGS is impacted by the provision allowing units of State government to request meter aggregation.

The system's institutions are public senior higher education institutions, which are newly eligible for meter aggregation under the bill, potentially impacting their energy costs and sustainability projects.
As a public senior higher education institution, the university is eligible to request meter aggregation for its electrical services under the bill's provisions.
As a public senior higher education institution, the college is eligible to request meter aggregation for its electrical services under the bill's provisions.
The commission oversees policies for public senior higher education institutions, which are specifically included in the expanded meter aggregation requirements.
The OAG provides necessary legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and the various executive departments involved in the implementation and enforcement of utility regulations.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse to study existing laws, policies, and practices relating to elder abuse and crimes commonly committed against older adults; and requiring the Task Force to submit a final report by December 31, 2024, to the Governor and the General Assembly with its findings and recommendations regarding changes to State law, policy, and practice that would aid in preventing elder abuse.
Title: Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Elder Abuse and Neglect -see also- Vulnerable Adults
Vulnerable Adults -see also- Developmental Disabilities; Eld

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse to study existing laws, policies, and practices related to elder abuse and crimes against older adults. The Task Force is charged with making recommendations for legislative and policy changes to improve the prevention, oversight, and prosecution of elder abuse in Maryland.
stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, particularly those aged 60 and older, victims of elder abuse, state and local law enforcement, and health and human services agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $26,500 in fiscal 2024 and $11,400 in fiscal 2025 to hire one part-time contractual employee to staff the Task Force. These costs include salary, fringe benefits, and operating expenses. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Aging is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. It is required to provide staff for the task force, and the Secretary of Aging (or a designee) and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman are designated members of the task force.

The Attorney General (or a designee) is a mandated member of the task force. The task force is charged with studying laws and making recommendations on prosecuting elder abuse, which falls under the OAG's legal and consumer protection mandates.

The Department of Health is highly relevant as the bill requires membership from the Maryland Chief Medical Examiner and a representative from the Maryland Office of Health Care Quality (an office within MDH). The task force's work also intersects with MDH's role in public health and regulating care facilities.
The Director of the Office of Adult Services, which is housed within the Department of Human Services and manages Adult Protective Services, is a mandated member of the task force.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is specifically named as an entity that must have a representative appointed to the task force by the Governor.

The Governor is responsible for appointing 11 members to the task force, designating the chair, and receiving the preliminary and final reports. The office also oversees the executive policy initiatives relevant to elder abuse mentioned in the preamble.

The Maryland State Police is specifically named as an entity that must have a representative appointed to the task force by the Governor to provide input on law enforcement and criminal investigations.

The fiscal note identifies a general fund expenditure increase of $26,500 in FY 2024 for contractual staff to support the task force. DBM is the principal personnel and budget agency responsible for managing these state resources.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in vetting and recommending candidates for the 11 appointed positions on the task force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill creates a new executive task force and also mandates membership from the Maryland Human Trafficking Task Force, which is an existing executive body.

The bill's preamble discusses the need to educate courts about elder abuse and mentions a representative from the Baltimore City Circuit Court. The AOC provides operational and legal support to the judiciary and would be involved in implementing judicial education recommendations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from parking certain vehicles in the Town of Sharpsburg, Washington County, subject to a certain exception.
Title: Town of Sharpsburg - Parking of Vehicles - Restrictions

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the parking of specific vehicle classes, including certain trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses, on any street or highway in the Town of Sharpsburg in Washington County, with an exception for vehicles in immediate use.
stakeholders: Owners and operators of commercial trucks, tractors, trailers, and buses, as well as residents and local authorities in the Town of Sharpsburg.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. Local enforcement can be managed with existing resources, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new parking prohibitions and fines for certain vehicle classes in Sharpsburg; the Judicial branch, supported by the AOC, will be responsible for adjudicating any contested violations and processing associated penalties.

The bill adds a new section to the Transportation Article, which is the primary legal framework overseen by MDOT. The regulations affect the operation and parking of vehicles within the state's transportation network.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency for motor vehicle laws and highway safety, the Maryland State Police may be involved in the enforcement of these new parking restrictions, particularly on state highways passing through the town.

The bill's parking prohibitions are specifically defined according to MVA-administered vehicle registration classes, including Class E (Truck), Class F (Tractor), Class G (Trailer), Class H (School Bus), and Class P (Passenger Bus).

The SHA is responsible for maintaining state-numbered highways and ensuring safety improvements; the bill restricts parking on any 'street or highway' in the town, which includes state-maintained routes under SHA jurisdiction.

Synopsis: Establishing a minimum training course compensation of $50 and minimum daily compensation of $250 for election judges for each election day and each early voting day actually served; requiring the State Board of Elections to reimburse each local board elections for $50 of the extra compensation that is paid to each returning election judge; and requiring the State Board to develop and implement a marketing campaign to assist in the recruitment of individuals to serve as election judges.
Title: Elections - Election Judges - Minimum Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill establishes minimum compensation for election judges at $250 per day for new judges and at least $350 per day for returning judges, plus a $50 minimum for each training course completed. It mandates the Maryland State Board of Elections to reimburse local boards for $50 of the extra daily compensation paid to returning judges and requires the Board to develop and implement a marketing campaign to recruit a diverse pool of election judges.
stakeholders: Maryland election judges, the State Board of Elections, local boards of elections, county governing bodies, and Maryland voters.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $1,600,000 to $2,100,000 annually starting in FY 2024. Local government expenditures increase collectively by approximately $3,200,000 to $3,800,000 annually. These increases are driven by mandated minimum pay levels, training stipends, state reimbursements to local boards, and shared costs for a recruitment marketing campaign.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SBE is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including establishing minimum compensation for election judges, reimbursing local boards for extra compensation for returning judges, and developing a statewide marketing campaign for recruitment.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and execution. The bill requires an estimated $1.6 million to $2.1 million annual increase in general fund expenditures to cover SBE's reimbursement and marketing costs.

The bill requires SBE to develop a marketing campaign with an estimated cost of over $1.25 million. Contracts of this size for state services typically require approval from the Board of Public Works.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller's office will be responsible for processing the actual disbursement of state funds to reimburse local boards of elections as mandated by the bill.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including SBE, and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which must now account for the mandated election judge compensation and marketing costs.
The Treasurer's Office manages the distribution of state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works, which may oversee procurement for the recruitment marketing campaign.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like SBE and will likely be involved in reviewing new regulations and procurement contracts for the mandated marketing campaign.
OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of executive agencies. It will eventually be responsible for auditing the new reimbursement program to ensure SBE correctly distributes funds to local boards.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations to provide coverage for biomarker testing that is supported by medical and scientific evidence; establishing requirements for deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for biomarker testing; and requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on the impact of providing biomarker testing.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Required Coverage for Biomarker Testing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and various health insurance carriers to provide coverage for biomarker testing used for the diagnosis, treatment, management, or ongoing monitoring of a disease or condition when such testing is supported by medical and scientific evidence.
stakeholders: Medicaid recipients, individuals with private health insurance, health insurance carriers, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures are expected to increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount beginning in fiscal 2026. For illustrative purposes, the Fiscal Note indicates that if 1% of Medicaid enrollees receive one biomarker test at a cost of $1,700, expenditures would increase by approximately $27,000,000 annually. These costs would be split approximately 60% federal funds and 40% general funds. The Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland Department of Health can handle reporting requirements with existing resources. Local governments that purchase fully insured medical plans may see increased expenditure costs due to the insurance mandate. Savings from more efficient and targeted clinical management are expected but cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill mandates that Medicaid and its Managed Care Organizations provide coverage for biomarker testing and requires MDH to submit a detailed report on fiscal and access impacts to the Governor.
The bill explicitly requires the MHCC to study and report on the impact of biomarker testing coverage, including an analysis of access and usage across demographics such as race, gender, and age.

MIA regulates the private insurance market, including the insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs that are mandated by this bill to provide coverage. The agency will oversee compliance and process related rate and form filings.

MHBE administers the marketplace for private health plans in Maryland. The bill's mandate for biomarker testing coverage directly affects the health benefits and coverage standards for plans offered through the Exchange.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal agency. The fiscal note indicates that the bill will have a potentially significant impact on Medicaid expenditures (general and federal funds) beginning in FY 2026, which falls under DBM's budget execution and planning duties.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies implementing the bill and is the direct recipient of the mandated report from the Department of Health regarding the program's fiscal and access impacts.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MDH and MIA. They will assist in interpreting the new statutory requirements and ensuring the legality of regulations used to enforce the coverage mandate.

Biomarker testing is highly relevant to the diagnosis and monitoring of chronic diseases and conditions prevalent in older adults, a demographic protected and advocated for by the Department of Aging.

The department coordinates services for Marylanders with disabilities, a population that may be significantly affected by the availability and mandatory coverage of biomarker testing for genetic and complex health conditions.

DHS manages eligibility for public assistance programs, and the socioeconomic impacts of expanded health coverage for vulnerable populations overlap with the agency's mission to assist those in economic need.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for early childhood education teacher certification completed through an alternative teacher preparation program; requiring the State Department of Education, in consultation with the Maryland Higher Education Commission, to establish specific goals for the recruitment and retention of teachers in teacher preparation programs; requiring that "high staff qualifications" for publicly funded eligible prekindergarten providers must be implemented by the 2027-2028 school year; etc.
Title: Maryland Educator Shortage Reduction Act of 2023

bill_summary: The Maryland Educator Shortage Reduction Act of 2023 implements several initiatives to recruit and retain teachers and school-based mental health professionals. It establishes the Teacher Development and Retention Program, a pilot initiative providing stipends for students in teacher preparation programs, and creates an educator recruitment and diversity dashboard. The bill expands eligibility for the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award to include school mental health professionals, modifies the Teaching Fellows for Maryland scholarship, and delays for two years the implementation of higher staff qualification requirements for certain prekindergarten providers.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC)
stakeholders: Current and prospective teachers, school mental health professionals (psychologists, social workers, counselors), teacher preparation programs, local boards of education, and prekindergarten providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $15,694,067 in FY 2024. This includes $10,000,000 for the Teacher Development and Retention Fund, $5,000,000 for the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award, and roughly $694,000 for data dashboard implementation, program evaluation, and IT updates. Expenditures are estimated to remain at $5,200,000 in FY 2025 and FY 2026. Local school systems can likely handle reporting requirements with existing resources. The pilot program is set to terminate on June 30, 2029.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is primary in the implementation of the bill, including establishing the Maryland Educator Recruitment, Retention, and Diversity Dashboard, setting teacher recruitment and retention goals, and developing standards for early childhood educator certification and alternative preparation programs.

The agency, specifically its Office of Student Financial Assistance, is responsible for administering the Teacher Development and Retention Program, the Teaching Fellows for Maryland scholarship, and the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award (part of the Loan Assistance Repayment Program).

Constituent institutions of the University System host teacher preparation programs that must meet new recruitment and retention goals, and their students are major recipients of the stipends and scholarships established or modified by the bill.

As an independent state university with a teacher preparation program and as a Historically Black College or University (HBCU), Morgan State is specifically targeted for program publicity, recruitment efforts, and its students' eligibility for stipends.

As a state institution with a teacher preparation program, the college is impacted by the bill's requirements for program goals, and its students are eligible for the financial support programs established under the act.
The Treasurer is responsible for holding the new Teacher Development and Retention Fund separately and managing the investment of its funds.
The bill includes mandated appropriations for scholarships and has significant fiscal impacts on state personnel and funds, which the department manages as the principal fiscal and personnel agency.
The Comptroller is responsible for the accounting of the Teacher Development and Retention Fund established by the bill.
This is an Administration bill that coordinates policy initiatives across multiple executive departments (MSDE, MHEC) and requires significant annual budget proposals overseen by the office.
The bill expands loan repayment award eligibility to mental health professionals employed by local health departments who provide services in public schools.

The bill incorporates registered apprenticeships as a recognized path for satisfying certification criteria for early childhood education, which relates to the department's oversight of workforce development.
The bill requires a notice and appeal process for individuals denied licensure under the new Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, a function typically adjudicated by this office.
The bill facilitates Maryland's membership and participation in the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact to support licensure reciprocity.
As a state-operated public school system, the agency is impacted by the bill's requirements regarding educator certification, diversity reporting, and workforce recruitment goals.

Synopsis: Requiring an adult family member to submit a death certificate or evidence of disability to the State Real Estate Commission before the family member may carry on the business of a disabled or deceased licensed real estate broker; permitting a certain business to designate a licensed real estate broker to provide real estate brokerage services under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Real Estate Brokers - Disability or Death and Termination of Employment of a Broker

bill_summary: This bill requires an adult family member of a deceased or disabled real estate broker to submit a death certificate or evidence of disability to the State Real Estate Commission before they can temporarily carry on the broker's business. Additionally, the bill establishes procedures for a real estate business to designate a new licensed broker if the current broker is terminated or if the documentation for a deceased or disabled broker is not provided within a reasonable timeframe.
stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, family members of deceased or disabled brokers, and real estate businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, as the State Real Estate Commission can implement the bill's changes with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency relevant to this bill as it oversees the State Real Estate Commission. The bill directly modifies the Maryland Real Estate Brokers Act, which the department is responsible for enforcing, specifically regarding the licensing, regulation, and business continuity of real estate brokers in cases of death, disability, or termination.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Real Estate Commission and the Department of Labor. They would be responsible for advising the commission on the legal implementation of these new requirements and representing the agency in any related legal challenges.

The Office of Administrative Hearings may be involved if there are contested cases or appeals regarding the State Real Estate Commission's decisions to approve or deny the designation of a new broker or the continuation of a business after a broker's death or disability.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs to the parent of a child with a disability who is the prevailing party in a certain special education proceeding; prohibiting a court from awarding attorney's fees and related costs to certain parents in a certain proceeding under certain circumstances; and authorizing an award of attorney's fees and related costs to a parent of a child with a disability who is a prevailing party under certain circumstances.
Title: Special Education - Judicial Actions - Attorney's Fees and Related Costs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland courts to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs, including expert witness fees, to parents of children with disabilities who prevail in special education legal proceedings concerning identification, evaluation, placement, or the provision of a free appropriate public education. It also sets conditions for these awards, including limitations if a parent rejects a settlement offer that is not more favorable than the final judgment, unless the rejection was justified.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education, local school systems, and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Parents of children with disabilities, students with disabilities, and local education agencies in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State agency expenditures are not significantly affected. Local school systems may experience increased expenditures for attorney's fees and related costs in cases where a parent prevails; the fiscal note assumes this may apply to 10 or fewer cases annually with variable total costs. No specific dollar amount for total annual expenditures is provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OAG serves as the primary legal counsel for state agencies, including the Maryland State Department of Education and the Department of Juvenile Services. This bill allows courts to award attorney's fees against these agencies if a parent prevails in a special education dispute, which impacts the legal defense and financial liabilities managed by the OAG.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state. While the fiscal note suggests state expenditures are not significantly affected, the bill introduces a potential fiscal liability for several state agencies in the form of court-awarded attorney's fees and expert witness costs.

As the agency responsible for coordinating services for residents with disabilities, this bill directly impacts the legal rights and judicial recourse available to the parents of children with disabilities seeking appropriate educational services.

MSDE is the primary agency responsible for overseeing special education and the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) in Maryland. It is explicitly defined as a 'public agency' in the bill and is responsible for ensuring the provision of free appropriate public education (FAPE).

The bill applies to any state agency responsible for providing education to students with disabilities. MDH oversees various developmental disability supports and may operate facilities that provide educational services, potentially making it a 'public agency' under the bill's definition.

The bill defines 'parent' to include foster parents with educational decision-making authority. DHS manages the foster care system and is responsible for the welfare and educational advocacy of children within that system who may be subjects of these special education proceedings.

The bill explicitly includes the 'Juvenile Services Education Program' within the definition of a 'public agency.' DJS provides education to youth in its facilities and is therefore subject to the bill's provisions regarding judicial actions and attorney's fees.

This office focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children and access to educational services. The bill's provisions regarding the enforcement of special education rights through judicial actions are relevant to the office's mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically mentions the Maryland School for the Deaf as a public agency. ODHH advocates for the welfare of Deaf residents and coordinates policy regarding sign language and educational accessibility, making these legal protections highly relevant.

The bill authorizes state courts (Circuit Courts) to award attorney's fees and related costs in special education appeals. The AOC provides operational and legal support to the judiciary, which will implement these new awarding provisions.

The Maryland School for the Deaf is explicitly named as a 'public agency' in the bill. It provides education to students with disabilities and could be a respondent in due process hearings liable for attorney's fees and costs.

The bill mandates that due process complaints regarding special education be filed with the OAH. ALJs within the OAH are responsible for conducting these hearings and making decisions that may later be appealed to the courts.

MCCR enforces anti-discrimination laws, including those related to disability. Although this bill is centered on the Education Article, the underlying issues of educational access and disability rights fall within the Commission's broad policy purview.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to annually proclaim January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day; and requiring the proclamation to include a declaration of the purposes of Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day.
Title: Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to annually proclaim January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day, designating it as a day of reflection and a pledge to educate future generations about the reality and lessons of the Holocaust to prevent future atrocities.
stakeholders: Maryland families, educators, religious communities, political bodies, media organizations, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact associated with this bill. According to the Fiscal Note, commemorating Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Governor to annually issue a proclamation for Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day and specifies the required content for this proclamation.
The Secretary of State is the official custodian of the state's executive records, including all proclamations and executive orders issued by the Governor.
This office manages ethnic and faith-based commissions and handles community affairs, making it likely to coordinate the community engagement and reflection activities encouraged by the proclamation.

The bill explicitly names educators as a group for whom the day is a day of reflection and includes a pledge to spread the lessons of the Holocaust to future generations, aligning with the department's oversight of public education.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Governor and executive branch, ensuring that proclamations and executive actions meet constitutional and statutory requirements.
The Archives preserves executive records of permanent value, including official proclamations, ensuring the historical record of this commemorative day is maintained.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date by 2 years for certain provisions of law relating to Maryland Insurance Commissioner enforcement duties regarding administrative services organizations that administer a certain delivery system for specialty mental health services.
Title: Maryland Insurance Commissioner Enforcement - Specialty Mental Health Services and Payment of Claims - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: This emergency bill extends the termination date by two years for provisions that require the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce clean claims laws for administrative services organizations (ASOs) that manage the Medicaid specialty mental health system. It ensures that ASOs remain subject to interest payments on unpaid clean claims and potential fines for violations.
stakeholders: Administrative services organizations (ASOs) managing Medicaid specialty mental health services, mental health service providers, and Medicaid enrollees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) can continue to enforce clean claims provisions using existing budgeted resources through fiscal 2025. MIA special fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount in fiscal 2023, 2024, and 2025 to the extent fines are assessed against ASOs, though the Commissioner may not impose penalties if the cost would be passed on to the State.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns the enforcement duties of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, who heads this agency. It extends the Commissioner's authority to enforce clean claims laws and oversee administrative services organizations (ASOs) that manage specialty mental health services.

The agency oversees the Medicaid specialty mental health delivery system managed by ASOs. The bill requires the Insurance Commissioner to provide investigation findings regarding ASO violations to the Maryland Department of Health.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the OAG provides legal counsel to both the Insurance Administration and the Department of Health regarding the enforcement of insurance laws and administrative disputes with ASOs.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM oversees budget execution and provides fiscal analysis for legislation, particularly regarding the potential use of state funds for penalties or interest on claims.

The office focuses on improving access to health services for families and children. The enforcement of mental health claim payments directly impacts the reliability and accessibility of specialty mental health services for these vulnerable populations.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved (MIA and MDH) and the Governor signed this emergency measure into law.

Synopsis: Exempting a certain retiree of the Employees' Retirement and Pension Systems from a certain earnings limitation when the retiree is reemployed by a certain previous employer for a certain time period to assist with the administration of federally funded grants or projects related to the COVID-19 pandemic; and providing for the retroactive application of the Act to January 1, 2020.
Title: Employees' Retirement and Pension Systems - Reemployment Earnings Limitation - COVID-19 Exemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill exempts retirees of the Employees’ Retirement and Pension Systems from statutory reemployment earnings limitations if they are rehired by the Maryland Department of Health for up to five years. The exemption specifically applies to those assisting with federally funded COVID-19 grants or working on projects related to COVID-19 staffing support and contact tracing. The bill is an emergency measure with retroactive application to January 1, 2020.
stakeholders: Retirees of the State Employees' Retirement and Pension Systems rehired by the Maryland Department of Health for COVID-19 response and administration efforts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no material effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because it applies to a limited number of individuals. However, any benefit offsets already taken in 2023 from rehired retirees must be repaid. The bill has no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) is responsible for the administration and management of the retirement and pension systems. This bill directly impacts its operations by exempting specific retirees from the statutory earnings limitation and requiring the agency to process retroactive adjustments and repayments for any offsets taken in 2023.

As the primary employing agency mentioned in the bill and the departmental sponsor of the legislation, the Department of Health is responsible for rehiring these retirees to manage COVID-19 pandemic response grants and staffing projects.

As the state's central personnel and fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management oversees employee benefits and reemployment policies across the executive branch, including the retirees affected by this legislation.
The bill specifically references reemployment for work within the COVID Unified Command, a coordinating body central to the state's emergency response efforts managed by this department.

The Office of the Attorney General provides essential legal counsel to the State Retirement Agency and the Department of Health regarding the implementation of statutory changes and the complex legal requirements of retroactive application.
The Governor's Office oversees all executive branch departments involved and coordinated the policy initiatives and emergency measures related to the state's COVID-19 response.
