bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to provide a $1,000,000 appropriation to the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund for the Nonprofit, Interest-Free, Micro Bridge Loan (NIMBL) Account in either fiscal 2024 or 2025. It also repeals the provision that previously allocated a portion of video lottery terminal proceeds to the NIMBL account from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account.
stakeholders: Maryland nonprofit organizations, the Maryland Department of Commerce, and small, minority, and women-owned businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no fiscal impact in fiscal 2024. General fund expenditures increase by $1,000,000 in fiscal 2025 due to a mandated appropriation for the NIMBL account. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund increase by $1,000,000 in fiscal 2025 as the funds are received and used for loans. The bill's repeal of the discretionary distribution of video lottery proceeds from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account is expected to have a minimal practical effect on revenue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program and its Fund, which are housed within the Department of Commerce. The agency is responsible for administering the Nonprofit, Interest-Free, Micro Bridge Loan (NIMBL) Account.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific appropriation of $1.0 million in the annual budget bill for the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund for either fiscal year 2024 or 2025.

As the principal agency for budget development and execution, DBM is responsible for implementing the mandated $1.0 million appropriation required by the bill and overseeing the fiscal impact on the state budget.

The bill modifies Section 9-1A-27 of the State Government Article, which directs the Comptroller to pay certain amounts from video lottery terminal proceeds into the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account and previously the NIMBL account.

The bill explicitly states that the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program Fund may be used by the Department of General Services to evaluate the participation of nonprofit entities in State procurement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the distribution of proceeds from video lottery terminals (VLTs). The State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission is responsible for preparing the transmittals that trigger the Comptroller's payments of these proceeds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the funding for the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account (SMWOBA) by repealing a discretionary transfer from that account to the NIMBL account, thereby potentially increasing the funds available for the programs overseen by this office.

Synopsis: Repealing the definition of "public safety officer" for purposes of a certain credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on a dwelling owned by a public safety officer; repealing a certain limitation on the amount of the credit; requiring the governing body of a county or municipal corporation that authorizes the credit to establish, by law, the definition of "public safety officer" for purposes of eligibility for the credit; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Property Tax Credit - Public Safety Officer

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to define the term 'public safety officer' for the purpose of local property tax credit eligibility and repeals the existing $2,500 cap on the amount of property tax credit that local governments may provide to such officers on their primary dwellings.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
stakeholders: Public safety officers (including firefighters, emergency medical technicians, correctional officers, and police officers) who own dwellings in Maryland, and local county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2024 because jurisdictions may expand eligibility definitions or increase the credit amount beyond the previous $2,500 limit. The exact fiscal impact is indeterminate as it depends on local legislative decisions. For context, historical data shows that Anne Arundel County's existing public safety tax credits totaled 1532513 in FY 2023, and Howard County's totaled 385111 in FY 2022.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and coordinates relations with local governments, which are granted expanded authority under this bill to define eligibility for property tax credits.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors tax laws and revenue trends, including local option credits that impact the overall fiscal health of Maryland jurisdictions.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly regarding the interpretation and application of the Tax-Property Article.
DGS manages the Maryland Capitol Police; its officers' eligibility for local property tax credits will now be determined by local jurisdictions rather than state law.
DJS employs personnel responsible for the supervision and treatment of youth, who may be included in expanded local definitions of public safety officers.
DNR oversees the Natural Resources Police, whose members are public safety officers affected by changes in local tax credit eligibility and limits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs a significant number of correctional officers, a group specifically targeted by the previous state definition and likely included in new local definitions.
MDOT oversees modal administrations with dedicated police forces (MTA and MDTA), whose officers' eligibility for tax credits is impacted by this bill.
MCSS coordinates school safety personnel across the state; these personnel are often defined as public safety officers for the purposes of local benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS regulates the state's EMS network, including the emergency medical technicians (EMTs) who are primary beneficiaries of the public safety officer property tax credit.
As the state's primary law enforcement agency, its officers reside in jurisdictions across the state and are directly impacted by the definitions and credit limits set by local governments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary coordinating body for public safety policy and advises the Governor on strategies affecting the recruitment and retention of public safety personnel.

Synopsis: Requiring an appointee for a civil commission to contact the clerk of the circuit court to which the commission was delivered by the Governor to coordinate a time and place for the administration of the oath of office and presentation of the commission; altering the frequency with which the clerk of a circuit court must report to the Secretary of State the name and office of each officer who has taken the oath of office; etc.
Title: Clerks of the Circuit Courts - Civil Commissions - Presentation and Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill requires civil commission appointees to coordinate with the clerk of the circuit court to schedule the administration of the oath of office and the presentation of the commission. It also adjusts the frequency of reporting from the clerks to the Secretary of State regarding individuals who have taken the oath from at least once a month to regularly, and it repeals obsolete provisions regarding taxes on commissions.
stakeholders: Appointees for civil commissions, Clerks of the Circuit Courts, and the Secretary of State
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact because it codifies existing practice and repeals obsolete statutory requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the duties of the clerks of the circuit courts, who fall under the judicial branch. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational and legal support to these courts and their clerks, who are responsible for administering oaths of office and reporting to the Secretary of State.

The Secretary of State is the primary recipient of the reports from the clerks regarding officials who have taken the oath of office. The agency is also responsible for delivering civil commissions to the clerks and serves as the custodian of the state's official records, including these commissions.

The bill concerns civil commissions issued by the Governor. The Governor's Office is responsible for overseen the executive branch and appointing officials to various positions that require these commissions.

The Office of Appointments, within the Executive Department, manages the appointment process for the boards and commissions for which the Governor issues these civil commissions. The bill's changes to how appointees interact with clerks directly affects the individuals processed by this office.

The bill repeals an obsolete provision requiring clerks of the circuit court to pay money received for taxes on commissions to the State Treasurer. The Treasurer's Office was historically the recipient of these funds and was consulted for the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Requiring that the Apprenticeship and Training Council and consultants to the Council include representation by individuals who are Asian, Black, and Latino; establishing the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine and make recommendations to expand access to apprenticeships to reduce skill shortages in high-demand occupations and provide affordable training for career pathways for young people; and requiring the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Labor and Employment - Apprenticeship 2030 Commission and Representation on the Apprenticeship and Training Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission to examine and provide recommendations for expanding registered apprenticeships in high-demand industry sectors, with the goal of reaching 60,000 apprentices by 2030 and ensuring 45% of high school graduates complete an apprenticeship. It also mandates that the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council and its consultants include representation from Asian, Black, and Latino individuals.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services and Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Maryland high school students, unemployed and underemployed adults, employers in high-demand sectors, and members of the Asian, Black, and Latino communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $36,900 in fiscal 2024 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire a half-time contractual policy analyst to support the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission. The Department of Legislative Services provides staffing using existing resources, although additional costs may be incurred if external consultants are needed. There is no fiscal impact on local governments or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council and the new Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, as well as jointly selecting the Commission's chair.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel; the bill results in a general fund expenditure increase of $36,900 for a new contractual position at the Maryland Department of Labor to support the commission.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is a mandated member of the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, which is tasked with identifying and addressing skill shortages in high-demand industry sectors.

The State Superintendent of Schools is a mandated member of the Commission. The bill specifically addresses the Blueprint for Maryland's Future goal of 45% of high school graduates completing a registered apprenticeship.

The Department of Labor is the primary agency impacted. The Apprenticeship and Training Council is housed within its Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning. The Secretary of Labor is a Commission member, and the department receives dedicated funding for a new staff position to support the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary body, the Apprenticeship 2030 Commission, and expands the representation requirements for the existing Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council.

The Chair of the Governor’s Workforce Development Board is a member of the Commission. Additionally, the GWDB houses the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee, whose policies regarding youth apprenticeships control in the event of a conflict with the new Commission.

The Secretary of Higher Education is a mandated member of the Commission, which is specifically tasked with exploring 'degree apprenticeships' in fields requiring higher education such as teaching and healthcare.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the diverse representation required for the Council and the employer representatives on the Commission.

Synopsis: Requiring certain notices relating to increases in property assessments; altering certain notice requirements relating to the intention of a county or municipal corporation to set a certain real property tax rate that exceeds the constant yield tax rate and requiring instead certain notice when a county or municipal corporation intends to increase its real property tax rate.
Title: Property Tax - Real Property Tax Assessment and Tax Rate Increases - Notice Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: This bill modifies the public notice requirements for real property tax increases by requiring counties and municipalities to provide notice specifically when they intend to increase the actual real property tax rate, rather than when the rate exceeds the 'constant yield' rate. Additionally, it requires property assessment notices and tax bills to include clear disclosures explaining that an increase in property assessment may result in a higher tax bill even if the tax rate itself does not increase.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), the Attorney General, and local taxing authorities (counties and municipal corporations)
stakeholders: Maryland real property owners and local government entities including counties and municipalities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no impact on State finances. Local expenditures may decrease due to reduced public notice requirements, as fewer jurisdictions may be required to place newspaper advertisements compared to the previous constant yield standards. However, local expenditures may increase slightly in fiscal 2023 to update property tax bill formats to comply with new disclosure requirements. Local revenues are not affected, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is relevant as the head of the executive branch which includes the primary agency responsible for assessments (SDAT) and the Office of the Attorney General. The Governor also signed this bill into law.

The bill specifies that the Department of Assessments and Taxation must notify local taxing authorities of any changes in estimated property assessments resulting from actions or decisions of the Maryland Tax Court.
The bill explicitly mandates the Attorney General to investigate reports of taxing authorities that violate real property tax notice requirements and to institute legal action to ensure compliance.

The bill specifies that the Department of Assessments and Taxation must notify local taxing authorities of any changes in estimated property assessments resulting from actions or decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board.

Synopsis: Altering a reporting requirement to require the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to report certain student Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) data to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 15 each year, beginning in 2023 and ending in 2028; and requiring the Maryland Higher Education Commission to provide the Center with access to student FAFSA data.
Title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center - Student FAFSA Data - Reporting Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: This bill shifts the responsibility for reporting student Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) data from local school boards to the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center. It requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to provide the MLDS Center with access to FAFSA data, which the Center will then use to report completion rates and related statistics to the General Assembly annually through 2028.
stakeholders: Maryland high school students, local boards of education, and the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a material impact on State finances, as both the MLDS Center and the Maryland Higher Education Commission can fulfill the requirements using existing resources. Local school system expenditures may decrease minimally due to the elimination of FAFSA reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the requirement for local county boards of education to report FAFSA data, which are overseen by this department, and the Maryland Longitudinal Data System matches FAFSA data against student data provided by this department.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Maryland Higher Education Commission and the Maryland State Department of Education, which are both integral to the data sharing and reporting processes established by this bill.
The bill explicitly requires the commission to provide the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center with access to student FAFSA data from federal and state financial aid systems.
The bill explicitly requires the commission to provide the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center with access to student FAFSA data from federal and state financial aid systems.
The bill centralizes FAFSA reporting within this agency, requiring it to collect data from MHEC and submit annual reports to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Increasing the maximum number of years of eligibility service that certain members of the State Police Retirement System or Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System may have to participate in the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) from 30 to 32; increasing the number of years that certain members of the State Police Retirement System or Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System may participate in the DROP from 5 to 7; and authorizing certain individuals to elect to extend their participation in the DROP.
Title: State Police Retirement System and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System - Deferred Retirement Option Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum time members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) can participate in the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) from five to seven years. It also extends the maximum eligibility service limit for the program from 30 to 32 years and allows current DROP participants to elect to extend their participation.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS), including State troopers and local law enforcement officers in participating governmental units.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State pension contributions (general and special funds) are expected to decrease by $400,000 in FY 2025, with annual savings increasing slightly in subsequent years through FY 2028. Total State pension liabilities are estimated to decrease by $2,780,000 because the retirement system's assumed investment return (6.8%) is higher than the interest paid on DROP accounts (4%). Local government pension contributions are also expected to decrease by approximately $150,000 annually beginning in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary entity responsible for the operation and management of the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the State Police Retirement System and the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System. This bill directly impacts the administration of the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) managed by the agency.

The bill specifically alters the retirement and DROP eligibility rules for the State Police Retirement System. The Secretary of State Police and the agency's Director of Human Resources are required to accept binding letters of resignation and acknowledge participation extensions.

The State Treasurer acts as the chief financial officer and typically chairs or holds a leadership position on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System. The office is responsible for the management and protection of state funds, which are impacted by the actuarial savings resulting from this bill.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency for the state, DBM is responsible for the state's budget execution and managing state employee benefits. The bill has a direct fiscal impact on state pension contributions (general and special funds) which DBM oversees.
The Department of Natural Resources employs the Natural Resources Police, whose officers are typically members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) affected by this bill.
MDOT oversees the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA), which employs a significant number of law enforcement officers who are members of LEOPS and therefore impacted by the DROP program changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency employs various law enforcement personnel, such as Fire Marshals and investigators, who participate in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS).

The OAG serves as legal counsel to the State Retirement and Pension System's Board of Trustees and the various state agencies whose personnel are affected by these statutory changes to retirement law.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain eligible customer-generator to accrue net excess generation for an indefinite period; requiring the Public Service Commission to establish a method for calculating the value of certain accrued net excess generation; and requiring that a subscriber of a community solar energy generating system accrue virtual net excess generation in the same manner as a certain eligible customer-generator.
Title: Electricity - Net Energy Metering and Virtual Net Energy Metering - Accrual of Net Excess Generation (Net Metering Flexibility Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: This bill allows eligible electricity customer-generators and community solar subscribers to accrue net excess generation credits indefinitely instead of being restricted to a 12-month accrual period. It requires the Public Service Commission to establish a method for calculating the value of these credits and removes the provision that previously limited community solar credits to 200% of a subscriber's baseline annual usage.
stakeholders: Eligible customer-generators (owners of solar, wind, biomass, and fuel cell facilities), community solar system subscribers, electric companies, and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State or local revenues or expenditures. Small businesses that utilize net metering may experience a meaningful benefit by carrying forward excess generation indefinitely to offset future energy costs, though the broader impact on electricity rates is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Public Service Commission to establish methods for calculating the value of accrued net excess generation and to oversee changes to net energy metering and virtual net energy metering regulations.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission, including those required by this bill to determine valuation and billing protocols for net excess generation.

The Maryland Energy Administration promotes renewable energy and energy efficiency. The bill's changes to the financial incentives and accrual rules for solar and other customer-generated electricity directly align with and impact the agency's policy goals.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and other state agencies regarding the implementation and enforcement of the Public Utilities Article affected by this bill.

The Department of General Services manages state-owned facilities and leads sustainability initiatives. As the state operates its own renewable energy facilities, the changes to net excess generation accrual could affect the state's energy utility accounts.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Social Work Examiners, under certain circumstances, to issue a conditional license to practice social work to an applicant who, except for passing a required examination, has met the appropriate education and experience requirements for a certain license if the required examination was unavailable to the applicant for a period of at least 15 business days; providing that a conditional license is valid until 180 days after the examination becomes readily available to the applicant; etc.
Title: State Board of Social Work Examiners - Conditional Licenses to Practice Social Work

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Board of Social Work Examiners to issue conditional and temporary licenses for bachelor and master social work applicants who have met all education and experience requirements except for passing the required examination. A conditional license may be issued if an administrative delay or unforeseen event prevents the examination from being available for at least 15 business days. The bill also mandates annual reporting by the Board on the status of examination availability and the issuance of these licenses.
responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
stakeholders: Applicants for bachelor and master social work licenses, the State Board of Social Work Examiners, and social work supervisors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Social Work Examiners special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount should the board issue conditional licenses, potentially charging a $75 fee per license. The FY 2024 budget included $75,000 in general funds for board operations contingent on the enactment of this bill to assist with implementation and other board costs. Local fiscal impact is none.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners is a regulatory board within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly mandates the Board's authority to issue conditional and temporary licenses and requires it to report specific data to the General Assembly.

The Department of Human Services is a major employer of social workers and was listed as an information source in the fiscal note. Changes to the availability of conditional or temporary licenses directly impact the department's ability to hire and retain essential workforce staff.

The fiscal note indicates that the bill has an indeterminate impact on special fund revenues and expenditures. DBM oversees state agency budgeting and personnel, including the allocation of general funds contingent on the enactment of this bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and its boards. The agency will be responsible for providing legal guidance on the implementation and regulation of the new conditional and temporary license categories.

As an agency that adjudicates contested cases for state regulatory bodies, OAH would be responsible for hearing appeals regarding the denial or revocation of the conditional and temporary licenses established by this bill.

The bill includes specific provisions for the renewal of temporary social work licenses for service members or military spouses, aligning with the department's advocacy and support mission for military families.
The bill grants the Board the authority to renew a temporary license specifically upon the Governor's declaration of a state of emergency by executive order or proclamation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop and implement a public awareness campaign to encourage the use of mental health advance directives in the State; and requiring the Behavioral Health Administration and the Maryland Health Care Commission jointly to study how first responders and behavioral health crisis providers can access a certain advanced directive database when responding to a behavioral health crisis and to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on their findings on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Public Health - Mental Health Advance Directives - Awareness and Statewide Database

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and implement a public awareness campaign to encourage the use of mental health advance directives. Additionally, the Behavioral Health Administration and the Maryland Health Care Commission must study how first responders and behavioral health crisis providers can access the statewide advance directives database when responding to emergencies.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Administration, and Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Recipients of mental health services and their families, health care providers, first responders, and various state and local health and public safety agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by at least $140,700 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire one administrative program manager and procure campaign materials. Ongoing expenditures for staffing and operations are estimated between $87,400 and $100,400 annually through FY 2028. The required study and report will be completed using existing resources, and there is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the Maryland Department of Health to develop and implement a public awareness campaign for mental health advance directives. Its Behavioral Health Administration is also tasked with jointly studying database access for crisis providers.

The Commission is explicitly required to jointly study the feasibility and implementation of access to the mental health advance directives database for first responders and behavioral health crisis providers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names this department as an agency that must be included in and support the public awareness campaign outreach efforts regarding mental health advance directives.
The Maryland State Police are specifically identified in the bill as an agency required to participate in and support the public awareness and outreach campaign for mental health advance directives.
The bill (referencing the Department of Veterans Affairs) identifies this agency as a required partner for outreach and awareness initiatives related to mental health advance directives.
The bill mandates outreach to academic institutions, which are overseen and coordinated by the Higher Education Commission.
As an academic institution, Morgan State University is identified in the bill as a target entity for outreach and participation in the mental health advance directive public awareness campaign.
The University System of Maryland's member academic institutions are listed as partners for the mandated public awareness campaign outreach efforts.
As a state academic institution, the college is included in the list of entities expected to participate in the mental health advance directive outreach initiatives.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor, for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2028, to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $500,000 to the Prince George's County Office of the County Executive to be used for the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program; and requiring that funds made available by the Act are supplemental to, and may not supplant, funds otherwise available for the reentry employment incentives in Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $500,000 in the state budget for fiscal years 2025 through 2028 to fund the Prince George's County Reentry Employment Incentive Program. The program provides financial incentives to businesses that hire qualifying formerly incarcerated residents of the county.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Office of the County Executive
stakeholders: Formerly incarcerated residents of Prince George's County, commercial and nonprofit businesses in Prince George's County, and the Prince George's County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2028 due to the mandated appropriation. Prince George’s County revenues and expenditures will increase by an equivalent $500,000 annually during this period as the funds are received and distributed to the county's reentry employment program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Governor to include a specific appropriation of $500,000 for the Prince George’s County Reentry Employment Incentive Program in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.
As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising its execution, DBM is the primary body tasked with implementing the mandated appropriation required by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill focuses on reentry employment for individuals who were previously confined for criminal convictions. This program aligns with the department's mission to reduce recidivism and manage justice-involved individuals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates state public safety strategies and manages funds to reduce crime and recidivism, making a reentry employment incentive program highly relevant to its policy goals.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the distribution of state funds and the payment of state bills, including the mandated grant to Prince George's County.

The Department of Labor oversees workforce development and adult learning programs; the reentry program incentivizes the employment of individuals, which falls under the broader scope of the agency's labor and economic growth mission.

The board sets the statewide vision for workforce development and coordinates solutions to ensure residents, including those facing employment barriers like former incarceration, have pathways to prosperity.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Aviation Commission to consider information and advice from certain additional stakeholders when carrying out the Commission's duties; requiring the Commission to consider the aviation, economic, business, environmental, health, and community-related impacts or any other impacts the Commission finds relevant; requiring that certain members of the Commission appointed by the Governor are to be recommended by the Anne Arundel County and Howard County Senate delegations; etc.
Title: Maryland Aviation Commission - Duties, Composition, and Member Orientation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Aviation Commission from 9 to 13 members and requires the commission to develop policies to mitigate the negative impacts of the aviation and airport industries on local communities. It mandates that four of the new members be recommended by the Anne Arundel and Howard county Senate delegations, requires new members to receive orientation on their duties, and subjects the commission to enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements, including live video streaming and specific online agenda posting timelines.
stakeholders: Residents in communities near airports (particularly in Anne Arundel and Howard counties), airport employees and their representatives, local governments, and the air carrier, concessionaire, and support services industries.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures may increase minimally to meet the bill's enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements, such as providing live video streaming and maintaining archived recordings. Other requirements, including the expansion of the commission and additional reporting, are expected to be handled using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Aviation Commission governs and directs the Maryland Aviation Administration, developing management policies and approving major capital projects and regulations for state-owned airports managed by the MAA.

The Secretary of Transportation serves as the Chairman of the Maryland Aviation Commission, and the MAA is a modal administration within MDOT. The bill significantly alters the commission's structure and duties.
The Governor appoints the majority of the commission members and receives approvals for major capital projects from the commission prior to legislative submission.

This office assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state commissions. The bill increases the number of appointees and mandates specific recommendations from local delegations and industry experience.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated as a nonvoting ex officio member of the Maryland Aviation Commission.
The commission's annual report, including its expenditure estimates, is subject to review by DBM. DBM also oversees state personnel resources and benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Aviation Commission is a permanent executive commission governed by the provisions of this bill regarding its composition, orientation, and reporting requirements.
As the chief legal officer for state agencies and boards, the OAG provides legal guidance on implementing new commission policies, composition changes, and Open Meetings Act compliance.
The bill requires the commission to establish policies to mitigate negative impacts on healthy and livable communities and to consider health impacts related to airport infrastructure.
The bill subjects the Maryland Aviation Commission to enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements, including live video streaming and online publication of agendas and minutes.

Synopsis: Clarifying the calculation for certain funding for the Maryland State Arts Council for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter; repealing a certain requirement for certain funds distributed to the Maryland State Arts Council to be included in the Council's prior fiscal year appropriation; etc.
Title: Maryland State Arts Council - Funding

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill clarifies the formula for calculating the annual mandated General Fund appropriation for the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) beginning in fiscal 2025. It defines the 'general fund growth adjustment' and specifies how revenues from the State admissions and amusement tax are factored into the Council's funding formula, effectively codifying current budgetary practices.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Budget and Management and the Maryland State Arts Council
stakeholders: Maryland arts organizations, local arts agencies, individual artists, public school students, and the general public benefiting from cultural arts programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill clarifies an existing mandated appropriation for the Maryland State Arts Council starting in fiscal 2025. According to the fiscal note, the bill has no effect on State expenditures or revenues as it aligns statutory language with the Department of Budget and Management's current interpretation of the funding mandate. No local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Governor to include a specific mandated appropriation amount for the Maryland State Arts Council in the annual budget bill submitted to the General Assembly.

The Comptroller is responsible for distributing the Admissions and Amusement tax revenues mentioned in the bill and chairs the Board of Revenue Estimates, whose revenue projections are the basis for the bill's General Fund growth adjustment calculation.

The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Revenue Estimates, whose report provides the revenue projection data used to calculate the General Fund growth adjustment for the Council's mandated funding.
As the state's principal budget agency, DBM is responsible for calculating and implementing the mandated appropriation formula specified in the bill for inclusion in the annual state budget.

The bill clarifies the funding formula for the Maryland State Arts Council and mentions the Maryland E-Nnovation Initiative Fund and the Special Fund for Preservation of Cultural Arts, all of which are programs or units overseen by the Department of Commerce.

The bill specifies the distribution of tax revenue to the Calvert County Youth Recreational Opportunities Fund, which is established under the Natural Resources Article and falls under the department's general domain of recreation and conservation.
The bill details the distribution of State admissions and amusement tax revenue to the Maryland Stadium Authority and funds it manages, such as the Michael Erin Busch Sports Fund.
The bill explicitly grants the Legislative Auditor the authority to conduct reviews or audits of any recipient of a grant from the Maryland State Arts Council.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Crime Classification to study and make recommendations regarding a method for classifying crimes and civil offenses under State law and to identify and logically categorize all crimes and civil offenses that exist under State law; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly on or before December 31, 2023.
Title: Task Force to Study Crime Classification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force to Study Crime Classification, which is tasked with recommending a method for classifying crimes and civil offenses under Maryland law and creating a logical categorization of all existing state violations.
stakeholders: State legislators, legal professionals, law enforcement, and individuals subject to Maryland's criminal and civil laws.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $177,400 in FY 2024 only for the Office of the Attorney General to staff the task force. This cost covers the hiring of contractual personnel, including one full-time attorney and one part-time paralegal. Any expense reimbursements for task force members are expected to be minimal and absorbable with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) is the primary agency responsible for providing staff for the task force. Additionally, the Attorney General (or their designee) is a mandated member of the task force. The fiscal note indicates that OAG will incur approximately $177,400 in costs for contractual personnel to fulfill these requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill explicitly creates the Task Force to Study Crime Classification, which is an entity that falls under this administrative category of temporary bodies established for special studies and recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or their designee) is a mandated member of the task force. The task force's focus on classifying and categorizing all crimes and civil offenses in Maryland directly impacts the agency's work in defending indigent individuals within the criminal justice system.

The task force is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor. As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the broader policy implications of crime classification and criminal justice reform.
The bill involves a significant fiscal impact of approximately $177,400 for personnel, which is managed and overseen by DBM as the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency.

The categorization and classification of offenses (e.g., felony vs. misdemeanor or civil vs. criminal) significantly impact judicial branch operations, jurisdiction, and the management of legal proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Crime classification determines the severity of penalties and sentences, which directly affects the management of the state's correctional facilities, pretrial detention centers, and parole and probation services.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the classification of offenses into criminal or civil categories directly impacts MSP's enforcement activities, reporting, and roadside safety operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As Maryland's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this agency has a high level of subject-matter interest in the classification and categorization of crimes, regardless of its removal from the formal task force membership in the final bill.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "organics recycling" to include the processing of certain compostable packaging materials in a certain manner; requiring the Department of the Environment to approve a single producer responsibility organization to represent the interests of producers by October 1, 2023; establishing a producer responsibility advisory council to provide advice and make recommendations regarding establishing and implementing a producer responsibility program in the State for packaging materials; etc.
Title: Environment - Statewide Recycling Needs Assessment and Producer Responsibility for Packaging Materials
