bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to conduct a statewide recycling needs assessment through an independent consultant and establishes a Producer Responsibility Advisory Council to develop recommendations for a producer responsibility program for packaging materials. It further mandates that MDE approve a single producer responsibility organization to represent producers and expands the definition of 'organics recycling' to include compostable packaging materials.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (Office of Recycling)
stakeholders: Producers of packaging materials, local governments, recycling and organics recycling processors, waste management companies, and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $532,100 in FY 2024 and $12,100 in FY 2025. These costs primarily cover the procurement of an independent consultant to conduct the statewide recycling needs assessment ($500,000) and a part-time contractual position within MDE to staff the advisory council and oversee the assessment. While the bill mentions fees from producer responsibility organizations to cover costs, the immediate fiscal impact is noted as general fund expenditures. State revenues are not affected, and local governments are expected to consult using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for environmental protection, MDE's Office of Recycling is responsible for hiring a consultant to conduct the statewide recycling needs assessment, staffing the new Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council, and approving the producer responsibility organizations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Producer Responsibility Plan Advisory Council, a formal body of appointed stakeholders tasked with evaluating and making recommendations on the establishment and implementation of a producer responsibility program for packaging materials.

MES is specifically named in the current law referenced by the bill as a coordinating body for recycling reports and studies. Additionally, the agency's operational role in managing state recycling infrastructure is directly impacted by the bill's assessment and infrastructure evaluations.

The bill requires the statewide recycling needs assessment to evaluate worker conditions, wages, and benefits at recycling facilities, as well as identify opportunities to increase employment in the industry, which falls under this agency's workforce oversight.

The assessment mandated by the bill must evaluate economic opportunities, business growth, and recommendations for incentives to stimulate the state's recycling industry, aligning with Commerce's mission to attract and retain businesses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The recycling needs assessment must specifically evaluate economic and participation opportunities for women and minority-owned businesses and individuals within the recycling system.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the State Recycling Trust Fund, which will receive registration fees and administrative penalties established by the bill.
The Treasurer is the custodian of the State Recycling Trust Fund, which is modified by the bill to include a separate account for producer responsibility organization fees and penalties.

This agency is responsible for overseeing the fiscal impact described in the fiscal note, including general fund expenditures for a new contractual employee and the costs associated with the independent consultant.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to MDE regarding the drafting of regulations, program oversight, and the enforcement of administrative penalties against producers.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch's implementation of this policy, receives the required reports from MDE and the Advisory Council, and manages related policy coordination.
The bill aligns with this multi-agency initiative's goals of sustainable development and reducing the state's carbon footprint through improved resource conservation and waste reduction strategies.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly or intentionally accessing and intentionally viewing a certain visual representation of a child under the age of 16 years.
Title: Criminal Law - Child Pornography - Accessing and Intentionally Viewing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Pornography -see also- Nudity and Sexual Displays; Obscenity

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from knowingly or intentionally accessing and viewing visual representations (including computer-generated images) of a child under the age of 16 engaged in sexual conduct, sadomasochistic abuse, or sexual excitement. It expands existing child pornography possession laws to include these specific acts, applying the same penalties and affirmative defenses.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals who access or view child pornography, law enforcement agencies, and the Maryland court and correctional systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a minimal increase in State and local general fund revenues and expenditures due to the expanded application of existing criminal penalties. First-time offenders are subject to a misdemeanor conviction with up to 5 years imprisonment and/or a $2,500 fine, while repeat offenders face a felony conviction with up to 10 years imprisonment and/or a $10,000 fine. The Fiscal Note indicates that while the number of new convictions is expected to be minimal, the average cost per inmate in State facilities is approximately $4,970 per month.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is responsible for the incarceration and supervision of individuals convicted under the bill's expanded criminal provisions. The fiscal note explicitly mentions increased expenditures for state correctional facilities and reimbursements to local detention centers.

This agency supports the judicial branch, which will adjudicate the new and expanded criminal cases. The fiscal note identifies the Judiciary as a primary source and notes a minimal impact on court operations and revenue from fines.

The office is responsible for prosecuting offenses related to the integrity of state officials and may investigate misconduct, though this specific criminal law more broadly impacts law enforcement and State's Attorneys.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD is mandated to provide legal representation for indigent defendants charged under the bill's new criminal prohibitions. The fiscal note lists them as a key stakeholder and source of information.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, the State Police are responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including those related to child exploitation and the investigation of child pornography crimes.

The department is Maryland's primary social service provider and protector of children from abuse and neglect. The bill addresses the sexual exploitation of children, which directly intersects with the agency's mission to protect vulnerable youth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, directly advising the Governor on policies like those established in this bill to combat child pornography.

The OAG represents the state in criminal appeals, including those resulting from convictions under child pornography statutes, and provides legal counsel to state agencies on criminal law enforcement.
The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues, including general fund revenues from fines imposed by the District Court for violations of this bill.

DBM oversees state budget execution and fiscal planning, including the anticipated minimal increase in general fund expenditures for incarceration and county reimbursements mentioned in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This entity includes the Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy, which is explicitly mentioned in the fiscal note as a source of sentencing data related to child pornography offenses.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for enforcing state laws and proposing the budget that supports correctional and judicial operations affected by this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing that the terms "spouse", "family", "immediate family", "dependent", and any other terms that denote a spousal relationship shall be construed to include a party to a domestic partnership for purposes of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; and establishing that the provisions of the Program that apply to spouses shall apply to parties who have entered into a domestic partnership.
Title: State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program – Domestic Partnerships
bill_summary: This bill expands the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program to include domestic partners of state employees and retirees. It mandates that terms denoting a spousal relationship in the context of the program's governing statutes be construed to include parties in a domestic partnership, thereby granting them and their dependents eligibility for health, life, and dental benefits equivalent to those provided to spouses.
stakeholders: Maryland State employees, retirees, and their domestic partners and dependents.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Budget and Management will increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2024 to provide health and welfare benefits to newly eligible domestic partners and their dependents. The exact fiscal impact cannot be reliably estimated because the number of individuals who will enroll under these new provisions is unknown. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary agency responsible for the administration and development of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The bill directly requires DBM to update contribution tables, eligibility rules, and internal systems to accommodate domestic partners.

As the state's chief financial officer and manager of the Central Payroll Bureau, the Comptroller's office must implement post-tax payroll deductions and calculate imputed income for domestic partner benefits to ensure compliance with IRS W-2 reporting.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, and the bill mandates that the health program encompass all units within the executive branch, including those with independent personnel systems.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including DBM, regarding the statutory interpretation of the new provisions and the legal requirements for establishing domestic partnerships.

The bill explicitly includes state retirees in the expanded eligibility for health benefits; the Retirement Agency manages communications and support services for the retiree population impacted by this change.

The Judicial branch is explicitly encompassed by the bill's provisions. As the central support agency for the judiciary, the AOC is responsible for the operational and financial administration of benefits for its employees.

The bill applies to units with independent personnel systems, specifically including large entities like the University System of Maryland, which must comply with the expanded benefit requirements for its faculty and staff.
Morgan State University operates an independent personnel system from the USM and is explicitly required to follow the updated health and welfare benefit provisions for domestic partnerships.
As an independent state college with its own personnel system, Saint Mary's College is encompassed by the bill's requirement to include domestic partners in the state health program.
MDOT manages various modal administrations with unique personnel requirements that are included in the scope of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

MDTA is an independent state agency with its own personnel and police force that operates within the state's health benefits program and is affected by the expansion of spousal terms to include domestic partners.

Synopsis: Providing, for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, an addition modification under the Maryland income tax for the amount of a certain tax credit claimed for certain taxes paid to another state by a pass-through entity under certain circumstances.
Title: Income Tax – Out–of–State Taxes Paid by Pass–Through Entities – Addition Modification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

bill_summary: This bill requires a resident member of a pass-through entity (PTE) to add back to their Maryland adjusted gross income the amount of any income tax credit claimed for taxes paid by the PTE to another state, provided those taxes were deductible in determining the PTE's income under the federal Internal Revenue Code. The measure is designed to align the state tax treatment of out-of-state PTE taxes with the treatment of Maryland-specific PTE taxes.
stakeholders: Resident members of pass-through entities, including shareholders of S corporations, partners in partnerships, and members of limited liability companies (LLCs).
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2024. The specific financial impact is indeterminate because it depends on the tax elections of out-of-state and multi-state pass-through entities and their respective tax treatments in other jurisdictions. Expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for tax collection and enforcement. As the agency that requested this bill, it will be responsible for implementing the new addition modification, updating tax forms, and collecting the resulting revenues from pass-through entity members.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. This bill is projected to increase general fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2024, which directly impacts the state's budget projections and execution managed by this agency.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes between taxpayers and the Comptroller. Changes to the tax code, specifically new addition modifications like the one proposed in this bill, can lead to factual or legal disputes that the Court would be responsible for resolving.

As the state's chief financial agency responsible for receiving and depositing state funds, the Treasurer's Office is impacted by the increase in tax revenues collected and distributed to the general fund.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. The fiscal impact of this bill on the general fund affects the financial resources available for the Governor's policy initiatives and budget proposals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of tax laws. They may be involved in defending the state's position in cases where the application of this new tax modification is contested.

Synopsis: Requiring the Comptroller, as Administrator of abandoned property in the State, to determine the value of certain nonmonetary abandoned property; and authorizing the Administrator, if it is determined the property has no commercial value and need not be offered for sale, to return the property to the holder, destroy the property, or dispose of the property.
Title: Commercial Law – Abandoned Property – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Comptroller, acting as the Administrator of abandoned property, to determine the commercial value of non-monetary abandoned property within one year of delivery. It authorizes the Comptroller to dispose of property that lacks commercial value by returning it to the holder, destroying it, or using other disposal methods instead of conducting a mandatory sale. Additionally, the bill replaces the requirement to publish sale notices in newspapers with a requirement to provide 'reasonable notice' to the public.
stakeholders: Owners and holders of non-monetary abandoned property, the Comptroller's Office, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances. However, the Comptroller's Office may realize cost efficiencies due to an expected reduction in storage, maintenance, and cataloging costs for items that have no commercial value and can now be disposed of rather than stored indefinitely for sale.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller, as the Administrator of abandoned property, with the responsibility to value and dispose of nonmonetary abandoned property. This significantly changes the agency's operational procedures for handling unclaimed assets.

The fiscal note indicates that the state may realize cost efficiencies, particularly in reduced storage costs, due to the new disposal authorities. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and estimating revenues affected by these efficiencies.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Comptroller and would be responsible for interpreting the new disposal authorities and the immunity provision (Section 17-316(F)) protecting the State from legal actions related to these transactions.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the Comptroller's operations and officially signed the bill into law (Chapter 19).

Synopsis: Correcting a certain incorrect cross-reference to the federal Internal Revenue Code relating to the federal work opportunity credit.
Title: Income Tax - Work Opportunity Tax Credit - Technical Correction
bill_summary: This bill makes a technical correction to the Maryland income tax law by updating an incorrect cross-reference to the federal Internal Revenue Code regarding the Work Opportunity Tax Credit. The correction ensures the State's nonrefundable income tax credit for employers correctly aligns with federal law.
stakeholders: Maryland employers, including not-for-profit entities, who hire individuals from targeted groups that face significant barriers to employment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is technical in nature and has no impact on State or local finances. Both state and local revenues and expenditures remain unchanged.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's chief tax collector and the agency that requested this bill. The bill corrects a technical error in the tax code related to the federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit, which the Comptroller's Office is responsible for administering at the state level.

The federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit requires certification from a designated state workforce agency. The Department of Labor typically handles these workforce certifications for targeted employment groups, making the correct statutory alignment of this credit relevant to their operational context.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management oversees revenue estimates and budget execution. While the fiscal note indicates no impact because the bill is technical, DBM monitors all changes to the Maryland tax code for fiscal policy consistency.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signs legislation into law. This bill was introduced as a departmental request from an executive agency under the administration's purview.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and reviews all legislation for legal form and sufficiency. This technical correction ensures that the Maryland Code correctly references the federal Internal Revenue Code.

Synopsis: Altering eligibility for the State child and dependent care tax credit; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
Title: Income Tax - Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit - Alterations
bill_summary: This bill modifies the eligibility requirements for the Maryland child and dependent care tax credit by limiting the credit specifically to resident taxpayers, thereby excluding nonresident taxpayers from claiming it.
stakeholders: Maryland resident and nonresident taxpayers who claim the child and dependent care tax credit
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $332,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2024 due to the elimination of the credit for nonresident taxpayers. There is no estimated impact on local government finances or State expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's income tax laws and collecting revenues. This departmental bill was introduced at the Comptroller's request and directly impacts the agency's duties in managing and enforcing eligibility for the child and dependent care tax credit.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and managing the state's fiscal planning. This bill has a direct impact on the general fund, with estimated revenue increases of $332,000 annually starting in FY 2024, which DBM must incorporate into the state budget.

The Maryland Tax Court is the administrative body that hears appeals from the final decisions of taxing authorities like the Comptroller. It would be the venue for adjudicating disputes regarding the denial of the tax credit based on the residency requirements established by this bill.

The State Treasurer is responsible for receiving and depositing state funds. As this bill is projected to increase state general fund revenues by over $300,000 per year, the Treasurer's Office will manage these additional deposits.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Comptroller and the state government. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal definitions of 'resident' and 'taxpayer' under the Tax - General Article as modified by this legislation.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and the state budget. This bill affects state revenues and tax policy, which are central to the Governor's fiscal and administrative oversight.

Synopsis: Altering the amount of a certain appropriation the Governor is required to make for the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund; and repealing a provision of law requiring 100% of the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund to be used for community enhancement projects in sustainable communities located, at least in part, within the boundary created by Interstate 495 in the State and the District of Columbia beginning in fiscal year 2024.
Title: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund - Annual Appropriation and Authorized Uses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill increases the mandated annual appropriation for the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund from $7,000,000 to $12,000,000 beginning in fiscal year 2025. It also updates the geographical boundaries for eligible community enhancement projects in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties, making existing usage requirements permanent and repealing a provision that would have restricted the fund's use starting in fiscal year 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Sustainable communities in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties, local government agencies, housing authorities, community development organizations, and small businesses involved in development activities.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in fiscal year 2025, State expenditures (either general funds or general obligation bonds) will increase by $5,000,000 annually to meet the new mandated appropriation level of $12,000,000. This results in a commensurate increase in special fund revenues and expenditures for the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent they receive additional financial assistance from the fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for community development and the administrator of the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund, the department is responsible for managing the fund, designating 'sustainable communities,' and overseeing the distribution of the increased appropriations for community enhancement projects.

The Governor is explicitly required by the bill to include the mandated $12 million annual appropriation in the state budget beginning in fiscal 2025 and oversees the executive branch's implementation of the economic development strategy.
This agency is responsible for developing the state budget and managing the fiscal impact of the $5 million annual increase in mandated appropriations required by the bill.

The agency provides data analysis and policy guidance for land use and is heavily involved in the definition and recommendation of 'sustainable communities' and 'priority funding areas' which determine project eligibility under the bill.
The Treasurer manages the state's funds and General Obligation bond issuances, which the fiscal note indicates are a likely source for the $5 million increase in funding for the development fund.
The Board, composed of the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, must approve the issuance of State bonds and significant expenditures related to the capital projects funded by this bill.
The Comptroller monitors state revenues and expenditures and serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which oversees the fiscal allocation of the fund's resources.

As the state's primary economic development agency, Commerce has a secondary interest in programs like the National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund that aim to stimulate regional job creation and business retention.
This multi-agency initiative coordinates the planning visions and sustainable development policies that underpin the eligibility criteria for the projects funded by the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing that a sheriff's sale of real property extinguishes subordinate liens on the land being sold; providing that certain provisions of the Act do not impair a lien on land affected by a judgment in favor of a local government for real property maintenance violations or nuisance condition violations that is indexed and recorded in accordance with the Maryland Rules; and authorizing the Judiciary to transfer up to $12,000,000 of a General Fund appropriation to a certain special fund on or before June 30, 2023.
Title: Real Property - Sheriff's Sales - Procedures and Subordinate Interests

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill establishes procedures for sheriff's sales of real property, including requiring judgment creditors to provide notice to record owners and subordinate lienholders. It specifies that a sheriff's sale extinguishes subordinate liens and allows sheriffs to use assessment records instead of appraisals for real property. Additionally, it authorizes the Judiciary to transfer up to 12,000,000 dollars from its general fund appropriation to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund.
stakeholders: Judgment creditors, property owners, subordinate lienholders, condominium and homeowners associations, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase by up to 12,000,000 dollars in fiscal 2023, while general fund revenues decrease by the same amount. This results from the bill allowing the Judiciary to transfer funds to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund that would otherwise revert to the general fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judiciary by authorizing a transfer of up to $12 million from its General Fund appropriation to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund. It also establishes new procedural requirements for sheriff's sales, including the filing of affidavits with the court and adherence to rules adopted by the Supreme Court of Maryland.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact by authorizing the transfer of $12 million that would otherwise revert to the State's General Fund. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and fiscal planning.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller oversees the collection and distribution of state funds, including the movement of appropriations between general and special funds.

The bill provides significant funding to the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund, which is used to support and preserve land records, a core interest and responsibility of the Maryland State Archives.

The legislation modifies the enforcement of liens and procedures for real property sales, including specific provisions for homeowners associations and local government liens related to property maintenance and nuisance violations.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the Judiciary regarding real property law, the extinguishment of subordinate liens, and the statutory requirements for judgment executions.
The bill's changes to sheriff's sales and subordinate interest extinguishment may impact small businesses that serve as judgment creditors or hold secondary interests in real property.
The Treasurer is responsible for the management and distribution of state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works, which oversees significant fiscal transfers and state property interests.

Synopsis: Expanding the investigative jurisdiction of the Independent Investigations Division of the Office of the Attorney General to include a police-involved incident resulting in serious bodily injury to an individual that is not otherwise within the jurisdiction of the Division; requiring the Division to submit an annual report on its activities in the prior calendar year to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before January 31; authorizing the Attorney General to prosecute certain criminal matters under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Office of the Attorney General - Independent Investigations Division - Authority to Prosecute

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: The bill expands the investigative and prosecutorial authority of the Independent Investigations Division (IID) within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). Specifically, it grants the Attorney General exclusive authority to prosecute criminal offenses discovered during investigations of police-involved incidents resulting in death or life-threatening injury. It also allows State's Attorneys to refer serious bodily injury cases to the IID and requires the division to submit annual reports on its activities to the Governor and General Assembly.
stakeholders: Police officers, law enforcement agencies, State's Attorneys, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $548,900 in FY 2024 for the Office of the Attorney General to hire four additional staff members and cover operational costs. Expenditures are projected to increase annually, reaching $729,700 by FY 2028. Local fiscal impact is expected to be minimal as resources are redirected within State's Attorney's offices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Office of the Attorney General by expanding the investigative jurisdiction of its Independent Investigations Division (IID) and granting the Attorney General exclusive authority to prosecute certain criminal offenses discovered during these investigations.

As Maryland's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is subject to the bill's notification and cooperation requirements. Furthermore, the bill explicitly authorizes the IID to detail MSP officers to assist with investigations of police misconduct.

The bill requires the IID to submit an annual report of its activities to the Governor. Additionally, the Governor is mandated to include funding in the state budget sufficient for the division's operation.

The bill has a significant fiscal impact, requiring an increase in general fund expenditures ($548,900 in FY 2024) for staffing and operations. DBM, as the state's principal fiscal agency, is responsible for overseeing these expenditures and the associated personnel management.

The bill involves the use of grand juries, issuance of subpoenas, and potential injunctive relief in court. The AOC provides the operational and legal support necessary for the judiciary to handle these expanded prosecutorial and investigative proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The expansion of the Attorney General's prosecutorial authority over police-involved incidents will directly impact the caseload and defense strategies of the OPD, which represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy, GOCPP is impacted by changes to the investigation and prosecution of police misconduct, which are central to its mission of reducing crime and improving public safety policy.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates criminal offenses related to the integrity of state officials. The IID's expanded jurisdiction over police misconduct may lead to overlapping areas of inquiry or require coordination between the two independent offices.

MDOT oversees several law enforcement entities, including the Maryland Transit Administration Police and the Maryland Aviation Administration's police force at BWI, all of which are subject to the bill's requirements to notify the IID of certain incidents.
The MDTA maintains its own nationally accredited police force, which must comply with the bill's mandates for notifying the IID of police-involved incidents and cooperating with investigations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The DPSCS employs law enforcement and correctional personnel who are subject to the bill's notification and cooperation requirements regarding incidents resulting in death or serious injury.

The DNR's Natural Resources Police must comply with the bill's requirements for reporting incidents to the IID and providing evidence during state investigations of police-involved deaths or injuries.
Member institutions within the USM operate their own police departments, which are law enforcement agencies required to adhere to the notification and cooperation protocols established by the bill.

Morgan State University operates its own police department, making it subject to the bill's requirements for reporting police-involved incidents to the Attorney General's Independent Investigations Division.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS regulates the state's EMS network; because the bill concerns incidents resulting in death or injuries likely to result in death, the protocols for medical reporting and prehospital care within their system are relevant to the IID's investigations.
MCSS oversees school safety personnel and resources; incidents involving school police officers that result in serious injury or death would be subject to investigation by the IID under this bill.

The OLA conducts fiscal compliance and performance audits of state agencies; the expansion of the OAG's IID and its associated funding will be subject to future audits by this office to ensure financial accountability and legal compliance.

Synopsis: Altering the term "inmate" to be "incarcerated individual" meaning an individual who is actually or constructively detained or confined in a correctional facility.
Title: Corrections - Incarcerated Individuals
bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland law by replacing the term 'inmate' with 'incarcerated individual' in all statutes, executive orders, rules, and regulations. It also directs the publisher of the Annotated Code of Maryland to update cross-references and terminology to reflect this change.
stakeholders: Individuals detained or confined in Maryland correctional facilities and State officials or units responsible for maintaining legal records and policies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the changes are technical in nature and do not affect governmental finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the state's correctional facilities and the supervision of individuals within them, this bill directly affects their core terminology, official documentation, and operational policies.
This agency manages youth in residential facilities and juvenile justice systems; the bill's requirement to update terminology in all state documents applies to their operations and records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in the justice system; the bill's mandate to rename 'inmates' to 'incarcerated individuals' affects their legal filings, case records, and communications.
The judiciary must update court rules, legal forms, and terminology in judicial proceedings to align with the new statutory definition.
As the chief legal representative for the state and its agencies, the OAG must ensure all legal advice, contracts, and regulations reflect the updated terminology.
The Department of Health provides behavioral and public health services to individuals within correctional facilities and must update its regulatory and service documents accordingly.
The State Police interact with individuals entering or being transported between correctional facilities and must update enforcement records and internal policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this agency is responsible for policy development that must now use the updated terminology.
This agency adjudicates contested cases for correctional and juvenile services; its administrative law judges and legal documents will be required to use the new term.
This agency interacts with individuals in correctional facilities regarding child support, foster care, and other social services, requiring updates to case management documents.
The Department of Labor administers workforce development and adult learning programs within correctional facilities, which will require terminology updates in program materials.
The Department oversees educational programs for incarcerated populations and must update its policies and certification documents.
The bill specifically mandates that Executive Orders and documents created by any official or unit of the state must adopt the new terminology.
As the custodian of state records and executive orders, the Secretary of State is responsible for the official transition of these terms in the state's permanent records.
The Archives preserve state executive, legislative, and judicial records; the renaming of 'inmates' in all future government documents affects their archival collection and categorization.

Synopsis: Authorizing and empowering the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow not more than $65,600,000 in order to finance the construction, improvement, or development of certain public facilities in Carroll County, and to effect such borrowing by the issuance and sale at public or private sale of its general obligation bonds; etc.
Title: Carroll County - Public Facilities Bond

NarrowSubjects.Name: Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Carroll County Commissioners to borrow up to $65.6 million by issuing general obligation bonds to finance various public projects, including school renovations, road improvements, water and sewer infrastructure, and loans for volunteer fire department equipment and facilities.
stakeholders: Residents, students, and emergency service providers in Carroll County
fiscal_impact_summary: Carroll County receives up to $65,600,000 in bond proceeds for capital projects. Debt service expenditures are estimated to increase by approximately $4,400,000 annually over a 20-year period, based on a 2.97% interest rate. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and signing legislation, including local bond authorizations such as this one for Carroll County.
The bonds and the interest they generate are exempt from state and local taxation; the Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and administrator of state tax laws.
The bill authorizes borrowing for the acquisition of agricultural land and woodland preservation easements, which is a core part of the agency's mission to protect environmental resources.
A significant portion of the bond funds ($21.2 million) is specifically earmarked for public school infrastructure projects, including HVAC and roof replacements.
The bill authorizes loans to volunteer fire departments for fire or emergency-related equipment and facilities, aligning with the agency's role in emergency preparedness and jurisdiction support.
The bond authorization includes financing for the construction and improvement of public health and social services facilities in Carroll County.
The bill explicitly allows for bond proceeds to be used for the development of buildings and facilities related to social services.
The bill funds conservation and open space projects, including stormwater facility renovations and woodland preservation easements.
The agency promotes sustainable growth and manages historic and cultural programs; the bill involves land use planning through agricultural and woodland preservation.
The bond proceeds are authorized for water and sewer infrastructure, landfills, and watershed assessment and improvement (NPDES) projects.
The bill authorizes the county to finance public works projects such as roads, bridges, and pavement management programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: A major portion of the bond authorization ($21.7 million) is designated for public safety, including a new headquarters for the Sheriff's Office.
The bill authorizes bond proceeds to be used for the construction and development of buildings and facilities at Carroll Community College.
The agency oversees the planning and funding of public school construction and capital improvements, which constitute a major expenditure category under this bill.
The bill identifies libraries as public facilities that may be constructed, improved, or developed using the authorized bond proceeds.

Synopsis: Altering the Black Bear Damage Reimbursement Fund to authorize grants from the Fund to be made for projects that prevent damages caused by black bears and reduce conflicts between black bears and humans; renaming the Fund to be the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund; increasing the maximum amount of reimbursement from the Fund per person annually authorized for damage caused by black bears to $5,000; authorizing the Governor to include at least $50,000 in the annual budget bill for the Fund; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund - Uses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill renames and expands the scope of the Black Bear Damage Reimbursement Fund to include grants for nonlethal bear damage prevention and conflict reduction projects. It increases the maximum annual reimbursement for bear-related damages from $3,000 to $5,000, establishes a $500 minimum reimbursement threshold, and authorizes a discretionary annual state appropriation of $50,000 to support the fund's activities.
stakeholders: Farmers, landowners, local governments, businesses, nonprofit organizations, tribes, and higher education institutions in Maryland's black bear regions.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $145,600 in FY 2024, which includes a $50,000 discretionary appropriation to the fund and $95,637 for administrative costs, including one natural resources technician and a vehicle. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $50,000 annually. Local governments and small businesses, especially farmers, may see a financial benefit through grants or increased damage reimbursements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for managing the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund, DNR is tasked with establishing the new grant program, accepting grant requests, determining project eligibility, and adopting regulations to carry out the bill's provisions.

The bill involves a potential annual appropriation to the fund and significant administrative costs for DNR, including the hiring of a new natural resources technician, which falls under DBM's oversight of state personnel and the budget.

The bill directly impacts the agricultural community by providing grants and reimbursements for damages to crops, beehives, livestock, and poultry, and references definitions within the Agriculture Article.

The bill identifies institutions of higher education as eligible grant recipients and specifically requires that damage amounts for reimbursement be determined by an extension agent of the University of Maryland Cooperative Extension Service.
The bill explicitly states that the State Treasurer shall hold the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund.
The bill explicitly states that the State Comptroller shall account for the fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of at least $50,000 to the fund in the annual budget bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources and would likely assist in the drafting of the required regulations for the expanded fund and grant program.

As an advocate for rural interests and housed within the Department of Agriculture, the Council is relevant because the bill addresses issues primarily affecting rural counties where black bear conflicts occur.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is identified in the bill as an entity eligible to apply for grants from the fund.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland is identified in the bill as an entity eligible to apply for grants from the fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the holder of a Class 4 limited winery license to prepare, sell, or serve any food under certain conditions; altering certain requirements for off-premises and on-premises consumption at a limited winery; and removing the 14-day notice requirement for certain planned promotional events at a limited winery.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 4 Limited Winery License - Food Service

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Class 4 limited winery license holders to prepare, sell, and serve a wider range of food items, specifically including sandwiches and other light fare. It extends the standard hours for on-premises consumption from 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily and removes the requirement that wineries provide 14 days' notice to the State before holding promotional events. Additionally, wineries may serve an unrestricted menu if they are licensed as food establishments and maintain certain food-to-alcohol sales ratios.
stakeholders: Class 4 limited winery license holders, small business wineries, and winery consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. However, the fiscal note indicates a meaningful impact on small businesses, as Class 4 limited winery licensees may see an increase in revenues resulting from expanded food service authorizations and extended operating hours.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments (Agriculture, Health, and Commerce) tasked with implementing the bill's provisions and coordinates the policy initiatives related to the state's winery industry.

The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. This bill directly alters administrative requirements for winery license holders under the Comptroller's purview, including the repeal of a 14-day notice requirement for promotional events and the oversight of product storage and warehouse access.

The Secretary of Agriculture is specifically authorized by the bill to grant annual exemptions to the requirement that 51% of a winery's ingredients be grown in Maryland and must adopt regulations for these exemptions.

The bill allows wineries to expand their food service operations provided they are licensed as food establishments under Title 21 of the Health - General Article, which is administered and enforced by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill impacts the economic viability and operational scope of Maryland wineries, which are significant small businesses and contributors to the state's tourism and agricultural economy promoted by the Department of Commerce.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to consult with the Governor’s Wine and Grape Advisory Commission, which falls under this category, when developing regulations for ingredient requirement exemptions.

Synopsis: Altering the salary of the Washington County Sheriff to be 90% of the salary of the State's Attorney of Washington County; and repealing the requirement for the Washington County Salary Study Commission to study and issue a report that contains recommendations relating to the salary of the Sheriff of Washington County.
Title: Washington County - Sheriff's Salary - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill changes the method for determining the salary of the Washington County Sheriff, setting it at 90% of the salary of the Washington County State's Attorney. It also removes the Sheriff's salary from the review and recommendation process of the Washington County Salary Study Commission.
responsible_party: Washington County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: The Sheriff of Washington County and the taxpayers of Washington County.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Washington County expenditures will increase by a minimum of $21,100 in fiscal 2027 and $36,200 annually thereafter. This increase is timed to coincide with the next term of office beginning in December 2026. There is no impact on State revenue or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Sheriff is an officer of the court, and the bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article. The Sheriff's salary is now linked to a percentage of the salary of a District Court judge (indirectly via the State's Attorney). Because the AOC manages operational and financial support for the judicial branch, including implementing judicial salary adjustments that will now trigger changes for the Washington County Sheriff, the agency is relevant.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Governor is responsible for signing this legislation into law. The Sheriff is a constitutional officer within the state's executive framework.

The Sheriff is a member of the State Retirement and Pension System. Alterations to the Sheriff's salary directly impact the calculation of pension contributions and future retirement benefits administered by this agency.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of General Services, in coordination with the Department of Information Technology, to negotiate certain contracts with third parties for the acquisition or maintenance of body-worn cameras, equipment, or technology for certain law enforcement agencies; requiring the Department of Information Technology, in coordination with the Department of General Services, to study the cost and feasibility of implementing a statewide uniform storage and access system for law enforcement body-worn camera data; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Law Enforcement - Body-Worn Cameras (Body-Worn Camera Appropriation and Financing Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of General Services, in coordination with the Department of Information Technology, to negotiate contracts for the acquisition and maintenance of body-worn cameras and related technology for law enforcement agencies upon request. It also requires the Department of Information Technology to conduct a study on the cost and feasibility of a statewide uniform storage and access system for body-worn camera data and report its findings to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of General Services and Maryland Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: Maryland State, county, and municipal law enforcement agencies and their officers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are expected to increase by between $200,000 and $400,000 in fiscal 2024 for a feasibility study conducted by a consultant for the Department of Information Technology. State and local law enforcement agencies may experience administrative efficiencies and potential cost variations through the use of centralized contract negotiations facilitated by the Department of General Services. No impact on revenues is projected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Department of General Services to negotiate contracts with third parties for the acquisition and maintenance of body-worn cameras and related technology for law enforcement agencies.
The bill mandates that the Department of Information Technology lead a study on the cost and feasibility of a statewide uniform storage system and coordinate with DGS on camera procurement contracts.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is a primary subject of body-worn camera requirements and will be impacted by the procurement contracts and storage study established by this bill.
The Department of Natural Resources operates the Natural Resources Police, a law enforcement agency that is eligible to utilize the body-worn camera contracts negotiated under this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees law enforcement and security organizations, such as the Division of Parole and Probation, which are impacted by the bill's provisions for body-worn camera procurement and data storage.
MDOT oversees modal administrations with their own police forces (e.g., MTA and MDTA Police) that are authorized to enforce state criminal laws and would be eligible for the BWC procurement programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety strategies and manages funds for law enforcement; the fiscal note mentions the office conducted a previous study related to body-worn camera costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This entity includes the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is tasked by the bill with ensuring body-worn camera equipment complies with their established training and policy standards.
DBM oversees state fiscal operations and the general fund expenditures required for the feasibility study mandated by the bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to DGS and DoIT in the negotiation of state contracts and the implementation of new regulatory requirements for law enforcement technology.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority; exempting the Authority from certain provisions of State procurement law; and altering the report on the Authority's comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy the Authority is required to submit to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly to be due by December 15, 2023, to include any procurement activities undertaken by the Authority, and to be also submitted to the House Health and Government Operations Committee.
Title: Baltimore City – West North Avenue Development Authority – Membership and Procurement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: This bill modifies the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority (WNADA) in Baltimore City, adding the Secretary of Commerce, the Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation, and other appointed members. It extends the deadline for the Authority to report its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to December 15, 2023, and grants the Authority an exemption from most State procurement laws, while still requiring adherence to the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program and the maintenance of written procurement policies.
stakeholders: Residents and community organizations within the West North Avenue target area and buffer zone in Baltimore City, including the Alliance of Rosemont Community Associations, Bolton Hill Community Association, Coppin Heights Community Development Corporation, Druid Heights Community Development Corporation, Greater Mondawmin Coordinating Council, Penn North Community Association, Reservoir Hill Improvement Council, Reservoir Hill Association, and Upper Eutaw Madison Neighborhood Association.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. WNADA intends to use $250,000 in existing funds for a revitalization strategy contract, and the bill's procurement exemptions are intended to expedite this process. The Authority's direct operations are supported by 11,400,000 dollars included in the fiscal 2024 budget.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a member of the West North Avenue Development Authority, and the Authority's mission of neighborhood revitalization directly aligns with this department's core responsibilities.
The Secretary of Transportation is a member of the Authority, and the Authority's comprehensive revitalization plan includes focus on motor vehicle and pedestrian transportation infrastructure.
The Secretary of Commerce is added as a new member of the Authority under the bill, reflecting the body's role in local economic development.
The Executive Director of MEDCO is added as a member of the Authority under this bill.
The President of Coppin State University, a USM institution, is a member of the Authority and is designated as its chair.
The bill exempts the Authority from most provisions of State procurement law (Division II of the State Finance and Procurement Article), for which DGS is the central procurement authority.
The procurement exemption in the bill removes typical Board of Public Works oversight and approval requirements for the Authority's contracts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly states that the Authority remains subject to the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program, which this office oversees and monitors.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The West North Avenue Development Authority is a state-created body with appointed members and specific reporting duties to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Governor appoints a member to the Authority and receives its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report.
This office assists the Governor in fulfilling the statutory responsibility to appoint a qualified individual to the Authority's board.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is impacted by the Authority's exemption from standard State procurement oversight.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer is impacted by the Authority's exemption from standard State procurement oversight.
The Authority manages appropriated funds from the State, and DBM oversees budget execution and personnel policies for state-created entities.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions, including advice on procurement exemptions and statutory duties.
OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of state-created bodies like the Authority to ensure financial accountability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The exemption from Division II procurement laws alters the standard path for bid protests and contract disputes that would typically be heard by this board.

Synopsis: Establishing certain procedures regarding the persons who may establish or receive distributions from an ABLE account in the Maryland ABLE Program for a certain eligible individual; and requiring the Maryland 529 Board to adopt certain procedures regarding the establishment and operation of an ABLE account by a person other than a certain designated beneficiary.
Title: Maryland Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) Program - Account Establishment - Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes procedures for authorized individuals to open and manage Maryland ABLE savings accounts for individuals with disabilities who cannot do so themselves. It aligns state law with federal IRS regulations by defining a priority list of family members, guardians, and agents who can establish accounts and request distributions, while excluding individuals with a history of financial exploitation or protective orders.
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities and their family members, legal guardians, and agents
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues are expected to decrease starting in FY 2024 due to increased personal income tax subtraction modifications; the State revenue loss is estimated at $135,700 per 1,000 new tax filers. Maryland 529 nonbudgeted revenues will increase from account fees, potentially offsetting the current $300,000 annual State grant for program operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland 529 is the state program that administers the Maryland ABLE Program, and its Board is explicitly required by the bill to adopt procedures for the establishment and operation of accounts by third-party individuals.
The State Treasurer's Office oversees Maryland 529 and its savings programs, including the ABLE program, making it the primary administrative agency responsible for the bill's implementation.
The Maryland Department of Disabilities is a statutory consultant for the Maryland ABLE Program and is responsible for promoting its use to the residents with disabilities it serves.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact on state income tax revenues, which the Comptroller collects, due to the potential increase in subtraction modifications claimed for ABLE account contributions and distributions.

The Department of Health administers the Medicaid program, and ABLE account assets are excluded from means-testing for Medicaid eligibility, requiring coordination on the program's impact on benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office advocates for the welfare and resource access of deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals, a significant demographic that is eligible for and served by ABLE accounts.

The bill establishes a priority hierarchy for account establishment that includes court-involved roles such as legal guardians and conservators, affecting the oversight of these legal representatives.
The agency manages means-tested programs like SNAP that are impacted by the federal and state exclusion of ABLE account assets from eligibility determinations.
The bill amends the Education Article of the Maryland Code and impacts financial planning for individuals receiving special education services overseen by the department.
DBM oversees the state's general fund and budget; it is impacted by the decrease in state tax revenues and the management of the annual grant currently provided to the ABLE program.
The office works to improve access to health services and economic opportunities for children, including those with disabilities who would benefit from ABLE account expansion.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland 529 Board and other state agencies regarding the regulatory changes and procedural compliance required by the bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy initiatives supporting individuals with disabilities, and the Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law.

Synopsis: Establishing the Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program in the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to provide eligible seniors access to affordable civil law-related services; and requiring the Governor to provide an appropriation of $225,000 in the annual budget for the Program.
Title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program
bill_summary: This bill establishes the Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program within the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. The program is designed to provide seniors aged 65 and older with family incomes up to 75% of the state median access to affordable legal services for essential estate planning, including the preparation of wills, powers of attorney, special needs trusts, advance health care directives, and life estate deeds, with a specific focus on reaching individuals in rural communities.
stakeholders: Maryland seniors aged 65 and older with family incomes at or below 75% of the state median and nonprofit legal service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $225,000 annually. Funding for fiscal 2024 is discretionary, but the bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation of $225,000 starting in fiscal 2025. The bill has no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a grant program specifically for seniors (aged 65 and older) to access civil legal services. This directly aligns with the Department of Aging's mission to improve the quality of life and protect the rights of older adults in Maryland.

The bill mandates a $225,000 annual general fund appropriation for the new program starting in FY 2025. DBM is responsible for developing the state budget and managing personnel/fiscal policies related to such appropriations.

The Governor is required by the bill to include the mandated appropriation in the annual budget. Additionally, the Maryland Legal Services Corporation (MLSC) is required to report implementation and utilization data to the Governor annually.

The grant program provides legal services primarily for last wills and testaments and life estate deeds. The Register of Wills is the state agency responsible for the administrative probate of estates and the safekeeping of wills, making this program highly relevant to their workflow.

The bill explicitly requires the program to provide services and outreach to rural communities, including funding grantees to represent clients in rural areas where other attorneys are not readily available.

As the support agency for the judicial branch, the AOC is impacted by initiatives that provide legal assistance in civil matters. The fiscal note also lists the Judiciary as an information source for the bill.

The bill amends the Human Services Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland. While MLSC is independent, the statutory location and the focus on vulnerable low-income seniors link it to the broad scope of human services regulated by the state.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to apply to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration at the Center for Mental Health Services for federal planning, development, and implementation grant funds related to certified community behavioral health clinics for fiscal year 2025; and requiring the Department to apply to the Administration for inclusion in the state certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration program for fiscal year 2026.
Title: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics - Planning Grant Funds and Demonstration Application

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to apply for federal planning and implementation grant funds in fiscal 2025 and to seek inclusion in the federal certified community behavioral health clinic (CCBHC) demonstration program for fiscal 2026. CCBHCs provide comprehensive, coordinated behavioral health care regardless of a patient's ability to pay.
stakeholders: Individuals requiring mental health or substance use treatment, military service members and veterans, and non-profit community behavioral health organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can apply for federal grants and program inclusion using existing budgeted resources. Although federal fund revenues may increase in fiscal 2025 if grant funds are awarded (based on a 65% federal matching rate), specific dollar estimates are not provided in the Fiscal Note. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including applying for federal planning grant funds from SAMHSA and applying for inclusion in the state certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration program.

The bill's definition of a 'Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic' specifically includes the provision of community-based mental health care for military service members and veterans as one of the required services.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising the execution of the budget, including the management and reporting of the federal grant funds the Department of Health is required to apply for under this bill.

The commission's responsibilities include planning for state health system needs and improving access to health care. The establishment of the CCBHC model and the regulatory standards for these clinics are relevant to their oversight of health system quality and availability.

The clinics established by this bill provide behavioral health and psychiatric rehabilitation services, which are critical components of the delivery of services to Maryland residents with disabilities, an area coordinated by this department.

Synopsis: Defining "commercial use" in Baltimore City to include multifamily residential development if the development is located within a waterfront commercial zoning district and within a 0.50-mile radius of a commuter rail station.
Title: Baltimore City - Commercial Use - Definition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of "commercial use" in Baltimore City to include multifamily residential development, provided that the development is situated within a waterfront commercial zoning district and within a 0.5-mile radius of a commuter rail station.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
stakeholders: Real estate developers, Baltimore City residents, and the Baltimore City government.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill is not anticipated to have a direct impact on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Land Use Article and directly affects zoning definitions in Baltimore City. The Maryland Department of Planning is the principal agency for promoting sustainable growth and providing technical assistance to local governments on land use and zoning.
The bill facilitates multifamily residential development in specific commercial zones. DHCD is responsible for supporting homeownership, rental housing, and community revitalization investments.
The bill's geographic criteria involve proximity to commuter rail stations and the preamble mentions the Port of Baltimore, both of which fall under MDOT's multimodal oversight.
The preamble explicitly states that the bill is intended to drive economic growth, tourism, and job creation in Baltimore's waterfront, which aligns with the Department of Commerce's mission.
The definition of 'commercial use' under this bill is triggered by proximity to commuter rail stations, which are operated and maintained by the MTA.
This multi-agency initiative focuses on sustainable development and revitalizing communities through land use planning, which is the core subject of the bill.
The preamble highlights the environmental health of the Chesapeake Bay and waterfront areas as a motivation for the bill; DNR is responsible for managing these natural resources.

The bill discusses waterfront development and the sustainability of the Chesapeake Bay. MDE is responsible for environmental restoration and enforcing laws related to water quality and waterfront development.
The preamble specifically mentions the health of the Port of Baltimore as a major economic driver for the State that is linked to the success of this waterfront development.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Council advises on the management and restoration of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, which the preamble identifies as a critical stakeholder in Baltimore's waterfront development.
MEDCO supports real estate development and economic prosperity; this bill facilitates the expansion of development types in key economic zones in Baltimore.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Physicians to place a licensee on emeritus status under certain circumstances; requiring the Board, under certain circumstances, to reinstate the license of an individual who is on inactive or emeritus status; exempting licensees who are on inactive status or emeritus status from continuing medical education requirements; repealing the requirement that the Board issue a license to an individual who is on inactive status under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: State Board of Physicians – Inactive and Emeritus Status

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
