bill_summary: This bill updates the notification requirements for health insurance carriers regarding adverse decisions in nonemergency cases. It allows carriers to provide notification through electronic means such as email, text, or online portals, provided they have affirmative consent from the member or their representative, as an alternative to oral notification by telephone.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health insurance plan members, their representatives, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact as the changes are procedural. The Maryland Insurance Administration also determined there is minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary regulatory body for health insurance carriers in Maryland and the author of the departmental bill. The agency is responsible for enforcing insurance laws, including the internal grievance and adverse decision notification processes modified by this legislation.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) administers the state's health insurance marketplace. The carriers offering plans through MHBE must comply with these modified internal grievance notification requirements.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) oversees broad health policy and the regulation of health care professionals and facilities. While this bill specifically amends the Insurance Article, it impacts the administrative processes of health care providers acting on behalf of members in grievance cases.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and enforces consumer protection laws. Changes to the legal requirements for how insurance carriers communicate adverse decisions to consumers fall under their scope of legal oversight and consumer advocacy.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) manages health benefits for Maryland state employees. As a major purchaser of health insurance plans, DBM is impacted by changes to the grievance and notification procedures that apply to the carriers providing these benefits.

The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is an independent regulatory agency within MDH that focuses on health system planning and accountability. The bill's modifications to carrier reporting and notification requirements relate to MHCC's mission of improving access and accountability in the health care system.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to offer and provide certain products or services in conjunction with a policy at no charge or at a discounted price under certain circumstances; and prohibiting certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from increasing a premium or denying a claim of a policyholder if the policyholder accepts, rejects, uses, or fails to use a certain product or service.
Title: Insurance - Product and Service Offerings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: This bill allows insurers, health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to offer products or services at no charge or a discount to policyholders if the offerings are related to risk mitigation, health enhancement, or the insurance policy's purpose. It prohibits insurers from increasing premiums or denying claims based on a policyholder's use or rejection of these services and requires that the offerings be available to all eligible policyholders.
stakeholders: Life insurers, health insurers, property and casualty insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and policyholders.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can absorb the bill's requirements within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no direct impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As an independent state agency that functions as an insurer of last resort, MAIF is directly impacted by the authorization to offer risk-prevention products or services (such as telematics or safety devices) in conjunction with its policies.

IWIF, acting as the administrator for the state's workers' compensation claims and a major workers' compensation insurer, is affected by changes to property and casualty insurance laws that allow for the provision of risk-mitigation products and services.

The bill affects the types of products and services that health maintenance organizations (HMOs) and health insurers can offer alongside their policies, which is directly relevant to the health insurance marketplace administered by the Exchange.

The Commission is responsible for planning the state's health system and improving access/quality. The bill's provision allowing products that 'enhance the health of the insured' (such as wearable medical devices) aligns with the Commission's oversight of health services and outcomes.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and would be responsible for advising on the interpretation of the new anti-rebating exceptions and defending any resulting regulations.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees public health policy and local health departments; it is relevant because the bill impacts nonprofit health service plans and HMOs, which are critical components of the state's healthcare delivery system.

As the central personnel agency managing benefits for state employees, DBM is relevant because the bill changes the offerings that can be provided by health and life insurers who contract with the state to provide employee benefits.

The Treasurer's Office manages the state's insurance protection through the State Insurance Trust Fund and would be affected by changes in the types of services and risk-mitigation products provided by property and casualty insurers.
MHIP manages health coverage and prescription drug assistance; changes to health insurance law regarding inducements and value-added services are relevant to its administrative functions.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date for the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists from July 1, 2023, to July 1, 2025, ensuring the board's continued operation and regulatory authority under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
stakeholders: Licensed psychologists, psychology associates, and consumers of psychological services in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the board are maintained through fiscal 2025. There is no local fiscal impact and minimal impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Psychologists is an entity within the Department of Health. The bill extends the board's termination date, ensuring the department continues to oversee the licensing and regulation of psychologists in Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Psychologists falls under this category of permanent bodies with regulatory and administrative duties. This bill directly impacts the board's statutory existence by extending its sunset provision.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in appointing members to various state boards. The continuation of the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists ensures the ongoing need to vet and recommend individuals for its nine board member positions.
DBM is responsible for the state's budget execution and personnel management. The extension of the board maintains its special fund revenues and expenditures through the fiscal years 2024 and 2025.
The OAG provides legal counsel and representation to all state boards and commissions, including the Board of Examiners of Psychologists, particularly in regulatory and disciplinary matters.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. The continuation of the Board's regulatory functions implies continued potential for licensing and disciplinary hearings managed by the OAH.
The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Health and its constituent boards, and is responsible for final approval of the sunset extension and appointing board members.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date for the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners by one year to July 1, 2025, allowing the board to continue its regulatory and statutory authority over the practice of physical therapy in Maryland under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act.
responsible_party: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed physical therapists, licensed physical therapy assistants, consumers of physical therapy services, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the board are maintained through fiscal 2025. The bill has no impact on local government and minimal or no economic impact on small businesses. Specific dollar estimates for the board's maintenance were not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is housed within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). The bill extends the board's termination date, directly impacting the department's regulatory oversight of health professionals.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Health and its various boards. The Governor also signs the legislation into law and appoints the members of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel. The fiscal note indicates that special fund revenues and expenditures for the board will be maintained through FY 2025 as a result of this bill.
The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides legal counsel to all state agencies, boards, and commissions, including the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in appointing individuals to state boards. By extending the sunset of this board, the office continues its responsibility to vet and recommend candidates for its eight member positions.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Examiners in Optometry in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Examiners in Optometry - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date for the State Board of Examiners in Optometry until July 1, 2025, allowing the board to continue its regulatory duties, including licensing optometrists and investigating alleged violations of the Maryland Optometry Act.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners in Optometry
stakeholders: Licensed optometrists in Maryland, applicants for optometry licensure, and consumers of optometric services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Examiners in Optometry through fiscal 2025. There is no fiscal impact on local governments, and the Maryland Department of Health indicates minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners in Optometry is a unit of the Maryland Department of Health. This bill extends the board's statutory and regulatory authority, directly impacting the department's oversight of health professional licensing.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its various regulatory boards. The Governor is responsible for signing the sunset extension into law and supervising the board's continued administrative functions.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising the board's budget execution and special fund expenditures, which are maintained by this extension.
The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for all state agencies, including the Board of Examiners in Optometry, providing counsel and representation for its regulatory and disciplinary actions.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and recommending qualified individuals to serve as members of the State Board of Examiners in Optometry.
The OAH provides an impartial hearing process for contested cases and disciplinary actions initiated by the Board of Examiners in Optometry.
The Treasurer's Office is responsible for the management and protection of state funds, including the special fund revenues collected by the board through licensing fees.
The Comptroller's Office, as the state's chief financial officer, oversees the collection of state revenues and manages the financial accounting for the board's activities.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill extends the statutory and regulatory authority of the State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals by one year, moving its termination date from July 1, 2024, to July 1, 2025, as part of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act.
responsible_party: State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals
stakeholders: Residential child care program administrators (RCCPAs), residential child and youth care practitioners (RCYCPs), the Maryland Department of Health, the Department of Human Services, and the Department of Juvenile Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues and expenditures for the board are maintained through fiscal 2025. Specific dollar estimates for the board's annual budget are not provided in the fiscal note, though it notes that as of June 2022, the board certified approximately 959 practitioners and 67 administrators.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals is housed within the Department of Health, which provides administrative support and oversees its regulatory functions. The department also licenses programs that employ these professionals.

The Board certifies professionals who work in residential child care programs that are licensed and monitored by the Department of Human Services. Additionally, the Secretary of Human Services or a designee may be involved in Board-related appointments.

The Board certifies professionals for residential child care programs that are licensed and monitored by the Department of Juvenile Services. The agency is a key stakeholder in the licensing and oversight of the facilities where these professionals work.

The Governor has the statutory authority to appoint six members of the Board and the agency receives the Board's annual reports. The bill was also approved by the Governor as an executive branch priority.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is relevant because the bill extends the Board's termination date, thereby maintaining its general fund revenues and expenditures through FY 2025.

The Board is required to submit annual reports to the Children's Cabinet, which is coordinated by the Governor's Office for Children. The office leads statewide efforts for child well-being that align with the Board's mission.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the process of recruiting and vetting candidates for the six gubernatorial seats on this regulatory board.

Synopsis: Transferring the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy to the Department of Disabilities; requiring the Department to provide staff for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs; and altering the membership of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities to add one individual with a traumatic brain injury.
Title: Department of Disabilities - State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and Maryland Commission on Disabilities - Alterations

bill_summary: This bill transfers the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and staffing responsibilities for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs from the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives to the Maryland Department of Disabilities. It also expands the membership of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities to include an individual with a traumatic brain injury.
stakeholders: Individuals with autism and their families, individuals with traumatic brain injuries, disability advocacy organizations, and state disability service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill transfers two positions and associated general funds from the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives to the Maryland Department of Disabilities. While this results in no net impact on State expenditures, the fiscal 2024 budget included $131,275 for the coordinator position. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOD is the primary agency impacted as it receives the transfer of the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and is tasked with providing staff for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs. The Maryland Commission on Disabilities, which is altered by this bill, is also the advisory body for this department.
The bill transfers the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and staffing responsibilities for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs away from GOCI.
The bill explicitly requires the Governor to transfer positions and associated general funds from the Executive Department (Governor's Office) to the Department of Disabilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership and staffing of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities and the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs, which fall under this collective designation.

DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and personnel transfers related to the moving of the Coordinator's positions. Additionally, the Secretary of Budget and Management is a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities.

The fiscal note indicates that MDH houses the State Traumatic Brain Injury Advisory Board; the addition of a TBI representative to the Commission on Disabilities is intended to balance representation across state agencies and advisory bodies serving individuals with TBI.

Synopsis: Requiring that any system operated by a vehicle manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch or its affiliate for allocating new vehicles to dealers be reasonable and fair.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Allocation of Vehicles

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches to use reasonable and fair systems when allocating new vehicles to dealers. It also requires these entities to disclose their allocation methods to dealers upon written request and places the burden of proof on the manufacturer or distributor in any dispute regarding compliance with these standards.
stakeholders: Vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and motor vehicle dealers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State finances or operations, and there is no impact on local government finances. Small business vehicle dealers may receive a minimal benefit from the requirement that vehicle allocation systems be reasonable and fair.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the regulation of vehicle manufacturers and dealers governed by the Transportation Article amended by this bill.

The MVA is the primary agency responsible for licensing and regulating motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and dealers, ensuring they comply with fair dealing standards established in the Transportation Article.
The OAH adjudicates contested cases and regulatory disputes involving the MVA, which may include enforcement actions or appeals related to vehicle allocation standards.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the MVA and MDOT and would be involved in interpreting the 'reasonable and fair' standards and representing the state in any resulting litigation or appeals.
Disputes regarding compliance with vehicle allocation methods may be litigated in the state court system, for which the AOC provides central operational support.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for enforcing vehicle laws and signed this legislation into law.
DBM reviews and monitors the fiscal impact and personnel needs of legislation affecting state agencies like the MDOT and MVA.

Synopsis: Extending through fiscal year 2027 a requirement that the Comptroller distribute $14,000,000 of certain abandoned property funds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund; and extending through fiscal year 2027 a requirement that the Governor include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $14,000,000 from the Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation.
Title: Access to Counsel in Evictions - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill extends the funding mechanism for the Access to Counsel in Evictions (ACE) Program through fiscal year 2027. It requires the State Comptroller to transfer $14,000,000 annually from unclaimed property funds to the ACE Special Fund and mandates the Governor to include an equivalent $14,000,000 appropriation for the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to provide legal representation in eviction proceedings.
responsible_party: State Comptroller, Governor of Maryland, and the Maryland Legal Services Corporation
stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents facing eviction or termination of housing subsidies
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state general fund revenues will decrease by $14,000,000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2027 due to the redirection of unclaimed property funds. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Access to Counsel in Evictions (ACE) Special Fund will increase by $14,000,000 annually during the same period to meet mandated appropriations. There is no direct fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is designated as the Administrator of the Unclaimed Property Fund from which $14 million is distributed annually to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund. Additionally, the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Special Fund.

The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $14 million from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the state budget through fiscal year 2027.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the state budget development and execution. The bill creates a mandated $14 million annual appropriation and impacts general fund revenues by diverting unclaimed property funds, which DBM must manage in the budget.
The State Treasurer is responsible for holding the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and investing the money within the Fund, with interest earnings credited back to it.

The Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund receives a portion of its funding from settlements or judgments obtained by the Division of Consumer Protection in the OAG related to unfair or deceptive trade practices for rental properties.
The bill provides funding for legal representation in eviction proceedings, which are judicial matters conducted within the state court system managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Fund supports legal representation in eviction and related proceedings, including administrative hearings to terminate housing subsidies, which are adjudicated by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

bill_summary: This bill requires security guards employed directly by businesses to be certified by the Secretary of State Police, establishing new standards for training, liability insurance, and recertification. It mandates that guards complete 12 hours of initial training and 8 hours of continuing education, and requires both agencies and employers to report use of force incidents to the Department of State Police within 48 hours.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police and the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
stakeholders: Security guards, security guard agencies, security guard employers, the Maryland Department of State Police, and the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $476,900 in FY 2024 for the Department of State Police to cover two administrative specialists and one-time technical system upgrades costing $365,000. Annual expenditures are projected to range between $129,500 and $148,900 through FY 2028. Local governments are not significantly impacted, and small businesses employing security guards directly will face increased compliance costs and oversight.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police, specifically the Secretary of State Police, is the primary agency responsible for the administration and enforcement of the bill. The agency is tasked with certifying security guards, issuing certification cards, processing applications and fees, receiving use of force reports, and regulating both security guard agencies and security guard employers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is a unit within this department, to identify or establish training programs for security guard certification. Additionally, the department's CJIS Central Repository is responsible for the background checks and fingerprinting required for certification.

The bill specifies that denials, reprimands, fines, or revocations of security guard certifications are subject to certain hearing provisions. As the central panel for contested administrative cases, the Office of Administrative Hearings would adjudicate disputes between individuals and the Maryland State Police regarding these certifications.

The Department of General Services employs security guards (such as the Maryland Capitol Police) and is explicitly mentioned in the fiscal note. The agency must ensure its security personnel meet the bill's updated certification and training standards.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact requiring significant general fund expenditures for personnel and technical system upgrades at the Department of State Police. DBM is responsible for the oversight of state personnel, benefits, and the execution of the state budget impacted by this legislation.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the Maryland State Police and would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the development of new regulations, enforcement of certification standards, and defending the agency in contested cases.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Public Works, in consultation with the Procurement Improvement Council, to publish a model policy on or before January 1, 2024, concerning the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in procurement contracts; requiring a unit of State government to adopt a written policy that is substantially similar to the Board's policy; requiring a unit that decides not to include a liquidated damages clause under certain circumstances to obtain the approval of the head of unit; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Board of Public Works to publish a model policy regarding the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in State procurement contracts. Every State government unit, including those otherwise exempt from procurement laws, must adopt a written policy similar to this model. The bill also mandates that a unit must obtain approval from its agency head to exclude a liquidated damages clause from a contract or to forgo pursuing liquidated damages for a breach in contracts valued at 5,000,000 dollars or more.
stakeholders: State procurement units and State contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Board of Public Works and other State procuring agencies can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources. The bill has no impact on State revenues or local government finances, and the effect on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is the primary implementing agency, tasked with publishing the model policy on liquidated damages and approving decisions by state units not to pursue liquidated damages for major contract breaches.
The Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works and the office is a Primary Procurement Unit responsible for establishing and following the new liquidated damages policies.

As a Primary Procurement Unit and the central procurement authority for many state agencies, DGS must adopt the liquidated damages policy and oversee its implementation across units within its control.
MDOT is a Primary Procurement Unit responsible for a high volume of construction and service contracts that will be subject to the new policy and reporting requirements for liquidated damages.
USM is a Primary Procurement Unit explicitly required by the bill to comply with the new liquidated damages policy and reporting provisions, notwithstanding its general procurement exemptions.
Morgan State is a Primary Procurement Unit explicitly required by the bill to comply with the new liquidated damages policy and reporting provisions.
St. Mary's College is a Primary Procurement Unit explicitly required by the bill to comply with the new liquidated damages policy and reporting provisions.

The bill explicitly includes the Maryland Stadium Authority under the scope of the new section 15-113, requiring it to follow the state's liquidated damages policy despite other procurement exemptions.
The Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System is explicitly named in the bill as being subject to the new liquidated damages policy and reporting requirements.
Maryland 529 is explicitly named in the bill as being subject to the new liquidated damages policy and reporting requirements for its investment and management services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees the Maryland Corps Program, which is explicitly cited in the bill as subject to the new liquidated damages reporting and policy provisions.
The Maryland Port Administration is a Primary Procurement Unit that must adopt and implement the new liquidated damages policies for its maritime and commercial contracts.
The OAG provides legal counsel for state agencies on contract drafting and is consulted regarding the legality and inclusion of liquidated damages provisions.
The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is responsible for publishing the model policy and approving contract modifications or waivers of liquidated damages.
The bill specifically references information processing and telecommunication services under Title 3.5, which are managed by DoIT, as being subject to high-value contract requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Includes the Procurement Improvement Council, which the Board of Public Works must consult when developing the model liquidated damages policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The board adjudicates contract disputes and bid protests, which often involve the interpretation and enforcement of liquidated damages clauses.
Commerce is identified in the fiscal note as a unit that is generally exempt from state procurement law but will now be subject to the bill's liquidated damages requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is listed as a unit generally exempt from state procurement law that must now comply with the bill's liquidated damages reporting and policy provisions.
The State Archives is identified as an exempt unit that must now follow the state's liquidated damages policies and obtain head-of-unit approval for deviations.
The commission is identified as a unit generally exempt from state procurement law that must now comply with the bill's liquidated damages requirements.
MEA is identified as a unit generally exempt from state procurement law that must now comply with the bill's liquidated damages policy and reporting requirements.
The trust is listed as an exempt unit that must now comply with the bill's liquidated damages reporting and policy provisions.
The council is identified as a unit generally exempt from state procurement law that must now follow the state's liquidated damages policies.
The authority is identified as a unit generally exempt from state procurement law that must now comply with the bill's liquidated damages requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Health & Higher Educational Facilities Authority
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The authority is identified as a unit generally exempt from state procurement law that must now comply with the bill's liquidated damages requirements.
The Governor chairs the Board of Public Works, which is the lead agency for implementing the bill's policy requirements.

Synopsis: Requiring an application for any new qualified offshore wind project and a certain proposal for an offshore wind transmission facility to be subject to a certain community benefit agreement; requiring the Public Service Commission to request that PJM Interconnection conduct a certain analysis of transmission system upgrade and expansion options; altering the requirements for a certain report on offshore wind projects; requiring the Commission, by a certain date each year starting in 2024, to report on its Supplier Diversity Program; etc.
Title: Offshore Wind Energy - State Goals and Procurement (Promoting Offshore Wind Energy Resources Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The Promoting Offshore Wind Energy Resources Act (POWER Act) establishes a state goal of achieving 8,500 megawatts of offshore wind energy capacity by 2031. It requires the Public Service Commission (PSC) to coordinate with PJM Interconnection to analyze and solicit proposals for transmission system upgrades to support this capacity. Additionally, the Department of General Services (DGS) is directed to procure up to 5,000,000 megawatt-hours of offshore wind energy annually through long-term power purchase agreements. The bill updates labor standards, requiring community benefit agreements and specific apprentice ratios, and allows developers to apply for exemptions from certain ratepayer remittance requirements if federal tax credit conditions are met.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission and Department of General Services
stakeholders: Offshore wind energy developers, residential and nonresidential electricity ratepayers, labor organizations and skilled craft workers, small and minority-owned businesses, PJM Interconnection, and state agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases state special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission by approximately $5,400,000 between FY 2024 and FY 2028, with these costs recovered via assessments on public service companies. This includes an intended appropriation of at least $3,500,000 in FY 2025 for required transmission studies and analyses. General fund expenditures for the Department of General Services increase by approximately $1,400,000 over the five-year period for procurement staff and management. The long-term impact on State and local electricity expenditures is indeterminate but potentially significant due to the 20-year duration of power purchase agreements and changes to ratepayer remittance of federal tax credits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory agency responsible for the bill's implementation, including requesting transmission system analyses from PJM, issuing solicitations for offshore wind transmission projects, and overseeing OREC order exemptions.
The Department of General Services is mandated to issue a competitive sealed procurement for a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) for offshore wind energy to meet state needs.
The Maryland Energy Administration is a key consultative agency required to work with the PSC on transmission analyses, solicitations, and evaluating project proposals.

The Department of Natural Resources, via the Power Plant Research Program, is responsible for evaluating project siting and proposing conditions for the construction and operation of transmission facilities.
The Department of Labor is involved in determining prevailing wage rates and registered apprenticeship standards required for community benefit agreements under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs is tasked with assisting applicants and establishing minority business enterprise participation goals for offshore wind projects.
The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential consumers in PSC proceedings, which will include evaluations of ratepayer impacts from the new transmission and energy procurements.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the implementing agencies and is specifically named to consult on minority business enterprise plans and agreements.
The Department of the Environment oversees the state's greenhouse gas reduction targets, which the bill explicitly aims to support through expanded offshore wind capacity.
The Department of Budget and Management is impacted by the creation of new personnel positions at the PSC and the fiscal requirements for the studies and procurements.
The Board of Public Works oversees significant state contracts; the DGS procurement of large-scale power purchase agreements typically requires its approval.
The Governor's Office coordinates high-level policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch agencies charged with implementing the state's offshore wind goals.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller will review and approve significant procurements related to the state's offshore wind energy goals.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer will review and approve significant procurements related to the state's offshore wind energy goals.
The Department of Planning coordinates land use planning, which is relevant to the onshore components of transmission system upgrades mentioned in the bill.
This multi-agency initiative is relevant as the bill's goals align with its mission to promote sustainable development and environmental protection through renewable energy.

Synopsis: Allowing multiple final tax certificates to be issued for a catalytic revitalization project in certain circumstances; and requiring the Smart Growth Subcabinet to study Maryland's historic complexes and make recommendations about an implementation plan to address the preservation and reuse of historic complexes in the State on or before December 31, 2023.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Smart Growth Subcabinet to study and make recommendations for an implementation plan to address the preservation and reuse of historic complexes in the State. It also modifies the Catalytic Revitalization Project tax credit program by allowing the Department of Housing and Community Development to issue multiple final tax credit certificates for projects completed in phases and establishing specific conditions for the transfer of initial tax credit certificates.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and the Smart Growth Subcabinet
stakeholders: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities involved in the rehabilitation of historic complexes, as well as local communities where such complexes are located.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State fiscal impact is indeterminate but potentially significant in any given year because the bill allows the Catalytic Revitalization Project tax credit to be claimed for completed phases rather than only upon total project completion, potentially accelerating revenue losses. Under current law, individual projects are capped at $15,000,000 in credits. The required study by the Smart Growth Subcabinet is expected to be completed using existing budgeted resources. There is also a potential impact on local highway user revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primary amends the Catalytic Revitalization Project tax credit, which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development. The Secretary of this department is responsible for issuing tax credit certificates and determining project eligibility.

The Department of Planning staffs the Smart Growth Subcabinet, which is mandated by the bill to study and make recommendations on the preservation and reuse of historic complexes. It also oversees the Maryland Historical Trust, the state's authority on historic property inventories.

As the state's tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for processing the income tax credits modified by the bill and manages the fiscal impact resulting from the potential acceleration of tax credit claims.

The department is involved in the disposition of state-owned properties and is specifically mentioned in the bill's study requirements regarding site assessments and the maintenance of historic properties prior to transfer.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Smart Growth Subcabinet—a collective body of agency heads—to conduct a comprehensive study and report on the implementation plan for historic complexes.
The bill requires the Treasurer's opinion to ensure that the disposition of historic properties does not adversely affect the tax-exempt status of outstanding State bonds.

The fiscal note indicates potential impacts on the Transportation Trust Fund and local highway user revenues. The bill also cross-references the Transportation Article regarding property re-acquisition rights.
The Smart Growth Subcabinet must report its findings and recommendations directly to the Governor, who also oversees the policy initiatives regarding community revitalization and smart growth.
The Secretary of Commerce is a member of the Smart Growth Subcabinet and the department is involved in assessing the economic impact of preserving and reusing historic complexes.
The agency is part of the Smart Growth Subcabinet and provides expertise on environmental remediation requirements for the redevelopment of historic state-owned properties.
The Department of Health is a member of the Smart Growth Subcabinet; many historic complexes eligible for revitalization were formerly mental health or hospital facilities under its jurisdiction.
As a member of the Smart Growth Subcabinet, the department oversees the fiscal implications of state personnel and resources used in the implementation of historic property reuse plans.
The Secretary of Labor is a member of the Smart Growth Subcabinet involved in the interagency study of historic property preservation.
The Secretary of Natural Resources is a member of the Smart Growth Subcabinet involved in the mandated study of historic complexes.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements for the registration and termination of domestic partnerships with the register of wills; repealing provisions on legitimacy and illegitimacy of children and providing for the parentage of a child born or conceived by registered domestic partners; requiring the register of wills to recognize as domestic partnerships relationships established under the laws of other jurisdictions if the laws are substantially similar to the provisions of the Act; etc.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Registered Domestic Partnerships

bill_summary: This bill establishes a process for two individuals to register a domestic partnership with the Register of Wills, granting them rights and benefits equivalent to marriage in matters of estates and trusts. These benefits include inheritance rights in cases of intestacy, family allowances, priority for appointment as personal representatives, and an inheritance tax exemption on all property passing to a surviving partner. The bill also updates terminology regarding children and parentage and removes inheritance distinctions based on legitimacy.
stakeholders: Unmarried couples in committed relationships, children of registered domestic partners, and heirs or legatees of decedents.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are expected to decrease annually due to the expansion of the inheritance tax exemption to include all property passing to a registered domestic partner. This revenue loss will be partially offset by a new registration fee of up to $25 per domestic partnership filing. The specific fiscal impact cannot be reliably estimated, though total inheritance tax revenue in fiscal 2022 was approximately 76900000. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency responsible for the registration and termination of domestic partnerships under the bill. It must maintain records, collect fees, and establish a certified list of recognized jurisdictions with similar laws, while also handling administrative probate and inheritance taxes involving these partners.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational, financial, and technological support to the state's courts and Registers of Wills. Since the bill creates new registration requirements and alters probate procedures, the AOC will be responsible for supporting the implementation of these functions.

As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is impacted by the bill's expansion of inheritance tax exemptions to include registered domestic partners. The agency will need to update tax enforcement and auditing processes to reflect these changes in state revenue.

The bill alters legal presumptions of parentage for children born or conceived during registered domestic partnerships and through assisted reproduction. These changes directly impact the agency's Child Support Services, which relies on legal parentage determinations for its programs.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates appeals from the final decisions of state taxing authorities. The new inheritance tax exemptions for registered domestic partners and resulting changes in estate distribution may lead to disputes and appeals within this court's jurisdiction.

The fiscal note indicates a decrease in general fund revenue due to the new inheritance tax exemptions. DBM, as the principal fiscal agency responsible for revenue estimation and long-term planning, must account for this impact in the state budget.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Registers of Wills and the Comptroller. They will likely be called upon to provide guidance on the interpretation of 'substantially similar' laws in other jurisdictions and the legal nuances of the new domestic partnership registration process.

Synopsis: Establishing the Cyber Maryland Program in the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to create and execute a talent pipeline that materially reduces workforce vacancies by July 1, 2026, build an advanced cybersecurity workforce, and carry out other purposes related to the cybersecurity workforce in the State; establishing the Cyber Maryland Fund; authorizing the Governor to include an appropriation of $250,000 for the Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter; etc.
Title: Economic Development - Cybersecurity - Cyber Maryland Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Cyber Maryland Program within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to develop a cybersecurity talent pipeline and reduce workforce vacancies. It creates the Cyber Maryland Fund to provide grants for cybersecurity programs and establishes the Cyber Maryland Board to oversee strategic planning. The bill also updates the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program to align with industry certification trends and modifies its funding allocation rules.
stakeholders: Cybersecurity professionals, IT employers, students in K-12 and higher education, Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), community colleges, and state and local government agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $690,000 in FY 2024 to support TEDCO staffing and the implementation of the Talent Pipeline Management Approach. Starting in FY 2025, the bill mandates an annual appropriation sufficient for program staff, with total estimated annual costs ranging between $669,300 and $705,400 through FY 2028. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Cyber Maryland Fund increase correspondingly. Local governments may see increased revenue through program grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Cyber Maryland Program and the Cyber Maryland Fund within TEDCO, making it the primary agency responsible for administering the program, hiring staff, and managing cybersecurity workforce initiatives.
The bill mandates that MHEC, in consultation with certain organizations, expand the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program and modifies how it allocates grants to participating institutions.

The Secretary of Labor serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and the program is required to coordinate with the department's workforce development efforts, including apprenticeships and the EARN program.
The Secretary of Information Technology serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and a primary purpose of the program is to support DoIT in improving the state government's cybersecurity posture.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is a member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and the program coordinates with the department on statewide cybersecurity strategic planning.
The Governor appoints several members to the Cyber Maryland Board and is responsible for including mandated appropriations for the program and fund in the annual budget.
DBM is responsible for overseeing the mandated appropriations for the program's staff and the Cyber Maryland Fund, as well as managing the fiscal execution of the bill.
Morgan State University is specifically named as a governing entity for the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program, which is modified and expanded under the bill.
The bill involves several USM institutions (Bowie State, UMES, and UMBC Training Centers) as governing entities and participants in the modified Cyber Warrior Diversity Program.
The Cyber Maryland Fund is authorized to provide grants to elementary and secondary schools for cybersecurity programs, which falls under the oversight of MSDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Cyber Maryland Board, a new advisory body composed of state officials and private sector representatives to guide the program's strategic plan.
The program's mission to create a cybersecurity talent pipeline and coordinate workforce development directly aligns with the board's role in setting the state's workforce vision.
The Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now the Secretary of Veterans & Military Families) is a designated member of the Cyber Maryland Board.
The State Treasurer is responsible for holding the Cyber Maryland Fund separately and investing its money.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Cyber Maryland Fund.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the various state agencies and boards involved in the implementation of the Cyber Maryland Program.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the newly created Cyber Maryland Board.
The program's requirement to conduct research and analyze workforce data may involve coordination with the MLDS Center's repository of student and workforce outcomes.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health to develop a report comparing options for offering affordable health care and dental care coverage to State residents who are ineligible for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, the Maryland Children's Health Program, qualified health plans, or stand-alone dental plans due to the individuals' immigration status; and requiring the Exchange and the Department to report to certain committees of the General Assembly by October 31, 2023.
Title: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and Maryland Department of Health - Health Care and Dental Care Coverage for Undocumented Immigrants - Report

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health to develop a report comparing options for offering affordable health and dental care coverage to Maryland residents who are currently ineligible for Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, or plans through the Exchange due to their immigration status.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland residents who are ineligible for state-funded health insurance or Exchange plans due to their immigration status.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note states that the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health can develop the required report and submit findings using existing budgeted resources. No impact on State revenues or local government finances is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Health to lead the development of the report comparing health care and dental coverage options for undocumented immigrants and to report findings to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to lead the development of the report, specifically focusing on options for qualified health plans and stand-alone dental plans through the Exchange.

As the independent agency responsible for planning for the state's health system needs and improving access to care, the MHCC's mission is directly aligned with the bill's objective to study expanded coverage options.
The bill requires the report to compare the 'cost to the State' for various implementation options, which involves the long-term fiscal planning and revenue estimation responsibilities of DBM.
The MIA regulates Maryland's insurance market, including the qualified health plans and dental plans that are the subject of the mandated report's study.

The bill specifically requires the report to analyze coverage options for individuals under the age of 21, aligning with the GOC's mission to improve access to health services for Maryland's children.
The bill specifically requires the report to analyze coverage options for individuals at least 65 years old, a demographic served by the Department of Aging.
The bill requires analysis of coverage for 'low-income individuals,' a core demographic served by DHS through various economic assistance programs.

This team is charged with identifying and testing novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility and address child poverty, which overlaps with the bill's focus on affordable health access for vulnerable populations.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, and would likely review the legal implications of the proposed coverage options in the report.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (MDH and MHBE) tasked with this report and coordinates the related policy initiatives.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to provide a discount of at least $40 on annual State park passes for Maryland residents who are law enforcement officers or first responders.
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers and first responders residing in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues will decrease minimally beginning in fiscal 2023 due to the mandatory discount. For illustrative purposes, the Department of Legislative Services estimates a potential annual revenue decrease of $9,360. State expenditures are not expected to be materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, as it manages the Maryland Park Service and is mandated to provide the discounted annual State park passes to law enforcement officers and first responders.
As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, its officers are direct beneficiaries of the annual State park pass discount established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department employs a significant number of law enforcement officers and public safety personnel who qualify for the discounts provided under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees and regulates the state's emergency medical services network, whose personnel are classified as first responders and are eligible for the discount.
The department coordinates the state's first responders, who are among the primary groups eligible for the discount on annual State park passes.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources and would assist in ensuring the new discount regulations comply with state law and existing park pass structures.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), in conjunction with the Board of Environmental Health Specialists, to conduct a study on the staffing needs of environmental health specialists in local health departments. It also requires MDE to study the implications of delegating its authority regarding well and septic systems permitting to MDH. Both studies require reports to the Governor and the General Assembly containing findings and recommendations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Environmental health specialists, local health departments, well and septic system permit applicants, and state environmental and health agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State finances are not materially affected as the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local finances are not directly affected, assuming local health departments can provide necessary data within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for conducting both studies mandated by the bill. This includes studying staffing needs for environmental health specialists and analyzing the implications of delegating its permitting authority for well and septic systems to the Department of Health.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is required to conduct a study on staffing needs for environmental health specialists in conjunction with MDE. Furthermore, the bill investigates the delegation of well and septic systems permitting authority to MDH, making the agency a central focus of the legislative review.

The bill explicitly requires the University of Maryland Agriculture and Food Systems Extension Program, which is part of the University System of Maryland, to be consulted and involved in the study of delegating authority related to well and septic systems permitting.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Environmental Health Specialists is specifically required to participate in the study on staffing needs for environmental health specialists alongside MDE and MDH.
The Governor's Office is the recipient of the final reports and recommendations produced by the mandated studies, and the bill was signed into law by the Governor.

The Department of Budget and Management is listed as an information source in the fiscal note. Although specific personnel increase requirements were struck from the final version of the bill, DBM remains relevant as the agency oversight for state personnel and fiscal impacts of the studies.

The Higher Education Commission is listed as an information source in the fiscal note, likely due to provisions in the earlier version of the bill regarding student loan forgiveness for environmental health specialists that were ultimately struck.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to provide grants to nonprofit and faith-based organizations for security enhancements to protect against hate crimes. The fund is used to provide physical security measures and includes a specific set-aside of at least 1,000,000 dollars annually for faith-based institutions.
responsible_party: Executive Director of the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, faith-based organizations, and Maryland residents belonging to groups targeted for hate crimes.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by 5,000,000 dollars annually starting in fiscal 2025 to capitalize the fund. According to the Fiscal Note, special fund revenues and expenditures increase by 5,000,000 dollars in fiscal 2024 (using existing program funds) and 10,000,000 dollars annually thereafter (reflecting 5,000,000 dollars for the existing program plus the new capitalization funding). There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Executive Director of this office (formerly GOCPYVS) to administer the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund, establish distribution procedures, and submit annual reports to the General Assembly.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund, a new special fund created by the legislation.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold and invest the money in the newly established Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the budget development and execution related to the $5 million annual appropriation authorized to capitalize the fund.

The Governor is authorized to include specific appropriations for the fund in the annual budget and the office oversees the executive branch policy priorities related to public safety and community protection.
This agency manages various ethnic and faith-based commissions and connects community organizations with government resources; these entities are the primary intended recipients of the grants.
OLA is responsible for periodic fiscal compliance audits of all executive branch agencies and special funds, which will include the new grant fund and its administrator.
The bill's purpose to protect against hate crimes aligns with the Commission's mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws and provide educational outreach regarding civil rights.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual budget bill of $500,000 for the State Department of Education to provide grants to local school systems for expenses related to student field trips to museums of cultural import.
Title: Local School Systems - Student Field Trips - Funding
bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to include $500,000 in the annual budget bill for the Maryland State Department of Education to provide grants to local school systems. These grants are intended to cover expenses related to student field trips to 'museums of cultural import,' which include the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, the National Museum of African American History and Culture, the Jewish Museum of Maryland, and the Reginald F. Lewis Museum of Maryland African American History and Culture. The bill also requires the department to submit an annual report detailing the schools that received grants, the grant amounts, student demographics, and the destinations of the field trips.
stakeholders: Local school systems, Maryland public school students, and the four designated museums of cultural import.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025 due to the mandated appropriation. The Maryland State Department of Education is expected to administer the grants using existing resources. Locally, school systems will receive a total of $500,000 in annual grant funding statewide starting in fiscal year 2025, with local expenditures increasing accordingly to support the field trips.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for administering the $500,000 annual grant program for student field trips and is required to submit a detailed annual report to the General Assembly regarding the grant distribution.
The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) must ensure the $500,000 mandated appropriation is included in the annual state budget and supervise the execution of these funds.
The bill explicitly requires the Governor to include a $500,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for the grants, impacting the Governor's executive budget planning.

The Reginald F. Lewis Museum of Maryland African American History & Culture, which is managed by this corporation, is specifically designated in the bill as a 'museum of cultural import' and a beneficiary of the funded student field trips.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which public, school, college, or university libraries must permit the inspection, use, or disclosure of the circulation record of an individual.
Title: Libraries - Circulation Records - Inspection, Use, or Disclosure Requirement Revision

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill updates the privacy standards for library circulation records in Maryland. It replaces the term 'free association' library with 'public' library and specifies that a library may only permit the inspection, use, or disclosure of an individual's circulation record if it is necessary for the reasonable operation of the library, if the individual provides written consent, or if required by a subpoena or court order.
responsible_party: Maryland public, school, college, and university libraries
stakeholders: Patrons and administrative staff of Maryland public, school, college, and university libraries.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State government or local library system finances or operations, according to the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the official state agency responsible for coordinating Maryland's 24 public library systems and the State Library Network, this agency is directly involved in the oversight of the public libraries affected by this bill's changes to circulation record disclosure requirements.
The MSDE oversees Maryland's public school systems, which include school libraries that are explicitly listed as entities subject to the updated circulation record privacy requirements.

The Commission establishes statewide policies for public and private colleges and universities; these institutions maintain libraries that are subject to the bill's provisions regarding the disclosure of circulation records.

The University System of Maryland manages multiple higher education institutions with libraries that must comply with the bill's revised standards for protecting and disclosing student and faculty circulation records.
As an independent state university, Morgan State operates its own library system which is directly subject to the bill's requirements for handling individual circulation records.
As an independent public honors college and state agency, it maintains institutional libraries that must adhere to the bill's revised protocols for the disclosure of library patron information.

The Maryland School for the Deaf provides tuition-free public education and maintains school library resources for its students, making it subject to the bill's privacy standards for school libraries.

The bill specifies that circulation records must be disclosed in response to a subpoena or court order, which involves the judicial branch operations supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and institutions, including libraries and universities, regarding compliance with privacy laws and responding to subpoenas or court orders.
