bill_summary: This bill establishes the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to provide rental vouchers and housing assistance payments to low-income families currently on a waiting list for the federal Housing Choice Voucher Program. The program is administered by DHCD and local public housing agencies, prioritizing households that include children, foster youth, veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, and elderly or disabled individuals.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and local public housing agencies
stakeholders: Low-income families on federal housing waitlists, specifically targeting those with children, foster youth (ages 18-24), veterans, homeless individuals, elderly persons, and disabled individuals, as well as participating landlords and property owners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $255,400 in FY 2024 for administrative startup. Beginning in FY 2025, the bill mandates a $10,000,000 annual appropriation for the voucher program through FY 2027, with total state expenditures estimated at approximately $10,290,000 per year including administrative costs. By FY 2028, mandated funding must be sufficient to maintain the previous year's voucher count, estimated at $10,620,000. Local government revenues and expenditures will increase as public housing agencies receive and distribute program funds; 6% of the annual appropriation is allocated to these agencies to cover staffing and administrative expenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for state housing programs, the Department of Housing and Community Development is responsible for establishing, administering, and overseeing the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program, including issuing vouchers in jurisdictions without local public housing agencies.

The Governor is required to include a mandated appropriation for the program in the annual state budget ($10 million for FY 2025-2027) and receives annual reports from the Department regarding program performance and demographic data.

As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and overseeing fiscal planning, DBM is directly involved in managing the mandated appropriations and personnel needs required to implement this new voucher program.

The bill prioritizes populations served by DHS, including families with children, former foster youth (aged 18-24), and individuals experiencing homelessness, making this program a significant resource for DHS's core client base.

The bill explicitly prioritizes disabled individuals for vouchers and includes detailed requirements for reasonable accommodations, such as the approval of live-in aides for residents with disabilities.

The bill prioritizes elderly individuals (62+) for vouchers and contains specific provisions regarding the continuation of benefits for surviving family members and the termination of payments if a recipient moves to a long-term care facility.
Military veterans are one of the specific groups designated for equal prioritization in the distribution of the new rental assistance vouchers.
The program aligns with GOC's mission to reduce child poverty and youth homelessness by prioritizing families with children and individuals experiencing homelessness for rental assistance.
The OAG will likely provide legal counsel to the Department regarding the drafting of regulations, program guidelines, and contracts required to implement and enforce the new voucher program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes specific criteria for the denial and termination of housing assistance based on criminal history, including mandatory exclusions for sex offenders and discretionary exclusions for those convicted of violent or drug-related crimes.
This program is a novel state-level initiative directly targeting child poverty and economic mobility, which are the primary priorities and areas of focus for the Maryland State Innovation Team.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain vacant property or nuisance property located in Baltimore City to be subject to a certain in rem foreclosure process; requiring certain procedures for an in rem foreclosure; requiring Baltimore City to take certain actions to compensate the interested parties in property that has value and is acquired through an in rem foreclosure; specifying the title acquired in an in rem foreclosure; specifying the circumstances under which an in rem foreclosure judgment may be reopened; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - Property Tax - In Rem Foreclosure of Vacant or Nuisance Property

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Baltimore City to establish and implement an judicial in rem foreclosure process for properties designated as vacant or nuisance properties under the city building code. It sets procedures for filing complaints, notifying interested parties, conducting hearings, and disposing of foreclosed properties through public auction or city retention while ensuring compensation for interested parties if the property has value.
responsible_party: Baltimore City and the Circuit Court for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Owners and mortgagees of vacant or nuisance properties in Baltimore City, the Baltimore City government, and the Baltimore City Circuit Court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact is indeterminate. State general fund expenditures may increase to accommodate additional foreclosure filings in the Baltimore City Circuit Court. State property tax revenues via the Annuity Bond Fund may be affected by changes in tax collection. Baltimore City may incur administrative and maintenance costs for foreclosed properties, though these may be offset by future property sales or increased tax revenue from rehabilitated properties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a specific judicial in rem foreclosure process that must be initiated in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City. The fiscal note indicates that general fund expenditures for the Administrative Office of the Courts may increase to support additional staff and operating expenses for the clerk of the circuit court to handle these filings.

The bill addresses the foreclosure and disposition of vacant and nuisance properties, which is central to the agency's mission of community revitalization and ensuring safe, secure housing. DHCD was also consulted for the fiscal note analysis.

The bill requires property valuations to be performed by real estate appraisers licensed under Title 16 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article, a profession regulated and licensed by the Maryland Department of Labor.

As the state's chief tax collector and financial officer, the Comptroller is relevant to the bill's impact on state property tax collections and the overall fiscal health of the state's revenue streams, specifically regarding properties in tax arrears.

The fiscal note identifies potential impacts on the Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues, which are used to pay debt service on state general obligation bonds. The State Treasurer's Office is responsible for managing state funds and bond sales.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and was consulted in the analysis of the bill. It provides counsel on the implementation of state tax and property laws and protects consumer rights related to foreclosure proceedings.

DBM is responsible for state personnel and budget execution. If the new judicial process requires additional personnel for the Circuit Court for Baltimore City, DBM would oversee the fiscal impact and staffing allocations.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including urban revitalization and tax-related legislation. The bill was signed by the Governor as a key piece of legislation affecting Maryland's largest city.

The Maryland Tax Court hears appeals regarding property tax assessments and credits. While this bill focuses on Circuit Court proceedings, the underlying issues of tax delinquency and property valuation are within the Tax Court's broader adjudicatory context.

The PTAAB hears disputes over property tax valuations. Because the bill's foreclosure trigger is based on delinquent taxes and property value as determined by the state, the PTAAB's role in the property tax ecosystem is relevant.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and community revitalization through land use policy. The management and foreclosure of vacant and nuisance properties in Baltimore City directly impact urban planning and resource management strategies.

Launched to address the Governor's priorities such as reducing child poverty and enhancing economic mobility, this team targets underinvested communities. Remedying urban blight through in rem foreclosure is a strategic tool for economic mobility in Baltimore.

Synopsis: Altering a certain provision relating to the storage of firearms and ammunition in a location that can be accessed by an unsupervised child; and requiring the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services to develop a youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide, with recommendations from a stakeholder committee.
Title: Firearm Safety - Storage Requirements and Youth Suicide Prevention (Jaelynn's Law)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill, known as Jaelynn’s Law, strengthens firearm storage requirements to prevent unsupervised access by minors and prohibited persons. It raises the age of a 'child' to 'minor' (under 18) regarding storage laws, establishes tiered penalties for violations based on the level of harm caused, and prohibits individuals from possessing firearms for five years after certain storage violations. Additionally, it requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop a youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide and establishes a grant program to support public education on safe storage practices.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services)
stakeholders: Firearm owners, minors under the age of 18, persons prohibited from possessing firearms, local school systems, local health departments, and nonprofit agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates a $1,000,000 annual general fund appropriation starting in fiscal year 2025 to the Maryland Department of Health for the development of a safe storage guide and the administration of education grants. For fiscal year 2024, general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $50,000 for guide development. There is a potential minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures due to the expansion of criminal penalties and incarceration costs related to storage violations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services (within the Maryland Department of Health) as the primary official responsible for developing the youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide, establishing a stakeholder advisory committee, and administering a grant program for family education.

The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $1,000,000 in the state budget for the Department of Health starting in fiscal year 2025, which directly involves DBM's role in budget development and long-term fiscal planning.

The Governor is required by the bill to include a specific $1,000,000 appropriation in the annual budget. Additionally, the Governor oversees the executive branch agencies (MDH, MSP, DJS) tasked with implementing and distributing the new safety guide.

The bill requires the distribution of the safety guide to state and local law enforcement and specifically mentions instructors licensed or certified by the Maryland State Police to teach firearm safety training courses. MSP is also responsible for enforcing the updated firearm storage and possession laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal penalties for reckless endangerment and illegal firearm storage, which impacts the state's correctional system, parole, and probation oversight managed by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the creation of a stakeholder advisory committee to make recommendations regarding the development of the youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide.
DJS is explicitly named as a recipient and distributor of the youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide to families and interested entities.
MSDE is explicitly named as a recipient of the guide and is involved in the distribution to local school systems, which may also apply for grants funded under this bill.
As an independent unit within MSDE focused on school safety, the Center is relevant to the bill's goals of youth suicide prevention and educating school communities on safe firearm storage.
The bill modifies criminal statutes and creates new misdemeanor penalties, affecting the adjudication process and operations within the Maryland Judicial Branch.
The bill maintains an exception for minors who possess a certificate of firearm and hunter safety issued by DNR under the Natural Resources Article, requiring coordination on certification standards.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Department of Health and other agencies during the development of the guide and the implementation of the new regulatory and criminal provisions.

Synopsis: Altering requirements for the removal from office of the State Administrator of Elections; and repealing the authority of the State Administrator to continue to serve in office until a successor is appointed and confirmed following a certain vote for removal of the State Administrator.
Title: State Administrator of Elections - Removal From Office

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill modifies the process for removing the State Administrator of Elections from office. It authorizes the State Board of Elections, when fully constituted with five members, to remove the Administrator by an affirmative vote of four members without requiring a showing of incompetence, misconduct, or other cause. It also repeals requirements for written charges, notice, and a hearing prior to removal, as well as the provision allowing a removed Administrator to continue serving until a successor is confirmed by the Senate.
stakeholders: State Administrator of Elections, State Board of Elections, and the Maryland State Senate
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State finances and has no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly alters the legal requirements and procedures for the removal of the State Administrator of Elections, who is the head of the Maryland State Board of Elections. It specifically changes the authority and notice requirements of the State Board.

As the state's principal personnel agency, DBM manages state employee resources and policies. The bill modifies the removal process for a high-level state official, and DBM was a contributor to the bill's fiscal analysis.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and appoints the members of the State Board of Elections. The bill impacts the governance structure of the state's election apparatus and the powers of those appointed by the Governor.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state boards and commissions. They would be responsible for advising the State Board of Elections on the legal implementation of these new removal procedures and representing the state in any subsequent litigation.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Social Work Examiners in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board; establishing the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure to make certain findings and recommendations regarding examination and licensure of social workers in the State; requiring the Workgroup to submit its final report to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Social Workers - Sunset Extension, Notification of Complete Application, and Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: The bill extends the State Board of Social Work Examiners' termination date to July 1, 2025, and mandates that the Board notify applicants within 15 business days if their application is complete. It also creates a Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure to investigate licensure qualifications, potential examination bias, and alternative assessment methods, requiring various reports through December 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Social Work Examiners
stakeholders: Social workers, licensure applicants, the State Board of Social Work Examiners, and organizations representing diverse social work interests including the Legislative Black Caucus, NAACP, and the Maryland Association of the Deaf.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2024 and $15,400 in FY 2025 to fund contractual staff for the workgroup and support Board operations. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Board are maintained through FY 2025 due to the sunset extension. No local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Board of Social Work Examiners, which is located within the Department. The Department is responsible for staffing the newly established Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure, and the Secretary of Health serves as a member. The fiscal note also identifies a significant general fund expenditure increase for the Department to support the board and workgroup operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure, a temporary body tasked with making findings and recommendations regarding state licensure for social workers. This workgroup falls under this collective agency designation as it is composed of appointed officials and private citizens conducting a special study.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of this office is a mandated member of the Workgroup. The bill specifically addresses the licensing process and requirements for social workers who are deaf or hard of hearing, aligning with the office's mission to ensure state programs are accessible and inclusive.

The Secretary of Human Services is a member of the Workgroup. As the state's primary provider of social services, the department is a major employer of social workers, and changes to licensure requirements or the establishment of temporary licenses directly impact its workforce pipeline.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Workgroup, including deans of social work and master's degree recipients, and must designate the chair. The office also oversees the executive department's boards and commissions affected by the sunset extension.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for the fiscal oversight of the general fund expenditures identified in the fiscal note. Additionally, as the central personnel agency, it is involved in the management of contractual staff required to support the bill's mandates.

The Workgroup must include a Dean of Social Work from a Maryland master's program at a historically Black college or university (HBCU). Morgan State University, as the state's preeminent urban research HBCU with a social work program, is directly involved in this policy development.

The Workgroup includes deans of accredited social work master's programs in the state. The University System of Maryland oversees several institutions that provide these programs, making it relevant to the study of licensure requirements and educational qualifications.

Synopsis: Generally curing previous Acts of the General Assembly with possible title defects; and generally repealing and reenacting without amendments certain Acts of the General Assembly that may be subject to possible title defects in order to validate those Acts.
Title: Annual Curative Bill
bill_summary: This annual curative bill is designed to correct technical title defects in previously enacted legislation. It repeals and reenacts specific sections of the Maryland Code without making substantive changes to ensure the legal validity of laws concerning the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund and penalties for fraudulent conduct during driver's license testing.
stakeholders: The Maryland General Assembly, Maryland Legal Services Corporation (MLSC), driver's license applicants, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is technical in nature and has no effect on governmental finances as it only cures potential legal defects in existing laws.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reenacts Section 16-301(q) of the Transportation Article, which prohibits fraudulent conduct in the driver's license and moped permit examination and testing process, a core administrative function of the MVA.
The bill cures and reenacts sections of the Transportation Article regarding driver's license fraud, which falls under the broad oversight of MDOT and its modal administration, the MVA.
The bill reenacts provisions for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund, specifically designating that the State Treasurer shall hold and invest the fund's money.

The bill specifies that the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund and notes that revenue from unclaimed property (under the Comptroller's jurisdiction) is a source for the fund.

The bill identifies the Division of Consumer Protection within the OAG as a primary source of revenue for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through settlements and judgments related to rental residential property.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific appropriation ($14,000,000 for FY 2024) in the annual budget bill for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund.
The bill contains specific budgetary requirements and appropriations for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund, which DBM oversees as the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of a "therapy horse" under the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program.
Title: Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program – Definitions – Therapy Horse

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill modifies the definition of a therapy horse under the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program by removing the requirement that a licensed stable be a 'premier accredited' member center of the Professional Association of Therapeutic Horsemanship, International (PATH, Intl.). It allows stables that are member centers, but not necessarily 'premier accredited' ones, to qualify provided they meet other criteria.
stakeholders: Maryland veterans seeking service animal assistance and nonprofit training entities or licensed horse stables providing therapy services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact because the change is technical in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances. The small business effect is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program, which is administered by the Department of Veterans & Military Families. The department is responsible for referring veterans to participating stables and managing the program's funding and outreach.

The bill defines a "therapy horse" as one belonging to a stable licensed by the State. The Department of Agriculture regulates animal health and agricultural businesses, including the licensing and oversight of equine facilities.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Veterans & Military Families, and signed this bill into law as part of the administration's policy coordination regarding veteran services.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to issue an annual fishing license and stamp exemption to governmental entities and nonprofit organizations to provide fishing clinics and instructional opportunities to certain individuals; and altering certain reporting requirements for governmental entities and nonprofit organizations that are issued certain fishing license and stamp exemptions.
Title: Natural Resources - Fishing Licenses and Stamps - Exemptions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to issue annual fishing license and stamp exemptions to government entities and nonprofit organizations that provide fishing clinics and instructional opportunities to veterans, active-duty military, individuals in wellness or special needs programs, scientific researchers, and underserved residents. It also modifies the reporting requirements for organizations that receive these exemptions.
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, governmental entities, veterans, active-duty military members, individuals in physical or mental wellness or special needs programs, scientific researchers, and underserved residents of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no material fiscal impact in fiscal 2023. Starting in fiscal 2024, state special fund revenues may increase if individuals who participate in the exempted fishing clinics later purchase their own licenses or stamps. While the Department of Natural Resources suggests this revenue increase could be meaningful, a specific dollar estimate is unavailable. There are no projected impacts on state expenditures or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including issuing the newly authorized fishing license and stamp exemptions, processing applications, managing reporting requirements, and adopting regulations.

The bill authorizes license exemptions specifically to provide fishing clinics and instructional opportunities to individuals who are serving or have served in the U.S. Armed Forces, directly benefiting the department's constituency.

The bill targets individuals with physical or mental disabilities and those participating in special needs outdoor events for recreational fishing license exemptions, which aligns with the department's mission to coordinate services for these residents.

The legislation includes specific license exemptions for patients of State-approved mental health facilities and residents of facilities for developmentally disabled individuals, which are overseen or regulated by this department.

The university system was a consulted source for the fiscal note, and its members may be affected by the bill's provisions regarding exemptions for individuals acting under scientific collection permits, which are often held by university researchers.

Synopsis: Increasing the mandated appropriation that the Governor is required to include for the Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund in the annual budget bill from $250,000 to $625,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
Title: Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund - Funding - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill increases the mandated annual appropriation for the Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund from $250,000 to $625,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2029. It also establishes that the mandated funding for the fund will terminate after fiscal year 2029.
stakeholders: The Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation (MCCEI) and the Maryland construction industry.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $375,000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2029 due to the increased mandated appropriation for the Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the fund increase by corresponding amounts each year. The mandated funding is entirely eliminated beginning in fiscal 2030.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific appropriation in the annual State budget bill for the Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund.
As the agency responsible for developing the state's budget and supervising budget execution, DBM must implement the mandated appropriation increase and was consulted in the fiscal note.
The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland. The Department of Labor oversaw early support for the center and was consulted for the fiscal analysis.

The Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation (MCCEI), which the fund supports, was established based on work by this board (formerly known as the Governor’s Workforce Investment Board).
The Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation (MCCEI) is a public-private partnership located at Towson University, which is an institution within the University System of Maryland.
The Treasurer is responsible for the distribution and management of state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works, which oversees fiscal integrity related to state appropriations.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for paying state bills and overseeing the disbursement of state revenues, including those appropriated to the fund.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Maryland Insurance Commissioner from removing from a certain list of reciprocal jurisdictions created and published by the Commissioner certain jurisdictions located outside the United States and certain jurisdictions in the United States that meet certain accreditation requirements.
Title: Insurance – Credit for Reinsurance Model Law – Reciprocal Jurisdictions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland Insurance Commissioner from removing specific reciprocal jurisdictions from a list of entities authorized to operate in the State without posting collateral. These jurisdictions include those outside the United States subject to covered agreements, member states of the European Union, and U.S. jurisdictions meeting NAIC accreditation standards. This legislation ensures Maryland law aligns with the NAIC Credit for Reinsurance Model Law and federal requirements to avoid preemption by the Federal Insurance Office.
stakeholders: Insurance and reinsurance companies, the Maryland Insurance Administration, and regulatory bodies in reciprocal jurisdictions including the European Union, the United Kingdom, and NAIC-accredited U.S. states.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, as stated in the fiscal note. There is no estimated impact on local government finances or small businesses. The legislation primarily serves to maintain compliance with federal standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the statutory duties of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, who leads the Maryland Insurance Administration. It mandates specific criteria for the Commissioner's list of reciprocal jurisdictions authorized to operate in the State's reinsurance market.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and would be responsible for interpreting the legal requirements of the NAIC Model Law and ensuring the state avoids federal preemption.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the administrative and policy functions of state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration's compliance with national regulatory standards and federal agreements.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Historical Trust, on or before July 1, 2023, to extinguish or terminate a certain easement the Trust holds in the parcel of land known as Warner Manor (also known as Brainard Warner House and/or Circle Manor) in the Town of Kensington, Montgomery County; and requiring the Trust to complete certain necessary recordings and filings to complete the extinguishment or termination of the easement.
Title: Maryland Historical Trust - Warner Manor in the Town of Kensington - Extinguishment or Termination of Easement

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Historical Trust to terminate its historic preservation easement on the Warner Manor property (also known as the Brainard Warner House or Circle Manor) located in Kensington, Montgomery County, by July 1, 2023.
stakeholders: Montgomery County government, the Town of Kensington, and the Maryland Historical Trust
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, there is no state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Historical Trust can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources, and the bill does not directly affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) is an agency within the Maryland Department of Planning. The bill specifically mandates that MHT extinguish or terminate a preservation easement it holds on the Warner Manor property.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland Historical Trust. They would be responsible for drafting and reviewing the legal instruments required to extinguish the easement and ensuring the recordings are legally sufficient.

The bill requires the extinguishment to be recorded in the Land Records of Montgomery County. These records are maintained by the Clerk of the Circuit Court, which falls under the operational and administrative support of the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves the acquisition, lease, or transfer of State property interests. Since an easement is a property interest held by the State, the Board maintains general oversight of the disposal of such interests, even when directed by the legislature.

Synopsis: Abolishing and repealing the Maryland 529 Board; specifying that the State Treasurer is the successor to the Maryland 529 Board; transferring to the Office of the State Treasurer the responsibility for administering the Maryland 529 Program, including the Maryland Prepaid College Trust, the Maryland College Investment Plan, the Maryland Broker-Dealer College Investment Plan, and the Maryland ABLE Program; authorizing and requiring the State Treasurer to take certain actions in administering the Maryland 529 Program; etc.
Title: Higher Education - Maryland 529 Program - Reform

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill abolishes the Maryland 529 Board and transfers the administration of the Maryland 529 Program—including the Prepaid College Trust, the College Investment Plan, and the ABLE Program—to the Office of the State Treasurer. It phases out the Maryland Prepaid College Trust (MPCT) by prohibiting new accounts after June 1, 2023, and establishes a formal claims resolution process for existing MPCT account holders to address issues related to the trust's administration and earnings calculations.
stakeholders: Current and future Maryland 529 account holders and beneficiaries (Prepaid College Trust, College Investment Plan, and ABLE Program), and employees of the Maryland 529 Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by 6,700,000 in FY 2024 to support the transition and eight new positions within the State Treasurer's Office. Additionally, approximately 17,000,000 in existing nonbudgeted, special, and reimbursable funds shift from the abolished Maryland 529 Board to the Office of the State Treasurer. The bill also authorizes the use of existing Prepaid College Trust assets to pay for settlements resulting from claims. There is a potential for a minimal increase in local income tax revenue as the phase-out of the Prepaid College Trust may lead to fewer tax deductions for that specific program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Treasurer's Office is the primary implementing agency, as the bill abolishes the Maryland 529 Board and transfers all responsibility for administering the Maryland 529 Program (including the Prepaid College Trust, College Investment Plan, and ABLE Program) to the State Treasurer.
The Maryland 529 Program is the central subject of the bill, which reforms its governance, abolishes its independent board, and initiates the phase-out of the Prepaid College Trust.

The bill requires the State Treasurer to consult with the Department of Disabilities regarding the administration and promotion of the ABLE program, and adds the Secretary of Disabilities to the Financial Education and Capability Commission.

MHEC is directly impacted as its Secretary is removed from the former 529 Board. Additionally, program funding and matching contributions are budgeted through MHEC before being transferred to the Treasurer's Office.
DBM oversees the transfer of state employees and assets, and manages the fiscal restructuring of how the Maryland 529 Program is funded and recognized within the state budget.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates coordination between the State Treasurer and this agency's board to develop marketing strategies to increase participation in Maryland 529 programs among state employees.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Legislative Auditor continue to perform audits of the Maryland 529 Trust.
The Comptroller is removed as a member of the 529 Board and the agency is responsible for verifying taxable income for the state matching contribution program.
The State Superintendent of Schools is removed from the 529 Board, and the bill requires marketing coordination with local school systems to reach families with low participation rates.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive reorganization and the bill repeals the Governor's authority to appoint public members to the former Maryland 529 Board.
The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland is removed as an ex officio member of the Maryland 529 Board.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Treasurer and the other affected agencies during the administrative transfer and the establishment of the new claims resolution process.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the membership of the Financial Education and Capability Commission by adding the Secretary of Disabilities and the Executive Director of Maryland 529.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Anne Arundel County to be a resident of the State, rather than the county, when an application for a license is filed; and providing that a certain license is valid only for as long as the resident applicant remains a resident of the State.
Title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages Licenses – Residency Requirement
bill_summary: This bill modifies the residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Anne Arundel County. It permits an applicant representing a partnership, corporation, club, or limited liability company to be a resident of the State of Maryland rather than specifically Anne Arundel County at the time of application. The license remains valid only as long as the resident applicant maintains Maryland residency.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Individuals and businesses applying for or holding alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County, specifically partnerships, corporations, clubs, and limited liability companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no impact on State finances and is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County operations or finances. Small business impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This category includes the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County, a state-appointed regulatory body responsible for directly implementing and enforcing the modified residency requirements for alcoholic beverages license applicants within the county.

As the state's chief regulator of the alcohol industry, the Comptroller provides the standardized application forms referenced in the bill that must be updated to reflect the new state-level residency criteria for Anne Arundel County.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions, including local liquor boards, regarding the interpretation and application of statutory changes to the Alcoholic Beverages Article.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "captive REIT" for purposes of a certain addition modification under the Maryland income tax in the amount of the federal dividends paid deduction for captive real estate investment trusts to exclude, under certain circumstances, corporations, trusts, or associations owned or controlled by certain qualified foreign entities and certain trusts owned or controlled by a listed Australian property trust.
Title: Income Tax - Captive Real Estate Investment Trusts - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland income tax definition of a 'captive REIT' to exclude entities owned or controlled by certain qualified foreign entities and specific trusts owned by listed Australian property trusts. As a result, these entities are no longer required to add back the federal dividends paid deduction to their Maryland modified income, which may reduce their corporate income tax liability.
stakeholders: Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), foreign corporations and trusts, Australian property trusts, and Maryland state and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund, Higher Education Investment Fund (HEIF), and Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues may decrease by an indeterminate amount starting in fiscal 2024. Local highway user revenues and corresponding TTF expenditures may also decrease. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the Comptroller’s Office requires a thorough examination of individual corporate structures to determine the full impact on corporate income tax revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's chief tax collector and is responsible for enforcing tax laws. This bill directly alters the definition of 'captive REIT' within the tax code, which impacts the Maryland income tax addition modification that the Comptroller administers.

DBM is responsible for estimating revenues and fiscal planning. The bill's fiscal note indicates an indeterminate decrease in general fund revenues, which DBM must monitor and account for in the state budget.

The fiscal note specifically mentions a decrease in Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues resulting from this bill. MDOT oversees the administrations funded by the TTF and manages the state's transportation network capital grants.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes between taxpayers and the Comptroller regarding income tax assessments. Altering definitions of corporate entities (like captive REITs) frequently leads to litigation that this court would hear.

The bill impacts revenues for the Higher Education Investment Fund (HEIF). As the regulatory and coordinating board for higher education, the commission is impacted by changes in its primary funding streams.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, and represents the state in tax-related litigation and interpretation of the Tax - General Article.

Synopsis: Requiring contractors operating State-owned nursing homes to promptly provide notice of certain deficiencies, enforcement actions, citations, and fines to the Governor, the State agency overseeing the nursing home, certain committees of the General Assembly, and members of the General Assembly who represent the district in which the nursing home is located; etc.
Title: State-Owned Nursing Homes - Deficiencies, Citations, and Fines - Contractor Reporting Requirements

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Nursing Homes -see also- Continuing Care; Long-Term Care

bill_summary: This emergency bill requires contractors operating State-owned nursing homes to promptly notify the Governor, the overseeing State agency, and the General Assembly of any deficiencies or enforcement actions issued by monitoring agencies. Within 30 days of receiving a citation or fine, contractors must provide detailed documentation, including deficiency statements, plans of correction, and survey-related communications. Additionally, the Maryland Department of Health is required to submit an annual report summarizing all federal and State survey activities and enforcement actions at contractor-operated State-owned nursing homes.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and contractors operating State-owned nursing homes
stakeholders: Residents of State-owned nursing homes, private contractors operating these facilities, the Maryland Department of Health, the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs, the Governor, and the Maryland General Assembly.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill's reporting and notification requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances, and no additional funding is mandated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires contractors operating State-owned nursing homes to promptly provide notice of deficiencies or enforcement actions directly to the Governor. It also requires the Department of Health to submit annual reports on these activities to the Governor.

The bill defines the Office of Health Care Quality (within MDH) as a monitoring agency. MDH is mandated to prepare and submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly regarding survey activities and enforcement actions at State-owned nursing homes operated by contractors.

This department (formerly the Department of Veterans Affairs) oversees the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, which the fiscal note identifies as a State-owned nursing home operated by a private contractor and thus directly subject to the bill's notice and reporting requirements.
